fujairah/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Each programme has its own milestone calendar, and the milestones are what a plan is built around. These are the four that matter on the east coast, described by when the pressure arrives rather than by what the programme contains.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years with the load concentrated unevenly. DP1 looks quiet and is not: subject choices, Higher Level levels, the Extended Essay question and the first assessed drafts are all decided inside it. DP2 is where everything internally assessed falls due, usually before the mock season, which is why a student who leaves the core until DP2 is revising and writing at the same time.
programmes.countryNote: A Fujairah student is more exposed to this than a Dubai one, because a small school coordinates the whole programme through fewer people. There is often no dedicated core team chasing a timetable, so an Extended Essay deadline in DP1 passes without anyone noticing until the draft is already late.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed continuously against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, so there is no single point where everything is decided. The Personal Project in the final year is the first long self-managed piece a student writes, and how it goes is a fair predictor of how the Extended Essay will go two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For east-coast families the useful MYP milestone is the options conversation in Year 9, because what is chosen there determines which Diploma or IGCSE routes a local school can actually staff. That conversation happens earlier than most parents here expect it to.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The milestone that catches families out is the entry deadline rather than the exam. Take Pearson's International GCSE November series: the November 2026 papers run from late October to 19 November 2026, yet the centre has to have lodged the entry long before any of that, and results only reach students in January. The Cambridge series a UAE candidate can sit are June and November, each with a closing date published ahead of the papers and repeated on the statement of entry. Tier and subject are fixed at entry, months before anybody sits a paper.
programmes.countryNote: Because east-coast schools sit as Cambridge centres allocated to an administrative zone, the correct timetable version depends on that zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one. Ask the school which zone it sits in before planning the final weeks.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in a May or June window and again in November, which creates a second attempt inside the same academic year. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: The November window matters on this coast because repeating a year is rarely practical when school choice is limited. A student who underperforms in June can re-sit in November without changing school, and the planning question becomes which subjects are worth the second attempt rather than whether to move.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects east-coast families ask about, described by when in the course the difficulty usually arrives. Knowing the month a subject tends to bite is what turns a vague worry into a dated plan.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Bites in the second term of DP1, when the algebra stops being revision of IGCSE and starts assuming fluency. Students who were comfortable to that point often slip quietly. The exploration lands in DP1 or early DP2 and competes directly with content revision for the same hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Difficulty arrives later, usually in the statistics and modelling units, and shows up as interpretation rather than calculation. A plan here is often shorter than for Analysis and Approaches: six to eight weeks to establish the habit of writing what a result means.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two pressure points: moles and stoichiometry early in DP1, organic mechanisms in DP2. The scientific investigation is normally due in DP2 before mocks, so a student with an unresolved content gap is writing it while still behind, which is the worst sequence available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circuits are where east-coast students most often stall, generally in the middle of DP1. Uncertainty treatment surfaces late, in the investigation, and is a fast fix once identified. The ten-week window after the DP1 mock is the most productive one in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rarely produces a dramatic failure and often produces a disappointing grade, because the revision method is the problem rather than the content. Gains come in a short block converting recall into extended-response structure, not in a year of weekly content coverage.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the analysis marks before the evaluation is read, and the Higher Level third paper arrives late in DP2 with quantitative questions students have never systematically practised. Budget specific weeks for Paper 3 rather than assuming it falls out of general revision.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The assessed research project is the timeline risk. A topic too broad to answer in the word limit is chosen in a busy week and the problem is baked in before the first draft. Fixing it after the data has been collected is expensive in weeks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is the component families forget to plan for, because it has no written deadline attached in most schools' minds. It needs a global issue argued rather than announced, and that argument takes weeks of practice rather than one rehearsal.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive skills under timed conditions improve steadily rather than suddenly, so this is one of the few subjects where a long, low-intensity arrangement genuinely beats a short block. Start early and keep sessions short.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: The tier decision in Year 10 is the real deadline, because it sets a ceiling on the grade and is fixed at entry. A borderline student has a genuine window in the first term of Year 10 and a much narrower job once entries have gone.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Required study alongside the licensed curriculum
subjects.description: Runs in parallel all year with first-language and additional-language streams taught separately. The timeline issue is that it is never the subject a family plans for, so it absorbs hours in the exam term that were budgeted for something else.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live in Fujairah changes what time a session can start and how reliably it holds, which is a timeline question rather than a geography one. These are the districts enquiries come from and the practical constraint in each.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Shortest school run in the emirate, so a four o'clock start is realistic for most households. The timeline risk here is the opposite of distance: families delay starting because everything feels accessible, then begin in DP2.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Corniche sports and club commitments run late, pushing a sustainable weekday slot past five. Two shorter sessions a week usually survive the term better here than one long evening that collides with fixtures.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: A mixed-curriculum intake where school reports rarely identify the component at fault, so the diagnostic session earns its place more clearly than elsewhere. Early-evening slots hold well once activities end.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Residential and close to the city schools. Households here often have children in two different year groups, which makes back-to-back slots the practical arrangement and a single visiting appointment awkward to price.

regions.name: Madhab and Al Gurfa
regions.note: A steady turnover of posted families means mid-year arrivals are common. A student joining a Diploma cohort in DP1 mid-term needs a compressed version of the whole sequence, starting with what the new school has already taught.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: An hour up the coast with minimal school choice in range. School buses arrive late, so a realistic first slot is after five, and any plan depending on a weekly drive from the city has a continuity problem built in.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Long gaps between settlements on the northern coast road. Timeline reliability here comes from the arrangement not requiring travel at all, which is the whole reason video sessions dominate this stretch.

regions.name: Masafi and the inland route
regions.note: On the road west, split between Fujairah and Ras Al Khaimah. After heavy rain the route closes, which turns a visiting lesson into a lost week at the point in the year when weeks stop being recoverable.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah City and the coastal districts
schoolClusters.note: The schools within a normal school run of the city, covering British and Indian curricula. Internal deadlines differ between them even for students sitting the same session, which is why a plan starts from the school's own dates rather than a generic calendar.
schools: Our Own English High School Fujairah

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Khor Fakkan corridor
schoolClusters.note: Minutes down the same coast and under the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than the Ministry of Education, with different term dates. Families who move between the two mid-course meet two calendars in one academic year.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses families consider for sixth form
schoolClusters.note: Where a Higher Level combination is not available locally, these are the realistic alternatives, usually on a weekly-boarding or relocation basis. Named as context for a decision, not as a daily commute over the mountain road.

modes.description: A single session that reads the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list, then produces a written assessment of what is actually wrong and how many weeks it is likely to take. Families regularly buy only this and act on it themselves, which is a legitimate outcome.

sections.heading: What a home tutor in Fujairah actually involves, and what happens here instead
paragraphs: Take the question literally for a moment, because it deserves a straight answer. Hiring someone to teach your child at a Fujairah address means hiring from the people who live within a sensible drive of it. In Fujairah City that is a real if small pool for general academic support. In Dibba, Qidfa or Mirbah it is a very short list, and for a Higher Level Diploma subject it is frequently empty. The hourly rate reflects the travel: published market figures for visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE run AED 180-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visiting sessions have sat at AED 1,599-1,799.

There is a legal dimension worth knowing before anybody is invited round. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated: individuals giving private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. MoHRE states that anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted online should be treated as unverified. Ask to see the permit. It costs the tutor nothing to hold.

IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Fujairah, and no tutor will be sent to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is offered only in India. The teaching here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The case for that on this coast is specific and it is about the calendar rather than the technology: a plan that depends on somebody driving the mountain road loses lessons to weather, traffic and the ordinary friction of rescheduling, and lost lessons in February are not recoverable in April. The table sets the two arrangements against each other on the terms that decide a timeline.

sections.heading: Step one: establishing where your child actually is
paragraphs: Everything downstream depends on this and almost nobody does it first. The usual sequence is that a report arrives, a grade looks wrong, and a weekly session is booked in that subject. Three months later the grade has not moved, because the session was aimed at the syllabus when the problem was two paper sections. One diagnostic hour, worked from the last two marked scripts, replaces that guess with a target.

What a diagnosis actually reads is the pattern of lost marks rather than the total. Method marks gone on questions where the final answer is right point at working and presentation. Marks draining through the last third of a paper point at pacing, which is a different fix entirely. Answers that are factually correct and still score below band point at command terms: describe answered as explain, deduce answered as state. Whole questions untouched, or working that fails at the same step every time, point at genuine content gaps. Those four diagnoses lead to four different plans of four different lengths.

The second document to put on the table is the school's internal deadline list for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and each subject's assessed component. These dates are set by the school rather than by the examination timetable, and they differ between schools sitting the same session. On the east coast, where a small staff coordinates the whole programme, they are also the dates most likely to arrive unannounced. A plan built without them will aim a term of sessions at content revision while an assessed draft quietly goes late, and that is the single most common way tutoring money is wasted in a Diploma year.
bullets: Bring the last two marked scripts, not the report card

sections.heading: The first six weeks: rebuilding what is actually missing
paragraphs: Content gaps are the slowest thing to fix and the most satisfying to watch close. The work is unglamorous: find the earliest point in the topic chain where understanding failed, rebuild from there, and resist the temptation to start at the point where the school currently is. A student who cannot rearrange an equation reliably will not be rescued by more practice on the topic that exposed it, and in a Diploma subject the exposed topic is usually three steps downstream of the actual break.

Six weeks is the realistic floor for one substantial gap in one subject, assuming a weekly session and work done between them. That is worth saying plainly because the market tends not to. A family starting in week one of a block should expect the first two sessions to look like going backwards, the middle two to feel slow, and the change to appear in the school's own assessment rather than in how the sessions feel. Judging progress by whether a lesson went well is the least reliable instrument available.

Two practical notes for this phase on the east coast. First, follow the school's teaching order rather than the textbook's, because a student who is behind cannot afford to be learning two sequences at once; that means the tutor needs to know what was covered in class last week. Second, protect the phase from the core. If an Extended Essay draft or an assessed component falls inside these six weeks, the content work has to be shortened rather than squeezed alongside, because a student doing both badly in the same fortnight is the position this whole exercise exists to avoid.

sections.heading: Weeks seven to fourteen: turning what they know into marks
paragraphs: This is the phase families skip, and it is where most of the recoverable marks live. A student who understands the material and still scores below expectation is losing marks in the translation: the question is read wrongly, the command term is answered generically, working is not written down, time is allocated badly across a paper. None of that is content, so no amount of further teaching fixes it. The work is timed questions, marked against the published scheme, with the mark scheme read afterwards line by line.

Reading a mark scheme is a skill in itself and it transfers across subjects. Students are usually astonished by how mechanical the marks are: a point scored for naming a variable, a point for a unit, a point for a comparison word. Once a student has seen three mark schemes for the same style of question, they start writing for the marker rather than for themselves, and the score moves without a single new fact being learned. In the sciences, where Paper 2 extended response carries 44 per cent, this is the highest-return work available in the whole Diploma.

Pacing is handled here too, and it needs real papers under real time. A student who scores well on untimed practice and badly in the hall is not short of knowledge; they are short of a plan for the hour. Working out how long each section may take, deciding in advance what to do when a question will not come, and practising the decision to leave something and come back are all trainable. Eight weeks is a comfortable window for this phase. Four weeks will shift one paper. Two weeks will shift one section, which is still worth having if that section is where the marks are.

sections.heading: The final stretch: what stops and what continues
paragraphs: In the last weeks before the papers, new content stops. This is the hardest instruction to follow and the most reliable one. A student learning a new topic in the final fortnight is spending the scarcest hours of the year on the least secure material, and doing it in place of consolidating the eighty per cent they already half know. The exception is narrow: a single identified topic that carries disproportionate weight and is genuinely absent rather than shaky.

What continues is timed practice, mark scheme reading and the mechanical business of exam logistics. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates, confirm which series and which timetable version applies, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable. For Diploma candidates, confirm dates with the school's coordinator. This page publishes no IB session or results date, because the IB's own assessment pages could not be verified for this project and an unverified exam date on a page like this is worse than no date at all.

The other thing that continues is sleep, and it is not a soft point. Students on this coast with long bus journeys are already losing an hour a day to travel, and families regularly add a late-evening session in the final fortnight that costs more in concentration than it returns in content. In the last two weeks the sensible pattern is shorter sessions, earlier, with a hard stop. If a tutor proposes intensifying in the final week, ask what will be dropped to make room, because something always is.

sections.heading: Starting late: what each remaining window can realistically achieve
paragraphs: A large share of enquiries from this coast arrive with the clock already running, and the useful answer is neither reassurance nor refusal. Each remaining window has a realistic aim, and naming it honestly is what lets a family decide whether the spend is worth it. The pattern below is drawn from how these blocks actually run rather than from what sounds encouraging.

Two principles run through all of it. The shorter the window, the narrower the aim: with a term left the target is a component, with six weeks it is a paper, with a fortnight it is a section. And the shorter the window, the more important it is to drop something. A student with four weeks who adds two sessions a week to an unchanged workload will do everything slightly worse. Deciding what comes off the list is part of the plan, not an afterthought, and it is a conversation for the family rather than the tutor to settle.

One more thing is worth saying for DP1 families reading this with nothing obviously wrong. The cheapest intervention in the whole Diploma is a single diagnostic session in the first term of DP1, when the Extended Essay question is still open, the Higher Level levels can still change, and a content gap can be closed before the course assumes it. Nobody searches for a tutor at that point, which is exactly why the phase is worth mentioning here.

sections.heading: Where the timeline breaks on the east coast
paragraphs: Plans fail for predictable reasons here, and all of them can be scheduled around if they are named in advance. The shortened Ramadan school day changes the whole rhythm for several weeks, and it lands in the part of the year where mocks have just been marked and the papers are close. A late-afternoon slot that worked all year stops working; a session after Iftar usually holds. Agreeing that shift before the month begins rather than during it is the difference between an adjusted plan and three missed weeks.

The second break is the collision of assessed components. Schools set their own internal deadlines, and two of them landing in the same fortnight is common rather than unlucky. A student with the scientific investigation and an Extended Essay draft due together will do both badly unless something gives. The adjustment is to pause content teaching for that fortnight and use the sessions for process coaching on whichever piece carries the most marks, which is a decision that needs the school's deadline list in hand.

The third is travel and the fourth is the school calendar itself. Families on this coast travel in the long breaks, often for extended periods, and the honest options are to continue over video from wherever they are, or to stop cleanly and restart with a short re-diagnosis rather than pretending a six-week gap did not happen. School events, fixtures and club commitments produce the slow version of the same problem: a slot that cannot move gets cancelled, and three cancellations become a lapsed arrangement. Building the ability to shift a lesson inside the week into the agreement at the start is worth more over two years than any difference in hourly rate.

sections.heading: What the timeline costs, stage by stage
paragraphs: Spreading the cost over the sequence makes it easier to judge than an hourly rate does, because the pattern changes as the plan progresses. A diagnostic is one hour. A content block is weekly for six to fourteen weeks. A technique block is often twice weekly for a shorter period. The final stretch is short sessions, more often, for two or three weeks. A family that budgets a flat weekly figure for two years is usually over-buying in the quiet terms and under-buying in the one that matters.

The figures in the table are market rates published by named providers in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. They are given so a family can size the commitment before starting rather than discovering it in month four. For what a specific subject, level and session length would cost, the route is a short consultation followed by one trial session per family at no charge, arranged after that conversation. There is no term block to exit and no package that renews unless somebody asks for it.

It is worth putting the number in context rather than in isolation. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees holding steady does not hold tutoring costs steady, but it does mean a family planning an exam year has one fewer variable. Set the tutoring figure against school fees, exam entry costs for any private-candidate subject, and the travel a visiting arrangement would add, and the comparison usually settles itself.

sections.heading: What stays the student's own work, whatever the deadline
paragraphs: The pressure points in a timeline are exactly where the honesty line gets tested, so it belongs on this page rather than in a footnote. A student two days from an internal deadline with an unfinished draft is the moment a family is most likely to be offered something they should refuse. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, read the criteria with the student, discuss the student's own ideas and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it to completion, or hand over a model to adapt.

The consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate, not the tutor. An academic-honesty finding is a far worse outcome than a late or weak piece of coursework, and it is not a theoretical risk: one site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright. If the deadline really is tomorrow, the useful help is triage. Work out what can be finished honestly, what has to be submitted incomplete, and what the school needs to be told, and then do that rather than buying a problem.

Materials follow the same rule. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and are referenced and linked at source rather than redistributed as a folder of downloads. A tutor who offers everything is convenient in the short run and is distributing somebody else's copyright. Ask the school which documents it has already provided; on the east coast the answer is often more than the family realised.

process.title: Book the diagnostic before anything else
process.description: One session, worked from the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list. The output is a written statement of what is wrong and roughly how many weeks it will take. Families who act on it themselves and buy nothing further have still had the most useful hour available.

process.title: Fix the end date before the start date
process.description: Agree how long the block runs and what the review point is, which should be the school's next assessment rather than a count of weeks. A block with a stated end makes renewing a decision. An open arrangement renews by default and nobody notices the target has drifted.

process.title: Decide what comes off the list
process.description: Adding sessions to an unchanged week makes everything slightly worse. Before the block starts, settle which commitment pauses, which subject stops getting general revision, and what happens in mock weeks. That conversation belongs to the family; the tutor's job is to say what the plan requires.

process.title: Agree the Ramadan and travel adjustments up front
process.description: Sessions after Iftar hold better than late-afternoon ones, and extended travel is easier handled as a clean pause with a re-diagnosis than as a silent lapse. Both decisions are cheap to make in September and expensive to make in March.

process.title: Review on the marks, then change the aim
process.description: At the review point, the only question is whether marks moved in the component the plan targeted. If they did, continue or stop. If they did not, the aim was wrong and the plan changes rather than the hours increasing. Buying more of a plan that is not working is the commonest mistake in this market.

whyPoints.title: A dated plan, not an open weekly habit
whyPoints.description: Every block has a stated length and a review point set at the school's next assessment. Nothing renews by default. The point of an end date is that it forces somebody to look at whether the marks moved, which an open-ended arrangement never does.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session reads marked scripts and internal deadlines rather than opening a textbook. Four different patterns of lost marks lead to four different plans of four different lengths, and guessing between them costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Continuity that weather cannot interrupt
whyPoints.description: Nothing in the arrangement depends on the Hajar road being open or on a two-to-three-hour round trip remaining attractive in February. Slots shift inside the same week at no cost, which over two years is worth more lessons than any hourly discount.

whyPoints.title: Visiting-tuition rates published honestly
whyPoints.description: The in-home option is described with its real market cost, AED 180-500 per hour with travel inside the fee, attributed and dated to October 2026. IB Gram does not sell it in the UAE and says so rather than leaving the question open.

whyPoints.title: No exam date published that could not be verified
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own published key dates. No IB session or results date appears, because the IB's assessment pages could not be verified for this project. Confirm Diploma dates with your child's coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and plain about the limits
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform holding no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority. No school named here is a client, and coursework support never includes producing the work.

faqs.question: Does anyone come to our house in Fujairah for the lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide visiting tuition anywhere in the UAE; that service is offered only in India. Teaching arranged here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the Fujairah school day. Visiting tutors do exist on this coast and families do hire them, with published market rates running AED 180-500 per hour because the travel is priced into the lesson. If you go that route, ask to see the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years and which any working tutor has no reason not to hold.

faqs.question: What should the first two weeks of tutoring actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written target, not a feeling. The first session should read the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list and come back with a short document naming which papers or criteria the marks are sitting in, which two or three topics come first and in what order, and when the plan will be reviewed. By the end of the second session you should know roughly how many weeks the gap is likely to take to close. If after two weeks you have warm impressions and no named components, the arrangement is not aimed at anything measurable.

faqs.question: How long does it take to close a content gap in a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: Six to fourteen weeks for one substantial gap in one subject, assuming a weekly session with work done between them. The variation depends on how far back the break is: a student whose problem is three steps upstream of the exposed topic takes longer than one with a single missing unit. Expect the first two sessions to feel like going backwards, because rebuilding from the earliest failure point is how this works. Judge it on the school's next assessment rather than on how the lessons feel, which is the least reliable instrument available to a parent.

faqs.question: We are six weeks from the papers. What is realistically achievable?
faqs.answer: One paper's technique, done properly. In six weeks a student can learn to read command terms accurately, write for a mark scheme rather than for themselves, and pace an hour sensibly, and those changes move scores without a single new fact being learned. What is not achievable is new content across a syllabus, and a plan that promises it is selling the wrong thing. Pick the paper with the largest recoverable mark total, work twice a week with marked practice in between, and decide what comes off your child's week to make room, because something has to.

faqs.question: My daughter is in DP1 with no obvious problem. Is this too early to start?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest point in the whole Diploma to do something, which is why almost nobody does. In the first term of DP1 the Extended Essay question is still open, Higher Level levels can still be changed, and a content gap can be closed before the course starts assuming it. A single diagnostic session at that stage often produces a plan a family executes themselves with no further sessions bought. The expensive version of the same conversation happens in DP2, when the levels are fixed, the core is late and the only available lever is intensity.

faqs.question: How much notice does a tutor need before the mock season?
faqs.answer: Three to four weeks to be useful, and the more important point is what happens afterwards. Mocks are the best diagnostic a Diploma year produces, so the valuable work sits in the weeks after the scripts come back rather than the fortnight before they are sat. A sensible arrangement pauses or switches to timed papers during mock week itself, then re-diagnoses from the actual script: which section, which command terms, where the pacing failed. Families who intensify before mocks and then stop have usually bought the less useful half of the opportunity.

faqs.question: What happens to the plan during Ramadan in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: It shifts rather than pauses, and the shift should be agreed before the month starts. The shortened school day changes the whole rhythm, late-afternoon slots stop working well, and sessions after Iftar generally hold better. Shorter sessions more often tend to survive the month better than one long evening. The timing matters because Ramadan falls close to the exam term, so three weeks lost here are three weeks that cannot be recovered later. Deciding the adjustment in advance is the difference between an adapted plan and a lapsed one.

faqs.question: We travel for several weeks in the summer. Should lessons stop or continue?
faqs.answer: Either is fine; drifting is not. Continuing over video from wherever you are works, with the slot moved to suit the new time zone, and suits students with an assessed component in progress. Stopping cleanly also works, provided it is a decision with a restart date and a short re-diagnosis when term begins, because six weeks away from a subject changes where a student is. What causes damage is the silent version: two sessions missed, then a vague intention to resume, then September arriving with the plan untouched and the target now out of date.

faqs.question: How do we know the plan is working before the next school report?
faqs.answer: Ask for marked work rather than progress reports. A session that produces an annotated script is evidence; a session that produces a verbal summary is not. Within a block you should be able to see the same style of question attempted twice, several weeks apart, with the second attempt scoring better against the same scheme. That is a smaller and faster signal than a report card and it is the one a tutor should be providing without being asked. If nothing written is coming home, there is nothing to review at the review point.

faqs.question: What does a visiting tutor on the east coast charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE ran AED 180-500 per hour in October 2026, with travel inside the fee, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visiting sessions sat at AED 1,599-1,799. Qualified subject tutors working online were published at AED 150-300, specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium or examiner-experienced tutors at AED 500-650 and above. Those are other providers' figures rather than a price list. On this coast the travel component dominates the visiting rate, because the round trip from the Dubai school belt is two to three hours.

faqs.question: Should we book a term in advance to secure a slot?
faqs.answer: Secure the slot, but be careful what else comes with it. A standing weekly time is genuinely worth holding, particularly for an evening slot on this coast where the usable window is narrow. Paying a term's fees up front is a different thing: it removes the main protection a family has, which is the ability to change a decision cheaply when a match turns out to be wrong. A reasonable arrangement holds the slot, has a stated end date for the block, and does not renew unless somebody asks. Ask what happens if you stop after two sessions.

faqs.question: My son has two assessed components due in the same fortnight. What comes first?
faqs.answer: The one carrying more marks, and the other one gets a reduced, honest submission rather than both being done badly. This collision is common rather than unlucky, because internal deadlines are set by the school and nobody coordinates them against each other. The adjustment is to pause content teaching for that fortnight and use the sessions for process coaching: narrowing the question, reading the criteria, feedback on the student's own draft. Content work squeezed alongside two drafts achieves nothing in any of the three. Getting the school's deadline list in September is what lets you see this coming.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor stay with my child across both Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it is worth asking for explicitly at the start rather than assuming. Continuity across DP1 and DP2 means the tutor already knows which topic chain was rebuilt in the first year and does not need to rediagnose, which saves real weeks. What breaks it is more often scheduling than availability: a slot that worked in DP1 collides with a DP2 timetable, and the arrangement lapses rather than moving. Agreeing at the outset that the slot can shift inside the week, and reviewing it at the start of each term, is what keeps a two-year arrangement intact.

faqs.question: What do we do if the marks have not moved after a term?
faqs.answer: Change the aim, not the hours. A term of sessions with no movement in the targeted component means the diagnosis was wrong, the plan was aimed at the wrong thing, or the work between sessions was not happening. Those are three different problems with three different fixes, and buying more sessions addresses none of them. Ask for the marked work from the term and look at whether the same questions improved. A tutor who responds to a flat review by proposing additional weekly hours is answering a commercial question rather than an academic one.

faqs.question: Is there a point in the Diploma where starting is genuinely too late?
faqs.answer: Not quite, but there is a point where the aim has to shrink to one section of one paper. With a fortnight left the honest target is the single section with the largest recoverable mark total, worked in two or three short sessions with everything else protected, including sleep. Anyone proposing a broad programme at that stage is not reading the calendar. No tutor can promise a grade at any stage, and a first conversation that opens with one has told you how the rest of the arrangement will go.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one hour and a date
fujairah/ib-home-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step is small: a diagnostic session worked from the last two marked scripts and the school's internal deadline list, which produces a written target and an honest number of weeks. From there a block has a length, a review point and an end date, and renewing it is a decision rather than a default. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video in Gulf Standard Time; nobody is sent to a Fujairah address, and visiting tuition is offered only in India. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board approval and names no school as a partner. What it offers is a plan with dates in it.

intro.heading: Plan early, because here you cannot plan twice
paragraphs: Fujairah is the only emirate on the Gulf of Oman coast, separated from Dubai and Sharjah by the Hajar mountains, and its private-school set is small. Those two facts together produce a particular planning problem: a student sitting a less common Diploma subject may have no local specialist at all, and a family whose arrangement fails in February has nowhere nearby to turn. That is not a reason for anxiety. It is a reason to put the year on paper in September.

Al Faseel sits on the coast at Fujairah city, near the corniche, residential and close to the city's school cluster. The journey is short and the housing is reasonable, so the usual constraints of time and space are mild here. What is genuinely scarce is choice: in a small cohort a particular Higher Level option may be taught by one teacher, and that teacher is frequently the person least able to tutor the students who need them.

So this page is a calendar rather than a pitch, and it is organised around commitment rather than revision. Which decisions close, and when. What each term of the two years has to deliver. Which document the plan is actually built from. What the mountains change and what they do not. And what the options are in the fortnight after results, when the local fallback is thinnest.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents search, and the honest answer for Al Faseel is that online delivery is not a compromise here but the mechanism that makes a specialist available at all, since no scheduling arrangement makes a subject teacher appear on this side of the mountains.

On dates, this page is restrained. No IB exam or results date appears, because the board's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the IB itself. What is safe to state is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route, and that every specific date should come from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly.

Where a figure or a regulatory statement appears it is attributed. Market rates are given with the provider that published them and the month they were read, October 2026. Regulatory statements come from federal sources. Where something could not be verified, this page says so rather than filling the gap with something plausible. That restraint costs a page some apparent authority and it is the right trade on a site this size, because a date or a figure that is wrong is wrong on every page at once.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.programmesIntro: Three IB stages reach Al Faseel households, and the commitment problem is sharpest at the last of them because that is where the decisions are irreversible.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external papers and no deadlines, which makes the calendar forgiving. The work that pays off later is mechanics: number bonds, written method, reading stamina, explaining an answer in a sentence. Nothing here is urgent and all of it is expensive to repair at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: Al Faseel's short journeys make a 4:00pm primary session easy to sustain. In a small emirate an external check once a year is more informative than a class position, because the cohort a child is being compared with is very small.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, assessed through tasks spread across the year rather than an examination window. The calendar is real and invisible, because MYP assessment arrives as projects rather than as exams, and a strand left unaddressed costs marks every time it recurs.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 11 is when Fujairah families most often start looking, because the Diploma decision and the first serious internal assessments arrive in the same term. Starting one term earlier makes that decision informed rather than reactive.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, each subject carrying an internally assessed component on a school-set deadline. The deadlines cluster in one autumn and the papers sit in the spring, which makes the whole thing a sequencing exercise rather than a revision one.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah's Diploma presence is small, so a student here may be the only person in the emirate taking a particular Higher Level option. The school's own deadline calendar is the only calendar they will be handed, and getting a copy in September is the highest-value administrative act of the year.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects most often requested from Fujairah, each with the calendar pressure point named alongside the content one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Non-calculator technique is the usual gap. The calendar pressure is the exploration, which needs a topic with genuine mathematics in it chosen a term before it is written rather than a fortnight.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led. Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late in the final year, so a student already behind meets new content and revision simultaneously.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses. The internal assessment needs a method settled early enough to collect usable data, which is the deadline most often missed in this subject.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit discipline, gradients and explanation questions. Technique responds quickly to timed practice, which makes a short block effective even late. Among the scarcest subjects locally at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Naming a process earns a mark and ordering its stages earns the rest. Statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand, which is a single-session repair.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline plus commentaries that need genuinely recent articles collected as they appear. Very scarce locally, which makes early booking a necessity rather than a preference.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the case stimulus is the whole paper. Higher Level adds the pre-released case study, published far enough ahead that early structured reading is unusually valuable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards argument about how a text works. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it, which is a term's decision.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are narrowing problems before they are writing problems, and both have no timetabled lesson. The decision that caps each one is taken long before the drafting starts.

regions.note: Residential district north of the city centre with family housing. A slightly longer run than Al Faseel and a 5:00pm realistic earliest start for most households.

regions.name: Merashid

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Coastal area south of the city centre. The drive lengthens, which pushes weekday sessions later and makes a weekend block more valuable than a weekday one.

regions.name: Dibba Al Fujairah
regions.note: Northern coastal town a substantial drive from Fujairah city, where the local school choice narrows further and online delivery stops being a preference.

regions.note: Coastal community south of the city with a long run into the school cluster. Families here usually plan around one weekend block and one short weekday slot rather than two weekday sessions.

sections.heading: The commitment calendar: decisions that close
paragraphs: Most tutoring advice is about revision, which is the part of a Diploma a family can always change. The part they cannot change is the sequence of decisions, and in a small emirate the cost of making one badly is higher because there is less room to correct it afterwards.

Listing them out is unglamorous and unusually useful. Subject and level choices close at the start of the first year, with a brief window for adjustment. The coursework topic and the method close when data collection or drafting begins. The Extended Essay research question closes in practice once several thousand words exist. Predicted grades close when the school issues them in the autumn of the final year, and they reflect work already completed. Entry decisions for a session close months before the papers. And the choice of tutor closes, in effect, when the term starts, because mid-year replacement in Fujairah means starting again rather than switching.

Reading that list the other way round gives a Fujairah family its plan. Everything with a late closing date can be left. Everything with an early one has to be dealt with in Grade 11, when nothing else is competing for attention and when specialist capacity is easiest to reserve. That is also the cheapest period in the whole course, which makes the sequencing argument and the budget argument point the same way.

The table lists the decisions with when each closes and what each one fixes. Dates are deliberately expressed as positions in the course rather than as calendar dates, because no IB date in this project has been verified and because school calendars differ.

sections.heading: What the Hajar mountains actually change
paragraphs: It is worth being precise about this rather than gesturing at remoteness, because the mountains change some things decisively and others not at all, and families here are frequently told that everything is harder when only a few things are.

What they change: the practicality of any in-person arrangement that originates outside the emirate. A tutor in Sharjah or Dubai is not making a weekday evening journey through the pass to Al Faseel, which means the realistic in-home pool is whoever already lives in Fujairah. They also change access to the sort of weekend enrichment and group provision that is abundant in Dubai, and they lengthen the school run for the small number of families who cross the pass for a particular school.

What they do not change: anything about the examination. The papers, the criteria, the command terms, the internal deadlines, the series and the standards are identical for a student in Al Faseel and a student in Jumeirah. Nor do they change the market rates a family should judge a quote against: a qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500, read October 2026, and those bands apply nationally rather than by emirate.

And critically, they do not change who can teach a student over live video. That is the whole point: the mountains are a constraint on bodies rather than on teaching, and a format that moves no bodies is unaffected by them. A student in Al Faseel has exactly the same access to a Higher Level Chemistry specialist as a student in Dubai, which is not true of any in-person arrangement at any price.
bullets: They make in-person arrangements from outside the emirate impractical.

sections.heading: A term-by-term map of the two years
paragraphs: This is the document the search was really after: not a tutor but a plan, written once in September, costing nothing, and the difference between a household that places its effort and one that reacts to each report.

The first Diploma year has two jobs and both are cheap. The autumn establishes whether the three Higher Levels chosen are the right three and builds content while nothing else competes for attention. The spring settles coursework topics and research questions that will actually work, which is the single highest-leverage decision in the course, and it produces a first full past paper attempted under time so that a classified error log exists.

The second year inverts the pattern. The autumn belongs to coursework: internal assessments across six subjects, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, and university applications, all in the same eight weeks. Nothing else should be attempted in that window, and any paper technique bought then produces two half-done jobs. The spring belongs to timed practice marked against published schemes, with nothing new taught.

The summer between the years is the one block nobody has already claimed, and it is where a named content gap from the spring should be closed in three or four weeks. The table sets out the map. Adapt it to your own school's calendar rather than to this page, because the value is in having one document in September rather than in matching somebody else's.

sections.heading: The school's calendar is the only calendar you will get
paragraphs: A Diploma student is governed by two sets of dates. The board sets the examination window, and the school sets everything else: internal assessment deadlines in six subjects, Extended Essay supervision meetings, Theory of Knowledge submission dates, the mock window, and whatever internal reporting cycle generates the information a family sees. Only the second set is actionable, and it is the set families least often hold.

Asking for it is straightforward and it should happen in September. The three documents that matter are the internal assessment calendar covering all six subjects, the Extended Essay supervision schedule, and the Theory of Knowledge dates. In a small school those may exist as one sheet; in a larger one they may need three requests. Either way the coordinator has them, and a family that holds them can place every tuition block before a cluster rather than on top of one.

The reason this matters disproportionately in Fujairah is that there is no second source. In a large market a parent can compare notes with several families at several schools and triangulate what a normal autumn looks like. Here the cohort is small, and if the calendar has not been requested, a household is reacting to deadlines as they arrive with no sense of what is coming next.

One related point about verification. The school's calendar is a document a family can hold and check; a tutoring provider's claimed timeline is not. Where this page gives sourced board positions it names them, and where it has no verified date it says so. No IB exam or results date appears here because none in this project has been confirmed from the board, whose own site returns an error to automated checking.
bullets: Request three documents in September: internal assessment calendar, Extended Essay schedule, TOK dates.
Place every tuition block before a deadline cluster, never on top of one.
In a small cohort there is no second source to triangulate against.

sections.heading: Who supervises your school here, and what to ask for
paragraphs: Parents arriving in Fujairah from Dubai look for a KHDA inspection report on a local school and find nothing, because KHDA's remit stops at the Dubai border. The UAE government's own portal describes the Ministry of Education as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is a different regime, with different publication habits, and a different set of documents to ask for.

The complete map is worth knowing because families move between emirates. KHDA regulates Dubai, where it is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, with both also approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain sit with the federal Ministry.

The practical consequence for an Al Faseel family is that inspection information should be requested from the school rather than downloaded, and that a federal baseline applies: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement sits on top of.

None of this gives a tutoring provider any standing, and this page claims none. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Ministry of Education, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry; an individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Neither is a badge a matching platform can wear.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the summer and a coastal school year
paragraphs: Three features of the local year reshape a plan and none of them appears on a board timetable. The first is Ramadan: school hours shorten, the useful study window moves to after Iftar, and a month of a two-year course runs on a different rhythm from the rest of it. The month also moves roughly eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so its position inside the school year changes and a plan reused unchanged will eventually place its heaviest weeks inside it.

The practical answer is to decide before the month begins rather than during it. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing, or shorten and keep their frequency. An online booking absorbs that easily; in Fujairah an in-home visit after Iftar is a much harder thing to arrange, because the local pool is small and the evening is late. A month quietly abandoned and resumed in a rush is where more Diploma momentum is lost than in any single bad mock.

The second is the summer, which is long, hot and the only unallocated block in the year. In an emirate where a content gap cannot be fixed by finding another local teacher mid-term, three or four weeks in the summer on one named target is the highest-value window available. What does not work is running a full programme through it: a student who studies all summer arrives in September already tired, which costs more than the gap would have.

The third is the local calendar's own breaks. Eid holidays, National Day on 2 December and mid-term breaks all sit inside terms rather than between them, which makes them the natural place for coursework rather than content. A student who finishes an internal assessment draft during a mid-term break buys two weeks of autumn back, and in the Grade 12 autumn two weeks is a substantial amount.
bullets: Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, so its term position changes.
Decide the Ramadan arrangement before the month, with the student.
Use the summer for one named target in three or four weeks, not a full programme.
Use mid-term breaks for coursework rather than content catch-up.

sections.heading: Results, the alternative session and a thin fallback
paragraphs: The fortnight after results is where a family in a small emirate is most exposed, because there is often nobody locally to ask and the decisions have deadlines. Three options exist and identifying which applies matters more than reacting quickly.

The first is an enquiry upon results, where the school asks the board to review a mark. It is a school process with its own deadline and criteria, and the right question for the coordinator is whether the component profile makes a review plausible rather than whether the result was disappointing. The second is a retake in a later session. The third is accepting the result, which is frequently correct and almost never presented as an option.

The deciding input in all three cases is the component breakdown: marks by paper and by internal component. A shortfall concentrated in one component is a different problem from one spread across all of them, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block of technique work. Asking for that breakdown before any decision is the step most families skip and the one that determines whether an entry fee is well spent.

On dates the same restraint applies as elsewhere here. UAE schools sit the May session and a November session exists as an alternative route, but no IB date in this project has been verified from the board, so none is published. Ask the coordinator about entry routes and deadlines, and tell any receiving institution about timing in advance rather than relying on it to accommodate a later result.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A page asking a family to commit a year in advance owes a clear account of its own limits. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it, which matters especially in a small cohort where work is read closely.

On materials: no tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and asks readers to confirm every allocation against the documents their own school issues.

On who may teach: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted. No tutor can promise a grade, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Ministry of Education, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

process.title: Request the three school documents in September
process.description: The internal assessment calendar for all six subjects, the Extended Essay supervision schedule and the Theory of Knowledge dates. The coordinator has them, and a family that holds them can place every block before a deadline cluster rather than on top of one.

process.title: Reserve a named tutor for the term, not the session
process.description: In Fujairah a mid-year collapse means starting again rather than switching, because there is no local replacement pool. A reserved weekly slot with a named tutor agreed in September usually holds for the year, and that continuity is worth more here than a marginally better rate.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken. It classifies lost marks into content, method, command term and timing, and you keep the written summary naming the first three targets whether or not anything else is booked.

process.title: Put the later blocks on the calendar now
process.description: The Grade 12 coursework block and the pre-series block are reserved at the start of the year rather than requested when they are needed, because specialist capacity tightens as a series approaches and the local alternative is thin.

process.title: Decide Ramadan and the summer in advance
process.description: Move sessions to post-Iftar timing before the month begins rather than suspending and resuming in a rush, and use three or four summer weeks on one named target. Both decisions cost nothing and both are routinely made too late.

whyPoints.title: The decisions that close, listed
whyPoints.description: Levels, coursework topics, research questions, predicted grades, entries and the choice of tutor all close earlier than families expect. Knowing when each closes turns a two-year course into a sequence of dated decisions rather than a series of surprises.

whyPoints.title: The mountains made irrelevant
whyPoints.description: The Hajar pass constrains bodies, not teaching. Over live video a student in Al Faseel has the same access to a Higher Level specialist as a student in Dubai, which is not true of any in-person arrangement at any price.

whyPoints.title: Continuity treated as the scarce resource
whyPoints.description: In this emirate a tutoring arrangement that fails in February cannot be replaced locally, so a named tutor reserved for a term matters more than it would in a large market. That is a commitment worth asking any provider to make in writing.

whyPoints.title: Built from the school's own calendar
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment dates, the Extended Essay schedule and the Theory of Knowledge deadlines are documents a family can hold and check. A plan built from them beats one built from anybody's claimed timeline.

whyPoints.title: No unverified dates, anywhere
whyPoints.description: No IB exam or results date appears on this page, because the board's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from it. An unverified date a family plans a year around is worse than an absent one.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated, including ours
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and written feedback on the student's own draft: yes. Producing any part of assessed work: never. No promised grades, and no claim of approval from the Ministry of Education or any other regulator or board.

faqs.question: Is there a Diploma specialist available locally in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: For the most widely taught subjects at Standard Level, sometimes. For a Higher Level science, Economics with its commentaries, or a minority language, frequently not at all, because the emirate's private-school set is small and a given option may be taught by one teacher in one school. That teacher is also often the person least able to tutor the students who need them. Online delivery is what changes the answer, since no scheduling arrangement makes a subject specialist appear on this side of the mountains.

faqs.question: Why does this page tell me to plan in Grade 11?
faqs.answer: Because that is when the decisions close. Subject and level choices settle in the first term, coursework topics and methods close when drafting or data collection begins, the Extended Essay question closes once several thousand words exist, and predicted grades are issued in the autumn of the final year reflecting work already done. Grade 12 can only execute decisions Grade 11 made, and in Fujairah a poor decision is harder to correct because the local alternatives are fewer.

faqs.question: What do the Hajar mountains actually change for tutoring?
faqs.answer: They make any in-person arrangement originating outside the emirate impractical, because a tutor in Sharjah or Dubai will not drive through the pass on a weekday evening, and they narrow access to the group and weekend provision that is abundant in Dubai. They change nothing about the papers, the criteria, the command terms, the internal deadlines or the standards, which are identical here and in Jumeirah. And they are irrelevant to a format that moves no bodies at all.

faqs.question: Which three documents should I ask my child's school for?
faqs.answer: The internal assessment calendar covering all six subjects, the Extended Essay supervision schedule, and the Theory of Knowledge submission dates. In a small school these may exist as one sheet; either way the coordinator has them. A family that holds them can place coursework blocks before a deadline cluster and paper work after it clears, which is the difference between a placed plan and a reactive one.

faqs.question: Who inspects private schools in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government's portal describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA covers Dubai, ADEK covers Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Practically, a parent here should request the school's latest inspection outcome directly rather than expecting to download it as a Dubai family would.

faqs.question: How far ahead should an Al Faseel family book a tutor?
faqs.answer: A term ahead, and for a scarce Higher Level subject the September before. Specialist capacity in this market is loosest in September and October while tutors are building a term, tightens from November as autumn reports land, and is tightest from the spring, which is exactly when most families start looking. A reserved weekly slot agreed early usually holds for the whole year, and in an emirate without a local replacement pool that continuity is the thing being bought.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutoring arrangement fails mid-year here?
faqs.answer: In a large market you switch; in Fujairah you often start again, which is why the replacement question should be settled before any payment. Ask any provider what happens in week three if the match is wrong, and expect a specific answer: a different tutor, with the session notes transferred, at no extra charge. An online arrangement has a bench behind it. A local in-home arrangement in this emirate frequently does not, because the person who did not fit may have been the only one available.

faqs.question: Can an in-home tutor from Dubai teach my child in Al Faseel?
faqs.answer: In practice, no, and it is better to hear that plainly. A weekday evening journey through the Hajar pass and back is not a sustainable arrangement for anybody, and a quote that implies it should be read sceptically. The realistic in-home pool is whoever already lives in the emirate, which is small. Published rates for context, read October 2026: a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500.

faqs.question: What is the best use of a Fujairah summer between Grade 11 and Grade 12?
faqs.answer: For one named target, in three or four weeks with two sessions a week, finishing before term begins. The usual target is the content gap identified in the spring, or settling a coursework topic and method so the autumn cluster starts with a viable plan. What does not work is a full programme across July and August: a student who studies all summer arrives in September already tired, which costs more than the original gap would have.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a plan in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the useful study window moves to after Iftar. Decide the arrangement before the month begins: move sessions to post-Iftar timing, or shorten them and keep the frequency. An online booking absorbs that easily, whereas an in-home visit after Iftar is hard to arrange here because the local pool is small and the evening is late. Note also that Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, so its position inside the school year changes.

faqs.question: Why are there no IB dates on this page at all?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project is confirmed from the board, and publishing an unverified date that a family builds a two-year plan around would be worse than publishing none. What is safe to state is that UAE schools sit the May session and that a November session exists as an alternative route. Take every specific date from your coordinator or from ibo.org.

faqs.question: What should we ask for in the fortnight after results?
faqs.answer: The component breakdown first, marks by paper and by internal component, before any decision. A shortfall concentrated in one component is a different problem from one spread across all of them, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block of technique work. Then ask the coordinator whether the profile makes an enquiry upon results plausible, which is a school process with its own deadline. Accepting the result is often correct and rarely offered as an option.

faqs.question: Is it worth getting an outside view if nothing seems wrong?
faqs.answer: In a small emirate, often yes, and it is a different purchase from remedial work. A Fujairah Diploma cohort can be very small, so a position inside it carries little information about absolute standing against published criteria, and a sole subject teacher has no colleague to moderate internal work against. One external check a year is calibration rather than tuition, and it is considerably cheaper than a repair bought in the final term.

faqs.question: Which Fujairah schools do Al Faseel students attend?
faqs.answer: Almost all of the emirate's private provision sits in or around Fujairah city, a short drive from Al Faseel, with Fujairah Private Academy, Our Own English High School Fujairah and Indian School Fujairah among the names families mention. A small number of households cross the Hajar pass into Sharjah for a particular programme, which places that school under the Sharjah Private Education Authority instead. Every school name should be checked against the Ministry of Education's own listing before it affects a decision.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit, and can I see it?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and yes, you can ask. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.closingHeading: Put the year on paper in September
fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.closingBody: For a family in Al Faseel the useful move is not finding somebody nearby but writing the year down before it starts. Request the three school documents, reserve a named tutor for the term rather than the session, and put the Grade 12 coursework block and the pre-series block on the calendar now, because capacity tightens later and the local alternative is thin. The first session is a free diagnosis on a recent marked paper, with no card details taken. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is the one arrangement the mountains cannot interrupt.

intro.heading: The Diploma week is already full before tutoring arrives
paragraphs: Al Gurfa sits south of Fujairah city along the coast road, spread out, with most students travelling in to the city-centre schools or further afield. Households here commonly run two school journeys rather than one, which means the practical question for Diploma tutoring is not whether a specialist exists but when a session could possibly happen. Neither child tends to be at a desk before 16:30 and often not before 17:00, and the Diploma student is the one with the fullest timetable to begin with.

That matters because the Diploma is not six subjects. It is six subjects plus an Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge course examined through an essay of up to 1,600 words and an exhibition with a commentary of up to 950, and a CAS programme that carries no points but blocks the award of the diploma if it is incomplete. Every one of those has deadlines, and the deadlines are set internally by the school rather than externally by the board, which means they arrive earlier than families expect and in clusters.

IB Gram delivers to Al Gurfa as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and that statement appears on every country page this site publishes. The practical gain is specific rather than rhetorical: an online slot does not depend on a tutor driving the coast road at seven in the evening, so the start time is a start time rather than an arrival window. Published in-home rates here run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and some of that is the journey.

So this page maps the two things that collide. On one side the Diploma year with its internal deadline clusters, its core components and its internal assessments. On the other a real Al Gurfa week with two school runs, a long school day lengthened further by the mandatory UAE subjects, and a finite number of usable evening hours. Where those two meet is where a tutoring plan either works or quietly turns fortnightly.

A note on dates, which applies throughout. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project. Diploma students in the UAE sit the May session; every specific date should come from your child's coordinator and the school's own calendar. The internal deadline pattern described below is a shape, not a schedule, and your school's version is the one that matters. The same applies to the component weightings quoted here: they were read from the current subject guides, guides get revised, and your child's coordinator holds the version that governs their cohort. Treat the figures as a map of where the marks sit rather than as the authority for them.
