fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-gurfa.programmesIntro: Three stages, each with a different relationship between the school week and the tutoring week. The scheduling answer changes completely between them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with a Personal Project in the final year marked out of 24 across planning, applying skills and reflecting. No terminal papers in the earlier years, so there is no exam schedule compressing the calendar.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Gurfa household this is the easiest stage to schedule, because deadlines are spread and nothing is timed. Two short sessions a week beat one long one at this age, and they survive a school run that overruns. It is also the cheapest point at which a criterion-level weakness can be fixed, which is why skipping it is expensive later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: Six subjects begin, the Extended Essay topic is chosen and a supervisor appointed, Theory of Knowledge starts, CAS begins accumulating, and the first internal assessment drafts appear. The workload is deceptive: it feels manageable until the first cluster of deadlines lands in the spring.
programmes.countryNote: This is the year in which an Al Gurfa family should fix a tutoring slot and keep it, because the calendar is still flexible enough to absorb a weekly commitment. One session a week running slightly ahead of the school's scheme costs least per grade gained, and nothing in this year is yet being repaired against a deadline.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: Internal assessment final submissions, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, mock examinations and the May session. The deadlines cluster heavily in the autumn and early spring, which is exactly when a weekly tutoring slot is most likely to be sacrificed to them.
programmes.countryNote: The trap for an Al Gurfa household is cancelling sessions during a deadline cluster and never restarting. The better move is to shorten them and change what they contain: process coaching on the piece that is due, rather than subject teaching that competes with it. Agreeing that pattern in advance prevents a term from evaporating.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-gurfa.subjectsIntro: Below, each Diploma subject is noted with how well it tolerates a compressed session, because in an Al Gurfa week that is often the deciding factor rather than the subject's difficulty.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Poor tolerance of a short session. Calculus and proof work need an uninterrupted stretch, and Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended-response problem paper worth twenty per cent that cannot be practised in twenty-minute fragments. Protect the full hour for this subject if you protect it for any.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Moderate tolerance. Statistics and calculator technique can be drilled in shorter blocks; modelling questions requiring written interpretation in context cannot. A sensible pattern alternates between the two according to how the week has gone.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mixed. Data-analysis practice for the thirty-six per cent Paper 1 works in short blocks; extended calculation and the independent investigation do not. Mathematical fluency is the hidden driver, and a Physics student who is weak algebraically needs the longer session more.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Good tolerance for recall work, poor for mechanisms. Organic conditions and definitions drill well in forty minutes; energetics calculation and the 3,000-word investigation need a clear head and a full hour. Split the week accordingly rather than treating all sessions alike.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The best short-session subject in the Diploma, because the content load is large and retrieval practice is what converts it. Ten-minute retrieval blocks on three evenings outperform one long revision sitting, and that is a scheduling decision rather than a teaching one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram drills are short and repeatable; evaluation writing and the portfolio commentaries, capped at 800 words each, need room. The portfolio is three commentaries on real published articles, and drafting one is a weekend-morning job rather than a weekday-evening one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The worst short-session subject here. Paper 1 analysis under timing, Paper 2 essay planning and the HL Essay at twenty per cent all need sustained attention. The Individual Oral, worth thirty per cent at Standard Level, is the exception and rehearses well in shorter bursts.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Good tolerance when the stimulus is sent in advance. Reading the case before the session converts an hour into something closer to ninety minutes of value. Ratio and break-even calculation drills work in short blocks and are the most reliable marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory and conversion work suit short sessions; the solution-development internal assessment does not, because the documentation is assessed alongside the product and needs to be written in sustained passes rather than fragments.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Variable, and often chosen as a lighter option before being found demanding. Data handling drills short; the evaluative writing about human systems needs the same room as an essay subject. Plan it as two different subjects sharing a timetable slot.

regions.name: Fujairah City centre
regions.note: Most of the emirate's private-school capacity, so the shortest afternoon in Fujairah. A student schooling locally can realistically start at 16:30, which is an hour of advantage over an Al Gurfa household across a week.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal, near the corniche and the port, roughly fifteen minutes from the city schools. Earlier starts than Al Gurfa and a single school run more often, which makes a weekday evening slot easier to hold.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Established residential district with a short but variable city run. Similar scheduling pressure to Al Gurfa when two children are involved, and the same thin specialist supply at Higher Level.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland and north-west with the longest afternoon return of the inner districts. Session starts move to 17:30 and the usable evening narrows, which matters most during a deadline cluster.

sections.heading: What an Al Gurfa Diploma week actually contains
paragraphs: Write out a real week before choosing an hour. A Diploma student at a Fujairah city school leaves early, has a school day lengthened by the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside the licensed curriculum, and returns along the coast road in whatever traffic exists that afternoon. If a sibling attends a different school, the household's effective arrival time is the later of the two journeys, not the earlier. Add food and a genuine break, which is not negotiable for a seventeen-year-old, and the first usable hour is commonly 17:30 rather than the 16:30 families assume.

Against that sit the school's own demands. Homework in six subjects, not evenly distributed across the week. Internal assessment work that arrives in bursts. CAS activities that happen in the evenings or at weekends and are frequently the first thing to be dropped, which is a mistake because an incomplete CAS portfolio prevents the diploma from being awarded regardless of how many points the subjects earn. Theory of Knowledge, which generates little weekly work and then a large piece of writing.

What this means for a tutoring slot is that the hour must be chosen for the worst week rather than the best one. A slot that works in October and fails in February has not worked, because the value of weekly tutoring is cumulative: work set, work done, work marked, next session built on the marking. Break that cycle twice and the arrangement is effectively monthly, at weekly cost.

Because lessons are online, one variable disappears from the calculation entirely. Nothing depends on a tutor's drive south along the coast road in the evening, so the slot is a slot. That is not an argument about teaching quality; it is an argument about reliability, and over two Diploma years reliability is what converts hours into marks.
bullets: Household arrival time is the later of two school runs, not the earlier
Choose the slot for February, not for October
CAS is the first thing dropped and the only one that blocks the diploma

sections.heading: The Diploma's internal deadline clusters, term by term
paragraphs: Families plan around the May session and are then ambushed by the internal calendar, which is set by the school and arrives much earlier. The pattern is reasonably consistent across Diploma schools even though the exact dates differ, and knowing the shape is most of the planning. Ask your child's coordinator for the full internal calendar at the start of the first Diploma year rather than in the spring of the second, when it is being enforced rather than explained.

The clusters have a logic. The Extended Essay topic and supervisor land early in the first year because the research has to happen before the second year's workload arrives. Internal assessment planning for the sciences sits in the first year too, since research design cannot be repaired once data has been collected. Then the second year front-loads: internal assessment final drafts, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay, and the exhibition, mostly in the autumn and early spring, with mocks folded in.

The consequence for an Al Gurfa household is that the hardest weeks of the Diploma are not the ones immediately before the examinations. They are the ones in the autumn of the final year, when three or four pieces of assessed coursework are due within a month of each other and the student is also sitting mocks. That is the period when a weekly tutoring slot is most likely to be cancelled and least likely to be restarted.

Planning for it is straightforward once the clusters are visible. Keep the frequency, shorten the sessions, and change what they contain: process coaching on the piece that is due instead of subject teaching that competes with it. The table below gives the shape of a typical internal calendar; yours will differ in dates and should be obtained in writing.

sections.heading: CAS, and the hours nobody puts in the schedule
paragraphs: CAS carries no points and is therefore the component most often treated as optional, which is exactly backwards. An incomplete CAS portfolio prevents the diploma from being awarded, however many points the six subjects produce. A student with 38 points and an unfinished portfolio does not have a diploma, and that is a worse outcome than one with 30 points and a complete one. It is also entirely avoidable, because the requirement is about evidence and reflection rather than about achievement.

The failure mode is consistent and recognisable. Activities accumulate across two years without the reflections that evidence them, because reflections feel like paperwork while the activities feel like life. Then in the spring of the final year the student has to reconstruct a portfolio from memory while also sitting examinations. The reconstruction is harder than the original work and lands in the worst possible month.

For an Al Gurfa household there is a practical wrinkle. CAS activities often happen in the evenings or at weekends, which is also when a tutoring slot sits, and the coast road makes attending anything in the city a longer commitment than it looks. Families that schedule a CAS evening deliberately, and a tutoring evening deliberately, and keep them on different days, have fewer collisions than families that improvise both.

A tutor's role here is near zero and should be stated as such. CAS is the student's own programme and its reflections must be theirs. What a tutor can legitimately do is notice, in the first Diploma year, that the portfolio is not being kept, and tell the parent. That is a five-second intervention with a very large downside avoided, and it is one of the better arguments for a tutor who sees the student weekly across both years rather than only in the final term.

sections.heading: Two school runs, one evening: scheduling with siblings
paragraphs: Most scheduling advice assumes one child. An Al Gurfa household with a Diploma student and a younger sibling at a different school has a harder problem, because the evening has to accommodate two sets of homework, possibly two tutoring arrangements, and one adult's attention. Treating them as independent decisions produces collisions that nobody notices until both children are behind.

The pattern that works is to stagger rather than parallelise. The younger child's session, if there is one, sits earlier and shorter, because attention is the binding constraint at that age and forty minutes twice a week does more than eighty once. The Diploma student's session sits later and longer, because the subjects that matter most at that level do not tolerate compression. Putting both on the same evening means one of them is competing with dinner.

There is a second-order benefit to staggering that families discover by accident. A Diploma student working at 18:30 while a younger sibling has already finished creates a quieter house, and the difference in output over a term is noticeable in marked writing. The reverse arrangement, where the older student works through the household's busiest hour, produces sessions that are technically delivered and practically wasted.

The last piece is the sibling subject overlap, which is where real money gets saved. A single tutor covering mathematics for a Diploma student and for a Year 9 student is rarely a good idea, because the specifications and the required depth differ too much. Two different subjects on two different evenings with two specialists costs the same and works. The table below is the staggering pattern that holds up over a term.

sections.heading: Boarding, commuting and keeping a tutor through a school change
paragraphs: Local Diploma provision in Fujairah is limited, which means a significant share of Al Gurfa students on this route are boarding, commuting weekly to another emirate, or have moved school entirely. Each of those disrupts a tutoring arrangement in a different way, and all three are survivable if the arrangement is online and planned rather than improvised.

Boarding changes the available hours rather than removing them. Boarding houses have study periods, and a fixed online session inside one of them is usually straightforward to arrange with the house staff, though it needs asking rather than assuming. Weekly commuting changes which days are usable: a student travelling on Sunday and Thursday has three reliable evenings rather than five, and the slot should be placed in the middle of that window rather than at either edge.

A full school move is the one that most often ends a tutoring arrangement, and it should not. The specification may change — a new school may enter a different board at IGCSE, or offer a different mathematics course in the Diploma — and that is worth checking immediately, because it can change the match. But the internal deadlines do not pause for a move, and a student mid-Diploma who loses both their school and their tutor in the same term has lost more continuity than either change alone would cost.

The practical instruction is short. If a move or a boarding placement is coming, say so when arranging the tutoring rather than afterwards. The slot can be positioned to survive it, the specification can be checked in advance, and the handover of the topic risk list is trivial if it is written down. Families that mention the move in week eight rather than week one lose a month to a problem that had a one-email solution.

sections.heading: Which Diploma subjects tolerate a short session, and which do not
paragraphs: Treating every session as sixty minutes of the same thing is the commonest planning error in a constrained week. Subjects differ enormously in how they respond to compression, and matching the format to the subject recovers time that an Al Gurfa household does not otherwise have.

Retrieval-heavy subjects thrive on frequency. Biology has the largest content load in the Diploma and the clearest evidence in favour of short, frequent retrieval work: ten-minute blocks across three evenings outperform one long sitting, and that is a scheduling decision rather than a pedagogical one. Chemistry recall, Economics diagram drills, Computer Science conversions and mathematics arithmetic fluency all behave the same way.

Subjects built on sustained production do not compress. English A analysis and essay planning, the HL Essay at twenty per cent, Higher Level mathematics problem work and Paper 3, extended Economics evaluation, and any internal assessment drafting all need an uninterrupted stretch and a student who is not already tired. For an Al Gurfa household that usually means a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening, and the quality difference in marked writing shows up within a month.

The mixed cases are worth planning rather than guessing. Physics splits cleanly: data-analysis practice for Paper 1 is short-session work; extended calculation and the investigation are not. Business Management becomes short-session work if the stimulus is sent in advance, because the reading happens outside the hour. sections.heading: What a tutor may do with the Diploma core
paragraphs: The core is where Al Gurfa families most often want help and where the boundary is tightest, so it deserves stating in the exact terms a tutor should be able to repeat. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, and the exhibition commentary at 950. Together the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute up to three bonus points through a published matrix, which is often the gap between meeting an offer and missing it.

A tutor may teach the content, explain each assessment criterion in the board's own published wording, show how a comparable piece is constructed, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach the student how to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the Extended Essay, draft the Theory of Knowledge essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become the tutor's. The distinction is who produced the sentences, and it is not a matter of degree.

The commonest legitimate intervention is also the most valuable and the least glamorous: narrowing a research question. A student chooses an Extended Essay topic because it interests them, discovers at the first draft that the available sources cannot support it, and loses a term. A tutor who spends one session turning a broad question into a researchable one has done more for the grade than ten sessions of content teaching later. The same applies to the science investigation, where research design cannot be repaired once the data exists.

A page in this search result sells completed internal assessment work at a fixed price. Under the board's rules, submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice, and the finding lands on the student. For the record, IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge or the Sharjah Private Education Authority; it holds no such relationship, claims none, and runs no UAE premises.

sections.heading: Fujairah's regulator, and what it means for an Al Gurfa family
paragraphs: Private schools in Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level authority, and families moving in from elsewhere in the country notice the difference. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah's to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's to its Department of Knowledge. The ministry supervises Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain.

That changes where things are looked up and who approves what. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection alone. For an Al Gurfa household with a child boarding or commuting into Sharjah, the school is operating under a different approval regime from the one their sibling's Fujairah school uses, and term dates occasionally misalign as a result.

Underneath all of it sits one federal rule that explains the length of the school day described earlier on this page. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the ministry's general regulations. That is why a Diploma student in Al Gurfa carries subjects a Diploma student in Europe does not, and why the week that tutoring has to fit into is fuller than the programme's own timetable suggests.

None of this is an argument for or against anything. It is the information a parent needs to read the right document, ask the right office and plan around the right calendar, and it is absent from every competitor page researched for this market: Abu Dhabi's regulator is named by none of them, Sharjah's by one, and Fujairah by nobody at all.

process.title: Write out one real week before choosing an hour
process.description: Both school runs, the later arrival time, food and a genuine break, and the nights homework is heaviest. Then book the slot thirty minutes after the latest realistic arrival. Choose for February rather than October, because a slot that fails in the busy term has not worked at all.

process.title: Get the coordinator's internal deadline calendar
process.description: The whole thing, at the start of the first Diploma year. Internal deadlines are set by the school, arrive in clusters, and land hardest in the autumn of the final year alongside mocks. That is the period a weekly slot gets cancelled, and knowing it is coming is how the arrangement survives it.

process.title: Match format to subject, not to habit
process.description: Retrieval-heavy subjects get two short sessions a week; sustained-production subjects get one protected full session or a weekend morning. Biology and Chemistry recall behave differently from Higher Level mathematics and English A, and allocating the same hour to both wastes one of them.

process.title: Run the free trial lesson in the real slot
process.description: The same weekday and hour you intend to keep, not a convenient demonstration time. It tells you whether your child can work then, which is a different question from whether the tutor can explain. Both are being tested, and the first is the better predictor of whether this lasts.

process.title: Agree the deadline-cluster pattern in advance
process.description: When internal assessments and core deadlines land together, sessions shorten and switch to process coaching on the piece that is due. Settling that in the first year prevents the autumn of the second from erasing the arrangement entirely and then never restarting it.

process.title: Say early if a move or boarding is coming
process.description: The slot can be positioned to survive a weekly commute, the specification can be checked in case the new school enters a different board, and the topic risk list hands over trivially if it is written down. Mentioned in week one it is an email; mentioned in week eight it costs a month.

whyPoints.title: The slot chosen for the hardest week
whyPoints.description: An Al Gurfa household's arrival time is the later of two school runs, and a slot that works in October and fails in February has not worked. Weekly tutoring is cumulative, so the hour is chosen against the worst week rather than the most convenient one.

whyPoints.title: Internal deadlines mapped, not just exam dates
whyPoints.description: The Diploma's hardest weeks are in the autumn of the final year, when coursework clusters collide with mocks. That calendar is set by the school and is obtainable in the first year. Knowing the shape is most of the planning and it is absent from every page in this market.

whyPoints.title: CAS flagged before it becomes a crisis
whyPoints.description: An incomplete portfolio blocks the diploma regardless of points, and the usual failure is activities without reflections. A tutor who sees the student weekly across both years can notice it in the first one, which is a five-second intervention against a very large downside.

whyPoints.title: Format matched to the subject
whyPoints.description: Biology retrieval wants frequency; Higher Level mathematics and English A want an uninterrupted hour and a rested student. Allocating limited evenings deliberately recovers time an Al Gurfa household does not otherwise have, and the split is set out rather than left to guesswork.

whyPoints.title: Built to survive boarding, commuting and a school move
whyPoints.description: Local Diploma capacity in Fujairah is limited, so many students on this route change school, board or travel weekly. An online slot survives all three, and the handover of a written topic risk list is trivial. The internal deadlines do not pause for any of it.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Gurfa household realistically hold a Diploma session?
faqs.answer: Usually between 17:30 and 20:30, and the determining factor is the later of two school runs rather than the earlier. Al Gurfa sits south of the city along the coast road and households here frequently run two journeys, so neither child tends to be at a desk before 16:30 and often not before 17:00. Add food and a real break and the first usable hour is later than families assume. Book thirty minutes after the latest realistic arrival, measured over a week.

faqs.question: Does an IB tutor travel to Al Gurfa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The in-home market here is real, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and part of the premium is the journey. The practical cost of a journey along the coast road is that an arrival time is not a start time.

faqs.question: When do IB internal deadlines actually fall?
faqs.answer: They are set by the school rather than the board, and they cluster. The Extended Essay topic and supervisor land early in the first year, science investigation planning sits in the first year because research design cannot be fixed after data collection, and the heaviest cluster is the autumn of the final year, when coursework finals and the Extended Essay submission collide with mock examinations. Ask your child's coordinator for the whole internal calendar at the start of the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: Why does CAS matter if it carries no points?
faqs.answer: Because an incomplete CAS portfolio prevents the diploma from being awarded however many points the six subjects produce. A student with 38 points and an unfinished portfolio has no diploma; a student with 30 points and a complete one does. The usual failure is accumulating activities without the reflections that evidence them, then reconstructing the portfolio in the spring of the final year while sitting examinations. Scheduling a deliberate CAS evening, separate from any tutoring evening, prevents most of it.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects can be taught in a forty-minute session?
faqs.answer: Retrieval-heavy ones. Biology content, Chemistry organic conditions and definitions, Economics diagram drills, Computer Science conversions and arithmetic fluency all respond better to frequency than to duration. What does not compress is sustained production: English A analysis and essay planning, the HL Essay, Higher Level mathematics problem work including Paper 3, and any coursework drafting. Those need an uninterrupted hour and a student who is not already tired, which usually means a weekend morning.

faqs.question: How should a household with two children schedule tutoring?
faqs.answer: Stagger rather than parallelise. The younger child goes earlier and shorter, because attention is the binding constraint at that age and two forty-minute sessions beat one long one. The Diploma student goes later and longer, because the subjects that matter at that level do not tolerate compression. Putting both on the same evening means one competes with dinner. A quieter house at 18:30 produces measurably better written work over a term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths for a Diploma student and a Year 9 sibling?
faqs.answer: It is usually a false economy. The specifications and the depth required differ too much, and the session that suffers is whichever one the tutor is less current in. Two specialists on two different evenings generally costs the same and works, because each is matched to a single course. The scheduling convenience is real but small, and it tends to be outweighed within a term by the gap in subject currency between a Diploma course and a lower-secondary one.

faqs.question: What happens to tutoring if my child starts boarding outside Fujairah?
faqs.answer: It continues, provided the slot is placed inside a study period and the house staff know about it, which needs asking rather than assuming. Because local Diploma provision in Fujairah is limited, boarding and weekly commuting are common on this route, and an online slot survives both. A weekly commuter has three reliable evenings rather than five, so the slot should sit in the middle of that window instead of at either edge.

faqs.question: Should we cancel sessions during a deadline cluster?
faqs.answer: Shorten them and change their content instead. During the weeks when internal assessments and core deadlines land together, a session that teaches subject content competes with the piece that is due. A session that explains the criteria and reviews the student's own draft supports it. Keeping the frequency while reducing the length preserves the weekly cycle, which is what makes the arrangement worth anything. Cancelling twice usually means it never restarts.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an Extended Essay for an Al Gurfa student?
faqs.answer: Explain the criteria in the board's own wording, help narrow a broad research question into one the available sources can support, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it. A tutor may not write the essay or draft sections of it. The cap is 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 and the exhibition commentary at 950, and together the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute up to three bonus points.

faqs.question: Why is the Fujairah school day longer than the Diploma timetable suggests?
faqs.answer: Because private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whichever curriculum they are licensed for, under the ministry's general regulations. That adds to the week rather than replacing anything, so a Diploma student in Al Gurfa carries more timetabled hours than one following the same programme elsewhere. The practical consequence is a later realistic session slot and less tolerance for a second weekly commitment in the same subject.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school if we board them in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education instead, alongside Ajman's and Umm Al Quwain's. A household with one child in each system is dealing with two approval regimes and occasionally two term calendars, which is worth knowing before booking anything that assumes a shared holiday.

faqs.question: Should the trial lesson be at a convenient hour or the one we plan to use?
faqs.answer: The one you plan to use. A trial at a convenient time tells you whether the tutor can explain; a trial at 18:30 on the Wednesday you intend to book tells you whether your child can work then, which is the question that decides whether the arrangement lasts a term. Run it in the real slot with yourself able to listen in, and judge the explanation and your child's alertness together rather than separately.

faqs.question: What should I ask for after the first month in an Al Gurfa arrangement?
faqs.answer: Two things: the updated topic risk list from the diagnostic, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged and the marked work behind it, and an honest answer about whether the slot is holding. If sessions have started late three times, the slot is wrong and should move rather than being tolerated. Those two questions catch both failure modes in this household type: the wrong content and the wrong hour, which are fixed differently.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-gurfa.closingHeading: Map the week, then get the internal calendar
fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-gurfa.closingBody: For an Al Gurfa household the two documents that matter are the household's own week and the school's internal deadline calendar. Write out both school runs and the later arrival time, then book the slot thirty minutes after it. Ask your child's coordinator for the full internal calendar at the start of the first Diploma year, and agree now what sessions will contain during a deadline cluster. Run the free trial lesson in the real slot. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, shifting later during Ramadan by agreement. Nobody is sent to an Al Gurfa address.

intro.heading: A Diploma deadline map for a town with a two-hour radius
paragraphs: Dibba sits at the northern end of the Fujairah coast, where the Hajar mountains come down to the Gulf of Oman. It is a beautiful place to live and a difficult place to find a Higher Level Chemistry teacher in. The nearest alternatives are south along the coast road to Fujairah City, or over the mountains towards Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, and neither is a journey anybody makes twice on a school day.

That is the context, and it changes the arithmetic rather than the advice. The Diploma makes the same demands on a student in Dibba as on one in Dubai: six subjects, an Extended Essay at four thousand words, a Theory of Knowledge essay at one thousand six hundred, six Internal Assessments, and Creativity, Activity and Service to evidence. The difference is that a Dubai family with a problem has options within twenty minutes and a Dibba family has options within two hours or online.

So this page does something no competitor page in this market does: it maps the core components onto the months they actually occupy. Not a list of deadlines, which every school hands out and every family loses, but a picture of which months are carrying two or three components at once. Once a family in Dibba can see the pile-up, they can move one item forward by three weeks, and that single act of rescheduling is worth more than a term of extra teaching.

Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is different from Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, each of which has its own emirate-level authority. Advice written for Dubai and relabelled for the east coast gets this wrong, which is one reason so little of what ranks for these searches is useful here.

IB Gram matches Dibba students to Diploma subject specialists and delivers every lesson one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. In a town this size that is not a limitation being apologised for, it is the only way a student sitting a less commonly taught Higher Level subject gets a specialist at all.

This page publishes no specific IB exam or results date. UAE candidates sit the May session and the board's own site is the only authority for the dates inside it; your child's Diploma coordinator is the person to confirm them with. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear below with their sources, because those boards publish theirs openly and a past date keeps its year so that it stays checkable.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-dibba.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes and the IGCSE route in produce the planning questions here. In a small east-coast cohort the programme a student is on often depends on what the one available school offers.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Standard and Higher Level plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment with published criteria, marked internally and moderated externally. Counting the core and the six Internal Assessments together, a Diploma student carries eight assessed deadlines that have nothing to do with sitting a paper.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the May session. For a Dibba family the governing dates are the school's internal ones, which sit earlier than the board's windows because the school needs time to mark and moderate. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the complete internal list at the start of Year 12, in writing, and put it on one calendar alongside family travel.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, reported one to eight per criterion, ending in the Personal Project. The Personal Project is the only long independent task most students complete before the Extended Essay, which makes it the cheapest rehearsal available for managing a deadline that is eighteen months away.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision on the east coast is thin, so most Dibba students arrive at the Diploma from an IGCSE route instead. Where a student does transfer in from the MYP, the gap is widest in mathematics and the sciences, because Diploma teaching assumes algebraic fluency the MYP does not require.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, transdisciplinary, with no external examinations and an exhibition at the end. For a Diploma-minded parent the useful feature is that the exhibition asks a young child to plan and present independent work, which is the same muscle the Extended Essay uses a decade later.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Dibba generally start in another curriculum and transfer later, because local provision is limited. A transfer at Year 6 or 7 is straightforward. A transfer into Year 11 or the first Diploma year is not, and the gap that needs closing is in independent written work rather than in subject content.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE as the route in
programmes.description: The usual entry path to the Diploma on the east coast. Extended or Higher tier in mathematics and the sciences is effectively the prerequisite for Higher Level in those subjects, so Year 11 grades set the ceiling on Diploma choices. The codes matter: 0580, 0620 and 0625 at Cambridge, 4MA1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 at Pearson.
programmes.countryNote: UAE centres sit the Cambridge June and November series; the February and March series belongs to India alone. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. A November resit sits inside the first Diploma term and competes with it directly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration occupies roughly three months of elapsed time even though it takes far fewer hours. Students who choose a topic late write about content they have not yet been taught, which is a scheduling failure dressed up as a mathematics problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The exploration suits this course because usable data is easy to find, so the elapsed time is shorter. The reflection criterion is where drafts fall down, by describing the data instead of asking how well the model actually fits it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The investigation needs a design settled, approved and then physically run, which spreads it across two to three months. Where school laboratory access is limited, that elapsed time grows, and in Dibba laboratory time is the binding constraint rather than the writing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation belongs in the first term because every write-up afterwards uses it. The investigation is usually quicker to run than a biology one and faster to analyse, which makes physics the subject to schedule into a crowded month if you have a choice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The longest elapsed time of the three sciences, because growth or sampling takes real weeks that cannot be compressed. A biology investigation started a month late cannot be rescued by working harder, which makes its design deadline the least forgiving on the whole Diploma.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and written assignments are scheduled by the school and land in whichever month the school chooses, often alongside two Internal Assessments. Choosing the global issue and extracts early is the only lever a student has over this.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries of eight hundred words, each tied to a published article and each with its own date. One per term is the fix. All three in one fortnight is the failure, and it is a scheduling decision rather than an ability one.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The investigation runs to about two thousand two hundred words and depends on source availability, which in Dibba means digital sources and interlibrary access rather than a physical archive. Choose sources before fixing the question or expect to change the question.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The project depends on an organisation replying, and on the east coast the pool of accessible organisations is smaller. Make the approach a month earlier than seems necessary, because the binding constraint is somebody else's inbox.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The experimental study requires an ethical design cleared by the school before any data is collected, and recruiting participants in a small community takes longer than it does in a large school. Both steps are elapsed time rather than working time.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A real client and a working artefact, which makes scope the trap. Students design ambitiously in the first year and spend the second finishing rather than documenting to the criteria, and documentation is what carries the marks.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition accumulate steadily across both years and nothing can be caught up at the end. The subject with the least forgiving calendar and the one where families least expect a calendar problem.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-dibba.regionsIntro: Distances on the east coast are longer than anywhere else in the UAE, so these notes are about travel time and what it does to an evening.

regions.name: Dibba
regions.note: At the northern end of the Fujairah coast where the mountains meet the sea. The nearest significant school alternatives are south along the coast road or across the Hajar range, so local provision is what most families work with.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Roughly an hour south along the coast and the emirate's main centre, holding most of its private-school provision. A daily commute from Dibba to Fujairah City is possible and absorbs most of the usable evening.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal district of Fujairah City near the corniche. Dibba families who move for schooling frequently land here, which is why the two areas share the same set of Diploma questions.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland district on the Fujairah City side, closer to the mountain road. Students here reach the city schools quickly and the east coast's Diploma cohort is concentrated in this direction.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Fujairah City district whose families face a shorter school run than Dibba's and the identical scarcity of specialist subject teachers, because scarcity here is an emirate-level fact.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Coastal Fujairah City district. The practical difference from Dibba is forty minutes of road, not a different set of available tutors or a different school calendar.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: Along the coast and administered by Sharjah rather than Fujairah, so its private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Worth knowing because families compare across that boundary without realising the regulator changes.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Hisn
regions.note: Immediately adjacent to Dibba and part of Sharjah, which means a different regulator for its schools despite being a short drive away. One of the few places in the UAE where two education authorities meet at a street.

schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private-school set is small, which is the single most important fact for a Diploma family in Dibba. A less commonly taught Higher Level subject may have no local teaching set at all, and that is arithmetic rather than anybody's failing.

sections.heading: What the distance from everywhere actually changes
paragraphs: Dibba's geography is the first thing to deal with honestly, because most advice in this market assumes a city. The town sits at the northern tip of the Fujairah coast with the Hajar mountains behind it. Fujairah City is about an hour south along the coast. Dubai is roughly two hours by the mountain road. Those distances do not change what the Diploma asks; they change which responses to a problem are available.

The practical consequences are three. A student who needs a subject the local school does not offer is choosing between a long daily commute, a move, weekly boarding, or a remote arrangement. A family who wants a tutor physically present is choosing from whoever lives within a reasonable drive of Dibba, which is a short list. And a plan that depends on a journey is a plan with a weather and road dependency built into it.

The in-home market does exist and it carries a published premium: UAE rate surveys place in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. On the east coast that premium buys more travel for the same teaching, and it narrows rather than widens the pool, because the constraint is who can get here rather than who can teach the subject.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run in India only. For a Diploma student in Dibba the trade is explicit: no tutor arrives at the door, and in exchange the tutor is chosen from a national pool for the subject and level your child is actually sitting.

sections.heading: The core components mapped onto the months they occupy
paragraphs: Schools hand out deadline lists and families lose them, partly because a list of dates does not show the shape of the problem. What shows the shape is elapsed time. An Internal Assessment is not a day's work due on a date; it is a design decision, an approval, a data-collection period, an analysis and a draft, spread across weeks. Put all eight of a Diploma student's assessed components on the same picture and the pile-ups appear.

The table below does that. Read the months column as elapsed time rather than working time, which is the distinction that makes the whole exercise useful. Biology's investigation occupies three months because growth or sampling cannot be compressed, even though the writing is a fortnight. Economics commentaries occupy nine months collectively if spaced and three weeks if not, and the spaced version produces better marks for less distress.

Two pile-ups are visible on almost every school's calendar. The first is the second term of Year 12, where the Extended Essay draft meets the earliest Internal Assessment designs. The second, and worse, is the first term of Year 13, where several Internal Assessments, the Theory of Knowledge essay and university applications land together. Those are the months to protect, and protecting them means moving something earlier rather than working harder later.

For a family in Dibba there is a local wrinkle worth adding to the picture. Anything requiring an external organisation, a participant pool or laboratory access takes longer here than in a city, because the available options are fewer and the travel is longer. Add two to three weeks to the elapsed time of any component with an outside dependency, and schedule it a month earlier than the school's list suggests.

sections.heading: Protecting the two months that always collide
paragraphs: Every Diploma cohort has the same two crunch points and almost every family meets them without warning. The first sits in the second term of Year 12, when the Extended Essay first draft is wanted at the same time as two or three Internal Assessment designs need approval. The second sits in the first term of Year 13, when several Internal Assessments, the Theory of Knowledge essay and university applications arrive together.

The remedy is unglamorous. Move one item three to four weeks earlier than the school asks. Not all of them, which is unrealistic, and not the one that feels easiest, which is usually the one with the least elapsed time. Move the item with the longest outside dependency: the biology investigation, the business project, the psychology study. Those are the components where three weeks of lead time converts directly into a better mark.

The second remedy is sequencing inside the month. A student facing three deadlines in five weeks should finish them in order of elapsed time remaining rather than in order of due date, because the item with a two-week dependency left cannot be started on the day before. This is obvious written down and almost never done, because due dates are what get written on calendars.

A tutor's role here is narrow and real. The core-component block is placed in the month the map says it belongs to, not the month the panic arrives, and it finishes two weeks before the internal deadline. That gap is deliberate: the student makes the final decisions and can therefore defend the work in a reflection session, which a student handed a polished draft cannot.
bullets: Crunch one: Year 12 term 2, Extended Essay draft meets investigation designs
Crunch two: Year 13 term 1, several Internal Assessments plus applications
Move the component with the longest outside dependency, not the easiest one

sections.heading: Mocks, predicted grades and the last useful signal
paragraphs: Mocks are the only external evidence that arrives in time to act on, and in a small cohort they matter more than usual because there is less day-to-day data about where a student actually sits. A class of eight generates fewer comparison points than a class of twenty-eight, and a teacher carrying three courses has less capacity to produce them.

So ask for the script, not the grade. From a marked paper a tutor reads four things in order: whether all questions were attempted or marks ran out in the final quarter, which is a timing problem and the fastest to fix; whether working is written or implied, since unwritten method lines forfeit credit; whether answers match the command terms; and only then whether content is genuinely missing.

Predicted grades are the consequence. They are issued by the school, they rest heavily on mock performance, and they decide which university offers are realistic. A student whose mock sits two grades below the prediction they need is short of evidence rather than short of time, which makes the weeks before predictions the highest-leverage point in the whole two years for one short, narrow block in one subject.

One caution about the numbers. Grade boundaries are set per series by the awarding body and genuinely move, so a school's mock boundary is an estimate drawn from earlier series rather than a line. A student two marks under an internal boundary is not necessarily two marks under the real one. This page publishes no boundary figures, because those belong to the boards, are published per series, and go stale.
bullets: Ask for the marked script and component marks, not just the grade
Read in order: timing, written method, command terms, then content
The weeks before predicted grades are the highest-leverage point in the Diploma
Mock boundaries are estimates from earlier series, not fixed lines

sections.heading: What support costs, and what the travel line is worth
paragraphs: Published UAE market rates are worth setting out in full, because three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all and two quote US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45-150 per hour, with one content platform publishing from AED 45-65 and one learning platform from AED 33-52.

Above that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150-300, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with a UK agency quoting AED 270 and a UAE rate survey showing AED 200-450 or more. Premium named and examiner-track tutors reach AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one, including travel, sits at AED 180-500.

For a household budget the monthly figures are more honest. Surveys put a weekly hour at roughly AED 240-600 for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include online bundles from around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions, which is where the travel component becomes visible as its own line.

Every one of those figures belongs to the provider or survey that published it. None is an IB Gram price, and nothing here is a quote. What we publish is the model, and a free trial lesson that comes before any payment with no card needed. For an east-coast family the in-home comparison deserves one extra thought: the premium reflects distance, and from Dibba the distance is larger than the survey averages assume.

sections.heading: The federal regulator, and why it matters on the east coast
paragraphs: Fujairah is one of three emirates where private schools are supervised federally rather than by an emirate-level authority. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge.

That distinction has a practical edge in Dibba specifically, because the town sits next to Dibba Al-Hisn, which is part of Sharjah. Schools a short drive apart can therefore answer to two different authorities with different approval processes. A family comparing two schools across that line is comparing institutions under different regulators, which is unusual anywhere in the world and routine here.

The federal baseline applies in all cases: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must otherwise adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So those subjects sit on top of a Diploma or IGCSE timetable rather than instead of part of it, and a revision plan that counts only the examined international subjects has assumed hours that do not exist.

None of these bodies accredits a tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A tutoring service using a regulator's name as an adjective about itself is making a claim it should be asked to evidence, and the KHDA permit for a training institute with premises is a specific instrument held by specific businesses.
bullets: The federal Ministry of Education supervises Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
Dibba Al-Hisn next door is Sharjah, so its schools answer to SPEA
Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies are required alongside any curriculum
No regulator or board accredits IB Gram, and this page claims none

sections.heading: The permit question, asked in one sentence
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE operates under a permit, and in a small community where tutoring is often arranged by word of mouth the question is worth asking out loud. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligible groups are broader than most parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service for private tutor licensing, through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time.

Two constraints attach. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published amounts, so any specific figure quoted to you has been made up by whoever quoted it. And the permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which matches ADEK's professional-ethics position for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi.

That last point lands harder in a small town than in a city. In Dibba the obvious person to ask is often your child's own teacher, and that is precisely the arrangement to avoid: the person marking an Internal Assessment should not also be paid to prepare it. An independent specialist gives a second, unconflicted read, and in a cohort of eight that second read is worth more than it would be in a cohort of thirty.
bullets: Ask directly whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit
It is free, valid two years, and applied for through MoHRE's own channels
No fine schedule is published, so any quoted amount is invented
Avoid paying your child's own teacher; the code of conduct bars it

sections.heading: The line on assessed work, drawn in public
paragraphs: A service in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price and ranks for searches a Dibba parent might reasonably run. So the boundary belongs on the page rather than in terms. A tutor explains the criteria, works through published exemplars, questions whether a research question or an investigation design can carry the required depth, and reads the student's own draft to name the weak criterion.

What a tutor does not do is produce the work. Nobody here writes, finishes or edits to completion an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any coursework. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under the board's rules and the penalty falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid, two years after the decision was made.

There is a parallel rule about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are cited and linked rather than reproduced or supplied here, because redistributing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure as well. A service offering a mark-scheme bundle as a selling point does not own what it is offering.

The operational effect is the two-week gap already described. A core-component block finishes before the school's internal deadline so the student makes the final decisions in their own words. That is both the compliant arrangement and the better one, because a student who has made the decisions can answer questions about them in a reflection session and a student handed a finished draft cannot.
bullets: Criteria, exemplars, questioning and feedback on the student's own work only
No writing or finishing of any assessed component, at any price
Official materials are cited and linked, never reproduced or supplied

sections.heading: Equivalency, and when to deal with it from the east coast
paragraphs: If your child intends to apply to a UAE university the certificate has to be made equivalent by the Ministry of Education, and the documentary work should happen in a term where the Diploma calendar is light. That is the whole of the useful advice from a tutoring page: it is a scheduling point, and the authority on the process is the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority rather than anybody selling lessons.

The published British-track rule, which applies to IGCSE siblings and to students on that route, asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

The American track differs in kind: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold appears on this page, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site and an unverified figure published across a page set like this would be a liability rather than a service.

Two limits stated plainly. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, does not submit it on anybody's behalf and guarantees no outcome from it. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, whatever urgency is attached to it elsewhere in this market. From Dibba the one genuine advantage is that the documentary work is almost all done remotely, so distance is not the obstacle it is for other errands.
bullets: Do the documentary work in a light term, not a crunch one
British track: five subjects at E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education
American track: SAT Math 450+ and English via IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450

process.title: Send the internal deadline list
process.description: Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for every internal date in writing: Extended Essay drafts and reflections, the Theory of Knowledge title and essay, and all six Internal Assessment dates. That list is what a plan is built from and most families have never seen it in one place.

process.title: Add the elapsed times
process.description: Against each deadline, note how long the component really occupies rather than how long the writing takes. Biology's investigation is three months; an Economics commentary is a fortnight. The pile-ups appear immediately, and from Dibba anything with an outside dependency needs two or three extra weeks.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your own material
process.description: A real lesson rather than a consultation, run on a question your child got wrong or a draft paragraph that is not working. No payment and no card needed, and you are welcome to watch. What you are judging is how the tutor behaves when your child is stuck.

process.title: Place the block in the right month
process.description: A core-component block goes in the month the map says it belongs to, not the month the worry arrives. It finishes two weeks before the school's internal deadline so the student does the final edit and can defend the work in a reflection session.

process.title: Session notes tied to a component
process.description: Every note names what was covered, what was set, and which deadline the week belongs to. Across eighteen months that is what stops a plan drifting, and it gives you something concrete to check in week four rather than an impression to trust in month six.

process.title: A straight answer on availability
process.description: For a less commonly taught Higher Level subject there may be nobody suitable free this month. You hear that, with a date or an alternative, rather than being placed with somebody adjacent to the subject. On a small cohort a wrong match costs more than a wait.

whyPoints.title: Elapsed time, not just deadlines
whyPoints.description: Every school hands out a deadline list and no school explains that a biology investigation occupies three months of calendar for a fortnight of writing. Mapping elapsed time is what makes the pile-ups visible early enough to move something.

whyPoints.title: Written for the east coast, not relabelled from Dubai
whyPoints.description: Fujairah's private schools are supervised federally, Dibba Al-Hisn next door answers to Sharjah, and the nearest alternative school is an hour away. None of that is true of the Dubai pages that rank for these searches.

whyPoints.title: Outside dependencies costed in
whyPoints.description: Anything needing laboratory access, an organisation's reply or a participant pool takes longer here than in a city. A plan that adds two to three weeks to those components is a plan that holds, and one that does not is a plan that fails in the second term.

whyPoints.title: Rates printed with their publisher
whyPoints.description: Every AED band names the survey or provider that published it and is presented as the market rather than our price. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote US dollars.

whyPoints.title: A specialist from a national pool
whyPoints.description: In a town where a Higher Level cohort can be a handful of students, matching on subject and level requires looking beyond the emirate. Online delivery is what makes that possible, and it is stated before booking rather than discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates invented here
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit the May session; the specific dates belong to the board's own site and to your child's coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates appear with their sources, and past dates keep their year so they stay checkable.

faqs.question: Is there any realistic way to get a tutor to our home in Dibba?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, and honestly not easily through anybody. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson here is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market exists at published rates of roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, but those averages assume city distances. From Dibba the nearest sizeable pool of subject teachers is an hour or two away, so the premium buys road time and the choice of tutor narrows sharply.

faqs.question: How many assessed deadlines does a Diploma student actually carry?
faqs.answer: Eight, counting the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and six Internal Assessments, plus Creativity, Activity and Service to evidence continuously. None of them involves sitting a paper, and together they decide a meaningful share of the final result before the May session begins. That is why this page maps them by elapsed time rather than listing dates: a list shows when things are due and a map shows which months are carrying three things at once.

faqs.question: Which component takes longest in real calendar time?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay, at nine to twelve months from research question to final draft, with Biology's investigation the longest of the sciences at around three months because growth or sampling cannot be compressed. A Physics investigation is often six to eight weeks and is therefore the one to schedule into a crowded month if there is a choice. Writing time and elapsed time are different quantities, and planning from writing time is how families end up with three deadlines in one fortnight.

faqs.question: When do the Diploma deadlines pile up on a Dibba student?
faqs.answer: Twice, predictably. The second term of Year 12, where the first Extended Essay draft meets two or three Internal Assessment designs needing approval. And the first term of Year 13, where several Internal Assessments, the Theory of Knowledge essay and university applications land together. The remedy is to move the component with the longest outside dependency three to four weeks earlier than the school asks, rather than attempting to move everything or working harder in the month itself.

faqs.question: Does being an hour from Fujairah City change the plan or just the logistics?
faqs.answer: Both, in specific ways. It changes logistics because every journey is longer and an in-home arrangement carries more road risk across sixteen sessions. It changes the plan because components with outside dependencies take longer: laboratory access, an organisation willing to be studied, a participant pool for a psychology study. Add two to three weeks to the elapsed time of anything that depends on somebody else, and schedule it a month earlier than the school's list suggests.

faqs.question: Who supervises private schools in Fujairah, and is that different from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, materially. The federal Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain, whereas Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. In Dibba this is unusually visible, because Dibba Al-Hisn next door is part of Sharjah, so two schools a short drive apart can answer to two different authorities.

faqs.question: My child's Higher Level subject is not taught locally. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Four, and they should be weighed openly. A long daily commute to Fujairah City or beyond. A family move. Weekly boarding, which some east-coast Diploma students use. Or remote one-to-one support alongside whatever the local school can provide. The fourth is the only one that does not change the household, which is why it is often the realistic answer, and it depends on the tutor being drawn from a national pool rather than a local one.

faqs.question: How should we use a mock in a cohort of eight students?
faqs.answer: More carefully than a large cohort would need to, because there is less routine data about where your child sits. Ask for the marked script and component marks rather than the grade. Read it in four passes: were all questions attempted or did marks run out late, is the working written or implied, do the answers match the command terms, and only then is content missing. The first three are habits that change in weeks and the fourth takes a term.

faqs.question: Can laboratory work for an Internal Assessment be done online?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should suggest otherwise. The experimental work belongs in the school laboratory and the school's own teaching. What can be done remotely, and is where most of the marks actually move, is the design before the data and the analysis afterwards: choosing a genuine independent variable range, planning repeats, handling uncertainty, and writing the evaluation against the criteria. The design session is the highest-value hour on the whole component and it sits weeks before any apparatus is touched.

faqs.question: Is paying my child's own teacher for extra lessons a problem here?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid, and in a small town it is also the most tempting one. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules, the person marking an Internal Assessment should not be paid to prepare it.

faqs.question: What does a block of Diploma support cost from published rates?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online is published at roughly AED 150-300 per hour, and specialists at AED 200-450 or more, with one UK agency quoting AED 270 and one UAE survey showing AED 200-450 and above. Monthly, surveys put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more for a weekly hour. Those figures belong to the providers and surveys that published them, not to us, and nothing here is a quote. Compare block totals against a named target rather than hourly rates.

faqs.question: Will sessions keep running if we are away from the coast for a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is one of the practical arguments for the format from a place like Dibba. The session runs from wherever the family is, so travel does not become a gap in a plan with deadlines at the other end. Agree in advance which time zone the sessions will run in, because a slot that works on Gulf Standard Time can land awkwardly elsewhere, and an awkward slot becomes a cancelled one within a fortnight.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic studies count against our revision time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most plans quietly ignore it. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must otherwise follow the Ministry's general regulations, so those lessons sit on top of the Diploma timetable rather than instead of part of it. Mapping the real week before booking sessions takes ten minutes and prevents a term of over-commitment, and it often explains why a slot that looked free keeps being cancelled.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with an Extended Essay draft, exactly?
faqs.answer: Explain the criteria, work through published exemplars, question whether the research question can be answered in four thousand words, and read the student's own draft to say which criterion is under-served. What a tutor must not do is supply sentences, restructure the argument into their own, or edit a draft to a finished state. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice and the penalty falls on the candidate, which is why blocks here finish two weeks before the internal deadline.

faqs.question: How early should we start if our child is in Year 11 now?
faqs.answer: Now is the ideal moment and almost nobody uses it. Six to eight sessions over the summer before Year 12 closes the gap between IGCSE Extended and what the Diploma assumes in its first term, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. It costs a fraction of the remedial work the same gap generates in Year 13 and it buys something that work cannot: a student who starts the Diploma believing they can do the subject.

faqs.question: If nobody is available for our subject, what will you tell us?
faqs.answer: That nobody is available, with a date or an alternative plan. Less commonly taught Higher Level options have small national cohorts and correspondingly few specialists, so this happens. Six sessions spent discovering that a general graduate has not taught the course are six weeks an exam-year student does not recover, and on a cohort this size a wrong match is also harder to replace quietly. A clear no in week one is the more useful answer.

intro.heading: Start from the syllabus, not the postcode
paragraphs: Fujairah City sits on the Gulf of Oman, on the far side of the Hajar mountains from Dubai. That geography decides almost everything about tutoring here. The emirate's private-school set is small, federal Ministry of Education territory rather than KHDA or ADEK, and the number of adults within half an hour of Al Faseel who have taught IB Chemistry HL to examination standard is very low. A parent who searches for an IB home tutor in Fujairah City and then restricts the search to people who can drive to the house has narrowed a thin pool to almost nothing.

So this page does not lead with the drive. It leads with the syllabus. An IB Diploma subject is a published document with named topics, named assessment objectives, fixed paper durations and fixed weightings. Marks are lost in predictable places: a Mathematics AA student who cannot set out a proof by contradiction, a Chemistry student who writes an equilibrium answer without stating the direction of shift, an Economics student who draws a diagram and then forgets to label the welfare loss. Those are diagnosable faults. Fixing them needs a teacher who has read that mark scheme, not a teacher who lives nearby.

IB Gram matches students in Fujairah City to that teacher and runs the lesson over live video. The tutor shares a screen, works through the student's own script, annotates the student's own past-paper attempt, and leaves a written note of what to do before the next session. Nobody travels. The hour you would have spent waiting for a tutor to come down from Masafi or over from Khorfakkan is an hour of teaching instead.

The honest comparison matters, so the page sets it out properly. In-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE is quoted on published market pages at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with travel already folded into the figure; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts the in-home band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. Online qualified subject tuition sits lower, at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Those are market rates from other providers, cited so you can check them, not an IB Gram price list.

What follows is subject-level detail: the papers your child actually sits, the weightings behind them, the mark-scheme traps that recur year after year, the Internal Assessment criteria by letter, and the past-paper method that turns revision into something measurable. There is also a plain account of what a tutor may and may not do with assessed coursework, because that line is where several providers in this market quietly cross into malpractice.
