fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-fujairah-city.programmesIntro: The IB is three separate programmes with three separate assessment logics. A Fujairah City family moving a child from one to the next is usually surprised by how little carries over. Here is what each one asks for and what it means locally.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examination. Progress is judged through transdisciplinary units, documented inquiry and an exhibition in the final year. Tutoring at this stage is almost never about content coverage; it is about reading fluency, number sense, written structure and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud. A tutor who tries to teach PYP like a syllabus has misread the programme.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah City primary pupils sitting the PYP also carry the federally mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies strands, which run alongside the licensed curriculum rather than inside it. Those classes are organised separately for Arab and non-Arab pupils, and the content is fixed by the Ministry, so any tutoring support must follow the school's own scheme of work.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP grades run 1-8 against four criteria per subject, each criterion carrying its own descriptor band. A student can be strong on knowledge and weak on criterion D communication and still lose a whole grade. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed on process rather than product. MYP maths splits into standard and extended pathways, and that choice shapes which Diploma maths course is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: Because Fujairah has few MYP-to-DP continuum schools, students here more often switch systems between Year 11 and Year 12 than continue. That transition is the single most common reason a Fujairah City family looks for an IB home tutor in Fujairah City: the child has arrived in DP1 from a different board and the assessment vocabulary is unfamiliar.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a fixed share of the final grade, and the written papers carry the rest. Points run to 45. The structural difficulty is not any single subject; it is six Internal Assessments and an Extended Essay landing in the same ten weeks.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May examination session. A Fujairah City student who needs a subject their school does not offer, or who wants to resit, has to work through their school's IB coordinator, and the coordinator is the only person who can confirm session dates. We do not publish IB examination dates on this page because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than no date.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-fujairah-city.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma Programme subjects Fujairah City students most often ask for, with what each one assesses and where marks go missing. The descriptions are deliberately specific: a tutoring hour is only worth buying if it targets a named weakness.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is non-calculator, Paper 2 is calculator, and HL adds Paper 3, a long two-part problem worth a fifth of the HL grade. Marks go missing in proof, in complex numbers at HL, and in the habit of writing a numerical answer with no supporting line of working. Paper 3 rewards students who can read an unfamiliar structure and keep going.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology sit at the centre. The usual fault is treating the graphic display calculator as the answer rather than the tool: a regression line quoted without interpreting the coefficient earns little. HL adds matrices, graph theory and vectors. Choosing AI over AA is a route decision with university consequences, not an easier option.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice, Paper 2 is structured, and the Internal Assessment carries a fifth of the grade. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where students stall. The recurring mark-scheme trap is the explanation question: stating that a rate increases without naming collision frequency and activation energy scores nothing at all.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity dominate the early course; fields, induction and nuclear physics arrive later and are where HL grades are decided. Students lose marks on unit conversion, on significant figures in data questions, and on describing a graph instead of deriving a relationship from its gradient. Practical skills are assessed through the Internal Assessment.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the hazard. Cell respiration, photosynthesis, genetics and physiology each carry dense terminology, and command terms separate outline from explain from discuss. A student who writes everything they know about a topic rather than answering the verb in the question will cap out well below their understanding.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed through written papers and a portfolio of commentaries built on real published articles. The commentary is where the marks are most winnable and most often wasted: students summarise the article instead of applying a diagram and evaluating. HL adds policy calculation and a quantitative paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two written papers, an Individual Oral on a global issue, and at HL a formal essay. The Individual Oral is the component students practise least and panic about most: ten minutes of structured analysis across one literary and one non-literary extract, followed by questions. Preparation is rehearsal, not reading.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across five prescribed themes. Paper 1 asks for a written text in a specified type, so a student who writes a strong essay when the task demanded a blog post loses conceptual-understanding marks immediately. The oral relies on describing a stimulus image accurately before interpreting it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a case study released in advance for Paper 1. The written answers reward tool-based analysis: a student who names a model and then applies it to the stimulus material outscores one who writes general commercial common sense. HL adds extended response on a longer case.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with written commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. Both are assessed on the quality of the knowledge question being explored, not on the student's opinion. Tutoring here is argument coaching: finding the real question inside the title and keeping examples doing analytical work rather than decoration.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Fujairah City actually has to teach
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Fujairah City has to teach a named syllabus to a named level, and that is a narrower job than it sounds. Diploma Programme Chemistry HL is not school chemistry with extra hours; it is a defined set of topics assessed through two written papers and an Internal Assessment with its own criteria. A tutor who has not taught that specification cannot diagnose why a student who understands equilibrium still scores four out of eight on an equilibrium question.

This is where the local-search instinct works against the family. The pool of adults in Fujairah City who have taught Diploma Chemistry to examination standard is small, and the pool who are free at 17:00 on a Tuesday is smaller again. The same is true of Mathematics AA HL, of Economics HL and of English B. Restricting the search to people who can drive to Al Faseel is a filter applied to competence, and it usually removes the candidates who would have been most useful.

IB Gram answers the search by matching the syllabus first and delivering the lesson over live video. The tutor and the student share a screen, work on the same script, and annotate the same past-paper attempt. sections.heading: Mathematics AA and AI: the papers, the weightings, the traps
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is two separate courses that share a name. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route: proof, calculus, functions and, at Higher Level, complex numbers. Applications and Interpretation is the statistical and modelling route, with matrices and graph theory arriving at HL. Both sit Paper 1 and Paper 2; both HL courses add Paper 3, a long two-part investigation. The Internal Assessment, a mathematical exploration, carries a fifth of the final grade in every version of the course.

The weighting pattern is where tutoring hours earn their keep. A Standard Level student is sitting two papers of equal weight, so a non-calculator weakness is worth the same as a calculator weakness and should get equal attention. A Higher Level student has a third paper that behaves differently from the first two: it is unfamiliar by design, it rewards persistence, and students who have only ever practised short questions tend to abandon it halfway. Paper 3 practice is a distinct skill and needs its own sessions.

The recurring mark-scheme losses are specific enough to list. Writing an answer with no working attracts the method penalty even when the number is right. Quoting a calculator regression without interpreting the coefficient earns the mark for the mechanics and nothing for the mathematics. Proof by contradiction is attempted without stating the assumption being contradicted. Trigonometric identities are used in the correct direction but with the domain quietly ignored. Each of those is correctable inside two or three sessions once somebody has seen the student's actual script.

Route choice matters more than most families realise, and it is a decision taken in Year 11 with consequences in Year 13. Engineering, physics and most mathematics degrees expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Business, psychology, design and many social-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation. Check the published entry requirements of the specific universities on the shortlist before the school's option form goes in, because switching course mid-Diploma is difficult and switching level is not always possible.

sections.heading: Sciences: where Chemistry, Physics and Biology marks really go
paragraphs: The three Diploma sciences fail students in three different ways, and a tutor who treats them as one subject wastes the first month. Chemistry punishes imprecision in explanation. A student can describe a shift in equilibrium position correctly and still score nothing because the answer never named the direction of the shift or the variable being changed. Energetics questions want the sign convention stated. Organic mechanism questions want the curly arrow starting at the right place, not a general account of what happens.

Physics punishes carelessness with data. Unit conversion errors, significant figures carried wrongly through a calculation and gradient questions answered by describing the shape of the graph instead of extracting a relationship account for a large share of lost marks at both levels. Fields and electromagnetic induction are where Higher Level grades separate, partly because they arrive late in the course and partly because the mathematics behind them is heavier than anything earlier. A student who is comfortable with mechanics can still be in trouble by the second year.

Biology punishes imprecise reading. The content volume is genuinely large, and students compensate by writing everything they know. The command term is the instruction: outline wants a brief account, explain wants causes, discuss wants a balanced argument, and evaluate wants a judgement supported by evidence. Marks for a correct fact written under the wrong command term are simply not available. Terminology discipline is the other half: osmosis, diffusion and active transport are distinguished in the mark scheme even when a student's answer treats them loosely.

All three carry an Internal Assessment built on the student's own investigation, and that is the one component a tutor can support without going near the examination. The support is methodological: is the research question answerable, is the independent variable genuinely controlled, is the uncertainty treatment honest, does the conclusion follow from the data collected rather than from the textbook. A Fujairah City student working online can do all of that with a specialist while running the practical work in their own school laboratory.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment, marked by the school against published criteria and then moderated. Students lose marks there for process reasons rather than knowledge reasons, which is why criterion-level feedback is worth more than general encouragement. The criteria are lettered, each carries its own maximum, and a student who scores well on three and ignores the fourth has capped their grade before the examination starts.

The pattern is consistent across subjects. There is a criterion for the framing of the question or focus, one or two for the handling of evidence or mathematics, one for analysis and evaluation, and one for communication. Communication is the criterion students treat as presentation and examiners treat as structure: a report that never signposts its own argument loses marks that have nothing to do with the quality of the work underneath.

A tutor's role here is bounded, and the boundary is not negotiable. The tutor may discuss a topic until the research question is narrow enough to answer, may ask why a method controls a variable, may read a draft and say which criterion is underserved, and may show the student how a referencing style works. The tutor may not write, rewrite, complete, draft or supply any part of the text. No IB Gram tutor will write the IA for a student, and anyone offering to is exposing that student to a malpractice finding that no grade is worth.

The table sets out the usual criterion shape so a parent can read their child's feedback sheet with some idea of what the letters mean. Exact criteria and maxima are published in each subject guide, which is held by the school's IB coordinator; we reference those documents rather than reproducing them.

sections.heading: Past papers: the only revision method that reads like the examination
paragraphs: Most students revise by reading. Reading produces recognition, and recognition feels like knowledge until a timed paper asks for recall under pressure. The method that works is attempt, mark, log, repeat. The student attempts a paper or a section under real timing. The tutor marks it against the published criteria. The losses go into an error log that persists across sessions. The next lesson targets the pattern in that log rather than the next topic in the book.

The log is the part families skip and the part that does the work. After four papers it stops being a list of mistakes and becomes a diagnosis: this student loses marks on explanation verbs, not on content; this one loses them in the last twenty minutes of every paper, which is a pacing problem; this one loses them in the first question of Paper 2 because they start before reading the stimulus. Each of those has a different fix, and none of them is more content teaching.

Sourcing matters and has a legal edge. Papers, mark schemes and subject guides are copyright material belonging to the IB, and we do not host, reproduce or supply them. The student's school holds what the student is entitled to use, and the IB's own store sells past papers to families directly. Your tutor will work from whatever the student legitimately has and will tell you plainly if a resource cannot be used.

For a Fujairah City student, the practical advantage of doing this online is that the marking is visible. The tutor annotates the scanned or photographed script on screen, the student watches the mark being awarded or withheld, and the annotated version is saved. That record is more useful at parents' evening than any verbal account of how the sessions are going.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IB academic-honesty rules make the student the author of their own assessed work. That applies to the Internal Assessment in every subject, to the Extended Essay, to the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and to any coursework submitted for a grade. A breach is investigated as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not on whoever supplied the text. This matters in the UAE market because at least one provider in this search space openly sells completed Internal Assessments.

The permitted support is wide and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the content, model how an argument is built, question a method until its weaknesses show, read a draft and name the criterion that is underserved, demonstrate a referencing style, and run the student through the school's own deadline sequence. All of that leaves the student as the author. What it does not include is drafting a paragraph, rewriting a section, supplying a research question fully formed, or editing a text to a finished state.

We state the boundary before the first coursework session, and we put it in writing. If a family asks for the other thing, the answer is no, and the reason is not squeamishness: an IB malpractice finding can cost a student the Diploma, and no amount of marks is worth that exposure. The tutor's declaration of support is also something the school may ask for, and a tutor who has stayed inside the line has nothing awkward to declare.

There is a second honesty question that gets less attention: who is allowed to tutor at all. A school teacher in Abu Dhabi is barred by ADEK's professional-ethics rules from taking paid private work with students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. Fujairah sits under federal Ministry of Education supervision rather than ADEK, but the permit rule is federal and applies here too.

sections.heading: The permit question, and how a Fujairah parent can check it
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is not an unregulated activity. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The u.ae federal portal records that the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

The portal is equally direct about the other side: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page does not quote an amount; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source and is left out deliberately. What a parent needs to know is that the permit exists, that it costs nothing, and that asking about it is reasonable rather than rude.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. In Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram does not hold that permit and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because it is not. We match tutors and deliver lessons online; the regulatory position is what it is and the page says so.

The practical check for a Fujairah City family is short. Ask what the tutor's status is, ask whether they hold the MoHRE permit if they are UAE-based, and apply the MoHRE service page as the reference point: the service is called Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, it lists no fee, and it quotes a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for a Fujairah City IB student
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that turns a foreign school certificate into something a UAE university or employer can accept. It is run by the Ministry of Education, not by the school and certainly not by a tutoring platform, and it is worth understanding early because the requirements are about subject counts and minimum grades rather than about overall strength.

For the British track the published rules are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the requirement is a test score rather than a subject count: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB there is no points threshold published on this page, because none has been read on a Ministry source, and publishing an unsourced number would be worse than leaving the row marked for verification.

Nothing about this process requires tutoring, and no page on this site will suggest otherwise. Equivalency is a documentation exercise with published rules. What tutoring can do is make sure the grades a student submits clear the thresholds comfortably, which is a different claim and an honest one.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the paper
process.description: Not the year group alone. Chemistry HL with a weak Paper 2 and an unstarted Internal Assessment is a brief a specialist can act on. The more precise the starting description, the shorter the diagnostic phase and the fewer hours you pay for somebody finding their bearings.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session, at no cost, on a topic the student is currently stuck on. You are watching for whether the tutor diagnoses rather than lectures, and whether the student talks. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it rather than persuading you to continue.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are scheduled in local time, so school pickups, prayer times and sibling timetables are all accounted for. Most Fujairah City families settle on a late-afternoon or post-dinner slot and keep it for the term, because an unmoved slot is the thing that keeps attendance honest.

process.title: Work from the student's own material
process.description: The tutor teaches against the school's scheme of work and marks the student's own scripts. Each session ends with a written note naming the next task and the criterion it targets, so there is a record a parent can read without having to sit in on the lesson.

process.title: Review at the half-term
process.description: Every six to eight weeks the error log is read as a whole, not session by session. That is where a pacing problem or a command-term habit becomes visible, and it is the point at which the plan changes: more past papers, fewer content hours, or a shift onto coursework supervision.

whyPoints.title: The specialist is not local, and that is the point
whyPoints.description: A Diploma Programme minority subject has few teachers anywhere and almost none within a short drive of Fujairah City. Matching by syllabus and teaching over video is how the student reaches the right teacher instead of the nearest available one.

whyPoints.title: Market rates are published here, with sources
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote US dollars. This page quotes AED bands, names the providers and the rate table behind them, and states plainly that they are market figures rather than ours.

whyPoints.title: The exam calendar is handled correctly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May to June and November. Any session table on this site links the live official timetable instead of restating dates that get revised.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft. We do not draft, complete or supply assessed work, and the boundary is stated before the first coursework session rather than discovered halfway through.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not approved, licensed or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here implies otherwise. The regulators are explained because parents need to understand them, not borrowed as credentials.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Fujairah City for IB lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Fujairah City students are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing on the student's own scripts and past-paper attempts. The reason is availability rather than preference: the number of people within driving distance of the corniche who have taught Diploma Chemistry or Mathematics AA to examination standard is very small, and insisting on travel would mean choosing the nearest tutor instead of the right one. You can test the format on a free trial lesson before deciding.

faqs.question: What does the market charge for an IB home tutor around Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market figures put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table gives AED 180 to AED 350 for in-home work rising to AED 200 to AED 450 and above for IB specialists. Online qualified subject tuition is quoted lower, around AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Those are other providers' figures, cited so you can check them. For Fujairah the travel component is larger than in Dubai because the distances are longer.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should a Fujairah City student choose, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree, not on which looks easier. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route with proof and calculus at its centre, and engineering, physics and mathematics degrees commonly require it, often at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is the statistical and modelling route and is accepted for business, psychology, design and many social sciences. Check the published entry requirements of the specific universities on the shortlist before the option form is submitted in Year 11. Changing course mid-Diploma is difficult, and a student who picked on perceived difficulty can find a target degree closed.

faqs.question: How much of the IB grade does the Internal Assessment carry?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject, and the subject guide held by your school's IB coordinator is the authority. In the sciences and in mathematics the Internal Assessment commonly carries around a fifth of the final grade, which makes it the single largest component a student controls outside the examination hall. That is also why marks are lost there for process reasons: a research question that is a topic rather than a question, data presented without processing, or a conclusion the evidence does not support. Criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft is the most efficient tutoring any Diploma student can buy.

faqs.question: Can a Fujairah City tutor help with my child's IB Internal Assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we state before the first session. A tutor may teach the content, help narrow a research question until it is answerable, question a method until its weaknesses show, read a draft and name which criterion is underserved, and demonstrate a referencing style. A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete or supply any part of the text. IB academic-honesty rules make the student the author, and a breach is investigated as malpractice with the consequence falling on the student. Any provider offering a finished Internal Assessment is selling your child an expulsion risk.

faqs.question: Does Fujairah have an education regulator like KHDA or ADEK?
faqs.answer: No. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA and Abu Dhabi's by ADEK, while the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Sharjah has SPEA and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. For a Fujairah City family that means inspection reports and curriculum approvals come through the federal route rather than an emirate authority. The federal baseline also explains the mandatory subjects: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit Cambridge IGCSE and IB examinations?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE centre does not use it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, and the only reliable source for session dates is the school's IB coordinator or the IB directly. We do not publish IB dates on this site because the IB's own site blocks automated verification.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and arrived from a different curriculum. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the fix is less about content than about assessment vocabulary. Students arriving in DP1 from another board typically know more than their marks suggest and lose grades to command terms, to criterion-based coursework they have never met, and to the habit of writing everything they know. The first sessions are diagnostic: a timed question, marked against the real criteria, with the losses logged. Most students see the pattern in their own script within three or four sessions, and from that point the work is targeted rather than general catch-up.

faqs.question: How do past papers work if we cannot download them from you?
faqs.answer: Papers, mark schemes and subject guides are copyright material belonging to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not host, reproduce or supply them. Your child's school holds what the student is entitled to use, and the IB sells past papers to families through its own store. The tutor works from whatever the student legitimately has: the attempt is scanned or photographed, annotated on screen during the session, and saved. That annotated script is the record of what was marked and why, which is more useful than a general progress report.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Fujairah need a permit from the authorities?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. The federal u.ae portal records that it is granted free of charge for two years and that eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The same portal states that anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here. MoHRE's application route is its app, website and e-services system.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for an IB Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For a student who is coping but not secure, one well-used hour a week alongside school teaching is often enough, because the hour pre-teaches rather than repairs. For a student who has fallen behind in a Higher Level subject with a third paper to sit, one hour a week will hold the line but rarely close a gap. The honest answer depends on the error log: if the losses are technique and command terms, a short intensive block of timed papers moves more marks than months of weekly content. We would rather tell you that than sell more hours.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a minority IB subject?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substitute. Some Diploma subjects have very few teachers anywhere, and if nobody with the right syllabus experience has a slot that fits a Fujairah City family's timetable, the useful answer is a date when one will, or a referral. What we will not do is put a general science teacher in front of a Chemistry HL student and hope. Availability transparency is uncomfortable to publish and almost nobody in this market does it, which is precisely why it is worth saying out loud on the page.

faqs.question: Can a Fujairah City session move during Ramadan or the school's own examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families change the slot rather than pause. During Ramadan the usual pattern in the Northern Emirates is a shortened school day and a shift of study into the post-Iftar evening, so a late slot replaces the late-afternoon one. During the school's own internal examination weeks many students want fewer content lessons and more marked practice, which is a change of mode rather than frequency. Because nothing depends on travel, moving a video session is a calendar change and nothing more.

faqs.question: How will I know the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Through three things you can read yourself. First, the written note after each session naming the task set and the criterion it targets. Second, the annotated scripts, which show the mark being awarded or withheld rather than describing it. Third, the error log reviewed every six to eight weeks, which turns a list of mistakes into a diagnosis: a pacing problem in the last twenty minutes of a paper, a command-term habit, a topic genuinely not understood. If the log stops changing, the plan needs to change, and that review is where we say so.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office or centre in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in Fujairah or anywhere else in the UAE, and no page here claims one. We are a tutor-matching platform delivering one-to-one lessons over live video, and the administrative contact is online. Two providers ranking for these searches show a UAE footer address on pages for emirates they do not operate in, and one routes UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying so. We would rather state the position plainly: online delivery, no UAE premises, no regulator accreditation claimed.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-fujairah-city.closingHeading: Start with the paper your child is losing marks on
fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-fujairah-city.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Fujairah City, the most useful thing you can tell us first is the subject, the level and the component that is going wrong. Chemistry HL with a shaky Paper 2 and an unstarted Internal Assessment is a brief a specialist can act on in the first session. Book the free trial lesson, watch whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures, and watch whether your child talks. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not send tutors to UAE addresses. If the match is wrong, tell us and we will change it.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-merashid.tutorsIntro: These specialists teach single IB Diploma subjects at Higher or Standard Level. A quote depends on the subject, the level and how often you want to meet, which is why it follows the free trial lesson rather than preceding it.

intro.heading: Nobody publishes a number, so here is one
paragraphs: Research on this search result produced an awkward finding. Of six pages competing for queries about tutoring in this market, three publish no price whatsoever, and the two that do quote in US dollars — a currency no family in Merashid pays school fees in, settles a utility bill in, or budgets a month in. One agency's own frequently asked questions asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer. A parent trying to work out whether a Diploma subject is affordable has nothing to compare, which is presumably the intention.

So this page leads with money. Not a price list, because inventing one would be dishonest, but the market: what providers in the UAE publish, what band each provider model sits in, what a month costs at one session a week and at two, and the six specific variables that move a quote up or down. Every figure below was read from a published source in October 2026 and is attributed where it sits. None of them is an IB Gram price. Ours follows a free trial lesson and depends on what you actually need.

Merashid is an established residential district of Fujairah with a high proportion of long-term resident families, and the subject demand that comes out of it skews towards the harder end: sciences and mathematics at Higher Level, where local specialist supply across the emirate is thinnest. That combination is worth naming because it drives price. Scarcity is one of the six variables, and in a small school market it is the one that moves a quote most.

IB Gram delivers to Merashid as one-to-one online lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and the same statement appears on every country page this site publishes. The in-home market here is real and the published band for it is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. A later section breaks that premium into its parts, because once you can see what the extra is paying for, the comparison stops being a matter of preference.

A caution on two numbers you will not find here. No UAE VAT treatment of tuition is stated, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and this page has none; ask any provider directly whether a quoted figure includes VAT. And no fine amount for unpermitted tutoring appears, because the ministry did not publish a schedule and the figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. Those two absences are deliberate, and they are the kind of absence worth looking for on any page that quotes money at you. A provider willing to publish a number it cannot source will publish others, and a parent has no way to tell which figures on such a page were read from a document and which were estimated into existence. The simplest protection is to ask where a number came from and to treat a vague answer as the answer.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-merashid.programmesIntro: Cost varies by programme as much as by subject, because the assessment load differs. Three stages account for nearly every Merashid enquiry about Diploma pricing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with a Personal Project in the final year marked out of 24. No terminal papers in the earlier years, which means tutoring here is development rather than repair and is usually booked at one session a week.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest stage at which to buy tutoring and the one Merashid families most often skip. A criterion-level weakness identified in Year 9 costs a handful of sessions; the same weakness surfacing in the second Diploma year costs a term. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind a reported grade rather than the grade alone.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: Six subjects begin, the Extended Essay is chosen, and the Internal Assessments are set up. One weekly session per subject at this stage runs ahead of the school's scheme of work rather than behind it, which is why the cost per grade gained is lowest here.
programmes.countryNote: In Merashid, where demand concentrates on Higher Level sciences and mathematics, this is the year in which a scarcity premium can be avoided. Booking a Higher Level Chemistry specialist in the autumn of the first year is easier and usually cheaper than booking one in the spring of the second, when every family in the Gulf is looking for the same person.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: Internal Assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay submission, mock examinations and the May session, usually in that order. Tutoring at this stage is repair under deadline pressure, which costs more per mark gained than the same work done a year earlier.
programmes.countryNote: Market monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run from roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a weekly hour, which is the highest band published for any kind of tutoring in this country. That premium is the price of lateness rather than of quality, and it is the single most avoidable cost in the entire Diploma.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-merashid.subjectsIntro: Subjects are not interchangeable in price, because the specialist pool differs. The note on each one below says what drives its cost rather than only what it assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested Higher Level subject in the Gulf and consequently the one where booking early matters most. Papers 1 and 2 at thirty per cent each, Paper 3 at twenty, Exploration at twenty. Paper 3 is the least practised component and the one a specialist adds most value on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Easier to staff than Analysis and Approaches because fewer families request it, which in practice means a shorter wait rather than a lower rate. Modelling questions require interpretation written in context, and calculator technique is examinable in itself.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Scarce at Higher Level across all the smaller emirates, which makes it the subject where a scarcity premium is most visible. Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, Internal Assessment at twenty, capped at 3,000 words across four criteria.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Comparable scarcity to Chemistry at Higher Level. Mathematical fluency is the hidden cost driver: a Physics student who is also weak algebraically needs more hours, and a good tutor will say so in the first fortnight rather than the third month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Easier to staff than the other two sciences and the heaviest on content, so the hours tend to be more numerous and individually less specialised. Systematic retrieval practice is cheaper than extra teaching and most of the gain comes from it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Reasonably available and often efficient to tutor, because diagram accuracy is a narrow, teachable skill that carries a disproportionate share of the marks. The portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Widely available, which keeps rates near the middle of the band. The Individual Oral is where hours convert fastest at Standard Level, because it is worth thirty per cent and is rehearsable in a way the written papers are not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Available and inexpensive to tutor relative to the sciences. The pre-released case for the Higher Level paper is the single best use of booked hours, because it can be worked through months ahead of the examination itself.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: One of the scarcest Higher Level subjects in the smaller emirates, so expect a wait rather than a surcharge. The solution-development Internal Assessment assesses documentation alongside the product, which is where strong programmers lose marks.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Chosen as a lighter option and frequently found demanding, because it requires both data handling and evaluative writing about human systems. Scarce enough that availability rather than price is the binding constraint.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-merashid.regionsIntro: Merashid and the districts around it. The comparison that matters for cost is scarcity of local specialists rather than distance, and it runs the same way across all of them.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Established residential district with many long-term resident families, and demand weighted towards Higher Level sciences and mathematics. That is the band where Fujairah's specialist supply is thinnest, so scarcity drives price more than anything local does.

regions.name: Fujairah City centre
regions.note: Most of the emirate's private-school capacity and the widest local subject range. Proximity to the schools shortens commutes but does not widen the pool of Higher Level specialists, which is the variable that sets a Diploma quote.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland and north-west, with the longest afternoon return among the inner districts. Longer journeys push an in-home tutor's effective hourly cost up even when the quoted rate stays the same.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal, near the corniche and the port, roughly fifteen minutes from the city schools. The shortest drive of the inner districts, which is the only respect in which an in-home quote should be cheaper here.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South along the coast road and more dispersed, frequently with two school runs per household. Families here often buy two subjects at once, which is where a package rate becomes worth asking about.

regions.name: Dibba Al Fujairah
regions.note: Around ninety minutes north, with the fewest local secondary options in the emirate. An in-home quote to Dibba carries a travel component large enough that online delivery is the only economically sensible route.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: A Sharjah enclave on this coast, so its schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. School fee structures differ from Fujairah's as a result, which changes the household budget tutoring sits inside.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and which model charges what
paragraphs: Start with the band rather than a single figure, because the spread is wide and the reason for the spread is the useful part. Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online platforms and university-student tutors between roughly AED 45 and 150 an hour, with some platform entry rates quoted from AED 33. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A named IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs roughly AED 200 to 450 or more; one agency publishes AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500. At the top, a single provider publishes AED 650 an hour for a premium named tutor.

Monthly packages advertised in the market include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those two figures are worth comparing carefully, because the second buys eight hours of contact and the first buys eight sessions, and a session is not always an hour. Always convert a package to a cost per contact hour before comparing it with an hourly rate.

Every one of those numbers belongs to the provider who published it, and quoting one is not an endorsement of the provider or a comment on their quality. They are here because a Merashid parent needs a reference range and the pages competing for this search decline to give one. IB Gram's own figure is not in this table, because a single number would be misleading: what we charge depends on the subject, the level and the frequency, and it follows the free trial lesson.

One practical instruction before you compare anything. Ask every provider, including us, whether the quoted figure includes VAT. This page states nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation, and we have none to offer. What a parent can always do is require the answer in writing from whoever is quoting.

sections.heading: The six variables that move a Diploma tutoring quote
paragraphs: A rate is not a property of a tutor. It is the output of six things, and knowing which ones apply to your request tells you whether a quote is reasonable before you have anything to compare it with. Most families only know about the first.

The first is level. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level because the pool of people who have taught it is smaller and the preparation per session is longer. The second is subject scarcity, which in the smaller emirates is the dominant factor: Higher Level Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science and Environmental Systems and Societies are harder to staff than English or Business Management, and scarcity shows up as a longer wait or a higher figure or both.

The third is timing, and it is the one families control and routinely waste. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist booked in the autumn of the first Diploma year is easier to find than the same specialist in the spring of the second, when every family in the Gulf is looking. Market estimates for specialist exam-year support are the highest published band for any tutoring in this country, and a good share of that premium is the price of lateness rather than of expertise.

The fourth is frequency: two sessions a week is not double the value of one, because the work between sessions is where most of the consolidation happens and a student can only absorb so much. The fifth is format, covered in its own section below. The sixth is scope — a defined block on one component is priced differently from an open-ended weekly commitment, and for a specific need the block is almost always better value.

sections.heading: What a month actually costs, in three realistic scenarios
paragraphs: Hourly rates are a poor planning tool because nobody buys an hour. Families buy months, and a month has four or five sessions in it depending on the calendar. Published monthly estimates for a single weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, roughly AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-range qualified tutor, and roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are the three bands worth planning against.

The first scenario is a first-year Diploma student with one weak subject, taking one session a week with a qualified subject tutor. That is the mid-range band, and over an academic year it is the lowest-cost route to a grade change because the work is developmental. The second is a final-year student with a short, specific list of lost-mark causes, taking two sessions a week for eight to ten weeks. That is a concentrated spend in the exam-year band, and it is justified only when a diagnostic has produced that list.

The third is a defined block: four to six sessions on one component, such as the Internal Assessment plan, the Individual Oral or Paper 3 at Higher Level mathematics. Priced as a block rather than monthly, it is the most efficient purchase available, because the target has a published weighting and a visible finish. Many families would be better served by two of these a year than by an open-ended weekly commitment they stop examining after the first term.

The scenario to avoid is the fourth one, which nobody plans and many end up in: two subjects at two sessions a week each, started in the spring of the final year, with gaps across the syllabus in both. That is four sessions and four sets of homework a week on top of a Diploma workload, at the highest published band, with insufficient time to close the gaps. It is the most expensive arrangement available and among the least effective.

sections.heading: What the in-home premium buys in Merashid, broken into parts
paragraphs: The in-home band and the online band overlap, which makes the comparison look like a matter of taste. It is more useful to split the in-home figure into what it pays for. A travelling tutor is paid for the teaching, for the journey, and for the scarcity of people willing to make that journey on a weekday evening. In a dense city the second component is small and the third barely exists. In Merashid both are substantial.

So the premium buys three things here and only the first is a benefit. A person physically present, which is genuinely valuable for a younger child who needs supervision as much as teaching. A shorter list of available subjects, because the set of people who will drive to Merashid and who have also taught Higher Level Chemistry is very close to empty. And a start time that drifts, because an arrival is not a slot and over a term the drift compounds.

For a Diploma student working towards a May session, the third is the one that costs marks. The weekly homework cycle only works if the sessions land where they were booked: work set, work done, work marked, next session built on the marking. A session that starts twenty minutes late and finishes on time has lost a third of itself, and a session cancelled because of traffic has broken the cycle for a fortnight.

The honest counterweight is that some students genuinely concentrate better with somebody at the table. The mitigations for a screen are practical rather than rhetorical: shorter sessions with a break, a shared document the tutor writes on live so the student watches working appear, a visible worked page rather than a talking head, and a parent within earshot for the first few weeks. Merashid families with a younger child should weigh that seriously; for a Year 13 student it is usually a secondary consideration.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entries and the two-year plan
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the largest education line in a Merashid household budget, and seeing it against the others changes how it gets decided. School fees dominate. Examination entry fees for a private candidate are a real cost that families forget until the invoice arrives. And a two-year Diploma plan at one session a week in one subject is a different kind of commitment from a short block, even though the hourly rate is identical.

For context on the wider picture, Dubai's authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by that authority, so the freeze does not apply here. It is still a useful data point: when the biggest line is held flat somewhere, the discretionary lines get examined more closely everywhere.

The Dubai market numbers give a sense of scale that is otherwise hard to picture. In 2024-25 the emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, American at fourteen and the International Baccalaureate at seven. Seven new private schools were announced for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Fujairah operates at a fraction of that, which is precisely why its specialist supply is thin.

The planning conclusion is boring and correct. Decide the annual tutoring budget as a line in the household education budget, before choosing a provider, and then choose the arrangement that fits it. A family that decides it can spend the mid-range monthly band on one subject for a year will make better decisions than one that starts with two sessions a week in two subjects and reviews it when the figure becomes uncomfortable in March.

sections.heading: Where Merashid families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: Five patterns account for most of the wasted spend, and none of them involves a bad tutor. The first is starting late. Market estimates for specialist exam-year support are the highest published band for any tutoring in the country, and a good part of that premium is the cost of scarcity in the spring rather than any difference in teaching. Booking the same specialist eighteen months earlier buys the same person at a lower band with more time to work in.

The second is buying hours without a diagnostic. If nobody has sat a timed paper, marked it against the official scheme and attributed every lost mark to a cause, then the plan is a guess and the hours go wherever the student's anxiety points. The six causes — content not known, content not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method not written, time ran out — need completely different remedies, and five of six are not fixed by more teaching.

The third is spreading across too many subjects. Two subjects at two sessions a week each is four sessions plus four sets of homework on top of a Diploma load, and the usual result is two half-improvements. Sequencing produces better outcomes for the same money: the subject with the shortest loss list first, banked, then the hours move. The fourth is paying for presence a student does not need, which is the in-home premium analysed above.

The fifth is the quietest and the most common: not reviewing. An arrangement that made sense in October is rarely examined in February. The thing to ask for is the written risk list from the diagnostic, updated, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged. An item that has not moved in three weeks is a conversation. Three unchanged items after two months is a reason to change something, and the something is not always the tutor.

sections.heading: Free trials, permits and the questions to ask about any price
paragraphs: A free trial lesson should be free without conditions attached that only appear later, and if any condition exists it should be stated on the same screen as the word free. Ours is one lesson with the matched tutor before anything is paid, with the parent able to listen in. What it is for is a test of explanation: whether your child can follow this person, and whether the tutor thinks in weightings, criteria and command terms rather than in enthusiasm.

On permits, the cost is zero and that is worth knowing because it removes an excuse. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. It is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service, with a stated two working days to complete. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because the ministry published no schedule, no amount appears here.

There is also a rule a Merashid parent should know before approaching a school teacher privately. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as exact regulatory wording and check the current policy, but the underlying principle holds across the country.

Five questions settle most price conversations. Does the figure include VAT, in writing. Is the rate per hour or per session, and how long is a session. What happens if we stop after one month. Who marks the work between sessions, and is that time included. And what happens if the matched tutor becomes unavailable. A provider that answers all five plainly is giving you more information than any of the pages competing for this search.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why a cheap Internal Assessment is the most expensive thing available
paragraphs: There is one purchase in this market that costs more than every premium rate combined, and it is advertised as a bargain. A page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessment work at a fixed price. Under the board's own rules, submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student's qualification rather than on the seller's business. Measured against two years of Diploma work and a university offer, that is the highest-cost item on any menu in this market.

The legitimate boundary is drawn by authorship. A tutor may teach the content, explain each assessment criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach the student to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become the tutor's own.

Knowing the limits is part of a specialist's competence and a cheap thing to test. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the exhibition commentary at 950, the sciences investigation at 3,000, and each Economics commentary at 800. A tutor who does not know those figures is not working from the subject guide. A tutor who offers to supply the guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads is redistributing the board's copyrighted material rather than teaching from it.

Finally, position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, and operates no premises in the UAE. Any price quoted here belongs to the provider who published it, and ours arrives after a trial lesson rather than before one.

process.title: Decide the annual budget before choosing anyone
process.description: Set the tutoring line in the household education budget first, then choose the arrangement that fits it. Families who pick a provider first and discover the annual figure in March make worse decisions than those who decide they can spend the mid-range monthly band on one subject for a year.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and how soon the deadline is
process.description: Higher or Standard Level, which subject, and whether the pressing thing is a paper, an Internal Assessment or the core. Those three facts drive both the match and the quote, because level and scarcity are two of the six variables that move a price.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before discussing money
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, with you able to listen in, before anything is paid. If the explanation does not land with your child, the price is irrelevant. If it does, the quote that follows can be judged against the market bands published on this page rather than against nothing.

process.title: Ask the five price questions in writing
process.description: Does the figure include VAT. Per hour or per session, and how long is a session. What happens if we stop after a month. Who marks work between sessions and is that time included. What happens if the tutor becomes unavailable. Answers in writing are the point.

process.title: Insist on a diagnostic before buying a block of hours
process.description: A timed paper marked against the official scheme with every lost mark attributed to a cause. Without it the plan is a guess and the hours follow the student's anxiety. With it, a short specific list makes a concentrated spend rational and a long diffuse list tells you to spread the work over longer instead.

process.title: Review the risk list monthly, not at the end of term
process.description: Ask for the updated list with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged, and the marked work behind it. An item unchanged for three weeks is a conversation. Three unchanged after two months means something should change, and it is not always the tutor.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost per hour for a family in Merashid?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, a named IB specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home visits including travel at roughly AED 180 to 500, and budget platforms between AED 45 and 150. One provider publishes AED 650 an hour at the premium end. Those belong to the providers who published them and are not IB Gram prices; ours follows a free trial lesson and depends on subject, level and frequency.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level cost more than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Because the pool of people who have actually taught the course is smaller and the preparation per session is longer. Level is one of six variables that move a quote; the others are subject scarcity in your emirate, how late you book, how often you meet, the format, and whether the engagement is a defined block or open-ended. In the smaller emirates scarcity is usually the dominant one, and it tends to show up as a longer wait rather than purely as a higher figure.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy a monthly package or pay by the hour?
faqs.answer: It depends on what a session is, which is why the first step is converting a package to a cost per contact hour. Advertised packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The second buys eight hours of contact; the first buys eight sessions of unstated length. Ask how long a session runs before comparing either with an hourly figure.

faqs.question: How much should a Merashid family budget per month for one Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for a single weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-range qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. The mid-range band taken across the first Diploma year is the lowest cost per grade gained, because the work is developmental rather than repair. Set that line in the household budget before choosing a provider rather than after.

faqs.question: Does the quoted tutoring price include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask whoever is quoting, in writing, and require the answer before paying. This page deliberately states nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and there is none on offer here. What a parent can always do is make the inclusive or exclusive position explicit in the quote. It belongs alongside four other questions: per hour or per session, session length, cancellation terms, and whether marking time is included.

faqs.question: Why is starting in the final spring the most expensive option?
faqs.answer: Because the premium you pay then is scarcity, not quality. Market estimates for specialist exam-year support are the highest published band for any tutoring in this country, and in the spring every family in the Gulf is looking for the same Higher Level specialists. Booking the same person in the autumn of the first Diploma year costs less per month, buys more time to work in, and turns the engagement from repair under deadline pressure into development. It is the single most avoidable cost in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are most expensive to tutor in the smaller emirates?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science and Environmental Systems and Societies, because the number of people who have taught those courses recently is smallest. English A, Business Management and Economics are easier to staff and therefore sit nearer the middle of the band. In Merashid, where demand skews towards Higher Level sciences and mathematics, scarcity is the variable most likely to be binding, and it often appears as a waiting period rather than a surcharge.

faqs.question: Is two sessions a week twice as good as one?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is where consolidation happens. Most of the gain from tutoring comes from the work done between sessions, marked and then built on, and a student can only absorb so much of that alongside a Diploma load. Two sessions a week is the right purchase for a defined eight to ten week run after a diagnostic has produced a short list of causes. As a permanent arrangement it tends to produce diminishing returns at double the monthly cost.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing I can buy for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: A defined block of four to six sessions on one named component with a published weighting: the Internal Assessment plan, the Individual Oral, the pre-released business case, or Paper 3 at Higher Level mathematics. Priced as a block rather than monthly, with a visible end point. Many families would do better with two of those a year than with an open-ended weekly arrangement nobody re-examines after the first term. The component is identifiable, so the result is too.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium make sense for a younger child in Merashid?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and more often than it does for an older one. The premium pays for three things: physical presence, a shorter list of available subjects, and a start time that drifts with the traffic. Presence is a real benefit for a child who needs supervision as much as teaching. For a final-year Diploma student the drift is the problem, because a session beginning twenty minutes late and ending on time has lost a third of itself and broken the weekly homework cycle.

faqs.question: How does tutoring compare with school fees in a Fujairah household?
faqs.answer: Fees dominate in almost every case, which is why tutoring is the line families examine and fees the line they absorb. For scale, Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, and its authority confirmed in May 2026 that fees would not rise for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Fujairah sits under federal Ministry of Education supervision, so that freeze does not apply, but the climate it reflects does.

faqs.question: What does the UAE private tutoring permit cost a tutor?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Because it is free and fast, there is no good reason for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one. Tutoring without it brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though the ministry published no schedule so no figure is quoted.

faqs.question: Can I pay less by sharing a tutor with another Merashid family?
faqs.answer: The cost per student falls and the attention each child receives falls with it, which is the trade. Group pricing is genuinely lower per head and works where two students are at the same level in the same subject with similar gaps, which is rarer than it sounds. It works poorly when one student needs content taught and the other needs technique fixed. In Fujairah the binding problem is usually timing: aligning two school runs to one slot is harder than finding the saving.

faqs.question: What should make me stop paying and change something?
faqs.answer: Three items on the risk list unchanged after two months, with marked work to show it. That is a concrete signal rather than a feeling, which is why the diagnostic and the written list matter from the start. The change is not always the tutor: it can be the subject being prioritised, the frequency, or the format. What should not happen is continuing an arrangement nobody has examined since October because the monthly figure has become a habit.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-merashid.closingHeading: Set the budget, take the trial, then ask the five questions
fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-merashid.closingBody: For a Merashid family the order matters more than the provider. Decide the annual tutoring line first. Send the subject, the level and how near the deadline is. Take the free trial lesson and judge the explanation rather than the enthusiasm. Then ask whether the figure includes VAT, whether it is per hour or per session, what happens if you stop after a month, whether marking time is included, and what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable — all in writing. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to a Merashid address, and every rate above belongs to the provider that published it.

intro.heading: The syllabus is the thing, not the postcode
paragraphs: Sakamkam sits inland from the Fujairah coast, closer to the Hajar mountain edge than the city-centre schools, and the afternoon drive back from those schools is longer than it looks on a map. That has one effect on tutoring and it is about timing rather than geography: a session booked for 17:00 that depends on somebody else's journey tends to become 17:20, then 17:30, and a homework cycle built on weekly sessions quietly stops working. A fixed online slot does not drift.

The bigger reason this page is written about the syllabus rather than about Sakamkam is supply. Fujairah's private-school sector is small, which means the number of adults within driving distance who have taught Higher Level Chemistry or Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches recently is small and in some subjects is zero. A family paying for proximity in that situation is paying more for a shorter list. IB Gram teaches Sakamkam students one-to-one over live video instead, on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and the same statement appears on every country page this site publishes.

So the useful content for a Sakamkam parent is not a description of the neighbourhood. It is the mechanics of how a Diploma grade is built, because once you can see where the marks are, you can tell within one trial lesson whether somebody knows the subject or merely knows about it. A Diploma subject grade comes from a small number of components with published weightings, assessed against published criteria, written in a command-term vocabulary that is itself examinable, inside word and page limits that are hard caps.

Those four things are what the sections below cover. There is a Higher against Standard comparison component by component, the scientific investigation criteria with their mark allocations, the two mathematics courses paper by paper, the command terms that decide more marks than content does, and the core — Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS — with every limit set out in a table. Nothing here is unique to Sakamkam, and that is the point: the syllabus is identical in Sakamkam, in Dubai and in Geneva, and the only variable is who is teaching it.

One honest caveat on dates. The IB's own session and results dates could not be verified from the organisation's own site for this project, so no IB exam or results date appears anywhere on this page. Diploma students in the UAE sit the May session; confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator rather than with any tutoring site, including this one. The same caution applies to the weightings and criteria quoted below: they were read from the current subject guides, but guides are revised, and your child's coordinator holds the version that governs their cohort. Treat the numbers here as a map of where the marks sit rather than as the authority for them, and ask the school to confirm anything you intend to plan around.
