fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to a Sakamkam family, and the assessment changes completely between them. A tutor who treats the Middle Years Programme like a junior Diploma will teach the wrong things.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examinations, ending in an Exhibition in the final year. Assessment is teacher-led and continuous, which means there is no paper to practise and no mark scheme to work from. Tutoring at this stage is about reading fluency, number confidence and written expression rather than about the programme itself.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah has limited local Primary Years provision, so most Sakamkam families on an IB pathway start later, often entering the Middle Years Programme or the Diploma from a British or Indian primary route. A tutor's job at that transition is vocabulary and written explanation, because inquiry-based assessment rewards a student who can justify an answer in prose.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Mathematics uses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The Personal Project in the final year is marked out of 24 across planning, applying skills and reflecting.
programmes.countryNote: The criterion structure is the single most useful thing a Sakamkam parent can learn, because a student losing marks on criterion C in mathematics has a communication problem rather than a mathematics problem, and the remedy is different. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind the last reported grade rather than the grade alone.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum and up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, generally twenty to thirty per cent.
programmes.countryNote: Local Diploma provision in Fujairah is limited, so Sakamkam students on this route often board, commute or move emirate. An online slot survives all three without the engagement restarting, which matters because the Internal Assessment deadlines a school sets internally are earlier than most families expect and do not pause for a move.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with the component weightings that decide where tutoring hours should go. Check the level with your child's coordinator first; a Higher Level plan applied to a Standard Level student wastes sessions on content that is not examinable.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level: Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 40% each, Exploration at 20%. Higher Level: Papers 1 and 2 at 30% each, Paper 3 at 20%, Exploration at 20%. Paper 3 is the extended-response problem paper and the least practised component in the whole course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Identical weighting structure, with modelling and statistics replacing the heavier pure content. Calculator technique is examinable in its own right, and marks go to students who show the method the scheme rewards rather than only the answer the screen produced.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36% including a data-analysis section, Paper 2 at 44%, Internal Assessment at 20%. Mechanics and fields questions lose marks on sign conventions and on diagrams drawn without labelled forces, both of which are correctable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same component split as Physics. Energetics and organic mechanisms account for most Higher Level losses, and the data-analysis section rewards practice on unfamiliar graphs rather than recall of familiar ones.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The heaviest content load in the science group, and the subject where revision most often becomes rereading. Command terms do the work: a question asking students to explain is not answered by a description, and that single distinction recovers more marks than extra content.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level: Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 40%, portfolio at 30%. Higher Level: Papers at 20, 30 and 30 with the portfolio at 20%. The portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each, built on real published articles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Standard Level: Paper 1 at 35%, Paper 2 at 35%, Individual Oral at 30%. Higher Level adds the HL Essay at 20%. The Individual Oral requires a global issue traced through two texts, and preparing it is a distinct skill from essay writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for the Higher Level paper. Ratio and break-even calculations are the most predictable marks available; the recurring failure is applying a sound concept to a business the stimulus does not actually describe.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a solution-development Internal Assessment where product and documentation are assessed together. Strong programmers routinely lose marks on documentation, because the criteria reward evidence of a design process rather than working code alone.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that students sometimes choose as a lighter option and then find demanding, because it requires both scientific data handling and evaluative writing about human systems. The Internal Assessment is a genuine piece of fieldwork or secondary-data analysis, not a write-up.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Sakamkam actually does, and where the lesson happens
paragraphs: Through IB Gram, an IB home tutor for a Sakamkam student means a named subject specialist teaching one-to-one over live video at a fixed time each week on Gulf Standard Time. It does not mean anybody arriving at the door. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and that is the stated position across every country page on this site.

The in-home market in the UAE is real and priced accordingly: published rates for a travelling one-to-one tutor run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. In Dubai the gap buys convenience. Inland from the Fujairah coast it buys a shorter list of subjects, because the set of people who will drive to Sakamkam on a weekday evening and who have also taught Higher Level Chemistry is very close to empty.

What a specialist does in those sessions is narrower than parents often expect, and the narrowness is the value. They work on one subject at one level. They work from past papers and the published assessment criteria rather than from a textbook alone. They mark what the student produces and attribute each lost mark to a cause. And they know the limits — 4,000 words on the Extended Essay, 3,000 on the sciences investigation, 800 per Economics commentary — because those are hard caps and a draft over the line loses marks for a reason unrelated to its quality.

The rest of this page is the mechanics of that: weightings, criteria, command terms and limits. If you read nothing else, read the command-terms section. It is the cheapest grade movement available in the Diploma and almost nobody teaches it explicitly.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, component by component
paragraphs: Families talk about Higher Level as though it were the same course with more of it. It is not. The content is wider, but the structural difference that costs marks is the extra component and the way weightings redistribute around it. In the sciences the weightings are the same at both levels — Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, the Internal Assessment at 20% — but the Higher Level papers examine additional material and allow less time per mark in practice.

In mathematics the structure changes outright. Standard Level is two papers at 40% each plus the Exploration at 20%. Higher Level is three papers, at 30%, 30% and 20%, with the Exploration still at 20%. That third paper is the extended-response problem paper, and it is consistently the least practised component in the Diploma, partly because it does not resemble the others and partly because schools reach it last. A Higher Level mathematics student who has never sat a timed Paper 3 is carrying an avoidable risk into the exam room.

In Economics the redistribution runs the other way: the portfolio drops from 30% at Standard Level to 20% at Higher, and a third paper appears at 30%. In English A: Language and Literature the HL Essay appears at 20% and the Individual Oral drops in weight. The general rule is that Higher Level adds a component and dilutes the others, so a student who is strong on internal assessment and weak on papers is relatively worse off at Higher Level than the content difference alone suggests.

What this means for a tutoring plan is specific. Find out which component is carrying the lowest marks, work out what percentage of the final grade it represents, and spend the hours there. A student losing marks evenly across Paper 2 at 44% needs different work from one losing marks on an Internal Assessment worth 20%, and the second is usually the faster fix because the criteria are published and the work is not timed.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: criteria, cap and where the marks actually go
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment in the Diploma sciences is worth twenty per cent of the grade, is capped at 3,000 words, and is marked against four named criteria. Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks, for twenty-four in total. Those four names are the most useful thing a parent can know, because a student who has been told their investigation is weak has almost always been told so about one criterion rather than all four, and the remedies are completely different.

A weak research design is a planning failure: an unclear research question, a variable not properly controlled, insufficient data planned. It is the only one of the four that cannot be repaired after the data is collected, which is why the planning conversation has to happen before the practical work and not after. A weak data analysis is usually about uncertainty and processing rather than about arithmetic. A weak conclusion typically states a result without linking it back to the scientific context. A weak evaluation lists limitations without saying how any of them would be addressed.

The 3,000-word cap is a hard limit and students treat it as a target, which is a mistake. Marks are awarded for what satisfies the criteria, not for length, and a tightly written investigation of 2,200 words routinely outscores a padded 3,000-word one because the padding dilutes the parts being marked. Tables, figures and calculations are not the problem; discursive background reading is where the words go.

A tutor's role here has a boundary that should be stated before the work starts. The investigation is the student's own from the research question onwards. A tutor explains each criterion in the guide's own wording, reads a draft the student has written, says which criterion it is missing and why, and teaches the technique needed to fix it. A tutor does not write the investigation, does not draft the evaluation, and does not edit a piece to completion so that the sentences become the tutor's.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks in the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject guide publishes a list of command terms with definitions, and every paper is written using them deliberately. State, outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss, justify and compare are not interchangeable synonyms chosen for variety. They specify what the answer has to do, and the mark scheme is built around that specification. A student who answers an explain question with a description has written something true and scored a fraction of the marks available.

This is the single most common diagnosable fault in marked Diploma scripts and it is almost never taught explicitly, because schools are busy covering content. It is also the fastest thing to fix. An hour spent sorting past-paper questions by command term, writing the first sentence of each answer, and comparing those sentences to the mark scheme moves more marks than an hour of new content at almost any point in the two years.

The pattern repeats per subject in recognisable ways. In the sciences, explain requires a mechanism and describe does not. In Economics, evaluate requires a judgement supported by the diagram, and a balanced list of advantages and disadvantages with no judgement scores in the lower band. In English, analyse requires the effect of a technique on a reader rather than its identification. In History, the source questions reward provenance over content summary. None of this is difficult. It just has to be noticed.

The practical test for a tutor is to ask them, in a trial lesson, what the difference is between describe and explain in your child's subject, and what it is worth. A specialist answers with an example from a paper. A generalist answers in the abstract. That one question is more diagnostic than any credential, and it takes thirty seconds.

sections.heading: The core from Sakamkam: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS
paragraphs: The Diploma core is where the most Sakamkam enquiries arrive, and it is the part schools in a small market have the least capacity to supervise closely. The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece with a supervisor appointed by the school. Theory of Knowledge is examined through an essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title and an exhibition with a commentary of up to 950 words. CAS is not graded but must be completed, and an incomplete CAS portfolio prevents the award of the diploma regardless of points.

Together the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute up to three bonus points through a published matrix, which sounds small until you notice that three points is often the gap between an offer and a near miss. More importantly, the core is where deadlines bite. A school sets internal submission dates well before any external one, and those internal dates are what a tutoring plan has to work around. Ask the coordinator for the full internal calendar at the start of the first Diploma year, not in the spring of the second.

The failure mode is consistent. A student chooses an Extended Essay topic they find interesting rather than one that can be researched within the available material, and discovers the problem at the first draft. A Theory of Knowledge essay restates the prescribed title in different words rather than arguing a position about knowledge. A CAS portfolio accumulates activities without the reflections that evidence them. None of these is a subject-knowledge problem, which is why a subject tutor is often the wrong help and a process coach is the right one.

What support legitimately looks like here is narrow. Explaining the criteria. Reading a draft and naming which criterion it misses. Teaching how to turn a broad question into a researchable one. Checking the limits. The work is the student's own, and a tutor who offers to produce the essay is offering the student a malpractice finding rather than a grade.

sections.heading: Why Sakamkam has no local Higher Level specialist in some subjects
paragraphs: This is arithmetic rather than a criticism of Fujairah schools. The emirate's private-school sector is small, local Diploma provision is limited, and a small sector employs few teachers per subject. For Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Computer Science or Visual Arts, the number of people living within a reasonable drive of Sakamkam who have taught that course recently may be one or none. Paying an in-home premium does not change that number.

The same arithmetic applies in Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain, and it explains something about the pages that rank for searches like this one. None of them mentions any of the three emirates. They are written for Dubai and Abu Dhabi and reach the rest of the country by substituting a place name, which means a Sakamkam family reading them is looking at a supply picture that does not exist on this side of the mountains.

The practical response is to change what you are shortlisting for. Stop looking for proximity and start asking about coverage: can this subject at this level actually be staffed, how soon, and what happens if it cannot. A common Standard Level subject staffs quickly. A Higher Level science staffs reasonably. A minority Higher Level subject in one specific evening slot sometimes cannot be staffed at all, and you should be told that before paying rather than discovering it in week three.

The second consequence is scheduling, which matters more in Sakamkam than on the coast. The afternoon drive back from the city-centre schools is longer, so a travelling tutor's arrival time compresses the session or pushes it late. An online slot at 17:30 is an online slot at 17:30 every week, and the weekly homework cycle only works if the sessions land where they are supposed to.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, materials and what a tutor should refuse
paragraphs: Assessed work in the Diploma must be the student's own, and the consequence of breaching that lands on the student. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessment work at a fixed price. That is not a service with a quality question attached; it is a malpractice trigger under the board's own rules, and the candidate carries the finding.

The line is drawn by who produced the sentences. A tutor may teach the content, explain criteria in the guide's published wording, model how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name the criterion it misses, and teach the student to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become theirs. Asking a prospective tutor what they would do if your child requested one written paragraph is a fast and revealing test.

There is a second rule about materials that parents rarely hear. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the board. A provider offering them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct practice is to reference them and link to the official source so that the parent reads the real document. Everything on this page about weightings and limits should be confirmed against the current subject guide through your child's coordinator.

Finally, a statement about this site's own position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge or the Sharjah Private Education Authority. It holds no such relationship and claims none, it runs no UAE premises, and it should never be described in those terms.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the component that is failing
process.description: Not just the subject. Higher or Standard Level, and which component is carrying the lowest marks: a paper, the Internal Assessment, or the core. Those three facts decide the match and the plan, and together they take one message to establish rather than two sessions to discover.

process.title: Get the coordinator's internal deadline calendar
process.description: Schools set internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines well ahead of any external date, and those are the dates a plan has to respect. Ask for the whole calendar at the start of the first Diploma year. The commonest cause of a crisis in the second year is a deadline nobody wrote down.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a specification test
process.description: Ask the tutor what the difference is between describe and explain in your child's subject, and what it is worth. A specialist answers with an example from a paper in thirty seconds. Your child's view on whether they could follow the explanation is the other half of the signal.

process.title: Diagnostic in the first fortnight
process.description: A timed past paper or a marked draft, returned with every lost mark attributed to a cause: content, recall under pressure, misread question, misread command term, method shown poorly, or time. Ask for it in writing. It is the document the whole plan should be built from.

process.title: Fixed slot, with Ramadan planned rather than improvised
process.description: Sessions run at the same time each week on Gulf Standard Time, after the Sakamkam school run. During Ramadan the slot usually moves later, often post-Iftar, agreed a week ahead so the work set between sessions still gets marked rather than quietly dropped.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the level, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry and Standard Level Chemistry are different papers with different time pressure per mark, and a plan written for one wastes sessions on the other. Matching to subject and level is a small distinction that decides whether the hours convert into marks at all.

whyPoints.title: Weightings decide where the hours go
whyPoints.description: A component worth 44% and a component worth 20% deserve different amounts of attention, and the untimed criteria-marked ones are usually the faster fix. Reading the weighting table before booking is the cheapest planning anyone can do, which is why it is published here in full.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: The most common diagnosable fault in marked Diploma scripts is answering the wrong command. Schools rarely teach it because they are covering content. An hour sorting past questions by command term moves more marks than an hour of new content at almost any stage.

whyPoints.title: Limits checked against the guide, not from memory
whyPoints.description: 4,000 words on the Extended Essay, 1,600 on the Theory of Knowledge essay, 950 on the exhibition commentary, 3,000 on the sciences investigation, 800 per Economics commentary. A draft over a cap loses marks for a reason unrelated to its quality, which is entirely avoidable.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops limiting the shortlist
whyPoints.description: Sakamkam's local pool of Higher Level specialists is small and in some subjects empty, and an in-home premium does not create one. Online one-to-one delivery replaces who lives nearby with who has taught the course, which is the only change that alters the outcome.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated before the work starts
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria, feedback on the student's own draft. Not writing, not completing, not supplying, and no reproduction of the board's papers or mark schemes as downloads. A page in this search result sells finished Internal Assessments, and the candidate carries that risk.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor come to our home in Sakamkam?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers lessons to Sakamkam students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. An in-home market does exist here and published rates for it run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. The question worth asking before paying that is whether a travelling tutor inland from the Fujairah coast has actually taught your child's subject at the level they are sitting, because in several Higher Level subjects nobody locally has.

faqs.question: What is the Internal Assessment worth in an IB science, and how long can it be?
faqs.answer: It is worth twenty per cent of the subject grade and is capped at 3,000 words. It is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks. The cap is a limit rather than a target, and a tightly written investigation of around 2,200 words often outscores a padded one at the cap because padding dilutes what is being marked. Confirm the current figures with your child's coordinator against the live subject guide.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level Mathematics have a third paper?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended-response problem paper, worth twenty per cent, and it exists to examine sustained mathematical reasoning that the shorter papers cannot reach. It does not resemble Papers 1 and 2, schools usually reach it last, and it is consequently the least practised component in the Diploma. A Higher Level mathematics student who has never sat it under timed conditions is carrying avoidable risk. It is worth drilling separately and early rather than in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: My child's science investigation came back marked down on research design. Can that be repaired?
faqs.answer: Research design is the one criterion that cannot be fixed after the data has been collected, because it is about the question, the controlled variables and whether enough data was planned. If the practical work is already done, the honest route is to maximise the other three criteria — data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — which together carry eighteen of the twenty-four marks. If the work has not been done yet, the planning conversation is the single highest-value session available.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Sakamkam students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain, evaluate and analyse, consistently. Explain requires a mechanism and a description does not, so an answer that is entirely true can score a fraction of the available marks. Evaluate requires a judgement supported by evidence rather than a balanced list with no conclusion. Analyse requires the effect of something rather than its identification. Sorting past-paper questions by command term and writing only the first sentence of each answer is a cheap exercise that moves marks quickly.

faqs.question: How many points does the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination add?
faqs.answer: Up to three bonus points, awarded through a published matrix that combines the grades for both components. Three points sounds minor until it is the gap between meeting an offer and missing it. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 and the exhibition commentary at 950. CAS carries no points at all but must be completed, and an incomplete portfolio prevents the diploma being awarded regardless of the subject scores.

faqs.question: Does local Diploma provision exist in Fujairah for a Sakamkam family?
faqs.answer: It is limited, which is why Sakamkam students on this route often board, commute to Sharjah or Dubai, or move emirate. The practical consequence for tutoring is that an online slot survives all three without the engagement having to restart, and that matters because internally set Internal Assessment deadlines do not pause for a school move. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level authority, so school-level enquiries go there.

faqs.question: Is a subject tutor the right help for the Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The failure in a Theory of Knowledge essay is rarely a knowledge gap; it is restating the prescribed title in different words instead of arguing a position about how knowledge is produced and justified. That is a process and argument problem, so process coaching fits better than subject teaching. The support is explaining the criteria, reading what the student has written, and naming where the argument is absent. The essay itself has to be the student's own work.

faqs.question: When should a Sakamkam student start Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: The cheapest point is the first Diploma year, running one session a week slightly ahead of the school's scheme of work so each topic is met twice. The second year is where tutoring becomes repair work under time pressure, and repair costs more per mark gained. If you are already in the second year, start with a diagnostic rather than a lesson: a timed paper marked against the published scheme, with each lost mark attributed to a cause.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two Higher Level subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Rarely well. Mathematics and Physics is a realistic pairing because the techniques overlap. Chemistry and Biology at Higher Level is not, and a language paired with a science almost never is. The attraction is scheduling convenience and the cost is depth in the weaker subject. Two specialists on two evenings works better, with one of them asked to keep sight of the overall deadline calendar so no core deadline is tracked twice or not at all.

faqs.question: Why are no IB exam dates printed on this page?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project, and an unverified date that a parent acts on is worse than no date. Diploma students in the UAE sit the May session. Cambridge and Pearson dates elsewhere on this site are sourced from those boards' own published guidance and are used with their framing. For anything IB-specific, ask your child's coordinator and work from the school's own calendar.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma tutor charge around Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and travelling in-home tutors at AED 180 to 500. Monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run around AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market rates with their sources named, not IB Gram prices; ours follows the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How is the Middle Years Programme assessed differently from the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The Middle Years Programme uses four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries, rather than terminal papers with percentage weightings. In mathematics the criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. That matters because a student weak on the communication criterion has a writing problem, not a mathematics problem, and the remedy differs completely.

faqs.question: What should I ask for after the first month of sessions?
faqs.answer: The updated topic risk list from the diagnostic, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged, and the marked work it is based on. If an item has not moved in three weeks, that is the conversation to have rather than waiting for a report. Progress in the Diploma is visible in marks on marked scripts and in criteria met on a draft. Anything reported as confidence or engagement alone is not yet evidence of a grade moving.

fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.closingHeading: Find the failing component, then book one trial lesson
fujairah/ib-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.closingBody: The useful first step for a Sakamkam family is not choosing a tutor but identifying the component. Get the subject, the level, and which part is carrying the lowest marks: a named paper, the Internal Assessment, or the core. Ask your child's coordinator for the internal deadline calendar at the same time. Then take a free trial lesson and ask the tutor what separates describe from explain in that subject and what it is worth. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, after the school day. Nobody is sent to a Sakamkam address, and every figure here is a published market rate with its source named.

intro.heading: Two boards, four years, and which term each problem belongs to
paragraphs: The households that search for this phrase in Fujairah are rarely looking for one tutor for one problem. They are managing a sequence. A Year 11 student is three terms from an IGCSE series while an older sibling is halfway through the Diploma, or a single student is about to cross from one board to the other and the family has worked out that nobody has explained what that crossing involves. The question underneath the search is not which tutor is nearest. It is which of the next eight terms each worry actually belongs to.

That sequence is unusually visible on the east coast. Fujairah's private-school set is small, and families here frequently split their children across boards or across emirates for sixth form, which means one household can be working to two sets of term dates, two assessment calendars and two sets of academic conventions at the same time. A parent who has only ever dealt with IGCSE meets the Diploma core in October of Year 12 and discovers that an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course and a service commitment have all started without anybody sending a letter about it.

Before the map, the honest answer to the home-tutoring part of the search. Visiting tuition on this coast is real and it is priced for the drive: published market bands put visiting one-to-one in the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a two-child household the arithmetic compounds, because two visiting tutors means two sets of travel, two availability windows and usually two different evenings committed. The first table on this page works that through.

IB Gram delivers to UAE families one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so each child's hour sits in a Fujairah evening. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. For a two-board household that limitation turns out to be less costly than it sounds, because the thing such a household most needs is two correctly matched specialists on one evening rather than two people who happen to be available in the same emirate.

The rest of the page is the sequence. The four-year map from Year 10 to Diploma results, with what each window decides. The IGCSE-to-Diploma gap set out subject by subject rather than as a general warning about rigour. What IGCSE attainment actually suggests about Higher Level, with the check worth running before the choice is made. The Diploma core and its internal deadlines. The handover summer, which almost nobody uses. The scheduling and cost of running two children at once. And the honesty boundaries, which differ between the two boards and matter more under the IB.

fujairah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four structures, in the order a Fujairah family meets them. Each has its own assessment logic, and most of the confusion in a two-board household comes from applying one structure's assumptions to another's deadlines.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's programme for the years before the Diploma, assessed against published criteria rather than by terminal written papers, and concluding with a Personal Project in the final year. Students coming out of it arrive at the Diploma already fluent in criterion language and in extended independent work, and slightly less practised at sitting a long written paper to time than an IGCSE student is.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools on the east coast run the MYP, so a Fujairah family in this programme has usually chosen a school in another emirate or is weighing that choice. The practical consequence is a different term calendar from their neighbours and a different kind of preparation gap on entering the Diploma, which is a reason to plan the handover summer deliberately.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years ending in written papers, usually across eight to ten subjects, on either a Cambridge or a Pearson Edexcel specification with tiering in many subjects. It produces students who are good at timed written papers and at closed questions, and who have rarely been asked to design their own line of enquiry or to sustain an argument across several thousand words.
programmes.countryNote: The dominant route in Fujairah's private schools, which is why most two-board households here are IGCSE below and Diploma above rather than the other way round. Cohorts are small, so a student's IGCSE subject list is sometimes shaped by what the school could staff, and that shaping carries forward into which Diploma subjects are realistic.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects studied simultaneously, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, scored on a 45-point scale, with internal assessment in every subject alongside the written examinations. The load is not simply harder than three A Levels; it is wider, and it is continuous, because internal assessment deadlines sit inside the two years rather than at the end of them.
programmes.countryNote: Some east-coast students travel or move for the Diploma, since the programme is concentrated in the larger emirates. That means term dates, internal deadlines and the school's own assessment calendar need reading from the specific school, and the IB coordinator rather than any website is the authority on every date that matters to a candidate.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: Three requirements running alongside the six subjects. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a 4,000-word upper limit. Theory of Knowledge is a taught course assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. Creativity, activity, service runs across both years as a commitment rather than an examination. Together the essay and TOK contribute up to three points to the total.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where two-board households are most often caught out, because nothing in an IGCSE year resembles it and its deadlines are set by the school rather than published nationally. Ask the IB coordinator in the first month of Year 12 for the school's own internal deadline calendar, then build the family's year around that document rather than around the examination season.

fujairah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects, with the note on each describing what a student arriving from IGCSE typically has not yet met. This is a transition list rather than a difficulty list: most of these gaps are three or four weeks of specific work, not a judgement about the student.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route for students heading towards engineering, physics, mathematics or economics at competitive universities. An IGCSE Extended student arrives with solid technique and no experience of proof, of the formal treatment of functions, or of calculus beyond whatever Additional Mathematics covered. Three to four weeks of bridging work on algebraic fluency and notation prevents most of the early damage.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving rather than proof. It is not an easier course, it is a different one, and the commonest error is choosing it to avoid difficulty rather than because it matches the degree intention. Check the stated mathematics requirement of the specific universities a student is considering before the choice is locked in.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The step from IGCSE chemistry is mostly quantitative. Equilibrium, energetics and the depth of organic mechanism are the three places where an IGCSE-strong student suddenly finds the ground moving, and they arrive early in the first year. A student who found moles calculations uncomfortable at IGCSE should close that gap during the handover summer rather than in October.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mathematical demand rises faster here than in any other science. An IGCSE physics student who was fine on substitution meets algebraic rearrangement, vectors and graphical analysis as routine expectations. The internal assessment also arrives sooner than most students expect, and designing an investigation is a skill nothing in IGCSE physics required.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than conceptual difficulty, as at IGCSE, but with a far greater emphasis on data analysis and on explaining mechanism in precise language. Students who revised biology by rereading at IGCSE plateau quickly here. The fix is retrieval practice and marking long answers against criteria, which is work done between sessions rather than inside them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline carries forward from IGCSE and is immediately insufficient, because Diploma answers require evaluation and real-world application sustained across several paragraphs. The internal assessment commentaries are the component families underestimate, since they are written to a strict word allowance against published criteria during term time.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Familiar territory for an IGCSE Business Studies student in content and unfamiliar in register. The Diploma rewards justified recommendation and the use of a given tool or framework rather than general commentary, and the written assignment at Higher Level is a different kind of task from anything in the IGCSE papers.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the guided analysis both ask for something IGCSE rarely does: a sustained reading of an unseen extract linked to a global issue, delivered under conditions. A student with a strong First Language English grade still needs teaching in how the Diploma's assessment reads a response, which is a technique gap rather than a reading one.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The theory broadens sharply beyond IGCSE 0478, into system fundamentals, networks and, at Higher Level, abstract data structures. The internal assessment is a developed solution with documentation, which demands project discipline over months rather than coding ability in an afternoon.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Two different courses for two different starting points, and the choice is consequential rather than administrative. An IGCSE Arabic grade does not map cleanly onto either, so the placement conversation belongs with the school before the Diploma starts, not in the first assessment week of Year 12.

fujairah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of a two-board household, with the note on each describing what it leaves a student ready and not ready for at Diploma level. These are the subjects whose Year 11 outcome shapes the following four terms most directly.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The single most consequential IGCSE result for a Diploma plan, because it gates both mathematics routes and affects physics, chemistry and economics. An Extended or Higher entry with secure algebra opens Analysis and Approaches; a comfortable but mechanical pass usually points to Applications and Interpretation.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
igcseSubjects.description: The best available preparation for Analysis and Approaches, because it introduces calculus, vectors and matrices a year early. Where a school offers it to a small set, it is worth taking for a student with secure algebra and worth declining for one still rebuilding it, since it otherwise becomes remedial work under another name.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Leaves a student fluent in equations and observation language and short of quantitative confidence. The specific gap that matters is moles work beyond the IGCSE treatment, which is exactly what Diploma energetics and equilibrium assume from week one.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Produces students comfortable with substitution into a formula and unpractised at rearranging one. Electricity and electromagnetism are where IGCSE marks are lost and also where Diploma physics builds fastest, so a weakness here is worth closing before the Diploma rather than during it.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Content-heavy and well matched in style to Diploma biology, which makes it the smoothest of the three science transitions. The habit worth building in Year 11 is answering long questions against published criteria rather than writing everything remembered, because that habit transfers directly.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Builds the close-reading and directed-writing skills English A assumes, without ever asking for a sustained argument across several thousand words. That second skill is what the Extended Essay needs, which is why strong English students still find the essay harder than they expected.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram technique and definitions transfer intact; evaluation does not, because IGCSE rarely demands it at length. A student who scored well through accuracy alone should expect the first Diploma assessment to feel like a different subject, and should plan for that rather than be surprised by it.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Covers programming and the written-paper conventions that Diploma theory extends. The gap is project discipline: the Diploma internal assessment is a solution developed and documented over months, which nothing in the IGCSE course rehearses.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
igcseSubjects.description: The route many east-coast students sit, and the one that needs the most careful Diploma conversation, since the trimmed content in each discipline can leave visible gaps at Higher Level. Worth auditing subject by subject in the handover summer rather than assuming the award covers the ground.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508) and Arabic Foreign Language (Cambridge 0544)
igcseSubjects.description: Neither maps automatically onto Arabic A or Arabic B at Diploma level, and the reading demand differs sharply between the two IGCSE routes themselves. Confirm the Diploma placement with the school rather than inferring it from the IGCSE grade.

fujairah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: What a two-board household looks like differs across the emirate, mostly because of where the Diploma is actually available. The notes below describe that picture community by community, since it decides whether a family is managing two boards in one house or two boards in two emirates.

regions.name: Fujairah city
regions.note: Where the emirate's private-school places are concentrated, and therefore where most IGCSE study happens. Households here running a Diploma student as well have usually placed that child in another emirate or are weighing the move, which means two school calendars under one roof and two sets of internal deadlines to track.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Residential and feeding the city schools, so the IGCSE side is straightforward and the Diploma side is the logistical question. Where an older sibling boards or commutes for the Diploma, the family's weekly tuition rhythm has to work around two different term patterns rather than one.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Frequently two children at different stages in one household, which is the exact case this page is written for. Consecutive evening slots with separately matched tutors work better here than any attempt to share a tutor across an IGCSE set and a Diploma set, because the two jobs need different preparation.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Good access to the city and to the Sharjah road, so visiting quotes arrive from outside the emirate and carry travel inside them. For a two-child household those quotes compound, since two visiting tutors means two journeys, two availability windows and usually two committed evenings.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Quieter households with one shared study space, which is the practical constraint when two children need hours in the same week. Consecutive slots in one prepared room solve it; parallel sessions on separate devices in one house compete for both quiet and bandwidth.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The thinnest local provision in the emirate, and the community where a Diploma student almost certainly studies elsewhere. Families here are often running the handover summer remotely while a child is between schools, which is precisely the window this page argues should be used deliberately.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Highway villages with long school journeys, so a two-child plan has to be built around energy as much as around time. A shorter session each for two children usually works better than one full hour each, and the plan should say so rather than defaulting to the longer slot.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: At the pass, with some students attending school in another emirate and therefore on different term dates. For a two-board household this is the hardest calendar to manage, and the only workable approach is to write both schools' internal deadline dates into one family document in September.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The IGCSE side of most two-board households on this coast. Small cohorts, short subject lists, and a Year 11 subject set that was sometimes shaped by what the school could staff rather than by the student's eventual Diploma intention. Students we support attend schools in this group; none is a partner, client or sponsor of IB Gram.
schools: Our Own English High School, Fujairah

schoolClusters.note: Where east-coast students most often sit the Diploma, since the programme is concentrated in the larger emirates. Internal deadlines for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and each subject's internal assessment are set by the individual school, so the coordinator's own calendar is the document that matters.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: The nearer alternative for families not travelling as far as Dubai, and where some Masafi and Dibba students attend school outright. Different regulator, sometimes different term dates, and therefore a second calendar for a household already tracking one.

modes.description: Two hours back to back on one evening, each with a tutor matched to that child's own syllabus code and level. One quiet room is prepared once, one evening is committed, and the two written records arrive to the same parent and are reviewed at the same points. It is the arrangement most two-board households settle on after trying the alternatives.

sections.heading: What visiting tuition costs a two-board household
paragraphs: A single-child family comparing tutors compares hourly rates. A household with one child on IGCSE and another on the Diploma is comparing something more complicated, because almost nothing scales cleanly. Two visiting tutors mean two journeys, two availability windows and usually two separate evenings, and on the east coast each of those journeys is an hour and a half from Sharjah or close to two hours from Dubai. The rate is the smallest part of what that arrangement costs a family in a week.

Published market bands put visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, with Bestimate's Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reported up to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits, which only become comparable once both are divided down to a per-hour figure.

The compounding problem for a two-board household is the match rather than the money. A visiting tutor is chosen from whoever will make the drive, and the chance that the same person teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended well and Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level is small. What families end up with is one good match and one approximate one, usually without being told which is which. One tutor covering both children across two boards is the arrangement that looks most efficient on paper and delivers least, because the preparation for each is genuinely different work.

IB Gram's position, stated rather than implied: no home visits anywhere in the UAE, with tutors at the door a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this particular household shape that removes the hardest constraint, because two correctly matched specialists can teach consecutive hours on one evening in one prepared room, and the family commits one evening rather than two.

sections.heading: The four-year map, from Year 10 to Diploma results
paragraphs: Most of the anxiety in a two-board household comes from problems being worried about in the wrong term. A Diploma subject choice worried about in Year 10 is premature; the same choice worried about in September of Year 12 is late. An Extended Essay question worried about in the final term of Year 13 is a crisis that six earlier months would have prevented. Laying the four years out on one page does more for a family than any individual lesson, because it tells them what this term is actually for.

Two anchors hold the map together. The first is the IGCSE entry deadline, because it fixes the tier and therefore the realistic range of Diploma options. Cambridge publishes a final entry date well ahead of the papers for each series it runs in the UAE, and those series are June and November; the February sitting some families have read about is offered in India only, so the honest plan is June with November held as the resit route. The exact closing date for the series you want belongs on the centre's statement of entry rather than on a tutor's page, because it moves. Pearson runs its International GCSE series in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and publishes provisional timetables in advance.

The second anchor is the school's own internal deadline calendar for the Diploma, and it is the document families most often never see. Internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay milestones and Theory of Knowledge submission dates are set inside the school rather than published nationally, and they fall during term time alongside everything else. Ask the IB coordinator for that calendar in the first month of Year 12. Dates for IB examination sessions and results should be confirmed with the coordinator or on ibo.org rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one.

The window families underuse is the handover summer, between the last IGCSE paper and the first day of Diploma Year 1. Nothing is being assessed, the student is as free as they will be for three years, and the gap between what IGCSE finished with and what the Diploma assumes is at its most addressable. Six to eight sessions there, aimed at mathematics notation and the shape of a long argument, consistently buy more than the same number bought in a panic in the following February.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: One competitor page in this market has a single heading about the IGCSE-to-IB gap. Nobody has a structured version, which is strange, because the gap is not general. It is specific, it differs by subject, and almost all of it can be named in advance. A student does not find the Diploma hard because it is prestigious. They find a particular week hard because a particular assumption was never taught, and most of those assumptions are listed below.

The pattern across subjects is consistent. IGCSE finishes a student at the point where a technique has been practised on structured questions. The Diploma begins at the point where the technique is assumed and the thinking starts. In mathematics that means notation and proof. In chemistry it means quantitative work beyond the moles treatment IGCSE stopped at. In physics it means rearranging rather than substituting. In the essay subjects it means sustaining an argument well past the length any IGCSE paper required.

The second half of the gap is assessment style, and it catches strong students hardest. IGCSE rewards answering the question asked, accurately, inside a tight space. The Diploma rewards meeting published criteria, which is a different skill: a student has to know what the criterion is asking for and write visibly towards it. A student who scored highly at IGCSE through accuracy alone often takes a full term to understand why their first Diploma piece came back lower than they expected, and that term is avoidable.

The weeks column in the table below is the honest part and should be read as typical rather than promised. These are bridging jobs, not rescues, and they are considerably cheaper in the handover summer than in Diploma term time. A family that audits four subjects over that summer and closes two gaps has spent a fraction of what the same two gaps cost to close in February of Year 12, with the Extended Essay and three internal assessments competing for the same hours.

sections.heading: What IGCSE results actually suggest about Higher Level
paragraphs: Three Higher Level subjects and three Standard Level is the Diploma's shape, and choosing which three go where is the most consequential decision of the handover summer. Families reach for the IGCSE grade as the evidence, which is reasonable but incomplete, because the IGCSE grade bundles together several different things: how much content was known, how well it was written, how fast it was written, and how much tuition was holding it up. Higher Level is sensitive to the first and the last of those in particular.

The more useful evidence is a marked script rather than a grade. A student with a high mathematics grade built on relentless practice of structured questions is in a different position from one with the same grade who could handle an unfamiliar problem with no scaffold, and Higher Level mathematics distinguishes between those two in its first term. The same applies in the sciences: a grade achieved with weekly tuition throughout Year 11 is a grade plus a support structure, and Higher Level assumes the support structure is not needed.

The practical check is cheap and almost nobody runs it. Take one piece of genuinely unfamiliar work at the Diploma's level in the subject under consideration, have the student attempt it without help, and read what they do when they are stuck. It will not be finished and it does not need to be. What it shows is whether they can get started, whether they reach for a method, and whether an unscaffolded question provokes thinking or paralysis, and that is a far better predictor of Higher Level than a grade is.

Two further honest points. Degree intention should lead, not comfort: the mathematics route in particular should be chosen against the stated requirements of the universities a student is considering, and verified on those universities' own pages. And a decision taken in the handover summer is not irreversible, because levels can usually be changed in the first weeks of Diploma Year 1 by agreement with the school. Ask the coordinator what that window is at the start of term, so a correction is a conversation rather than an emergency.

sections.heading: The Diploma core and the deadlines set inside the school
paragraphs: Nothing in two IGCSE years prepares a family for the core. Alongside six subjects, a Diploma student carries an Extended Essay with a 4,000-word upper limit, a Theory of Knowledge course assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition, and a creativity, activity and service commitment running across both years. The essay and TOK together contribute up to three points to the 45-point total, which understates how much of the student's year they occupy.

The scheduling problem is that these deadlines are internal. The school sets them, they fall during term time, and they are not published anywhere a parent would stumble across. A household that only tracks the examination season discovers in March of Year 12 that an Extended Essay research question was due in November and a first full draft is expected before the summer. Getting the coordinator's own deadline calendar in the first month of Year 12 and writing it into one family document is the single most useful administrative act of the two years.

What tuition can usefully do here is narrower than families hope and more valuable than they expect. It can help a student frame a research question that is answerable in 4,000 words rather than a topic that is not. It can read the published criteria with them until they can say what each one is asking for. It can read a draft the student has produced and name which criterion is thin and why. It cannot and must not supply text, restructure the piece on the student's behalf, or edit it to a point where the words are no longer theirs.

That boundary matters more under the IB than anywhere else, because the consequence lands on the student. Assessed work has to be the student's own, and the IB's academic-honesty rules treat breaches as a malpractice matter affecting the whole diploma. One page competing for these searches sells finished internal assessments outright. A tutor's role is to teach, question, point at the criteria and give feedback, and a tutor who offers more than that is offering the student a risk dressed up as help.

sections.heading: The handover summer, which almost nobody uses
paragraphs: Between the last IGCSE paper and the first day of Diploma Year 1 sit six to eight weeks in which nothing is assessed, the student has more free attention than they will have again for three years, and the gap between what IGCSE finished with and what the Diploma assumes is at its most addressable. Most families use none of it, understandably, because the household has just survived an examination series and wants a holiday. A fortnight of that holiday, used well, changes the following October.

The order of work matters. Mathematics notation and algebraic fluency come first, because everything in the sciences and in economics rests on them and because they are the cheapest thing to fix with a clear head. Quantitative chemistry comes next for anybody taking the subject, since energetics and equilibrium arrive in the first term. Then one piece of extended writing, longer than any IGCSE answer, with feedback against criteria rather than against accuracy, so the student has met criterion-based assessment once before it counts.

The audit is as valuable as the teaching. Sitting down with the chosen Diploma subjects and listing, for each, what the course assumes on day one produces a short document that tells a family where the following year's risk actually sits. Sometimes it changes a level choice, which is far cheaper to change in August than in November. Sometimes it confirms that nothing needs doing, which is also worth knowing and costs one session to establish.

For east-coast families there is often a logistical layer on top, because a student moving to a Diploma school in another emirate is also changing cohort, timetable and sometimes accommodation. The academic bridging is the part that can be done from Fujairah over video while the rest is arranged, and doing it then rather than after term starts means arriving as a participant rather than as somebody catching up in a new place.

sections.heading: Running two children on two boards in one week
paragraphs: The practical questions a two-board household asks are rarely academic. Can both children be taught on the same evening. Is one tutor cheaper than two. Who reads the two written records. What happens when one child's internal deadline collides with the other's mock week. Those are scheduling and information questions, and getting them wrong is how a family ends up paying for four hours a week and getting the benefit of two.

On the tutor question, the honest answer is two. One tutor across an IGCSE Extended set and a Diploma Higher Level set is the arrangement that looks efficient and quietly serves whichever child is more demanding, because the preparation for each is different work and one of them will get less of it. Two separately matched tutors in consecutive hours on one evening costs the same number of hours, commits one evening rather than two, and gives each child somebody who knows their specification.

On information, the thing that makes a two-child plan manageable is a single shared view. Two written records in the same format, arriving to the same parent, reviewed at the same points in the term. That is what allows a parent to notice that one child's recurring error stopped appearing at week five while the other's did not, and to act on it rather than discovering it at the end of a term. Records in two different formats from two unconnected tutors are the commonest reason a two-child plan drifts.

On collisions, the only workable approach is to write both schools' calendars into one document in September: mock weeks, internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay milestones, and the IGCSE entry date. When a Diploma internal deadline lands in the same week as an IGCSE mock, something has to give, and deciding in advance which child's hour moves that week is a far better conversation than having it on the evening itself.
