sections.heading: Where the honesty line sits, and it differs by board
paragraphs: Both boards require assessed work to be the student's own, and the IB enforces it with the most consequence because the whole diploma is at stake rather than one grade. The line itself is the same in both systems: teaching is allowed, feedback is allowed, supplying content is not. What differs is the surface area. An IGCSE student has limited coursework; a Diploma student carries internal assessment in every subject plus an essay and a TOK submission, so the line comes up many more times.

The things a tutor may legitimately do are specific. Teach the skill the task requires. Work through a comparable example that is not the student's own task. Read the published criteria with the student until they can state what each one asks for. Read a draft the student has produced and name which criterion is thin and why. Ask the questions that make a student notice their argument does not follow. Teach referencing and have the student check their own.

The things nobody may do are equally specific: supply text for an assessed piece, restructure it on the student's behalf, correct it line by line until the voice has changed, or hand over a model close enough to the set task to be copied. The same applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards; the honest approach is to reference them and link to the board's own site rather than to redistribute them.

For a parent the test is what arrives after a session. Written notes, a marked set with the criterion named against each loss, and a short statement of what to practise next are evidence of teaching. A finished piece of assessed work in your child's subject that your child did not author is evidence of something else, and under IB rules it is the student who carries the consequence. That is why this page states the boundary rather than leaving it to be inferred.

process.title: Write both calendars into one document
process.description: In September, put the IGCSE entry date and mock weeks alongside the Diploma school's internal deadlines for internal assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Ask the IB coordinator for that calendar; it is not published anywhere a parent would find it. One document for the household is what makes a two-board year navigable.

process.title: Send each child's code and level separately
process.description: Subject, board, syllabus code, tier or level, and the series or session, for each child individually. A two-child enquiry that arrives as one description of two students takes three conversations to untangle. With the details split, each child is matched to somebody who teaches their specification rather than their subject.

process.title: Take a 45-minute diagnostic for each
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details required, and for a two-child household it is worth using it on whichever situation is less clear. Each diagnostic produces a written statement: code and level, which topics are secure, whether losses are content, technique or timing, and a realistic number of weeks.

process.title: Book consecutive slots on one evening
process.description: Two hours back to back in one prepared room, each with a separately matched tutor, on Gulf Standard Time after the bus and a meal. It commits one evening rather than two, which is the difference between a plan a household sustains for a term and one it abandons in week five.

process.title: Use the handover summer for the audit
process.description: Before Diploma Year 1 starts, list what each chosen subject assumes on day one and check the student against it. Mathematics notation first, quantitative chemistry next, then one piece of long-form writing marked against criteria. If a level choice needs changing, August is much cheaper than November.

whyPoints.title: Each child matched to their own specification
whyPoints.description: An IGCSE Extended set and a Diploma Higher Level set are different jobs requiring different preparation, so each child is matched separately to a syllabus code and level. One tutor spanning both looks efficient and quietly serves whichever child asks for more attention.

whyPoints.title: One evening, one room, two records
whyPoints.description: Consecutive hours in a single prepared room, with two written records in the same format arriving to the same parent and reviewed at the same points in the term. That shared view is what lets a parent notice one plan working while the other stalls, rather than finding out at the end of a term.

whyPoints.title: The transition mapped, not described
whyPoints.description: The IGCSE-to-Diploma gap is set out subject by subject with the assumption each course makes on day one and the typical bridging weeks attached. One competing page has a single heading on the subject; nobody has a structured version, and a family planning four years needs the structure rather than the warning.

whyPoints.title: The core's internal deadlines taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and internal assessment deadlines are set inside the school and fall during term time. Support blocks are planned against that calendar rather than against the examination season, which is the mistake that turns a manageable year into a March crisis.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, reads criteria and gives feedback on drafts the student has authored. Nobody here supplies text for an assessed piece or edits one until the voice changes. Under IB rules the consequence of crossing that line lands on the student, which is why it is written down rather than left to be assumed.

whyPoints.title: No dates or claims we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: IB session and results dates belong to the coordinator and to ibo.org, not to a tutoring page, so none are published here. No regulator or board approval is claimed, no UAE office exists, no grade is promised, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover IGCSE for my daughter and the IB Diploma for my son?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually the wrong arrangement even when it is possible. Teaching Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier and Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level are different preparation jobs, and one person doing both tends to serve whichever child is more demanding that week. Two separately matched tutors in consecutive hours on one evening costs the same number of hours, commits one evening rather than two, and gives each child somebody who knows their own specification rather than their subject in general.

faqs.question: What changes between IGCSE Year 11 and the first year of the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three things at once. The subjects assume techniques rather than teaching them, so notation, algebraic rearrangement and quantitative confidence are expected from week one. The assessment rewards meeting published criteria rather than answering accurately in a tight space, which is a different skill. And the core starts: an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and a service commitment all running alongside six subjects, with deadlines set inside the school during term time rather than at the end of the course.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grades suggest Higher Level rather than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The grade is weaker evidence than the script. A high grade built on relentless practice of structured questions is a different signal from the same grade achieved on unfamiliar problems with no scaffold, and Higher Level separates those two in its first term. A grade achieved with weekly tuition all year is a grade plus a support structure. The cheap check nobody runs is one unfamiliar Diploma-level question attempted unaided, read for what the student does when they are stuck rather than for whether they finish.

faqs.question: When should a Fujairah student start thinking about Diploma subject choices?
faqs.answer: Lightly in Year 10, when the IGCSE subject set is being fixed, because a subject not taken at IGCSE can narrow what is realistic later. Seriously in the handover summer, once actual results exist. Year 10 is for making sure nothing is being closed off, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. The handover summer is for the real decision, and it should be driven by degree intention checked against the universities' own stated requirements rather than by which option feels more comfortable.

faqs.question: How long is the gap between IGCSE results and the start of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Results generally arrive during the summer break, with Pearson's June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026 as a recent example, so the window between the last paper and the first Diploma day is roughly six to eight weeks depending on the series and the school. That window is the most underused period in the whole four years: nothing is assessed, attention is free, and the specific gaps the Diploma assumes are at their most addressable. Confirm your own school's term start before planning around it.

faqs.question: Does my child need Additional Mathematics before IB Maths Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is not required and it is the best available preparation. Cambridge 0606 introduces calculus, vectors and matrices a year early, which removes much of the first-term shock in Analysis and Approaches. The condition is secure algebra: for a student still rebuilding indices, surds and rearrangement, 0606 becomes remedial work on main-course content under a different name. Without it, three or four weeks of bridging work on notation and unscaffolded problems in the handover summer closes most of the same ground.

faqs.question: What does the Extended Essay timeline look like across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: It starts earlier than families expect and its milestones are set by the school rather than published nationally. Typically a subject and a supervisor are settled during the first Diploma year, a research question is agreed, and a substantial draft exists before the second year begins, with the final submission falling in the second year well ahead of the written papers. Ask the IB coordinator for the school's own milestone dates in the first month of Year 12 and build the household calendar around that document.

faqs.question: Is the Middle Years Programme better preparation for the Diploma than IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It is different preparation rather than better. MYP students arrive fluent in criterion-based assessment and in extended independent work, which is exactly where IGCSE students struggle first. IGCSE students arrive better practised at sitting a long written paper to time, which is where MYP students often need work. Each has a predictable gap, and knowing which one your child has is more useful than ranking the two programmes. Few east-coast schools run the MYP, so most Fujairah households face the IGCSE version of this.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes in Fujairah for either IB or IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, for either board; tutors arriving at a family's door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so the hour falls in a Fujairah evening. This page prices visiting tuition anyway, including the way its cost compounds for a two-child household, because a parent weighing the options deserves real figures for the arrangement we do not sell as well as the one we do.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a household running two boards realistically need?
faqs.answer: Usually two, one per child, and almost never four. A weekly hour with a marked set done between sessions moves a subject; two hours a week in the same subject without the set being done does not. The exception is a short period around a collision, such as a Diploma internal deadline landing in an IGCSE mock week, where one child may need an extra session and the other's hour moves. Decide in advance whose hour gives way, rather than on the evening.

faqs.question: What does the Theory of Knowledge course actually require from a student?
faqs.answer: It is a taught course rather than an add-on, assessed by an essay written on one of the IB's prescribed titles and by an exhibition built around objects and knowledge questions. Together with the Extended Essay it contributes up to three points to the 45-point total. What it demands from students is unfamiliar: holding a question open rather than answering it, and using examples as evidence rather than as illustration. Its deadlines, like the Extended Essay's, are set inside the school during term time.

faqs.question: Can a student move from the IB Diploma back to A Levels after the first year?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on the schools involved rather than on any general rule, so it is a conversation with both the current coordinator and the receiving school rather than something to plan from a web page. What is more often available and less often used is a change of level within the Diploma, from Higher to Standard, in the early weeks of Year 12. Ask the coordinator at the start of term what that window is, so a correction is a conversation rather than an emergency.

faqs.question: How does equivalency differ for an IB graduate and an IGCSE plus A Level student?
faqs.answer: The British route is the documented one. Reported Ministry requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one, because it has not been verified on the Ministry's own site. Check moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: What does the first term of Diploma Year 1 feel like for a former IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Wide rather than deep, and continuous rather than terminal. Six subjects run at once, each assuming techniques that IGCSE practised on structured questions, and the first pieces of assessed work come back marked against criteria the student has not yet learnt to read. Most students who found IGCSE comfortable have one bad month somewhere in that term, and the ones who recover fastest are the ones who did the notation and long-form writing work over the summer rather than the ones who were cleverest.

faqs.question: Should we start Diploma preparation during the summer after Year 11?
faqs.answer: A fortnight of it, yes, and it is the best-value tuition in the whole four years. Six to eight sessions aimed at mathematics notation, quantitative chemistry for anyone taking it, and one piece of long-form writing marked against criteria will remove most of the predictable first-term shock. The same work bought in February of Year 12 competes with three internal assessments and an Extended Essay for the same evenings. Keep the rest of the summer as a holiday; the household has just survived an examination series.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects do east-coast students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at both routes and Higher Level chemistry and physics, in roughly that order, followed by the Extended Essay as a process rather than a subject. The pattern reflects the transition rather than the subjects being unusually hard: all three assume quantitative fluency that IGCSE practised in a more structured form. For Fujairah families specifically, the second pattern is subjects with very small cohorts, where a student may be one of a handful and the school has no second set to join.

fujairah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Find out which term each worry belongs to
fujairah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: Most of what a two-board household worries about is real and misdated. A Diploma level choice belongs to the handover summer, not to Year 10. An Extended Essay question belongs to the first Diploma year, not to the last term. A tier decision belongs to the autumn of Year 11, before entries close. Put both schools' calendars in one document, audit the subject gaps before the Diploma starts, and match each child separately to their own syllabus code. One free 45-minute diagnostic per family, no card details, gives you a written view of where each child actually is before anybody asks you for money.

intro.heading: Four kinds of help, one search box
paragraphs: A parent on the east coast types IB IGCSE tuition near me and expects a short list of people living within ten minutes of the house. The results are a mixture instead: a tuition centre in Fujairah City running group classes, two or three freelance profiles carrying Sharjah mobile numbers, a Dubai agency that will quote for travel, and online platforms with no address at all. Every listing uses the same vocabulary about experienced teachers and proven methods. None of them explains what the practical difference is on a wet Tuesday in February.

That difference matters more here than it does in Dubai Marina. Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman with the Hajar mountains between it and the western conurbation, and the private-school set on this coast is small. A student sitting Chemistry at Higher Level, or Business Studies at IGCSE Extended, may be one of four in the teaching group. The person who knows that syllabus properly is usually not resident on this coast. Proximity and subject fit therefore pull in opposite directions, and a near-me search quietly resolves the conflict in favour of proximity.

This page refuses to do that. It prices the four options in dirhams using rates their own providers publish, sets out who is legally permitted to give private lessons in the UAE and how a parent verifies it, and does the drive-time arithmetic that decides whether a twice-weekly slot is still running at half term. It then separates the two different jobs hiding inside one search: supporting a child in the IB Middle Years Programme, and supporting a child two terms from an IGCSE paper.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Fujairah families live online, over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India - and no line on this site should be read as a promise that someone will knock on the door in Al Faseel. The reason is not cost. It is that an online match draws on a pool of subject specialists which a twenty-minute radius around Fujairah City cannot contain.

What follows is written for the decision, not for the brochure. If you read one table, read the second one: it is the only place in this search cluster where the four options sit side by side with their AED rates, their travel cost in minutes, the tutor pool each one draws on, and the kind of student each actually suits. Bring your child's school report and the syllabus codes from their option sheet, and the page will tell you which column you belong in. Everything after that is detail: the permit rules, the exam calendar and the questions worth asking before any money moves.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for almost every IB IGCSE tuition near me search placed from Fujairah. They sit at different ages, they are assessed in completely different ways, and a tutor who is strong in one is not automatically useful in another.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and converts those into a single 1-7 subject grade through published boundaries. There is no paper to past-paper your way through in MYP 1-3. Progress comes from understanding what a criterion rewards: criterion C in sciences wants processing and analysis of data, not a tidy write-up. Most Fujairah students meeting an MYP grade drop are losing marks in one criterion consistently.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah has few MYP cohorts, so a student can spend three years without ever being taught by a specialist in their weakest subject group. That is the single most common reason east-coast families start looking for outside help in MYP 4, a year before the Diploma choices land.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, two sets of rules. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended, caps the Core grade at C, and runs June and November series with six administrative timetable zones. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE offers May/June and November entries and uses Foundation and Higher tiers in maths. The syllabus code on the option sheet - 0580, 0620, 4MA1, 4CH1 - tells a tutor more than the subject name does.
programmes.countryNote: Most private schools on this coast run a British or Indian curriculum, so IGCSE entries are the bulk of external exam traffic in Fujairah. Entry decisions are made by the school as the exam centre, which is why a parent should ask for the centre zone and the entry deadline in writing rather than guessing from a UK timetable.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, and its deadlines are set by the school rather than by the IB. UAE schools sit the May session. The Diploma punishes a weak Higher Level choice harder than IGCSE punishes anything, because the grade is built from papers and internal work across two years.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision in Fujairah is thin enough that families routinely compare a local sixth form against weekly boarding in Sharjah or a daily run west. Tuition is often what makes the local option viable, by covering the Higher Level subject the school cannot staff deeply.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Fujairah parents ask about first, with what each one actually assesses. A tutor is matched to the level and the board, because the gap between IGCSE Core and Extended is wider than the gap between two different subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers in most routes, no coursework. Extended adds functions, calculus-adjacent gradient work, vectors and harder trigonometry. Marks are lost on method presentation in multi-step questions, not on arithmetic. A Core entry caps the grade, so the tier decision needs checking against sixth-form entry requirements before the entry closes.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Papers cover motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics, magnetism and atomic physics, with a practical or alternative-to-practical component depending on the route. Electricity and moments are the reliable weak points. The command terms matter: a question asking to explain and one asking to describe are marked against different criteria.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis, rates, organic families and qualitative analysis. Students who can recite the content still lose marks because they cannot set out a calculation the mark scheme can follow. Practical skills are assessed on paper for most UAE candidates, which makes question-style practice more valuable than extra lab time.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to under-prepare. Transport in plants, homeostasis, inheritance and ecology carry most of the marks that students drop. The skill being tested is precise terminology under time pressure, so written answers marked against the real scheme are worth more than another read-through of notes.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510/0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and an oral component. For many east-coast students this sits alongside Arabic as a first language, and the two compete for revision time. Writing marks come from register and task fulfilment as much as accuracy, which is coachable quickly once a student sees a marked script.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study based, with application marks that reward using the stimulus material rather than reciting theory. Fujairah students with a family business often over-rely on real-world knowledge and under-answer the case. Teaching the mark allocation inside a six-mark evaluate question is usually the fastest available gain.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks that prose cannot recover. Demand and supply analysis, elasticity and government intervention are where answers drift into description. The Fujairah port and the wider logistics economy give usable local examples, which strengthens the application marks examiners look for.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.description: A mandatory subject in UAE private schools and taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students under the regulator's rules. It is examined seriously and it eats revision time in Year 11. Support here is about examination technique in Arabic, not conversational fluency.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for Mathematics at Higher Level or A-Level. Small cohorts mean this is often the subject no local tutor covers. It is the clearest case for an online match, because the teaching requirement is narrow and specific rather than general.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data representation and logic gates make up more of the mark total than coding does. Students who program confidently still lose marks on trace tables and binary conversion. A tutor should be marking written answers against the scheme rather than reviewing project code.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Fujairah is a strip of coast and a set of inland and northern communities, and the distance between them changes what a weekday session can look like. The notes below are about session timing, not scenery.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: The administrative and school centre of the emirate, and where the tuition centres are. A student living here can reach a centre class after school, which is exactly why group classes feel like the default option even when one-to-one is the better fit.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Close to the corniche and to the main school run, so late-afternoon traffic is short. Families here often start with a 4.30pm slot and shift it later once they see how long homework actually takes on a Tuesday.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland from the city, with school transport that arrives home later than parents expect. A 5pm start is usually optimistic in term time; 6pm holds through the year, which matters more than it sounds for consistency.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: A residential district whose students are spread across several private schools, so two neighbours can be sitting different boards in the same subject. Any outside help has to be matched to the school's own syllabus code rather than the area.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South along the coast road, far enough that a visiting tutor would be charging for the drive in both directions. This is the point on the map where online one-to-one stops being a compromise and starts being the only sensible arithmetic.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: At the northern end of the coast, with a jurisdictional complication: neighbouring Dibba Al-Hisn is Sharjah territory and its private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority instead. Families here should confirm which regulator covers their own school.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Smaller coastal communities between the city and Dibba. Students travel for school, so the useful question is not where a tutor is but what time the bus actually gets back and whether a session can start before fatigue wins.

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually returns on the east coast
paragraphs: A near-me query is a location query, so the results are ranked largely by distance and by how aggressively a provider has filled in its address fields. That rewards whoever has a Fujairah City pin on the map, and it quietly removes from view every tutor who could teach the subject but lives elsewhere. For a general Year 8 maths catch-up, the trade is fine. For Chemistry at Extended tier eight weeks before a paper, the trade is expensive.

The second thing the search hides is what kind of thing each result is. A tuition centre with premises and staff is a licensed business and sells group classes by the month. A freelance tutor is an individual who needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE. An agency sells a matching service and may or may not employ the person who turns up. An online platform sells the same matching service without the travel. Four different products, one result page, no labels.

Reading the results properly takes two questions. First, what is the smallest unit you can buy - an hour, a month, a term - because that tells you how much risk you are carrying if the match is wrong. Second, who exactly is teaching, and can you check their permit and their subject level before paying. Anything that cannot answer both in writing is not a cheap option; it is an unpriced one. A provider that will put the tutor name, the permit status and the syllabus code in a single message has already told you most of what the search engine could not.
bullets: Distance-ranked results favour an address, not a subject specialism

sections.heading: The four options a Fujairah family is really choosing between
paragraphs: Set side by side, the four options separate cleanly. A tuition centre in Fujairah City is the cheapest per hour and the weakest on subject depth, because a group class has to move at the pace of the group. A freelance tutor who drives from Sharjah or Dubai is the most expensive per contact hour once travel is priced, and the most fragile: one road closure and the week is gone. A school teacher with free evenings is the best informed about the school and the most constrained by the rules governing who they may teach. Online one-to-one costs less than a visit, holds its slot, and draws on a pool no local radius contains.

The AED figures below are market rates published by providers, not IB Gram prices. The budget band sits where university-student and generalist online tutors advertise, from roughly AED 45 upwards. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted from AED 150 to 300. In-home visits are quoted from AED 180 to 500 including travel, and IB or IGCSE specialists from AED 200 to 450 and beyond. Those bands come from provider pricing pages and from a published 2026 Dubai rate survey, and a Fujairah family should expect the travel element of the in-home band to sit at the top of its range rather than the bottom.

The column that decides most Fujairah cases is the fourth one. A tuition centre draws on whoever it employs locally. A visiting tutor draws on whoever is willing to spend two hours in a car for a one-hour lesson. Online one-to-one draws on every tutor who teaches that syllabus at that level and can make a Gulf Standard Time slot. For a mainstream subject at Core tier the three pools overlap. For Additional Mathematics, Higher Level Chemistry or Further Pure, they do not overlap at all.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rule is specific. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so anyone quoting you a figure is guessing.

This is not a technicality a parent can leave to the tutor. The permit carries a code of conduct, and one of its effects is to limit a teacher tutoring students affiliated with their own school. Abu Dhabi press reporting describes ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff along the same lines, prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. Fujairah schools answer to the federal Ministry of Education rather than ADEK, but the MoHRE permit conditions apply across the country, so the question is worth asking in every emirate.

A tuition centre with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. In Dubai that means a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation of any kind and does not claim one: no KHDA permit, no Ministry of Education endorsement, no board affiliation. What a parent can verify is the individual - the permit, the subject, the level - and that is the verification worth doing before money changes hands.

sections.heading: The drive-time arithmetic nobody does before signing up
paragraphs: A visiting tutor is a transport problem wearing an education label. From Fujairah City to the Sharjah and Dubai school belt is a mountain crossing, and the return leg in the evening is the slower one. A one-hour lesson therefore costs the tutor the better part of three hours. Rational tutors price that in, which is why published in-home bands reach AED 500 an hour and why the first thing to go when the tutor has a busy week is the Fujairah slot rather than the one ten minutes from their flat.

The fragility shows up in the calendar rather than the price. Across a thirty-week school year, a weekly in-home slot that loses four sessions to weather, traffic and the tutor's own commitments has lost over a month of teaching, usually in the weeks that matter most. Rain on the mountain road and a cancelled Thursday are not dramatic events; they are the normal operating condition of an east-coast schedule. A plan that only works when nothing goes wrong is not a plan for Year 11.

Online removes the variable entirely, and it changes what a session can be. A tutor who is not driving can run two forty-five-minute sessions on different evenings instead of one marathon, which suits a tired fifteen-year-old better. Work can be shared on screen and kept, so a marked script from October is still available in March. The trade is real - a screen is not a kitchen table - and it is a trade most Fujairah families make once they count the lost weeks rather than the hourly rate.

sections.heading: IB or IGCSE: the two jobs hiding inside one search
paragraphs: The phrase IB IGCSE tuition near me is typed by two different parents. One has a child in the Middle Years Programme being assessed against criteria, with no external paper in sight and a report full of numbers out of eight. The other has a child in Year 10 or 11 heading for a Cambridge or Pearson series with a published entry deadline. The subject may be the same. The teaching job is not, and a tutor who treats the first as early exam preparation wastes a year.

In the MYP, the work is to find which criterion is costing marks and teach to it. A science student losing marks in criterion C needs practice in processing and analysing data, which no amount of content revision supplies. In IGCSE, the work is question technique against a published mark scheme, tier choice while the entry can still be changed, and triage across topics with the series date fixed. One is diagnostic and developmental; the other is engineering against a deadline.

The transition between them is where east-coast families most often lose ground. A student arriving in Year 10 from an MYP cohort meets tiering, command terms and timed papers at the same moment, and the school has one term to settle thirty of them. This is where a few weeks of targeted help pays for itself, and where the table below is worth reading against your child's own option sheet rather than in the abstract.

sections.heading: What a Fujairah City tuition centre can and cannot do
paragraphs: A centre class has genuine advantages, and parents who dismiss it are usually wrong about the cheapest useful option. It gets a student out of the house and away from a phone, it imposes a routine that homework at the kitchen table does not, and it is the best value per hour on this coast for a student whose problem is work habits rather than content. For a Year 9 student who simply is not sitting down to study, two hours at a centre every week solves more than an expensive specialist would.

What a group cannot do is teach to one student's gap. A class of eight moving through a scheme of work has to pick a pace, and the student who is behind in one topic and ahead in two gets the average of their needs. Centres also tend to teach a subject rather than a board, which matters when half the room sits Cambridge 0580 and the rest sit Pearson 4MA1 with different question styles and tiering rules. A monthly package also removes the ability to stop after one session.

The honest split is this. Use a centre for structure, discipline and routine subjects at the mainstream tier. Use one-to-one, online or otherwise, for a diagnosed weakness, for Extended or Higher Level work, and for anything where the specialist does not exist locally. Families who do both are not overspending; they are buying two different things, and the total is usually less than the in-home rate for a single subject.

sections.heading: The school-teacher option and the rules around it
paragraphs: Asking a teacher at the school for private lessons is the most natural move a parent makes and the one most likely to run into a rule. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct whose effect is to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school, and Abu Dhabi reporting describes ADEK professional-ethics rules prohibiting Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students. The intention is obvious: a teacher should not be paid twice for the same child, and a child should not be advantaged by paying their own assessor.

There is a quieter problem as well. The teacher who set the internal assessment, marks it and predicts the grade is not a neutral second opinion. The value of outside help is that it tells you something the school has not told you - that the content is secure but the exam technique is not, or that the tier is wrong, or that a criterion has been misunderstood for two years. A second voice from inside the same staffroom rarely delivers that.

A teacher from a different school in the emirate is a legitimate option, provided the permit is in place and the student is not theirs. That is worth asking about directly rather than assuming. The questions are simple: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, which school are you at, and have you taught this syllabus code at this tier. A tutor who answers all three without hesitation is a reasonable bet whatever their postcode.

sections.heading: What to ask before paying for anything
paragraphs: The first question is about the problem rather than the provider. If you cannot say which topics and which question types are costing marks, no purchase will be well targeted, and that is what a diagnostic session is for. Ask for a marked piece of the student's own work to be read in front of you and for the output to be written down. An hour that ends with a named weakness and a realistic number of weeks is worth more than a month of general sessions.

The second question is about exit. What is the smallest unit you can buy, what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions, and is there a replacement without a new fee. Any provider confident in its matching will answer plainly. A monthly package with no replacement policy puts all the risk on the family, and on this coast, where the alternative tutor may be ninety minutes away, that risk is not small.

The third is verification. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, the syllabus code the tutor has taught, the tier, and whether they have marked against the published scheme rather than simply taught the subject. IB Gram claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because it holds none. What it does publish is the market rate, the delivery format and the fallback when no specialist is free - and those are the three things parents on this coast are least often told.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus code, not just the subject
process.description: Send the subject, the board and the code from the option sheet - 0580, 4CH1, 0625 - plus the level or tier and the school. On this coast the same subject is taught to two different boards within one street, and the code is what makes a match specific rather than approximate.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a marked piece of work
process.description: The first session is a free trial and runs online at a time that fits the school transport. Bring a marked paper or report. The tutor reads the work, teaches for most of the hour and finishes by naming the weakness. No card details are needed to book it.

process.title: A written plan with a number of weeks on it
process.description: After the trial you get a short written plan: the topics and question types to fix, the order to fix them in, and a realistic number of weeks. If the honest answer is that the school is already handling it, the plan says so and you spend nothing further.

process.title: Fixed weekly slot, reviewed against marked work
process.description: Sessions run at a set time on Gulf Standard Time, same tutor, following the school's own deadlines. Every few weeks the tutor marks a fresh timed piece against the published scheme so progress is measured rather than assumed, and the plan is adjusted from the evidence.

process.title: Say so early if the match is wrong
process.description: Two sessions is enough to know whether the fit works. If it does not, say so and the subject is rematched to a different tutor without a new fee. Families on the east coast have too little slack in the calendar to spend a term being polite about a bad match.

whyPoints.title: The pool, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: A twenty-minute radius around Fujairah City contains a limited number of people who can teach Additional Mathematics or Chemistry at Extended tier. An online match draws on everyone who teaches that syllabus and can make the slot. For mainstream subjects this changes little; for narrow ones it changes everything.

whyPoints.title: Rates published, with the source named
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page come from provider pricing pages and a published 2026 Dubai rate survey, and are presented as the market rather than as our price list. Five of six pages ranking for these searches publish no figure at all, and the one that does contradicts itself.

whyPoints.title: Written diagnosis before a package
whyPoints.description: The first output is a note naming the topics and question types where marks are going, with a number of weeks attached. That is checkable, and it lets a family decide against buying more. A plan a parent cannot read is not a plan.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that respects the east coast
whyPoints.description: School transport from Sakamkam and the northern coast arrives later than a Dubai timetable assumes, Ramadan hours change the evening, and prayer times are fixed points. Slots are built around those realities and can be moved permanently, not just once as a favour.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has done. Nobody at IB Gram supplies finished internal assessments or coursework, and we do not reproduce board papers or mark schemes as downloads. Those boundaries are why the support is safe to use under IB and Cambridge honesty rules.

whyPoints.title: An honest fallback when nobody is free
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based tutor covers a narrow subject at the level needed, you are told that and offered a specialist elsewhere teaching into your time zone, or told to wait. Silence or a weak substitute costs a family more than an awkward message does.

faqs.question: What does a near-me search for IB and IGCSE tuition actually return in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Four different products ranked mostly by distance: tuition centres with a Fujairah City address, freelance profiles that often carry Sharjah or Dubai numbers, agencies that will quote for travel, and online platforms with no address at all. The ranking rewards whoever filled in their location fields, not whoever teaches your child's syllabus at the right tier. Before comparing prices, work out which of the four each result is, because an hour at a centre and an hour of one-to-one teaching are not the same unit. Then ask who is teaching and on what permit.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Fujairah City cheaper than one-to-one online lessons?
faqs.answer: Per hour, almost always. Centre and budget-tier rates start from around AED 45 to 150 an hour per student, where qualified one-to-one online tutors sit in a published band of roughly AED 150 to 300. The two are not substitutes though. A group moves at the pace of the group and usually teaches a subject rather than a specific board, so a diagnosed gap at Extended tier is not what it fixes. Many east-coast families use a centre for routine and structure and one-to-one for the one subject that is actually costing grades.

faqs.question: Which exam boards do private schools in Fujairah use for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel appear on this coast, and the school is the exam centre that makes entries. That matters because the rules differ: Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended and runs June and November series across six administrative timetable zones, while Pearson offers May/June and November entries with Foundation and Higher tiers in maths. Ask the school for the syllabus code, the tier and the entry deadline in writing. A tutor matched to 0580 Extended is a different match from one used to 4MA1 Higher.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask for it directly, in a message you keep. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no reason for a legitimate tutor to be vague about it. Eligible categories include school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private lessons without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no published fine schedule exists.

faqs.question: Can a tutor living in Sharjah realistically hold a twice-weekly Fujairah slot?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for a whole school year. The crossing to the western emirates is a mountain route and the evening return is slower, so a one-hour lesson costs the tutor close to three hours. Published in-home bands of AED 180 to 500 reflect that, and so does the cancellation pattern: when the tutor has a difficult week, the far slot goes first. Across thirty teaching weeks, losing four sessions to weather and traffic removes more than a month of teaching, usually in the term where it mattered most.

faqs.question: Which authority supervises private schools on the Fujairah coast?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education. Under the UAE government's own description, the Ministry plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. The practical consequence for a Fujairah parent is that you will not find a KHDA inspection report for your school, and a provider advertising KHDA approval is telling you nothing relevant to this emirate.

faqs.question: My son is at an Indian-curriculum school in Fujairah. Can he add IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the answer comes from the school rather than from a tutor. Entries are made by a registered exam centre, so the first question is whether his school enters candidates for Cambridge or Pearson at all, and whether it will enter him for a subject it does not teach. Where it will not, families look at another centre in the northern emirates. Start that conversation early: final entries close months before the paper, not weeks, so a decision taken in the spring is usually a decision taken too late.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of IGCSE tuition make sense alongside a full school day?
faqs.answer: One 60 to 90 minute session per subject through most of the year, rising to two in the target subject from January of Year 11. More than that and the student stops having time to do the work the session sets, which is where the learning actually happens. Two shorter sessions on separate evenings generally beat one long block for a tired fifteen-year-old, particularly where school transport from inland districts gets home late. The limiting factor is independent practice time, not teaching time.

faqs.question: If nobody in the UAE teaches the subject, who ends up teaching my child?
faqs.answer: You get told, in plain words, before you pay. Narrow subjects at the top tier - Further Pure Mathematics, some Higher Level sciences, a minority language - may have no UAE-based specialist available at a workable hour. The options are then a specialist outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time, or waiting until one is free. Both are better than a generalist who has never taught the syllabus. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, which does not mean they do not have one.

faqs.question: Are online lessons workable if our home internet on the east coast is slow?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because a one-to-one lesson is mostly voice plus a shared writing surface, which needs far less bandwidth than video streaming does. Where the connection is unreliable, the practical fixes are to use a phone hotspot as a backup, keep the camera off during written work, and have the tutor share a document that survives a dropout so nothing is lost. Ask for the lesson notes to be written up afterwards as well, so a bad connection costs a few minutes rather than the session.

faqs.question: Can we begin with one subject and add a second later in the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is usually the better order. Taking two subjects at once halves the independent practice time available for each and makes it hard to tell which intervention is working. Fix the subject that is costing the most, confirm the change on marked work, then decide. Adding a second tutor mid-year is straightforward; each subject gets its own specialist rather than one person covering both, since a Chemistry match and a Mathematics match are different teaching jobs.

faqs.question: Does the free trial lesson need card details or a commitment to a package?
faqs.answer: No. The trial is one lesson, booked without card details, and it is a real teaching session rather than a sales call: the tutor reads a marked piece of the student's work, teaches for most of the hour, and names the weakness at the end. The output is a short written plan with a realistic number of weeks on it. If the plan says the school is already handling the problem, that is an acceptable result and nothing further is owed. The condition attached is simply one lesson per student.

faqs.question: What should a first paid session produce if we are paying for a diagnosis?
faqs.answer: Something written and specific. Not a general impression of ability, but the topics and question types where marks are being dropped, evidence from a marked script, and a view on how many weeks the fix needs. A good diagnosis often reduces the plan rather than expanding it - one topic and two question styles rather than a whole syllabus. If a session ends with nothing more precise than a recommendation to book more sessions, you have learned something about the provider instead of about your child.

faqs.question: Which evening slots survive prayer times and school transport in Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: A 4.30pm start works for families close to the corniche and the city schools, while students travelling back to inland districts like Sakamkam are more reliably settled by 6pm. Keeping the slot after Maghrib suits many families, and during Ramadan the whole pattern shifts to a post-Iftar session, which online delivery makes straightforward. The point of a fixed slot is that it should hold for the year, so it is worth choosing the later time that always works over the earlier one that works in October.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then decide what to buy
fujairah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: A near-me search is a reasonable way to find a room and a bad way to find a specialist. On this coast the two are rarely the same thing. Send the subject, the syllabus code and the tier, book the free trial, and let an hour with a marked script tell you where the marks are actually going. The written plan afterwards will say how many weeks the fix needs, and sometimes it will say the school has it covered. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, from Fujairah City to Dibba Al-Fujairah, and the slot can move when school transport or Ramadan hours change.

intro.heading: Near me is the wrong filter on this coast
paragraphs: A search for a tutor near me assumes that proximity narrows a long list. In Dubai that holds. There, a family in Jumeirah has a genuine choice between several equally qualified people inside a twenty-minute drive, so distance is a reasonable way to pick between them. On the Fujairah coast the list is not long enough to narrow. Al Faseel, Fujairah city, Sakamkam, Merashid and Al Gurfa are all within a short drive of one another and all draw on the same small set of subject teachers, because the emirate's private-school sector is small and a small sector employs few people per syllabus.

That is why this page is built as a comparison rather than a sales pitch. If you compare Al Faseel with the next district over, and then with the next one, the honest conclusion is that the answer is the same in each: for a common subject the local option exists, and for a minority subject at Higher Level or Extended tier it usually does not. Moving along the coast does not change the supply. Changing the format does.

IB Gram's answer for every one of those districts is identical and worth saying plainly: one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, matched by subject and level. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That service runs only in India, and it is stated on every country page the site publishes. Your URL says home tutor and near me because those are the phrases parents type, and they deserve a straight answer rather than a quiet redirect.

There is a second comparison running underneath the first, and it matters more than geography. Al Faseel families at the end of Year 11 are choosing between an IB Diploma route and an A Level route, and the two have different shapes, different workloads and different consequences for university applications. The Diploma asks for six subjects plus an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the minimum. A Levels ask for three or four subjects taken deeper. Neither is better. They suit different students, and a tutor who cannot describe the difference is not the right person to advise on it.

So the sections below compare: districts against each other, IB against IGCSE and A Level, online against in-home with the travel cost broken out, and the regulator in Fujairah against the emirate authorities everyone else writes about. Each comparison ends in the same place, which is the honest outcome of a comparison rather than a weakness in it. Where a figure appears it is a published market rate read in October 2026 with its source named, because almost nobody ranking for these searches publishes a number in dirhams at all, and a parent who cannot see a number cannot compare anything. Where a date appears it is named by its month rather than its year, so that the page stays true after this session has passed. And where something could not be verified against an official source, it is left out rather than guessed, which is why you will find no IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency on this page even though competitor pages publish one.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-fa.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every Al Faseel enquiry. The differences between them are structural rather than a matter of difficulty, and knowing which structure your child is inside changes what tutoring should do.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal written paper. Cambridge syllabuses split into Core and Extended with a grade ceiling of C on Core; Pearson Edexcel splits maths into Foundation and Higher tier. Coursework appears in some subjects and not others, and the school decides which components it enters.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Faseel families the practical issue is tier placement. In a small school market the maths and science sets are coarser, so borderline students land on Core and lose the top four grades before teaching starts. Two terms of Extended-only content in Year 9 or early Year 10, proved by a timed Extended paper, is what reopens that decision with a teacher.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Graded out of 45 points with 24 as the diploma minimum and up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah's local Diploma offer is limited, so students who want it often move school or emirate, and some keep a Fujairah home while boarding elsewhere. That makes a fixed online slot unusually valuable: it survives a change of school, a weekly commute and a holiday period without the engagement collapsing and restarting.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken deeper than the Diploma allows, with AS sometimes cashed in at the end of Year 12 as a standalone qualification. Entry is usually gated on IGCSE grades in the same subject, which is why Year 11 results matter beyond the certificate itself.
programmes.countryNote: The sourced Ministry of Education equivalency rule for the British track names this stage: one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five IGCSE or GCSE passes at E or grade 3. A student dropping to two AS subjects should check that against the ministry's own channel first.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-fa.subjectsIntro: IB Diploma subjects first, with the assessment weightings that decide where tutoring hours should go. Ask your child's coordinator which level each subject is being taken at before booking anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 40% each and the Exploration 20%. At Higher Level the papers are 30, 30 and 20 with the Exploration at 20%. Paper 3 at HL is the extended-response problem paper and the one students least often practise.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure as Analysis and Approaches, with modelling and statistics in place of the heavier pure content. Graphical display calculator technique is examinable in itself, and marks go missing on candidates who can get the answer but cannot show the method the scheme rewards.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current guide, Paper 1 carries 36% and includes both multiple choice and a data-analysis section, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the Internal Assessment 20% at both levels. The scientific investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same component weightings as Physics. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations account for most lost marks at Higher Level, and the data-analysis section of Paper 1 rewards practice on unfamiliar graphs rather than recall.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-content science subject, where revision most often becomes reading. Command terms do the real work: a question asking students to explain is not answered by a description, and that single distinction moves more marks than extra content does.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Standard Level Paper 1 is 30%, Paper 2 is 40% and the portfolio 30%. At Higher Level the split is 20, 30, 30 for papers one to three with the portfolio at 20%. The portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each, built on real published articles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Standard Level runs Paper 1 at 35%, Paper 2 at 35% and the Individual Oral at 30%. Higher Level adds the HL Essay at 20% and rebalances the rest. The Individual Oral is where a global issue must be traced through two texts, and preparation is a skill in itself.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for the higher-level paper. Calculation questions on ratios and break-even are predictable marks; the common failure is applying a correct concept to a business the stimulus does not describe.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a solution-development Internal Assessment where the product and the documentation are assessed together. Students who code well often lose marks on the documentation, because the criteria reward evidence of a design process rather than a working program alone.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Separate courses with separate expectations, and placing a student in the wrong one is common. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, so Al Faseel students usually arrive with more exposure than an international cohort elsewhere would.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-fa.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE grid, with syllabus codes for both boards. Al Faseel schools may enter either, and the two assess the same subject differently enough that a tutor must know which.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980; Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tier
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge splits the entry between a non-calculator and a calculator paper at 50% each; Edexcel runs two calculator papers. Bounds, vectors and algebraic fractions are where Extended candidates lose most marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 0972; Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge: a multiple-choice paper at 30%, theory at 50% and a practical component at 20% sat as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Edexcel examines practical skills inside two written papers instead, with no separate practical exam.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 0971; Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations requiring two conversions, the exact wording of ion and gas tests, and balanced ionic equations are the three places Extended candidates give marks away most predictably.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 0970; Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Water-potential language, genetic-cross notation and data-handling on unfamiliar graphs carry the losses. The recall load is large enough that a topic-by-topic risk list is more useful than a general revision timetable.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a First Language (0500 / 0990; Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading and writing rather than literature. Directed writing is marked against register and audience, so a technically clean answer in the wrong voice sits below its potential. Summary questions punish lifted phrasing.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455 / 0987; Edexcel 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries weight the surrounding prose cannot recover. Extended papers reward a judgement supported by the diagram rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages on either side.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 0986; Edexcel 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: The insert decides the answer. Break-even, cash-flow and ratio questions are the most reliable marks on the paper and are usually lost to arithmetic rather than to misunderstanding.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 0984; Edexcel 4CP0)
igcseSubjects.description: Pseudocode is marked on logic, not syntax, which students find counterintuitive after a year of Python. Binary, hexadecimal and two's complement conversion appear every series and reward drilling to automatic accuracy.

igcseSubjects.name: Geography (0460 / 0976; Edexcel 4GE1)
igcseSubjects.description: Map, graph and photograph skills are the dependable marks. Case studies decide the grade, and a named example with figures scores where a generic one does not. Fujairah coastal processes are usable local material.

sections.heading: What a tutor near me in Al Faseel can and cannot mean
paragraphs: Searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Faseel returns two kinds of result, and they are not alternatives. The first is somebody who will drive to a Fujairah address. The published market rate for an in-home one-to-one visit runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the upper end for a named specialist, and that range is real. The second is a subject specialist teaching over live video, which the same market prices at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified tutor. IB Gram is the second kind. It does not offer home visits in the UAE, and nothing on this site will suggest otherwise.

The reason to compare them on supply rather than on price is that Al Faseel's local supply is genuinely thin at the level most families need. For IGCSE at Core tier in maths or English, a local option exists. For Chemistry at Extended tier, Economics, Computer Science, or any Diploma Higher Level subject, the set of adults within driving distance who have taught and marked that specification recently may be empty. Paying the travel premium does not conjure one into existence.

That gives a straightforward test for any shortlist, wherever it came from. Ask which specification the tutor has taught, in which series, and ask them to describe where candidates lose marks on one named paper. A specialist answers in specifics within a sentence. A generalist answers with enthusiasm. The answer is more informative than a certificate and takes less time to obtain.

Everything after this section is a comparison, because that is what a near-me search is really asking for. District against district, Diploma against A Level, online against in-home with the travel broken out, and Fujairah's federal regulator against the emirate authorities the rest of this market writes about.

sections.heading: Al Faseel against the next district over, on the things that change
paragraphs: Comparisons between Fujairah districts are usually written as if the schools and the tutors differ. They mostly do not. What differs is time: how long the afternoon drive takes, when a child is actually home, and therefore which session slot survives contact with a normal week. That is worth comparing properly, because a slot that does not hold is the most common reason a tutoring arrangement quietly stops working.

Al Faseel has the easier end of this. It is coastal, close to the city-centre schools, and a 16:30 start is achievable most days. Sakamkam adds drive time from the inland side and pushes realistic starts later. Al Gurfa spreads families out along the southern coast road and often means two school runs rather than one. Dibba is in a different category entirely: around ninety minutes north, with the fewest local secondary options in the emirate, so for a family there the question of a nearby tutor does not really arise.

The second axis is the regulator, and it catches families who move along this coast without realising they have changed system. sections.heading: Diploma or A Level after IGCSE: the comparison Year 11 families actually need
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects an Al Faseel student's next four years, and it is usually made on hearsay. The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum and up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. A Levels are three or four subjects, taken further within each, with no equivalent core. Those are different shapes of work, not different difficulties.

The Diploma suits a student who is broadly strong and reasonably organised, because the core alone is a standing commitment across two years and the Internal Assessments arrive in every subject. A Levels suit a student who is sharply stronger in some subjects than others, or who already knows the degree they want and can afford to drop the rest. A student who struggles with deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way that no amount of subject tutoring fixes.

There is also a mathematics decision inside the Diploma that families underestimate. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate courses with the same component weightings but different content, and some university programmes expect one rather than the other. Check the prerequisites for the courses your child is considering before the subject form is signed, because changing course after the first term is disruptive and sometimes not possible at a small school.

On equivalency, the sourced position differs between the two routes and that difference is worth knowing. The British track has published figures: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No equivalent IB points threshold could be verified from an official source for this project, so none appears here. Ask the Ministry of Education directly.

sections.heading: Online against in-home, with the travel cost separated out
paragraphs: Comparisons between online and in-home tuition usually collapse into a preference argument. It is more useful to break the in-home price into its parts, because then the question stops being about taste. A travelling tutor is paid for the lesson and, implicitly, for the journey. In a dense city the journey is short and the convenience is genuine, which is why the format is popular in Dubai and priced accordingly. On the Fujairah coast the journey is longer and, more importantly, it filters the candidate list down to people willing to make it.

So the in-home premium buys three things here: somebody physically present, a shorter list of available subjects, and a start time that drifts. The first is worth something, particularly for a younger child who needs supervision as much as teaching. The second and third are costs, not features. For a Year 11 or Diploma student working against a paper, a specialist who holds the same slot every week is worth more than a generalist in the room.

The counter-argument deserves a fair hearing. Some students genuinely work better with a person at the table, and a screen adds a layer of friction, particularly for practical subjects and for students who need their attention externally managed. The honest mitigations are specific rather than rhetorical: shorter sessions with a break, a shared document the tutor writes on live, a visible worked page rather than a talking head, and a parent within earshot for the first few weeks.

sections.heading: The regulator comparison nobody in this market writes
paragraphs: Every competitor page researched for this market writes about Dubai's authority or writes about nothing. Abu Dhabi's Department of Education and Knowledge is named by none of them. Sharjah's authority appears once across an entire cluster. For a family in Al Faseel that absence is not a minor omission, because the body that supervises your child's school decides where you look up an inspection outcome, who approves the curriculum, and which complaint route exists.

The map is short enough to state in full. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there; both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is all five bodies.

Underneath all of them sits one federal rule that explains the shape of every UAE school week. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the ministry's general regulations. That is why an Al Faseel student on a British or IB pathway carries subjects a student in the United Kingdom would not, and why the week is fuller than the curriculum's own timetable implies.

For a tutoring plan the consequence is practical rather than administrative. Session slots have to fit around a longer school day. Arabic coursework and assessments arrive on their own schedule. And a parent comparing two schools in two emirates is comparing two regulatory systems, which is worth half an hour of reading on the authority's own site before the deposit is paid.

sections.heading: Availability, honestly: which subjects staff quickly and which do not
paragraphs: No page researched in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a phone number in another country. That is worth naming, because availability is the single most useful thing a parent can be told before paying, and the silence is deliberate across the cluster.

The pattern is consistent. Common subjects at the common levels staff quickly: IGCSE maths, the three separate sciences at Core and Extended, English as a first language, and the Diploma's most-entered subjects at Standard Level. A minority subject at Higher Level is slower, and a minority subject at Higher Level in one specific evening slot sometimes cannot be staffed at all. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision sit somewhere in between, because the supervision is a process skill rather than a subject.

What should happen when a match is not possible is simple and rarely done. You should be told, given a realistic timeframe, and offered the alternative explicitly rather than quietly: a different slot, a different week, or nothing. What should not happen is being handed the nearest available generalist and left to work out the mismatch in the third session, by which point a month of a Year 11 spring has gone.

Ask the question in those words of anybody you are considering. If the answer is that everything is always available immediately, in every subject, at every level, in any slot, in a market this size, that answer is the information you needed.
