sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an Internal Assessment, and where the line sits
paragraphs: This matters more on an IB page than on an IGCSE one, because the Diploma puts assessed coursework in every subject and the consequences of getting it wrong land on the student. One page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessment work at a fixed price. That is academic malpractice under the board's own rules, and the student carries the result of it, not the seller.

The boundary is clear once stated in terms of who produced the sentences. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name where it misses a criterion, and teach the student how to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words are the tutor's own.

Limits are part of this and are easy to check. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600 and the exhibition commentary at 950, the sciences investigation at 3,000, and the Economics portfolio at 800 words per commentary. A tutor who does not know those numbers is not working from the subject guide, and a tutor who offers to supply the guides or the mark schemes as downloads is reproducing the board's copyrighted material rather than teaching from it.

Use it as a selection question. Ask what they would do if your child asked them to write one paragraph of a coursework draft. A refusal with an explanation of the alternative is the right answer. Treating it as negotiable tells you exactly what will happen the week before the deadline.

sections.heading: Getting started from Al Faseel, including what can go wrong
paragraphs: The first useful step is paperwork rather than shopping. Get the subject, the level or tier, and the syllabus code from the school — the code sits on the entry confirmation, and for IGCSE it decides whether a practical exam exists. For a Diploma student, get the coordinator's internal deadline calendar for Internal Assessments, because those dates are earlier than families expect and they are the ones tutoring has to work around.

Then take a trial lesson and treat it as a test of explanation, not of warmth. The thing to listen for is whether the tutor talks about the mark scheme, the command terms and where candidates lose marks, or whether they talk about potential and confidence. Both kinds of tutor are pleasant. Only one of them will change a grade. Your child's view after that lesson is the single best signal available, and it is worth more than any credential list.

Things that go wrong are predictable. The slot drifts and the homework cycle collapses. The tutor turns out to know the other board. The student is working at Core tier while the tutor teaches Extended content, or the reverse. A Diploma student gets subject teaching when the actual problem is the Extended Essay deadline. Every one of those is caught by a diagnostic in the first fortnight and by a written topic list that gets updated.

And the limit should be said once more, because it is the honest end of a near-me search: no tutor comes to a Fujairah address through IB Gram. Lessons are online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, and the reason to choose that is not convenience. It is that the person teaching your child has taught the specification your child is sitting.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE tutor actually based near Al Faseel?
faqs.answer: For common subjects at common levels, usually yes. For Higher Level Diploma subjects or Extended-tier Chemistry, Economics and Computer Science, often not, because Fujairah's private-school sector is small and a small sector employs few teachers per specification. Al Faseel, Sakamkam, Merashid and Al Gurfa draw on the same pool, so moving a few kilometres changes nothing. faqs.question: Should my child choose the IB Diploma or A Levels after IGCSE in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: It depends on the shape of the student rather than on difficulty. The Diploma is six subjects plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the minimum, which suits a broadly strong and organised student. A Levels are three or four subjects taken deeper, which suits a student who is sharply uneven or already certain of a degree. A student who struggles with deadlines finds the Diploma core hard in a way subject tutoring does not fix. Fujairah's local Diploma offer is limited, so the choice often involves a school move.

faqs.question: Which maths course should a Diploma student from Al Faseel take?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate courses with the same component weightings but different content: the first is heavier on pure mathematics, the second on modelling and statistics. Some university programmes expect one specifically, so check the prerequisites for the courses under consideration before the subject form is signed. Changing after the first term is disruptive and at a small school may not be possible. A tutor can walk through both syllabuses with the student before the decision rather than after it.

faqs.question: Why does Khor Fakkan have a different school regulator from Al Faseel?
faqs.answer: Khor Fakkan is a Sharjah enclave on the Gulf of Oman coast, so its private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education instead. A family moving between the two changes regulatory system without leaving the coastline, which affects where inspection outcomes are published and which approval route applies to a curriculum change.

faqs.question: How long before the exams should an Al Faseel family start looking?
faqs.answer: For building knowledge, a term ahead of the content being taught in school, which in practice means Year 10 for IGCSE and the first Diploma year rather than the second. For converting existing knowledge into marks, eight to twelve weeks before the paper is workable if the first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The expensive version is starting in the spring of the final year with gaps across the syllabus, because at that point every hour spent learning new content costs marks somewhere else.

faqs.question: What does the Extended Essay word limit actually allow a tutor to do?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, and a supervisor or tutor may discuss the research question, explain the assessment criteria, point out where a draft misses one, and teach the student how to improve it. A tutor may not write the essay or draft sections of it. The Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 words and the exhibition commentary at 950. A tutor who does not know those limits is not working from the subject guide, which is a useful thing to test early.

faqs.question: Are online lessons workable for a student who needs someone sitting next to them?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, with specific adjustments rather than reassurance. Shorter sessions with a break, a shared document the tutor writes on live so the student watches working appear rather than a face, and a parent within earshot for the first few weeks all help. For a younger child who needs supervision as much as teaching, the honest answer is that a screen adds friction. For a Year 11 or Diploma student working to a paper, a specialist on screen generally beats a generalist in the room.

faqs.question: Do tutors teaching UAE students need a permit, and is it expensive?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects for the same Al Faseel student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and only where the specifications genuinely overlap: maths and physics is a realistic pairing, chemistry and biology less so at Higher Level, and a Diploma language and a science almost never. The temptation is scheduling convenience, and it usually costs depth in the weaker of the two. A better arrangement for two subjects is two specialists on different evenings, with one of them nominated to keep an eye on the overall deadline calendar so nothing is tracked twice or not at all.

faqs.question: What should a trial lesson from Al Faseel actually tell me?
faqs.answer: Whether your child can follow this person's explanation, and whether the tutor thinks in mark schemes. Listen for command terms, named papers and specific places where candidates lose marks. A specialist produces those within a minute. A generalist talks about potential and confidence, which is pleasant and changes nothing. Your child's verdict afterwards is more reliable than any credential list, and if the fit is wrong the match should change without a discussion about commitment.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic studies change the tutoring timetable in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: They lengthen the school week rather than altering the international grades. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must follow the ministry's general regulations, so those subjects run alongside the licensed curriculum. For an Al Faseel family that means a fuller day and later realistic session slots. For equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five-subject IGCSE count, which is worth knowing before subject choices are finalised.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a specialist for on this coast?
faqs.answer: Extended-tier Chemistry and Physics, Economics, Computer Science and Business Studies, in roughly that order, with Additional Mathematics and International Mathematics behind them. The pattern is not about difficulty but about how many local teachers have taught the specification recently. Core-tier maths, English as a first language and the separate sciences at Core are comfortable. If your request falls in the first group, expect a longer match and ask for a realistic timeframe rather than an assurance.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or while we are travelling from Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning the change beats improvising it. Most families shift the slot later during Ramadan, often to a post-Iftar time, and because the lesson is online nothing depends on a tutor's drive home. Travel is handled as a one-off time adjustment rather than a cancelled term, which keeps the homework cycle between sessions intact. Agree the change a week ahead so the work set before the move still gets marked before the next session rather than being quietly dropped.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor turns out to be teaching the wrong specification?
faqs.answer: It gets caught by the diagnostic in the first fortnight, which is one of the reasons the diagnostic exists. A past paper marked against the official scheme makes a specification mismatch obvious immediately: the question styles do not match what the student recognises, and the practical component is either there or it is not. Report it and the match changes. The expensive version is discovering it in the third month, which is why the syllabus code belongs in the first message rather than the fourth.

intro.heading: What "near me" can and cannot deliver in Al Gurfa
paragraphs: The phrase "near me" is a proximity instruction to a search engine. Google reads your location, looks for tutoring businesses with an address inside a few kilometres of Al Gurfa, and returns whatever it finds. That mechanism works beautifully for a dentist. It works poorly for a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 teacher, because the thing you actually need is not nearness. It is somebody who has marked Paper 4 answers, knows which of the six Cambridge administrative zones your child's centre sits in, and can tell the difference between a lost mark for method and a lost mark for notation.

Fujairah is the only emirate on the Gulf of Oman coast, cut off from Dubai by the Hajar mountains. That geography is pleasant to live in and unhelpful for specialist supply. The private-school set here is small by national standards, so a student sitting a less common IB subject — Economics HL, Spanish ab initio, Computer Science — may genuinely have no local specialist within an hour's drive. A parent in Al Gurfa who insists on proximity is choosing from a list of perhaps a handful of people, and the odds that one of them has taught your child's exact syllabus at your child's exact level are not good.

So we will answer the question you asked rather than the question that is easy to answer. Yes, home tutoring exists in Fujairah, and the market charges for it: in-home one-to-one visits across the UAE run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour according to Bestimate's 2026 rate survey and the published rates of in-home providers, with travel time built into the figure whether or not it is itemised. No, IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we do instead is match your child to the person who knows the syllabus, wherever that person is, and run the lesson over live video.

That trade is worth examining honestly rather than asserting. A video lesson loses something: the tutor cannot lean over a page and point, cannot read a room, cannot build the small social obligation that makes a teenager open a textbook on a Thursday. It gains something larger in a place like Al Gurfa: the pool stops being the dozen people who will drive to your door and becomes every specialist who teaches that syllabus. A screen-shared past paper with annotation is closer to the real thing than most parents expect, and a recorded session is something no kitchen-table lesson has ever produced.

The rest of this page is built to let you decide rather than to persuade you. There is a table of what the UAE market charges by format, a table of the exam calendar counted backwards from the June and November Cambridge series, a note on what the Ministry of Education requires of Fujairah private schools, the equivalency rules your child will meet when applying to a UAE university, and a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment. If any of it tells you that a local in-home tutor is the right answer for your family, that is a reasonable conclusion and we would rather you reached it with the numbers in front of you.

programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and converts to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. There are no external papers until the optional eAssessment, which means a student can drift for two years without a single externally benchmarked mark. The criteria language — inquiring and analysing, knowledge and understanding, communicating — is what students are actually assessed on, and almost nobody teaches it explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah the MYP-to-DP step is where the thin specialist supply bites hardest. A student who has never sat a timed external paper arrives in DP1 and meets Paper 1 multiple choice under clock pressure for the first time. A tutor working from Al Gurfa over video can run that transition in the spring before DP1 starts, which is cheaper in hours than repairing it in DP2.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE splits most subjects into Core and Extended tiers, with Core capped at grade C and Extended reaching A*. The tier is a decision made in Year 10 that sets the grade ceiling for two years. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is untiered in most subjects and awards 9-1, and its specification codes — 4MA1 Maths, 4PH1 Physics — behave differently from Cambridge 0580 and 0625 in paper structure and in what the mark scheme rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah's private schools run both boards, and a family moving between schools inside the emirate can find a child halfway through Cambridge 0580 arriving at a Pearson 4MA1 cohort. That is a real syllabus mismatch, not a formality. The first thing a tutor should ask for is the specification code printed on your child's exam entry slip, because the two boards diverge on tiering, calculator rules and the weighting of the non-calculator paper.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7 with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE combination. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and in most sciences the HL extension material appears on a separate paper rather than being folded into the SL papers.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. For a Fujairah student the binding constraint is rarely the exam — it is the Internal Assessment deadline set by the school's own coordinator, which usually lands in DP2 and is immovable. A student on the Gulf of Oman coast with no local specialist in their HL subject can still get criterion-by-criterion feedback on their own draft over video, which is what the IB permits and all that it permits.

programmes.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in private schools
programmes.description: Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver. These sit alongside IGCSE or IB rather than replacing anything, and they carry their own assessment. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai calculates mandatory-subject time in 40-minute lesson units and advises that no mandatory lesson run shorter than 25 minutes.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah schools answer to the Ministry of Education on this rather than to an emirate-level authority, but the federal baseline is the same: Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies are not optional extras. Families who moved from a system without them often discover the gap in Year 9. For the mandatory subjects, schools may not use different or additional content without prior MoE permission, so tutoring here means supporting the school's own material.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-gu.subjectsIntro: Below are the IB and IGCSE subjects Al Gurfa families request most, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks go missing. The descriptions are deliberately specific: a tutor who cannot tell you which paper carries the weight has not taught the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA is the proof-and-algebra route. HL adds complex numbers, vectors, induction and a far harder calculus load, and Paper 3 is a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the HL grade. Marks go missing in Paper 3 more than anywhere else, because students have never practised sustained unfamiliar mathematics without a prompt structure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is the modelling-and-statistics route, calculator-permitted on every paper. HL carries graph theory, Voronoi diagrams and complex matrices that surprise students who chose AI expecting an easier course. The usual loss is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means scores the calculation marks and none of the rest.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge IGCSE 0625 · Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: At IGCSE the predictable losses are in electricity and in the practical paper, where students who have only read about circuits cannot describe a method that would actually work. At IB level Paper 2 extended response punishes thin explanation: a numerically correct answer with no reasoning chain loses the explanation marks every time.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge IGCSE 0620
subjects.description: Organic chemistry is where Al Gurfa students most often ask for help, and the real problem is usually mechanism notation rather than memory. At IB HL the energetics and equilibrium topics carry heavy mark weight in Paper 2. The IGCSE 0620 Paper 6 alternative-to-practical rewards precision about apparatus that no amount of theory revision supplies.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge IGCSE 0610
subjects.description: Biology looks like the recall subject and is marked like a precision subject. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, describe, suggest and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and a student who writes everything they know scores the marks for one command and none for the others. Genetics and homeostasis are the common collapse points.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The Diploma Economics IA is three commentaries, each 800 words, each built on a news article the student finds. Students lose marks by choosing an article with no diagram in it and by summarising rather than analysing. HL adds the Paper 3 quantitative component, which is arithmetic under time pressure rather than deep theory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against a guiding question; Paper 2 is comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral asks the student to link a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract, and it is internally assessed and externally moderated. Weak IOs are almost always weak on the global issue rather than on the texts.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: 0580 Extended reaches grade A* and Core is capped at C, which makes the tier decision the single most consequential choice in Year 10. The Extended papers reward algebraic fluency under time pressure. Students most often lose marks on transformations, on bounds and on the final part of multi-step problems where method marks were available for working they did not show.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.levels: Cambridge IGCSE 0450 · IB Business Management HL and SL
subjects.description: The case-study paper is where Business is won and lost. Candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus material write generic answers and collect low marks on high-tariff questions. Application to the named business in front of them is the skill being tested, and it can be taught in a handful of focused sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge IGCSE 0478
subjects.description: A subject Fujairah's smaller school cohorts often cannot staff twice. At IGCSE the pseudocode and trace-table questions are mechanical marks that students throw away for want of practice. At IB level the solution requirement in the Internal Assessment demands a real client and documented testing, not a working program alone.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Federal rules make Arabic mandatory in UAE private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA's Dubai guidance requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and the same distinction shapes how tutoring has to be pitched. Support here means working with the school's own prescribed material.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-gu.regionsTitle: Al Gurfa and the rest of Fujairah, for scheduling purposes
fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-gu.regionsIntro: Fujairah is compact and linear, running along the coast with the mountains at its back. These notes are about the practical question a tutoring schedule actually turns on: when does the school day end, how long is the journey, and what time can a session realistically start.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: A residential pocket on the Fujairah coast with a short run into the city schools. A video session at 16:00 Gulf Standard Time is achievable on a normal school day, which is unusual — in most of the UAE a 16:00 start assumes nobody is in traffic.

regions.name: Fujairah City
regions.note: Where the emirate's private-school capacity is concentrated. Most Al Gurfa students commute into the city, so the end-of-day time that matters for scheduling is the city school bell plus the return journey, not the distance on the map.

regions.name: Dibba
regions.note: North along the coast, with its own school provision and a longer run to Fujairah City. Families here feel the specialist-supply problem most sharply, which is precisely the case where a video lesson stops being a compromise and becomes the only route to a subject specialist.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Close to the corniche and the port, within a short drive of the city centre. Evening sessions after 18:00 work well for DP students who have CAS or sport commitments stacked into the late afternoon.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland of the coast road, feeding the same city schools. The commute is short enough that a late-afternoon session does not require a parent to collect and deliver a child across the emirate twice in an evening.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: A residential area within the Fujairah city envelope. Siblings in different year groups are common here, and consecutive video slots for two children on one evening are simpler to arrange than two separate in-home visits at two different rates.

regions.name: Mirbah
regions.note: On the coast between Fujairah City and Dibba. The drive matters more here than the kilometres suggest, and families running a weekday in-home arrangement typically pay for travel time inside the hourly figure whether the invoice itemises it or not.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah City and the coastal strip
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level regulator. The set is small, which is the whole reason this page exists: a cohort of a few dozen in a given IB subject rarely supports two specialist teachers, and when the one specialist is stretched, families look outward.

schoolClusters.note: Provision thins as you go north. A Dibba family choosing in-home tuition is paying for a driver as much as a teacher, and the specialist pool within reasonable driving distance of the northern coast is smaller again than it is in Fujairah City.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-long
modes.description: One or two sessions a week across a term, following the school's own scheme of work. This is the format that changes a grade, because it builds the habit of weekly accountability rather than reacting to a crisis. The tutor works from your child's school assessment calendar, which means asking for it in the first session and holding you to it afterwards.

modes.title: Exam-series intensive
modes.description: A compressed block of sessions aimed at a named Cambridge or Pearson series. For UAE candidates that means the June series or the November series. The work is past-paper diagnosis: find the question types where marks are reliably lost, drill those, and leave the topics the student already handles alone. It cannot manufacture two years of missing content.

modes.title: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay coaching
modes.description: Process support on the student's own work: choosing a workable research question, understanding what each assessment criterion rewards, reading a draft the student wrote and giving feedback on it. A tutor may teach, review and comment. A tutor may not write, complete or produce any part of an IA, Extended Essay, TOK essay or coursework, and we do not.

modes.title: Curriculum transition support
modes.description: Short blocks for the step changes: MYP into DP, IGCSE into DP1, a move between Cambridge and Pearson specifications, or an arrival into the UAE system from elsewhere. The work is gap-closing against a named entry point rather than general improvement, and it is usually measured in weeks rather than terms.

sections.heading: The honest answer to "is there anyone near me who knows this syllabus?"
paragraphs: Probably not, if the subject is at all specialised and you are restricting the search to people who will drive to Al Gurfa. That is not a reflection on Fujairah. It is arithmetic. A specialist teacher of IB Chemistry HL exists in proportion to the number of students sitting IB Chemistry HL, and the emirate's private-school cohort in any single Diploma subject is small. Multiply that by the subset who tutor privately, then by the subset free at the hour your child is free, and the list is short.

The uncomfortable part is that the market does not tell you this. A search for a tutor near Al Gurfa returns results, because businesses optimise for the query whether or not they have the person. What arrives at the door may be a graduate who studied the subject at university, a teacher of a neighbouring subject, or someone who teaches the right subject on a different board. All three can help a struggling Year 9. None of them is the right answer for a DP2 student eight weeks from a Paper 3 they keep failing.

So the question to ask a prospective tutor is not where they live. It is: which syllabus code, which level, how many cohorts have you taken through it, and what do candidates reliably lose marks on in Paper 2? A person who has taught Cambridge 0620 answers that in one breath. A person who has not changes the subject to their qualifications. That single question sorts the field faster than any amount of proximity filtering, and it is the question this page is built to make you ask.

Our position is that geography should be the last filter applied rather than the first. Match on syllabus, level and availability, then deliver over video. That reverses the usual order, and it is the only order that gives an Al Gurfa family the same specialist access as a family in Dubai Marina.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus code, not the degree subject
Ask which paper candidates lose most marks on and why
Ask how many cohorts the tutor has taken through that exact specification
Treat proximity as a scheduling convenience, not a quality signal

sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs in the UAE market, by format
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all. Of the competitor pages examined for this project in October 2026, three of six quoted nothing and two quoted in US dollars, a currency no Fujairah family transacts in. The figures below are market rates gathered from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list.

Read the table from the cheapest row upward rather than downward, because the interesting question is what each step up buys. Moving from a budget online tutor at AED 45 to 150 an hour to a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 buys subject training and syllabus familiarity. Moving from there to an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 buys travel — a driver's hour, embedded in your hourly rate, in exchange for a tutor who sits in the room. Moving to the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above buys board-specific experience. Each step is a different purchase, and only one of them is about location.

Monthly packages are the other way the market is sold. Published figures include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so a tutoring budget set last year has not been squeezed by fees in that emirate.

What a parent can verify: ask whether the quoted rate is per hour or per session, whether it includes VAT, what a cancellation inside 24 hours costs, and whether the figure changes closer to an exam series. Those four answers tell you more about a provider than any rate card does.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home tutor in Al Gurfa, compared properly
paragraphs: This comparison is usually written by someone selling one of the two options, which makes it useless. Here is the version that names the real costs on both sides. An in-home tutor in Al Gurfa gives you presence: a person in the room, no connection to fail, a teenager who cannot quietly open another tab. It costs more per hour because travel is inside the rate, it narrows the tutor pool to people willing to drive the coast road, and a cancellation on either side wastes a journey rather than a click.

Online delivery inverts every one of those. The pool becomes everyone who teaches the syllabus, which in a small emirate is the difference between a specialist and whoever is available. The rate drops because nobody is paid to drive. Sessions can be recorded for revision, past papers can be screen-shared and annotated live, and a 19:00 slot costs the tutor nothing extra. Against that: it needs a reliable connection, it needs a desk rather than a sofa, and a younger child needs an adult within earshot for the first few weeks.

The honest summary is that format matters less than match. A specialist over video beats a generalist in the room for an exam-year student, and the reverse is often true for a nine-year-old who needs someone physically present to stay on task. IB Gram only offers the online route in the UAE, and we would rather say that plainly than pretend the trade-off does not exist. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

One practical note for Al Gurfa specifically: because the commute into the Fujairah city schools is short, families here have more usable late-afternoon time than families in Dubai or Abu Dhabi. A 16:00 start is realistic. That makes a weekly rhythm easier to hold than it would be in an emirate where a 16:00 session means a child arriving at 16:35.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody else in this market publishes this, which is strange, because it is the single most actionable thing a parent can be given. An exam series is not a date. It is a chain of deadlines, most of which fall months before the paper, and the ones that bite are the ones a school sets internally rather than the board.

For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a March window to a Fujairah parent is quoting a date from another country. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in before you plan anything around a published time.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams run in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking facts and they are useful as a shape: a November series means results in January, which matters if your child has a university application in train. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so work from the live official timetable PDF rather than from any date restated on a page like this one.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB exam or results dates on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date that a parent acts on is worse than no date. Get the session dates from your child's IB coordinator, who has them from the IB directly, and build the plan around the school's internal Internal Assessment deadlines, which almost always bind earlier than anything the board sets.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it changes nothing about the tutor
paragraphs: Fujairah private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. That is different from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education, and different again from Abu Dhabi, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools.

Parents reasonably assume that a regulator who inspects schools also licenses tutors. It does not. School regulation and individual tutoring sit in different places. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. That is the official route, and it is the one to check a tutor's claim against.

Two things follow for a Fujairah family. First, nobody can honestly describe themselves as a Ministry-approved tutor or a tutor approved by KHDA. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and IB Gram holds no such permit, no accreditation from any UAE authority and no partnership with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Second, if your child's own class teacher offers private lessons, check the rules: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars the same thing.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that matters most, and it is the one the market is worst on. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach, and the person who carries the consequence is the student, whose Diploma is at risk if the work is not their own.

What a tutor may legitimately do is teach. That means helping a student understand what each assessment criterion actually rewards, reading a draft the student has written and saying where it falls short of the criterion descriptors, pointing out that a research question is too broad to answer in the word limit, teaching the statistics a Biology IA needs, and explaining why a Maths IA that applies a standard method without personal engagement will sit in the middle bands however neat it looks. All of that is feedback on the student's own work, and it is permitted and expected.

What a tutor may not do is write, draft, complete, rewrite to completion or produce any part of an IA, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or coursework. IB Gram does not do it, will not do it, and declines the request when it is made. There is also a less obvious line: a tutor should not supply the student with syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the board, and reproducing them is a copyright matter. We reference them and link to the official source instead.

Practically, this changes what you should expect to see. A good IA coaching session ends with the student holding a list of things to change, not with a cleaner document in their inbox. If a provider's work product is a finished essay, you are buying something that can cost your child their Diploma, and the price is never the point.
bullets: Permitted: criterion explanation, feedback on the student's own draft, research-question triage, method teaching
Not permitted: writing, completing, ghost-drafting or editing coursework to completion

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what your child needs for a UAE university
paragraphs: A Fujairah student finishing IGCSEs or the Diploma and applying to a UAE institution meets the Ministry of Education's equivalency process. It converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE universities and employers can read. It is worth understanding in Year 10, not in the summer after Year 13, because it constrains subject choices.

On the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the detail families most often get wrong — and at least one ranking competitor page publishes a six-subject figure, which is simply incorrect.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, we publish no points threshold on this page. We have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and an invented figure on a page like this is the kind of thing a parent plans a year around. Ask the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process the Ministry performs, not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or expedites — we describe it and point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what we tell you instead of nothing
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider in this market writes as though a tutor is always available. None of them is. Coverage in a niche subject at a specific level at a specific hour is a real constraint, and concealing it is how families end up with a mismatched tutor two weeks before a paper.

Our position is to disclose it. If a UAE-based specialist in your child's subject and level is not free at the times that work for your family, we say so and offer the alternatives: a specialist based elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, a different slot with the right person, or a wait. What we do not do is substitute a generalist and leave you to discover the gap in week three. For a subject like IB Computer Science HL or Spanish ab initio, the wait is sometimes the right answer.

The matching conversation is short and specific. We ask for the board and specification code, the level, the school's assessment calendar, the two or three things the student keeps losing marks on, and the hours that actually work after the school run. A free trial lesson follows, which exists so you can judge the fit rather than so we can collect a deposit. If the fit is wrong, say so and we rematch; a mismatch identified in week one costs an hour, and one identified in week six costs a term.

A note on fallback delivery, because some providers hide it: if the specialist who fits your child is not in the UAE, the lesson still runs over live video on your timetable, and we tell you where the tutor is based before the first session rather than after it. Two ranking competitors route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying so. That is the thing we are trying not to be.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written against a European academic calendar fails in the UAE, because the shape of the year is different. The school year typically runs from late August or early September to late June or early July, with a long winter break in December and a spring break in the first half of the year. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, and when it lands in the spring it sits directly on top of the revision weeks before the June Cambridge series and the May IB session.

During Ramadan school days shorten and household routines invert. An afternoon session that worked in January becomes the worst possible hour, and the productive window shifts to after Iftar. Online delivery handles that better than any in-home arrangement can, because moving a video session to 21:00 costs nobody a journey. Plan for it rather than discover it: agree before Ramadan starts whether sessions pause, shorten or shift later.

The other calendar feature that catches families is travel. Fujairah households often travel during Eid and over the summer, and an exam-year student who loses six weeks of momentum in July pays for it in September. A short maintenance rhythm across a break — one session a fortnight, a past paper between them — holds more than it costs. Sessions can follow a family abroad, since the only requirement is a connection and a time both sides agree on.

Counted practically, a DP student has roughly four usable blocks between the start of DP1 and the May session: the first autumn term, the spring of DP1 when the IA work really begins, the autumn of DP2 when mocks land, and the final run-in. Three of those four are better spent on coursework and content than on past papers. Families who arrive in the fourth block asking for a grade change are asking for the only thing a tutor genuinely cannot supply at short notice.

process.title: Tell us the specification, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is short and precise: board and syllabus code, level, year group, school, and the two or three question types where marks keep going. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different courses. That one line removes most of the mismatch risk before anyone has spent an hour.

process.title: Send the school's assessment calendar
process.description: The dates that bind are usually the school's own: coursework deadlines, mock windows, report dates. A tutor working without them plans against the wrong clock. For a Fujairah student the coordinator's Internal Assessment deadline almost always falls earlier than anything the exam board sets.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session, no commitment, with the tutor we think fits. It exists so you can watch the match rather than take our word for it. Listen for whether the tutor diagnoses or lectures: a specialist spends the first twenty minutes finding out what the student can already do.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot around the real school run
process.description: Al Gurfa's short commute into the Fujairah city schools makes a 16:00 start realistic, which it is not in most of the UAE. Pick the hour you can hold every week for a term, not the hour that looks convenient this week. Consistency does more than frequency.

process.title: Review against marks, every half term
process.description: Every six weeks or so, compare the plan against actual marked work: school assessments, past paper scores by question type, coursework drafts. If the numbers have not moved on the things you targeted, change the plan or change the tutor. Say so early; a rematch in week two costs an hour.

whyPoints.title: Match on syllabus first, geography last
whyPoints.description: For Al Gurfa this is the whole argument. Filtering by driving distance in a small emirate leaves a handful of candidates, few of whom have taught your child's exact specification. Filtering by syllabus code and level first, then delivering over video, gives a coastal Fujairah family the same access as a Dubai one.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, as read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price. Three of six competitor pages examined published no price at all, and two quoted US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA or ADEK, no Ministry accreditation or affiliated with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what each body does and link to it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises, and implying one you do not hold is the most dangerous sentence in this market.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. We do not write, complete or produce an IA, Extended Essay, TOK essay or any coursework, and we decline the request. One page in this SERP sells finished Internal Assessments; the student, not the seller, carries that risk.

whyPoints.title: Exam dates that are correct for your country
whyPoints.description: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series. The February/March series is India-only, and pages quoting a March window to UAE parents are quoting another country's calendar. We also publish no unverified IB date, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and a wrong date is one a family plans around.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Gurfa?
faqs.answer: Within driving distance of Al Gurfa, for a specific syllabus at a specific level, usually not. Fujairah's private-school cohort in any single IB subject is small, so the number of people who have taught Cambridge 0620 Chemistry or IB Mathematics AA HL and live nearby is genuinely limited. Searches return results regardless, because businesses optimise for the query. IB Gram's answer is to match on syllabus and level rather than on distance, and to deliver the lesson over live video. That gives an Al Gurfa family access to specialists the local market cannot supply.

faqs.question: Will anyone from IB Gram teach in person at a Fujairah address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The URL you arrived on uses the phrase parents search, and we would rather target it honestly than imply something we do not sell. If an in-home tutor is what your family needs, the UAE market provides it at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour according to published 2026 rates, with travel time inside that figure.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, budget online tutoring from around AED 45, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500, and board specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Those are market figures from providers' own pages and Bestimate's 2026 survey, not an IB Gram price list. Fujairah is not separately surveyed, so treat the national bands as the guide and ask any provider whether the quoted rate is per hour or per session and whether it includes VAT.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Fujairah actually sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page quoting a March window to a UAE family. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. IB schools in the UAE sit the May session. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's own risk, so ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in before planning anything.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Fujairah, as it does in Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. That differs from Dubai, where KHDA oversees private education quality, and from Abu Dhabi, where ADEK handles licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has SPEA and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Practically, this means Fujairah has no emirate-level inspection portal of the kind Dubai parents are used to, so ask the school directly for its most recent reports rather than expecting to look them up.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE permit required to tutor privately in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is regulated through a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service page is the route to verify a claim.

faqs.question: Where does IA coaching stop being legitimate help?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach what each assessment criterion rewards, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, help narrow a research question that is too broad for the word limit, and teach the method or statistics the task requires. A tutor cannot write, complete, rewrite to completion or produce any part of it. IB Gram does not do that and declines the request. The distinction is not a formality: work that is not the student's own puts the Diploma at risk, and the student carries that consequence, not the provider.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking competitor page states six, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees, so verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: My child is in Dibba rather than Al Gurfa. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes the in-home maths considerably and the online maths not at all. Dibba sits north along the coast with a longer run to the Fujairah city schools, so an in-home tutor there is being paid for a substantial drive as well as an hour's teaching, and the pool willing to make that drive is smaller again. Over video the distance is irrelevant: the same specialist, the same rate, the same slot. For families on the northern coast the case for online delivery is stronger than it is in the city, not weaker.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as effective for an exam-year student?
faqs.answer: For an exam-year student the dominant variable is whether the tutor knows the specification, not whether they are in the room. Past papers screen-share and annotate well, mark schemes can be worked through line by line, and the session can be recorded and rewatched the night before a paper, which no kitchen-table lesson produces. The honest caveat is at the other end of the age range: a younger child who needs physical presence to stay on task is a harder case for video, and a parent within earshot for the first few weeks helps.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you. For less common options such as IB Computer Science HL or Spanish ab initio, a UAE-based specialist may not be free at the hours that suit your family. In that case we offer a specialist based elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, a different slot with the right person, or a wait, and we name which it is before you commit. We do not substitute a generalist and leave you to find the gap in week three. No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Will the Ramadan timetable disrupt our weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. School days shorten during Ramadan and the productive hours shift late, so the afternoon slot that worked in January becomes the wrong hour. Online delivery absorbs that easily because moving a session to 21:00 costs nobody a journey. The practical advice is to agree the arrangement before Ramadan begins, deciding whether sessions pause, shorten or shift later, rather than renegotiating week by week. When Ramadan falls in spring it sits on top of revision for the June Cambridge series.

faqs.question: How do I tell a real subject specialist from a general tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask one question: which paper do candidates reliably lose marks on in this specification, and why. Somebody who has taught Cambridge 0580 Extended or IB Chemistry HL answers in a sentence, naming a paper and a failure mode. Somebody who has not redirects to their degree or their years of experience. Follow it with the syllabus code and how many cohorts they have taken through it. Those two questions sort the field faster than any amount of filtering by distance, and they cost you nothing to ask.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to study Arabic alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Federal rules require UAE private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and Fujairah schools answer to the Ministry of Education on this. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai gives a sense of the detail involved: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, specified languages of instruction, and no use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission. Tutoring in these subjects therefore means supporting the school's own prescribed material rather than introducing anything else.

faqs.question: Is six weeks before the papers too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is late, and it is not useless. Six weeks is enough to change how a student handles question types they are losing marks on, to fix notation and working habits that cost method marks, and to make them faster under timing. It is not enough to install two years of missing content, and a provider who tells you otherwise is selling you something. The realistic plan at that point is diagnostic: find the three highest-yield question types from past paper evidence and work only on those.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being sceptical about when. Maths and Physics overlap enough that a single specialist often handles both well. Chemistry and Biology are further apart than they look at Higher Level. Across two boards or two levels the case weakens quickly. Our default is one specialist per subject at exam level, because the thing you are buying is specification depth, and the convenience of one timetable is rarely worth diluting that for a DP2 student.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-gu.closingHeading: Start with the syllabus code, not the postcode
fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-gu.closingBody: If you remember one thing from this page, make it the question to ask a prospective tutor: which specification, which level, and which paper do candidates lose marks on. A specialist answers it immediately. For an Al Gurfa family that question matters more than distance, because distance in a small emirate narrows the field to a handful of people who may not have taught your child's course at all. Send us the board and syllabus code, your child's year group and the school's assessment calendar, and take the free trial lesson before committing to anything. If the match is wrong, say so in week one and we will rematch.

Matching is done on the board, the code and the level, which is what makes a comparison between two schools in two emirates workable at all.

intro.heading: Three Dibbas, two authorities, one decision
paragraphs: There is an unusual fact about Dibba that no tutoring page in this market mentions and every family living here knows. The town is divided. Dibba Al-Fujairah belongs to Fujairah. Dibba Al-Hisn, immediately adjacent, belongs to Sharjah. And further along the coast Dibba Al-Baya sits in Oman's Musandam governorate, under a different national system entirely. Three places, one name, and schools answering to different authorities a short drive apart.

That makes comparison the natural shape for this page. A family in Dibba comparing two schools may be comparing institutions regulated by two different bodies with different approval processes. A family comparing curricula is choosing between the IB Diploma and an IGCSE route whose assessment models barely resemble each other. And a family comparing ways to get subject help is choosing between four genuinely different answers, not a preference about format.

The regulatory position is worth stating precisely because so much advice in this market gets it wrong. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Those are different frameworks meeting at a boundary within this town.

On Oman we make no claims. Dibba Al-Baya is in another country with its own national education system, and nothing on this page should be read as a statement about its rules. It is mentioned because it is part of the geography a family here lives with, and because a page that pretended the coast ended at the border would be describing somewhere else.

IB Gram matches Dibba students to subject specialists and delivers every lesson one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. In-home tutoring exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. On this coast the premium buys road rather than expertise.

What follows is seven comparisons: the three Dibbas, the IB Diploma against an IGCSE route as assessment systems, which route suits which student, the four ways of solving distance, the provider models, which subjects are realistically available locally and which are not, and what each option costs. Every table has information in each cell, because a comparison table whose answers are all yes is worse than no table.

One thing to settle before reading further, because it changes which tables matter. Decide whether your question is about one subject or about the whole programme. If a single subject is the problem, the comparison to read is the provider-model table and the availability table, and the decision is small. If the programme itself is not offered within reach, the comparison to read is the four-options table, and the decision involves the whole household. Families frequently arrive believing they have the first problem and discover halfway through that they have the second, which is an expensive order to find out in.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dibba.programmesIntro: Two systems and one bridge produce every comparison on this page. A Dibba family may be weighing them against each other rather than already committed to one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Standard and Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment mixes external papers with Internal Assessments marked by the school and moderated externally, so part of the grade is settled months before any paper. Breadth is compulsory: a language, a humanity, a science and mathematics are all required.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision on the east coast is limited, which is why so many Dibba families end up comparing a local IGCSE route against a Diploma elsewhere. UAE candidates sit the May session; this page publishes no specific IB date, because the board's own site is the only authority and your child's coordinator is the person to confirm them with.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Nine or ten subjects assessed by terminal written papers, with Core and Extended tiers at Cambridge and Foundation and Higher tiers in Pearson mathematics. Coursework exists in some subjects and is the exception rather than the model. Breadth comes from the number of subjects rather than from a required structure.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah candidates sit the Cambridge June and November series; the February and March window Cambridge runs is offered to India only. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The main alternative to the Diploma at post-16: three or four subjects taken deeper, with AS as a halfway point. No Extended Essay, no Theory of Knowledge, and no Internal Assessment culture, which makes the preparation almost entirely about papers and makes specialisation possible two years earlier.
programmes.countryNote: On the east coast this is often the more available route, simply because more schools offer it. It also satisfies the published Ministry of Education British track, which asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than E or grade 3.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment on a one-to-eight scale per criterion across eight subject groups, ending in the Personal Project. The alternative pre-16 route to an IGCSE entry, and the one that produces no external certificate, which is the detail families comparing the two most often miss.
programmes.countryNote: That missing certificate matters for a Dibba family weighing a possible move. An IGCSE student transferring at sixteen carries portable external grades; an MYP student carries a school report. Neither is better, but they are not interchangeable when the next school is in another emirate and makes its own entry decisions.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dibba.subjectsIntro: This list pairs the Diploma course with its IGCSE counterpart, because the comparison between them is what a Dibba family weighing two routes actually needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: DP AA and AI, HL and SL · IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1
subjects.description: The Diploma splits mathematics into four courses with an assessed exploration; IGCSE is one entry with terminal papers. The Diploma route forces an early decision about analytical against applied mathematics that an IGCSE route defers for two years.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Both cover bonding, energetics and organic chemistry at different depths. The real difference is the Diploma's scientific investigation, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, which requires laboratory access over weeks rather than a single examination.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: IGCSE rewards recall of relationships; the Diploma rewards algebraic derivation and uncertainty handling. A student strong on IGCSE physics can still find Diploma Paper 2 unfamiliar, because the question style asks for a derivation rather than a formula.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Content volume is heavy on both and command-term discipline decides the grade on both. The Diploma adds an investigation whose elapsed time is the longest of the three sciences, because growth or sampling cannot be compressed by working harder.

subjects.name: English
subjects.description: Four distinct courses behind one word. IGCSE First Language and English as a Second Language measure different things from each other, and Diploma English A assesses analysis of how meaning is made while English B assesses comprehension and production.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries the grade at both levels. The Diploma adds three commentaries of eight hundred words each, drawn from published articles, which is a scheduling task as much as an economics one.

subjects.name: Business
subjects.description: IGCSE rewards applying definitions to a case study in the paper. The Diploma requires a project built on a real organisation, which means the binding constraint is somebody else's willingness to respond, and on this coast the pool of accessible organisations is smaller.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Both test data representation and algorithmic thinking. The Diploma adds a solution with a real client and a working artefact, where scope is the trap: ambitious designs in the first year become unfinished documentation in the second.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: IGCSE rewards structured source questions and essay planning. The Diploma adds a historical investigation of around two thousand two hundred words, which depends on source availability and therefore on digital access rather than a physical archive here.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study specificity carries the top band on both, where a named place with a figure and a date outscores a general description. IGCSE map and graph skills are the most teachable part of the syllabus and routinely the least practised.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The Diploma accumulates a comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition across two years with nothing recoverable at the end. IGCSE art is a shorter commitment, and the difference in calendar discipline required is larger than the difference in talent required.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic studies
subjects.description: Required alongside any international curriculum under the federal rules, and assessed separately from the IB or IGCSE timetable. Support here means working with the school's own approved scheme rather than an external paper, which is a different kind of brief.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-dibba.regionsIntro: This list is the heart of the page's comparison, because on this coast the place name does not tell you which authority, which school or which journey you are dealing with.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Hisn

regions.note: About an hour south along the coast, holding most of the emirate's private-school provision and most of its exam centres. The default destination for a daily commute or an administrative errand.

sections.heading: The three Dibbas, and what changes between them
paragraphs: Start with the comparison nobody publishes, because it affects practical decisions a family here makes several times a year. Dibba Al-Fujairah, Dibba Al-Hisn and Dibba Al-Baya are three adjoining places with one name, split across two emirates and two countries. The schools in the first are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The schools in the second fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority. The third is in Oman and under a separate national system.

What changes is administration rather than examinations. A Cambridge or Pearson paper is identical either side of the Fujairah and Sharjah line, and so is an IB Diploma. What differs is who approves the school's fees and curriculum, who you escalate to when something administrative goes wrong, and which authority's published school listing is the one to check a name against. Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods; Fujairah's schools sit under federal supervision instead.

The practical advice is short. When comparing two schools across that line, ask each one which authority regulates it and check the name against that authority's own listing rather than against a directory site. When a question arises about fees or an assessment policy, the route depends on which side of the line the school sits, and getting that wrong costs a fortnight of being told to ask somebody else.

None of it changes the tutoring question. A tutor matched by board and syllabus code serves a student in Dibba Al-Fujairah and one in Dibba Al-Hisn identically, because the paper is the same. That is the useful thing about separating the administrative comparison from the academic one, and it is why this page runs them as separate tables.

sections.heading: The Diploma against an IGCSE and A Level route, as systems
paragraphs: This is the comparison a Dibba family most often has to make properly, because local provision may push them towards one route while their preference sits with the other. It deserves to be made on how each system assesses rather than on reputation, since both are well recognised and the difference that matters to a particular student is structural.

The Diploma is six subjects with required breadth, assessed through a mix of external papers and Internal Assessments marked internally and moderated externally, plus an Extended Essay at four thousand words and a Theory of Knowledge essay at one thousand six hundred. Part of the grade is therefore settled months before any examination, and the student's ability to manage long tasks against deadlines is itself being assessed.

An IGCSE route followed by A Levels is narrower and more terminal. Nine or ten IGCSE subjects assessed almost entirely by written papers, then three or four A Levels taken deeper with no comparable coursework culture. A student who performs well under examination conditions and poorly against long deadlines will usually do better here, and a student with the reverse profile will usually do better in the Diploma.

Both routes satisfy university requirements in the UAE and abroad, and neither is a soft option. The table sets them against each other on the dimensions that genuinely differ, and the row worth dwelling on is the one about coursework, because it is the structural difference that determines which students thrive and it is almost never discussed in these terms.

sections.heading: Which route suits which student, read from their own work
paragraphs: A prospectus cannot answer this and neither can a preference. What answers it is the student's existing marked work, read for behaviour rather than for marks. The question is not which system sounds better; it is which system rewards what this particular student already does and punishes what they already struggle with.

Four signals do most of the work. Does the student finish long tasks without a deadline immediately in front of them, or do they produce excellent work in the last forty-eight hours. Do they perform better in class assessments or in timed examinations. Do they have a settled subject direction at sixteen or not. And can they write at length with a sustained argument, which is a different skill from writing well.

A student who produces strong work only under immediate deadline pressure will find the Diploma's Internal Assessments and Extended Essay genuinely punishing, because the elapsed time is long and the deadline arrives once. A student who underperforms in timed conditions but works steadily all term will find an entirely terminal route punishing for the mirror reason. Both failures are structural rather than about ability.

This is also where an honest tutor says something uncomfortable. If a student is struggling across five of six Diploma subjects, the problem may be the programme rather than a shortage of tuition, and that conversation belongs in Year 11 or the first term of Year 12 rather than in Year 13. On this coast a route change may also mean a school change, which lengthens the lead time considerably.

sections.heading: Four ways to solve the distance, compared
paragraphs: A Dibba family whose local school does not offer what their child needs has four options, and they are rarely laid out together. Commute daily. Move the household. Use weekly boarding, which some east-coast students do. Or keep the local school and add remote specialist support. Each has a real cost and a real failure mode, and the right answer varies by how many subjects are affected.

The arithmetic favours different options at different scales. If one subject is the problem, remote support is clearly cheapest and least disruptive. If three or four subjects are unavailable, remote support becomes a large commitment running alongside a school that cannot deliver the course, and a commute or a move starts to look proportionate. If the whole programme is unavailable, only the last three options exist.

The option families most often underestimate is the daily commute, because a two-hour round trip is not two hours of cost. It is two hours plus the fatigue, plus the homework that does not get done in the car, plus every activity that no longer fits, for two years. Families who try it often shift to boarding or moving within a year, having paid for both the commute and the change.

IB Gram offers exactly one of these four and says so plainly: remote one-to-one support over live video. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses and home visits are a service we run in India only, so there is no fifth option on offer here. The table includes the others at their real cost because a family deciding between four things deserves all four, including the three we do not sell.
