sections.heading: The provider models, compared on structure rather than brand
paragraphs: Every page in this market compares itself favourably against an unnamed set of other platforms, which tells a parent nothing. A comparison of models is more useful, because each model has structural properties that hold whichever company operates it, and a family in Dibba should know which model they are buying before they buy it.

A tuition centre with premises carries fixed overheads and therefore tends to fill seats, which pushes towards small groups. A marketplace is cheap and transfers the whole vetting task to the parent, who is usually the person least equipped to assess mark-scheme familiarity. A freelance tutor may be excellent and is a single point of failure with no replacement mid-term. An agency does the matching and charges for doing it.

On this coast two of those models are thinly represented, which narrows the real choice. There are fewer tuition centres than in Dubai or Sharjah, and the freelance pool is smaller, so a family in Dibba is often choosing between a marketplace, an agency and an online platform whether they intended to or not. That is worth knowing before concluding that the local options have been exhausted.

Our own row in the table below is included because omitting it would make the comparison dishonest. IB Gram is an online matching platform: one-to-one over live video, matched on board, code and level, with a free trial lesson before payment and no in-home service anywhere in the UAE. The rate column names published market bands rather than our price, because we do not publish a rate card on these pages.

sections.heading: Which subjects are realistically available locally
paragraphs: No page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which makes every claim about availability unverifiable. Here is an honest version for the east coast, built on what the local school set can reasonably staff rather than on what any provider would like to promise.

Mathematics, the three separate sciences and English are taught everywhere, so local provision exists and the question is quality rather than existence. Economics, business studies, computer science and geography are taught in some schools and not others. Less commonly taken Higher Level Diploma options, second modern languages and specialised arts subjects may have no local teaching set at all, and in a cohort of a dozen that is not a surprising outcome.

What this means for a family comparing options is that the answer differs per subject rather than per school. A student needing mathematics support has a local market and a national one. A student needing a Higher Level option with a small national cohort has a national one and nothing else. Treating availability as a single yes or no produces the wrong decision in both cases.

Our own position follows the same honesty. For mathematics, the sciences, English and economics a match is usually available within days. For a less commonly taught Higher Level option it can take longer and occasionally cannot be made at all in a given month, and in that case you will be told rather than matched with somebody adjacent to the subject. On a small cohort a wrong match is also harder to replace quietly.

sections.heading: What each route costs, with every figure attributed
paragraphs: Comparisons without numbers are decoration, so here are the published ones. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45-150 per hour in the UAE, with one content platform publishing from AED 45-65 and one learning platform from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150-300, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

Above that, IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200-450 and beyond, with a UK agency quoting AED 270 and a UAE rate survey showing AED 200-450 or more. Premium named and examiner-track tutors reach AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one including travel sits at roughly AED 180-500, and from Dibba that travel component is larger than the survey averages assume.

Monthly, UAE surveys put a weekly hour at roughly AED 240-600 for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include online bundles from around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

sections.heading: The permit, the regulators, and what nobody can claim
paragraphs: Two separate things get confused in this market and they are worth separating. Schools are regulated; tutors are permitted. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Dubai's by KHDA, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's by ADEK, and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge. Those five bodies cover the country's private schools between them.

Tutors fall under a permit instead. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students, and the route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

Two cautions follow. Individuals tutoring without the permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has published no amounts, so any specific figure quoted to you has been invented. And the permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which matches ADEK's professional-ethics position for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi and is worth remembering in a small town.

What nobody in this market can claim is accreditation by any of those bodies. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and this page claims none. A KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute is a specific instrument with its own application sequence and annual renewal, held by businesses with premises.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do, in either system
paragraphs: The boundary is the same whichever route a Dibba family chooses, and it needs printing because services in this market sell completed assessed work and rank for searches a parent here might run. A tutor explains the criteria, works through published exemplars, questions whether a research question or an investigation design can carry the required depth, and reads the student's own draft to name the weak criterion.

What a tutor does not do is produce the work. Nobody here writes, finishes or edits to completion an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any coursework, in either system and at any price. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under board rules and the penalty falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid.

There is a parallel rule about materials. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are cited and linked here rather than reproduced or supplied, because redistribution is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure as well. A service offering a mark-scheme bundle is offering something it does not own.

The operational effect is identical in both systems: a block aimed at an assessed component finishes two weeks before the school's internal deadline, so the student makes the final decisions in their own words. In the Diploma that also means they can answer questions about it in a reflection session, which a student handed a polished draft cannot do convincingly.

process.description: The script, not the grade. It shows within minutes whether marks are being lost to timing, unwritten method lines, command terms or missing content, and those four need very different plans over very different timescales.

faqs.question: Which Dibba do you mean, and does it change what we can get?
faqs.answer: It changes the administration and not the teaching. Dibba Al-Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, Dibba Al-Hisn next door is part of Sharjah and its schools fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Dibba Al-Baya is in Oman under a separate national system. A Cambridge, Pearson or IB paper is identical either side of the UAE line, so a tutor matched by board and code serves both the same way.

faqs.question: Should my child do the IB Diploma or IGCSE and then A Levels?
faqs.answer: Decide it on assessment style rather than reputation. The Diploma is six subjects with required breadth, Internal Assessments, an Extended Essay at four thousand words and a Theory of Knowledge essay at one thousand six hundred, so part of the grade is settled long before any paper. An IGCSE and A Level route is nine or ten terminal papers then three or four taken deeper. A student who produces strong work only under immediate deadline pressure usually fares better on the terminal route.

faqs.question: How do we tell which route suits our child without guessing?
faqs.answer: Read their existing marked work for behaviour rather than marks, and ask four questions. Do they finish long tasks without a deadline immediately in front of them. Do they perform better in class assessments or in timed examinations. Do they have a settled subject direction at sixteen. Can they sustain an argument at length, which is different from writing well. Those four answers point at a route more reliably than any prospectus or open evening does.

faqs.question: What are the options if the Diploma is not offered near us?
faqs.answer: Four, and they should be weighed together. A daily commute to Fujairah City or beyond, which costs two hours plus fatigue plus every activity that no longer fits, for two years. Moving the household. Weekly boarding, which some east-coast students use. Or keeping the local school and adding remote specialist support, which only works where one or two subjects are the problem rather than the whole programme. We offer the fourth and set out the other three honestly.

faqs.question: Is a two-hour daily round trip really that hard to sustain?
faqs.answer: It is the option families most often underestimate. The cost is not two hours; it is two hours plus the tiredness, plus the homework that does not get done in a car, plus the activities that stop fitting, repeated for two academic years. Families who try it frequently move to boarding or relocate within a year, having paid for both the commute and the change. If the commute is the plan, agree in advance what the review point is.

faqs.question: Are there tuition centres on the east coast we should consider?
faqs.answer: Fewer than in Dubai or Sharjah, and that thinness changes the real choice. Centres with premises carry overheads and tend to fill seats, which pushes towards small groups, and a small group suits a student who is broadly on track and needs structure rather than one with a specific component problem. On this coast a family is often choosing between a marketplace, an agency and an online platform whether they intended to or not.

faqs.question: Which subjects simply are not available locally?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, the three separate sciences and English are taught across the local school set. Economics, business studies, computer science and geography appear in some schools and not others. Less commonly taken Higher Level Diploma options, second modern languages and specialised arts subjects may have no local teaching set at all, which in a cohort of a dozen students is arithmetic rather than a failing. Availability differs per subject, so treat it that way rather than as one answer per school.

faqs.question: Does crossing into Sharjah change my child's exams?
faqs.answer: No. A Cambridge, Pearson or IB qualification is set by the board and is identical in Dibba Al-Fujairah and Dibba Al-Hisn. What changes is who approves the school's fees and curriculum and who you escalate to administratively: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, while Fujairah's schools sit under federal supervision. Ask each school which authority regulates it and check the name on that authority's own listing.

faqs.question: Can we get one or two sessions just to help us decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a sensible use of a small amount of money. One or two sessions reading the student's own marked scripts against what each system rewards is a different exercise from reading a prospectus, and it ends with a written summary you keep. It is not a course and there is no ongoing commitment. The free trial lesson comes first in any case, runs on your child's own material, and you are welcome to watch it.

faqs.question: Is the Diploma's coursework an advantage or a risk for us?
faqs.answer: Both, depending on the student. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay mean a meaningful share of the grade is controllable months in advance, which rewards steady work and punishes last-minute work harder than a terminal paper does. For a student who manages long tasks, that is the Diploma's biggest advantage. For a student who produces everything in the final forty-eight hours, it is the structural reason the programme will be difficult.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects apply on both routes?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families comparing routes often forget to count them. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must otherwise follow the Ministry's general regulations. Those lessons sit on top of an IGCSE or Diploma timetable rather than instead of part of it, so both routes carry them and a revision plan that counts only the examined international subjects has assumed hours that do not exist.

faqs.question: Who should we ask when something administrative goes wrong?
faqs.answer: It depends which side of the line the school sits on, which is exactly why the question is worth settling in advance. For a school in Dibba Al-Fujairah the supervision is federal, through the Ministry of Education. For a school in Dibba Al-Hisn or Khor Fakkan it is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Getting that wrong costs a fortnight of being redirected, and the school's own office will tell you which applies if you ask directly.

faqs.question: What does a block of support actually cost here?
faqs.answer: From published bands, a qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300 per hour and a specialist AED 200-450 or more, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, a UK agency quoting AED 270 and one survey showing AED 200-450 and above. In-home sits at AED 180-500 including travel, and from Dibba the travel share is larger than those averages assume. None is our price and nothing here is a quote.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of an Extended Essay if we are short of time?
faqs.answer: No, in either system and at any price. A tutor explains the criteria, works through published exemplars, questions whether a research question can be answered in four thousand words, and reads the student's own draft to name the weak criterion. Supplying sentences or editing a draft to a finished state is malpractice territory, and the penalty falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. Blocks here finish two weeks before the internal deadline for that reason.

faqs.question: Is a tutor required to hold a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and asking is reasonable. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published amounts.

faqs.question: If we move schools mid-stage, what support does the transition need?
faqs.answer: Usually six to eight sessions in one subject, taken before the new course starts rather than after the first report. The gap is specific: what one system left the student with against what the next assumes in its first term, which is widest in mathematics and the sciences. On this coast transfers happen often, and the students who struggle are almost always the ones who arrived mid-year with nobody having mapped that gap in advance.

intro.heading: Six things that all call themselves a tutor near you
paragraphs: A parent in Fujairah City searching for help does not have one decision to make. They have two, and the second one is usually invisible. The first is which subject and which component needs work. The second is which kind of supplier to buy it from, and the options behave so differently that comparing their hourly rates alone is close to meaningless.

There are six models in this market. An agency takes a brief, assigns a tutor from its own bench and manages the relationship. A marketplace lists individuals and lets you pick, with the price set by the tutor. A freelancer is a single person, often a serving teacher, found by word of mouth in a city this size. A tuition centre runs small groups on its own premises under its own licence. The school's own support means a department running catch-up or a teacher giving extra time. An online platform matches a tutor remotely and delivers over video. All six exist on the east coast in some form, and they fail in different places.

The differences that matter are not the ones in the marketing. They are: how large the pool of available tutors actually is once you specify a board and a paper, whether a replacement is offered when a match goes wrong, whether the individual holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, what happens when nobody covers the subject you need, and how much of the fee is paying for travel rather than teaching. This page compares the six on exactly those points. Those five questions take about ten minutes to ask and they are the whole of due diligence in a market where every provider sounds the same on its own website.

The honest headline for Fujairah City is that market size, not model, drives most of the outcome. The emirate's private schools are few and their year groups are small, so the local pool behind an agency, a marketplace or a freelance recommendation is largely the same set of people. The model that changes the pool is the one that removes distance from the equation, because then the pool stops being the east coast and becomes everyone who teaches that component at that hour on Gulf Standard Time.

IB Gram is the online model, and the disclosure that belongs at the top rather than in a footnote is this: there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE. That service exists only in India. Fujairah City students are taught one-to-one over live video, matched to the IB component or the IGCSE syllabus code rather than to a street. Everything below, including the AED figures and the availability table, is written so that you could use it to buy from somebody else if that suits your family better.

programmes.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah these subjects sit under the federal Ministry of Education framework. The practical effect on an east-coast revision plan is collision: Arabic assessments regularly fall in the same fortnight as IGCSE mocks or Diploma internal deadlines, and the clash is best mapped in September rather than discovered in January.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-fujai.subjectsIntro: IB Diploma subjects as Fujairah City families ask about them, described by where the marks sit. Confirm current weightings and criteria through your child's subject teacher.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus carry the Higher Level load. The exploration loses most marks in reflection, where students describe their process instead of evaluating what the mathematics showed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling, with calculator technique examinable in itself. Modelling questions want assumptions stated explicitly, which candidates routinely leave implicit and lose marks for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions are marked literally: omit per unit mass or charge and the mark goes, however sound the understanding. Uncertainty handling in the data questions is weaker than the content knowledge around it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate Higher from Standard. Mechanism marks need curly arrows originating from a lone pair or a bond, and significant figures carried consistently.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the difficulty. Extended responses want a named mechanism in sequence, and examiners do not credit paraphrase of defined terms. Statistical reasoning on data is the common weak point.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams marked on labelled axes, labelled curves and the new equilibrium. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that essay-only revision does not prepare a candidate for.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus divides the grades. Answers drawn from the textbook rather than the case lose application and analysis marks even when the theory is correct.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Quotation followed by effect on the reader, sustained as an argument. Higher Level adds the essay component, where a controlling thesis matters more than coverage.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed on an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Marks are lost writing about the topic rather than about knowledge, its methods and its limits.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with formal supervision and a reflection requirement. Weak essays usually fail on research-question scope rather than on writing quality.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-fujai.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE half of the same market, by code, because paper structure follows the code rather than the subject name.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics 0580 / 4MA1
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Functions, graph transformations and conditional probability take the Extended marks. Unshown working is the largest avoidable loss, since method marks sit on nearly every question.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics 0625 / 4PH1
igcseSubjects.description: Potential dividers and the difference between potential difference and current are the reliable failure points. The alternative-to-practical paper wants a method with a named control variable.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry 0620 / 4CH1
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and qualitative-analysis tables dominate the lost marks. Half-equations must balance charge, and reaction conditions are asked for more often than names.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology 0610 / 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Defined vocabulary used precisely, mechanisms in sequence for six-mark questions, and graph answers that quantify the trend from the axes rather than describing its shape.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies 0450 / 4BS1
igcseSubjects.description: Break-even and cash flow answered in the abstract instead of with the figures in the stimulus. Evaluation marks need a judgement with a stated condition.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics 0455 / 4EC1
igcseSubjects.description: Data-response answers must use the extract's own figures. Imported textbook examples lose the application marks regardless of how accurate they are.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science 0478
igcseSubjects.description: The board's pseudocode conventions are examinable, so fluent coders still lose marks. Trace tables and the validation-versus-verification distinction are the dependable earners.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
igcseSubjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and the binomial theorem well beyond 0580. Local teaching capacity on the east coast is effectively nil, which is why it leads the availability table below.

sections.heading: Six ways to buy tutoring on the east coast, compared
paragraphs: Every competitor page in this market compares itself to an unnamed set of other platforms. Here instead is a comparison of models, which is the thing a parent is actually choosing between, with no brand named in the rows.

Read the fallback column first. It is the one nobody publishes and it decides what happens in the situation that actually arises: your child needs Additional Mathematics 0606 or a Pearson science paper, and the model you have chosen has nobody who teaches it. An agency with a local bench will offer the nearest available person. A marketplace will show you an empty search result. A freelance recommendation will become a polite no. A tuition centre will suggest a group that covers something adjacent. None of those is dishonest, but only one of them gets your child taught.

The permit column matters too, and it is easy to check. Any individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one. An organisation running premises is different: in Dubai that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval first and annual renewal at least thirty days before expiry. A centre and an individual are not the same legal animal and should not be assessed as if they were.

What the table does not show is quality, because model does not determine it. A serving teacher found by word of mouth in Fujairah City may be the best teacher your child ever has. The table shows structural risk: how deep the bench is, what happens when it is empty, and who is accountable when the match fails.

sections.heading: IB Diploma or IGCSE: which instrument is measuring your child
paragraphs: Households on this coast often contain one of each, and the two are assessed so differently that a single tutoring approach cannot serve both. Knowing which instrument applies decides where the hours go.

The Diploma puts a meaningful share of the grade inside work the student produces over months, marked against lettered criteria whose descriptors are published in advance. That makes it the most controllable part of the course and the part most often left until it is too late to control. It also carries a core, with Theory of Knowledge and a 4,000-word Extended Essay, assessed on submitted work with no paper to revise for. Written papers have fixed weightings that differ between Higher and Standard Level, and Higher Level is not Standard plus an extra paper; the added depth changes what the shared papers may ask.

IGCSE puts nearly everything in externally examined papers at the end. There is no slow-burn component to manage, which removes one kind of stress and adds another: a bad fortnight in June cannot be offset by good coursework. The decisive structural feature is tiering. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade available and an Extended entry raises both the ceiling and the difficulty. In a small market that decision is sometimes taken for timetabling reasons, which is a good reason to ask the school to revisit it rather than treating it as settled.

For a tutor the practical difference is what the first session looks like. With a Diploma student it opens a draft and a criterion descriptor. With an IGCSE student it opens a marked paper and a mark scheme. Both are specific work. Neither is a general review of the subject.

sections.heading: Availability on this coast, and the fallback nobody discloses
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-local delivery behind a phone number from another country. The table below does the opposite: it names where availability on the east coast is genuinely thin and what the fallback is.

The pattern is predictable once you understand the supply. Core IGCSE subjects taught in every school on the coast have the deepest cover, because the people who teach them are numerous. Subjects taken by small numbers of strong candidates have almost none, because the teaching population is tiny everywhere and vanishing on a coastline with this few schools. Diploma subjects sit in between, with the complication that there is no Diploma provision inside Fujairah at all, so there is no local teaching population to draw on in the first place.

The fallback that matters is honesty about timing. If a specialist for a scarce paper is not free this week, the useful answer is a date or a no, not a substitute who will be learning the syllabus alongside your child. That is how a family loses a term they cannot recover, and it happens most often in exactly the subjects where the parent is already anxious and least able to judge the match.

Where a subject is covered, the match is made on the component rather than the label: the Cambridge or Pearson code for IGCSE, the paper or criterion for a Diploma subject. Where it is not covered, you get told. The table is deliberately specific enough to be checkable against what we actually offer you when you ask.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Revision plans built on a European academic year fail in the UAE, and nowhere more predictably than in the weeks before a May or June series.

Two things interact. The UAE school year has its own shape, with the long break in summer and term dates that do not match the northern European pattern, and Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the exam season shifts from one year to the next. When Ramadan falls close to the final revision window, school days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and the useful study hours move to after Iftar. A plan that assumed a 5pm session four times a week simply stops happening.

The workable response is to schedule against the family's actual day rather than against a template. Sessions after Iftar work well for older students and are a normal request rather than an imposition. Where a student fasts and has a morning exam, the revision pattern needs to protect mornings, which means moving the heavy cognitive work earlier in the plan rather than cramming it into the last fortnight. Because lessons are delivered over live video, a slot can move to 9pm without anyone driving anywhere, which is a practical advantage of the model rather than a marketing one.

The other calendar to put on the same sheet is the school's internal one. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are assessed on the school's own schedule, and those assessments land alongside mocks and Diploma internal deadlines with some regularity. Mapping board dates, school internal dates and Ramadan onto one page in September is twenty minutes of work that prevents the collision every east-coast family describes after it has happened.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the main course
paragraphs: No competitor page in any of the researched clusters has a section on this, and every UAE family lives with it. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, so these subjects run all year beside the IB or IGCSE course.

The most detailed public statement of how they are organised is KHDA's guidance for Dubai schools, and it is specific. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

One rule constrains tutoring directly: for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support therefore means working within the school's prescribed material rather than importing an alternative syllabus, which is a narrower brief than families expect when they ask for Arabic help. KHDA also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools hold appropriate approval to teach those subjects, which is a fair credential question to ask of anyone, anywhere.

For a Fujairah City family the practical consequence is to treat these as a fixed claim on the week rather than an afterthought. They occupy timetable space, they carry assessments, and they cannot be dropped to make room for IGCSE revision. Planning around them is easier than planning despite them.

sections.heading: The one thing the cheap end of this market actually sells
paragraphs: There is a model this page has not listed in the table, because it is not tutoring. It needs naming anyway, because it ranks for these searches and it is the single largest risk to a student on this coast.

At least one provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The page is thin, it has no FAQs, and it offers finished assessed work for a fee. Buying that does not save a student time; it puts their entire qualification at risk, because submitting work that is not their own is a malpractice matter for the board and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller. A parent under deadline pressure in February is exactly the person that offer is designed for.

The legitimate boundary is clear and worth stating positively. A tutor can teach a method, model it on a different question, interrogate whether a research question is answerable, point at a criterion descriptor and ask the student to show where their draft meets it, and explain why a paragraph earned nothing. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete, edit to finish or produce assessed work. IB Gram does not offer that and will not, and a provider that does should be read as telling you how it treats every other rule as well.

There is a materials boundary too. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should reference and link them and work from copies the student legitimately holds through school, not hand out reproduced packs. Any site offering downloadable mark scheme bundles is distributing someone else's property, and for unreleased material that is a more serious problem than copyright alone.

faqs.question: What should I actually compare when looking for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: Compare models before you compare prices. An agency, a marketplace, a freelancer, a tuition centre, school support and an online platform differ on how deep the bench is, whether a replacement is offered when a match fails, whether the individual holds the MoHRE private tuition permit, and what happens when nobody covers your subject. In a market this small, all the local models draw on the same school staff rooms, so the one variable that genuinely changes the pool is whether distance is part of the requirement.

faqs.question: Is an agency better than finding a freelance tutor in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in quality terms, because the model does not determine the teacher. An agency gives you a replacement if the match fails and takes responsibility for the brief; a freelancer found by word of mouth may be an excellent serving teacher at a lower price with no fallback at all. The structural difference shows up on the day the subject is not covered: the agency offers its nearest available person, the freelancer offers a polite no, and you start again.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor in Fujairah City is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask directly. Individuals giving private lessons need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, which covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Since there is no fee, there is no cost reason to be without one. A centre with premises is different and holds an educational services permit from the relevant emirate authority instead.

faqs.question: Can a Fujairah City school teacher tutor their own pupils for a fee?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a question for the school rather than an assumption. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against current policy. In a small market the conflict arises often enough to be worth raising before money changes hands.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma or IGCSE harder to support from the east coast?
faqs.answer: The Diploma, because there is no Diploma provision inside Fujairah, so there is no local teaching population at all to draw on. Those students are enrolled outside the emirate or boarding, and they are often working to internal deadlines with a supervisor who may be allocated outside their subject specialism because the cohort is small. IGCSE at least has local teachers for the core subjects. Both are supported online by component, which is the only route that does not depend on local supply.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost across the models in AED?
faqs.answer: Marketplaces and budget platforms run AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Agencies and established online providers sit at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Anything delivered in-home runs AED 180 to 500 because the journey is inside the price, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table. Exam-year specialists reach AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270, and the premium end is quoted at AED 650.

faqs.question: Which IB session do UAE schools sit?
faqs.answer: The May session is the one UAE schools sit. Results and session dates for the IB are not restated here, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated check for this project, and publishing an exam date a parent acts on without confirming it would be worse than publishing nothing. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages. For Cambridge and Pearson the dates are sourced and appear elsewhere on this site.

faqs.question: Will a tutor work around Ramadan timings for a Fujairah family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and after-Iftar sessions are a normal request rather than a concession. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the exam season changes, and when it falls near a final revision window school days shorten and useful study hours move later. Because lessons run over live video, a slot can move to 9pm without anyone driving anywhere. The better move is still to shift heavy work earlier in the plan rather than compress it.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect an IGCSE plan in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: They affect the calendar and the available hours. UAE private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum, assessed on the school's internal schedule rather than the board's, and those assessments regularly land in the same fortnight as mocks. For these subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, so any support must work within the school's own material rather than substituting another syllabus.

faqs.question: What happens when nobody on the east coast teaches the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get a date or a no. Additional Mathematics 0606 has effectively no local teaching population on this coast, Computer Science 0478 is very limited, and no Diploma subject has a local base because the emirate has no Diploma provision. The dishonest resolution is a substitute who learns the syllabus alongside your child, which is how a family loses a term. The honest options are to wait for the right match, start on an adjacent paper where the diagnosis still transfers, or look elsewhere.

faqs.question: Would a Fujairah City tuition centre group class be better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It can be, for a student whose problem is pace and motivation rather than a specific component. Group teaching is cheaper per hour and the social pressure helps some students work. It is the wrong purchase when the loss is specific, because a group cannot stop to examine why one student's half-equation did not balance charge. From Dibba or the northern coast a weekly centre commitment in Fujairah City is also impractical, which removes the option on logistics alone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write my child's Internal Assessment if we are out of time?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who offers to should be avoided. At least one provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter for the board, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. What a tutor legitimately does is teach the method, model it on a different question, interrogate the research question and give criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own draft, which is slower and survives submission.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office or a centre in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: No. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor visits a UAE address. Tuition for Fujairah City families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with home visits offered only in India. We say that plainly because two of the pages ranking for these searches show a UAE footer address on a page about a different emirate, and one routes UAE parents to a phone number in another country.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Fujairah City family start lessons?
faqs.answer: For a core IGCSE subject with a named code, usually within a few days, because the free trial can be scheduled as soon as a tutor matching the paper has a slot. For a scarce paper it can take longer and you will be told how long rather than offered the first available person. The slower step is usually ours rather than yours: finding the right component match takes time, and rushing it produces the rematch nobody wants in week three.

faqs.question: What makes the first session useful rather than just introductory?
faqs.answer: Bringing something already marked. A paper with examiner or teacher comments on it, or a Diploma draft with the criterion the teacher flagged, turns the hour into a diagnosis instead of a conversation about how things are going. The tutor sorts the lost marks into content, command term, working shown and timing, and tells you which column is largest. That written summary is what the block of sessions is then built against.

intro.heading: The real question is competence, not proximity
paragraphs: Nobody types a near-me search because they want a short drive. They type it because they want somebody real, somebody accountable, somebody who knows the thing their child is sitting. Distance is a proxy for all of that, and in a market like Fujairah's it is a bad proxy, because the small size of the private-school sector means the nearest available adult is often the least likely to have taught Higher Level Chemistry or Extended-tier Economics. Merashid families discover this quickly and then have no second filter to fall back on.

This page supplies the second filter. Not credentials in the abstract, which are easy to assert and hard to check, but specific questions whose answers cannot be faked by somebody who has not taught the course. A tutor who has marked a Cambridge Extended paper can tell you in one sentence where candidates lose marks on it. A tutor who has supervised an Internal Assessment can name the criteria and the word cap without looking. A tutor who has not can only talk about potential, enthusiasm and results in general terms, and both kinds of person sound equally reassuring on a phone call.

That matters more here than it would in a larger market, and it matters for an uncomfortable reason. The competitor pages researched for this search include real liabilities: self-published star ratings, statistics with no sample or method, pages claiming a regulator relationship that cannot exist, and one page selling completed Internal Assessment work outright. A Merashid parent working through a shortlist is not only choosing between competent and less competent. They are also filtering out claims that should not be on a page at all.

IB Gram's own position belongs in the same paragraph as that warning rather than after it. Lessons for Merashid students are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits exist only in India. It is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, it runs no UAE premises, and nothing on this site claims otherwise.

Use what follows on us as well as on everyone else. The twelve questions work in any trial lesson. The permit check takes one question and costs nothing. The red flags are observable from a page without speaking to anybody. And the coverage section says plainly what happens when the honest answer to a Merashid request is that no specialist is free, which is a sentence no page researched in this market contains.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-meras.programmesIntro: Verification differs by programme, because what a tutor needs to know differs. Three programmes cover almost every Merashid enquiry, and each has its own set of questions that cannot be bluffed.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by terminal paper, with tiering and in the sciences a board-dependent practical arrangement. A tutor who knows the course can state the syllabus code, the papers, the component weightings and whether a practical exam exists, without reference to anything.
programmes.countryNote: The decisive question for a Merashid family is which board. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component worth twenty per cent, sat as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam. A tutor who does not ask you which board before the first lesson has told you something already.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum. Internal assessment carries weight in every subject, which means every Diploma tutor must know criteria and word caps rather than content alone.
programmes.countryNote: Local Diploma capacity in Fujairah is limited, so a Merashid student on this route is often at a school in another emirate or boarding. The verification question that separates real Diploma experience from adjacent experience is about the core: ask what the Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary limit is, and why research design cannot be fixed after data collection.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with a Personal Project in the final year marked out of 24 across planning, applying skills and reflecting. Terminal papers do not exist in the earlier years.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme most often misunderstood by tutors whose experience is examination-based, because there is no paper to practise. The test question is to ask what the four criteria are in the subject concerned. A tutor who treats the Middle Years Programme as a junior Diploma will teach content where the marks are being lost on communication.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-meras.subjectsIntro: For each subject, the single question a parent can ask that reveals whether the tutor has taught it. None of these can be answered convincingly by somebody who has only taught the subject in general.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask what Paper 3 is and what it is worth. The answer is the Higher Level extended-response problem paper at twenty per cent, usually reached last by schools and therefore the least practised component in the Diploma. A tutor who has not taught the course will not volunteer that.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask how it differs from Analysis and Approaches in what the examiner wants, not in content. The answer involves interpretation written in context and calculator technique being examinable in itself, which is a different skill from getting the right number.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask what the Internal Assessment is marked on and what the word cap is. Four criteria at six marks each — research design, data analysis, conclusion, evaluation — and 3,000 words. Then ask which of the four cannot be repaired after data collection.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask what sits in Paper 1 besides multiple choice. The answer is a data-analysis section, and the follow-up is that Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent against Paper 2's forty-four. A tutor who thinks Paper 1 is purely multiple choice is working from an older guide.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask the difference between describe and explain in a mark scheme and what it costs. A specialist gives an example from a paper. This is the highest-volume avoidable loss in the subject and the quickest thing to fix, so a tutor who does not mention it has not marked much.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask what the portfolio consists of and the word limit per piece. Three commentaries of no more than 800 words each, on real published articles. Then ask what separates a judgement from a two-sided list in an evaluate question.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what the Individual Oral requires and what it is worth. A global issue traced through two texts, at thirty per cent at Standard Level. Then ask what the HL Essay adds and at what weighting, which is twenty per cent.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask about the pre-released case and when work on it should start. The answer is months ahead rather than weeks, because the case can be analysed before the paper is written. A tutor unfamiliar with it will treat the Higher Level paper as another unseen.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Ask what the solution-development Internal Assessment assesses besides the working product. Documentation and evidence of a design process, which is exactly where strong programmers lose marks. A tutor who is a developer rather than a teacher often misses this.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Ask why students who choose it as a lighter option find it demanding. The answer combines scientific data handling with evaluative writing about human systems, which is two skill sets rather than a reduced version of one.

fujairah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-meras.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same approach on the IGCSE side: one question per subject whose answer requires having taught the specification rather than the subject.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980; Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask how Cambridge splits the papers against how Edexcel does, and what that changes for practice. One board's entry includes a non-calculator paper; the other runs two calculator papers. A tutor who does not distinguish them will prepare for the wrong one.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625; Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask whether a practical exam exists. Cambridge: a twenty per cent component, practical test or alternative paper. Edexcel: none, with practical skills in the theory papers. This single answer identifies board experience immediately.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620; Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask which marks are the fastest to recover in eight weeks. The answer is organic reaction conditions and the exact wording of ion and gas tests, because both are pure recall. A tutor who says the whole syllabus has not marked scripts.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610; Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask where candidates lose marks in genetics. The answer involves writing crosses out in full rather than in shorthand, and the language of water potential in osmosis questions. Both are notation problems rather than knowledge problems.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a First Language (0500; Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask what the summary question penalises. Lifted phrasing from the passage, because the marks are for the student's own words. A tutor who treats it as a comprehension exercise will coach the wrong behaviour for a term.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455; Edexcel 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask what a diagram has to show to earn its marks. Labelled axes, correct initial position, correct direction of shift, and the new equilibrium identified. Marks go individually, and the prose around a wrong diagram cannot recover them.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450; Edexcel 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask what the commonest error is on an insert-based paper. A correct textbook point applied to a business the insert does not describe. A tutor who has marked these will say it without prompting, because it dominates the scripts.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (0478; Edexcel 4CP0)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask whether pseudocode is marked on syntax. It is not; it is marked on logic, which students find counterintuitive after a year of Python. A tutor who insists on exact syntax is teaching programming rather than the specification.

igcseSubjects.name: Geography (0460; Edexcel 4GE1)
igcseSubjects.description: Ask what separates a top-band case-study answer. A named example with figures rather than a generic description. Fujairah's own coastline and water scarcity are usable material, and a tutor who knows the region will suggest it.

sections.heading: Twelve questions that separate a specialist from a generalist
paragraphs: These work in a trial lesson, on a phone call, or in a message, and they share one property: a person who has taught the course answers each in a sentence, while a person who has not produces a paragraph about approach. You do not need to know the right answers in advance. You need to notice the difference between a specific answer and a general one, which anyone can do.

Start with identification. Which syllabus code or which level is my child sitting, and how would you confirm it? A specialist asks this before you do. Then: what are the components and what is each worth? Then: does a practical exam exist on this specification? Then: what are the three places candidates most reliably lose marks on this paper? Four questions, under two minutes, and most shortlists halve.

Then move to assessed coursework, because that is where the real divergence appears. What is the word cap on this piece? What is it marked on? Which criterion cannot be repaired once the work has been done? And what would you do if my child asked you to write a paragraph of it? The last question is not technical, and the right answer is a refusal with a description of the alternative. An answer that treats it as negotiable has told you what happens the week before the deadline.

Finish with process. How will you mark work between sessions? What will you send me after four weeks? What happens if the match is wrong? And what happens if you become unavailable? None of those requires subject knowledge and all of them predict whether the engagement survives a term. The table sets each question against the shape of a good answer and the shape of a weak one.

sections.heading: Checks a Merashid parent can actually make
paragraphs: Most credential claims cannot be verified by a parent, which is why the questions above matter. Two things can be checked, and both are worth doing. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

Because it costs nothing and the ministry's own service page states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system, there is no reasonable explanation for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source and is deliberately omitted.

The second check is the entity. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it needs a Knowledge and Human Development Authority educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. If a provider describes itself as holding such a permit, it has a number, and the number can be checked with the authority. If it cannot produce one, the claim should not be on the page.

There is also a rule limiting who may teach your child. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as press-reported rather than exact wording and check the current policy document, but the principle holds nationally: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to engage privately.

sections.heading: How this market oversells, in patterns you can spot from a page
paragraphs: Sixty-odd competitor pages were fetched and read for this market, and the overclaiming follows a small number of repeated shapes. Knowing the shapes lets a Merashid parent filter a shortlist without speaking to anybody, which is faster than any conversation.

The first shape is the self-published rating. Several pages display a star rating and a review count that exist only on that page, with no countable, attributable reviews behind them. On one, two different ratings and review counts appear in the same document. On another, a five-star figure drawn from twenty reviews sits beside a claim of 2,500 students taught. Review markup that is not backed by real, dated, attributable reviews is a structured-data violation and, as a commercial representation, a consumer-protection exposure.

The second is the statistic with no sample, date or method. Satisfaction percentages, median tutor scores, proportions of students achieving top grades: all presented as facts, none with the underlying data. A figure without an n and a date is not evidence. The third shape is the accreditation claim — a regulator or board described as having approved, accredited or licensed the provider, which for a tutoring platform is not a thing that exists. That phrase is the single most dangerous sentence available to a page in this market.

The fourth is the school list. Pages display twenty-five or more school names under a heading implying a relationship, with no relationship in existence, and at least one lists a school that appears not to exist. Writing that students supported attend a school is accurate; presenting the school as a partner or client is not. The fifth and worst is the essay mill: a page in this search result sells completed Internal Assessment work at a fixed price, which is an academic-integrity breach whose consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: What a diagnostic proves that a curriculum vitae cannot
paragraphs: There is one piece of evidence that settles the competence question better than any claim, and it costs one or two sessions. A diagnostic: a full past paper sat under genuine exam timing, marked against the official mark scheme rather than a model answer, returned with every lost mark attributed to a cause. The document it produces tells you about your child, and the quality of the document tells you about the tutor.

A specialist's diagnostic looks specific. Lost marks are grouped: content not known, content known but not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method correct but not written out, time ran out. Each group has a count and examples. The topics named are narrow — two-step mole conversions, bounds, water-potential language — rather than broad. And the remedies attached to each are different from one another, because the causes are different.

A generalist's diagnostic looks like a school report. It says the student needs to revise more, build confidence and practise past papers. All three may be true and none of them is actionable, because they do not distinguish between a student who cannot do the content and a student who can do it but not in forty minutes with a clock running. Those two children need opposite interventions, and giving either the other one wastes a term.

The practical move for an undecided Merashid family is to buy the diagnostic alone, with no commitment beyond it. You keep the document whatever happens next, it can be taken to a different tutor, and it converts the shortlist decision from a judgement about people into a comparison of two pieces of work. That is a much easier decision than the one a near-me search presents you with.

sections.heading: When the honest answer is that nobody near Merashid knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Sometimes the search returns nothing useful because nothing useful exists locally, and the honest version of that sentence appears on no page researched for this market. Fujairah's private-school sector is small, local Diploma capacity is limited, and for Higher Level Chemistry, Higher Level Computer Science, Visual Arts or a less common language, the number of people within a reasonable drive of Merashid who have taught that course recently may be zero. Paying an in-home premium of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour does not alter that figure.

What changes the answer is removing geography from the problem. Online one-to-one delivery replaces who lives nearby with who has taught the course, which is the only move that affects the outcome rather than the convenience. That is the whole argument for the format, and it is strongest precisely in the emirates competitor pages ignore: Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain are named by none of the pages researched across ten query clusters.

Even then, availability is finite and should be stated rather than implied. Common subjects at common levels staff quickly. Higher Level sciences and mathematics staff reasonably. Minority Higher Level subjects take longer, and in one specific evening slot sometimes cannot be filled at all. In that case the right answer is a realistic timeframe, an alternative slot, or a straight no with the reason — never the nearest available generalist offered as a specialist.

Ask the question in those words of everybody on your shortlist, including us. The answer is informative either way. A provider that says everything is always available immediately in every subject at every level in any slot, in a market this size, has answered a different question from the one you asked.

sections.heading: Materials, mark schemes and the authorship line
paragraphs: Specifications, subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge and Pearson. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and where a paper is unreleased it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct practice is to reference and link, so a parent reads the authoritative document rather than a third party's version of it. Everything factual on this page should be confirmed that way.

On assessed work the line is authorship, and it is worth stating in the exact terms a tutor should be able to repeat. A tutor may teach the content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach the student to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the sentences become theirs.

The limits are part of the same competence. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the exhibition commentary at 950, the Diploma sciences investigation at 3,000, and each Economics commentary at 800. Those numbers are verification questions as much as planning facts, because a tutor who does not know them is not working from the guide, and a draft over a cap loses marks for a reason that has nothing to do with its quality.

Last, the statement that belongs on every page in this market and appears on almost none. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, and publishes no star rating or statistic it cannot evidence.

sections.heading: Putting it together: a Merashid shortlist in one evening
paragraphs: The whole method fits into a single evening and one trial lesson, which is faster than most families spend on the decision anyway. Step one is filtering from the pages themselves, without contacting anybody: remove anything carrying a self-published star rating, an unsourced statistic, an accreditation claim, a long school list implying a relationship, or any offer to produce coursework. In this market that removes a surprising proportion of the field before you have spoken to a single person.

Step two is the specification message. Send the subject, the level or tier, and the syllabus code, and ask two of the questions from the twelve: the components with their weightings, and where candidates lose marks on the main paper. The replies sort themselves within a day, because a specialist answers in a sentence and everybody else answers in a paragraph about their approach.

Step three is the trial lesson, run in the slot you actually intend to use rather than a convenient one, with you able to listen in. Watch whether the tutor asks which board before teaching anything. Watch whether your child can follow the explanation, which is the better predictor of the two. Ask the coursework-authorship question at the end, and treat anything other than a clear refusal as the answer.

Step four is the diagnostic in the first fortnight and a written risk list, then the same list again a month later with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged. That is the loop. It costs one evening, one trial lesson and two sessions, and it replaces a near-me search with something that actually tells you whether the person teaching your child knows the paper your child is sitting.

A person who has taught the course answers each in a sentence; a person who has not produces a paragraph about their approach. faqs.question: Should a Merashid parent trust the star rating printed on a tutoring page?

faqs.question: Can a tutoring platform be approved by KHDA or the Ministry of Education?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense the phrase implies. A Knowledge and Human Development Authority educational services permit is issued to a training institute with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the steps and annual renewal at least thirty days before expiry. faqs.question: What should I ask about a tutor's permit before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and takes a stated two working days through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service. Because it is free and fast there is no reasonable explanation for not holding one. Also ask which school employs them, if any, and whether your child is in their class, because tutoring one's own enrolled students is barred.

faqs.question: A tutor offering lessons in Merashid says they are a board examiner. Does that help my child?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unverifiable unless they can evidence current status, and treat the implication as wrong regardless. Examiner experience does not provide access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or paper content, and any suggestion that it does should end the conversation. The useful version of the same claim is demonstrable instead: ask where candidates lose marks on a named paper. Somebody who has marked scripts answers that precisely, whether or not they currently hold an examiner contract.

faqs.question: What does a good diagnostic report actually look like?
faqs.answer: Specific and grouped. Lost marks sorted into six causes — content not known, content not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method not written out, time ran out — each with a count and examples, and narrow named topics rather than broad ones. A report that says the student should revise more, build confidence and do past papers is a school report, not a diagnostic, and it cannot distinguish between a child who does not know the content and one who cannot produce it under timing.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a diagnostic with no further commitment?
faqs.answer: Often yes, especially when you are undecided. One or two sessions produce a document about your child that you keep regardless of what happens next, and it can be taken to any other tutor. It also converts a difficult judgement about people into a comparison of two pieces of work, which is much easier. The quality of the document is itself the strongest evidence you will get about whether the tutor knows the specification.

faqs.question: What are the word limits a Diploma tutor should know without checking?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition commentary at 950, the sciences investigation at 3,000, and each Economics commentary at 800. These function as verification questions as well as planning facts: a tutor who does not know them is not working from the subject guide. A draft over a cap loses marks for a reason unconnected to its quality, which is entirely avoidable.

faqs.question: What is the right answer if I ask a tutor to write one paragraph?
faqs.answer: A refusal, followed by a description of what they would do instead: explain the criterion, show how a comparable passage is built, read what your child writes and say where it falls short. Anything that treats the request as a matter of degree has told you what will happen in the week before the deadline, when the pressure is real and you are not in the room. A page in this search result sells completed assessed work outright, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Why does the near-me search work badly in Fujairah specifically?
faqs.answer: Because the private-school sector is small and local Diploma capacity is limited, so the pool of people who have taught a particular course recently is small and in some subjects empty. Merashid, Sakamkam, Al Faseel and Al Gurfa draw on the same pool, so moving a few kilometres changes nothing on the shortlist. Distance is a proxy for competence and in this market it is a poor one, which is why specification questions replace it rather than supplement it.

intro.heading: The crossing from Year 11 is the real problem here
paragraphs: A near-me search in Sakamkam looks like a question about distance and is usually a question about a transition. The pattern is consistent: a student is finishing Extended IGCSE, the family is weighing an IB Diploma against A Levels, and nobody within reach can explain what actually changes between the two in each subject. Fujairah's private-school sector is small and its local Diploma provision is limited, so the people who have taught both systems to the same student are rare on this side of the Hajar mountains. That is a supply problem, not a geography problem, and no amount of driving solves it.

Sakamkam is inland and north-west of Fujairah city, nearer the mountain edge, and the afternoon return from the coastal schools runs longer than the map suggests. The consequence for tutoring is timing: a session that waits on somebody else's journey drifts, and a weekly homework cycle collapses once the sessions stop landing where they were booked. An online slot at 17:30 is still 17:30 in February. That is a small practical argument, but over two years of Diploma deadlines it does more work than it sounds like.

IB Gram teaches Sakamkam students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India, and the same statement appears on all of the country pages this site publishes. The URL contains the phrase near me because that is what parents type, and the right response to it is a straight answer rather than a redirect buried in the eighth paragraph. There is a real in-home market here, priced on published figures at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and what it buys inland from this coast is a narrower subject list.

So this page is written around the crossing rather than around the neighbourhood. There is a subject-by-subject map of the gap between Extended IGCSE and Higher Level Diploma, which nobody in this market publishes in a structured form. There is the Ministry of Education equivalency picture with the British-track figures quoted because they are sourced and the IB figure omitted because it is not. There is what the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement adds to a UAE school week, which no competitor page researched for this market addresses at all. And there is an honest account of which subjects can be staffed and which cannot.

A note on dates before any of it. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project. Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session; confirm every date through your child's coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates used elsewhere on this site are taken from those boards' own published guidance and are named by month rather than by year, so that the page stays true after a session has passed.
