sections.heading: The core, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Three parts of the Diploma are self-managed, and all three fail the same way. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the internally assessed component in each subject run to dates the school sets rather than to the examination timetable, and nobody rings a bell. A Fujairah student with a supervisor who teaches a different subject, in a school where one person coordinates the whole programme, is more exposed to this than a student in a large Dubai cohort with a dedicated core team.

The most useful intervention is also the earliest and the cheapest: narrow the research question until it can be answered in the word limit, and read the criteria before writing anything. Most weak Extended Essays are not badly written. They are answering a question nobody could answer in four thousand words, chosen in a week when the student was busy, and the problem was baked in before the first draft. The same is true of the mathematical exploration and the scientific investigation: the research question decides the ceiling.

Where the line sits should be stated before anybody pays for anything. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss the student's own ideas with them, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it to completion, or supply a version to adapt. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright; a candidate who submits one is exposed to an academic-honesty finding, and the exposure falls on the student. Board syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked at source rather than redistributed, because they belong to the IB and to Cambridge, not to a tutoring platform.

sections.heading: Who supervises a Fujairah school, and what follows for sixth form
paragraphs: Private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in overseeing private schools in those three emirates. That is different from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education, and from Abu Dhabi, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Minutes down the coast at Kalba and Khor Fakkan, the Sharjah Private Education Authority applies instead, and Sharjah's authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

What that means for a parent is practical. There is no emirate-level inspection portal for Fujairah of the kind a Dubai parent is used to, so school-level information comes from the school and from ministry circulars. The federal baseline also applies: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind the required subjects running alongside whatever international programme a school is licensed for.

Looking further ahead, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements decide what a leaving certificate is worth for UAE university entry. On the British track, students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the Diploma, no points threshold is published here, because the figure could not be verified from the ministry's own source. Equivalency is a ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs; check the current requirements through the official channel before relying on any restatement.

sections.heading: The east-coast week, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Scheduling is where arrangements on this coast actually break. A Fujairah school day ends in the early afternoon, clubs and sports run on into the late afternoon, prayer timings shape the evening, and families working shifts at the port need a slot that can move between weeks rather than a fixed hour for two years. Add the shortened Ramadan school day, when the whole rhythm changes for several weeks, and a rigid weekly slot looks less like discipline and more like a plan that will lose lessons.

What works in practice is a standing slot that can be moved inside the same week, a shorter session more often rather than one long evening for younger students, and an explicit decision about mock weeks and exam weeks: either pause or switch the content to timed papers, but decide rather than drift. During Ramadan, sessions after Iftar tend to hold better than late-afternoon ones, and it is worth agreeing that change before the month starts rather than during it.

The last thing to say is the one most providers in this market leave out. Some Diploma subjects at Higher Level have no UAE-based specialist free at the hour a Fujairah family needs. It happens most in the smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options, in Higher Level physics and in Further Mathematics where a school offers it. When it happens, the straight answer is to say so and name the alternative: a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait for a slot to open. No tutor can promise a grade, and a conversation that starts with one has told you how the rest will go. Coverage limits disclosed in advance are the reason this page is longer than the ones it is competing with.

process.title: Name the subject and the level, not the year group
process.description: Start with the Diploma subjects your child takes and whether each is Higher or Standard Level. On the east coast this matters more than anywhere else, because the Higher Level extras are exactly the components a local generalist has never taught and the ones where marks are usually going.

process.title: Send the last two marked scripts and the internal deadlines
process.description: A recent marked paper shows whether marks are lost on method, pacing or command terms. The school's internal deadline list for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the subject's assessed work shows what is genuinely urgent, which is rarely the thing that feels urgent.

process.title: Agree a slot that can move inside the week
process.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around the Fujairah school day, clubs and prayer timings. Build in the ability to shift a lesson rather than cancel it, because over two years that single arrangement decides how many lessons actually happen.

process.title: One trial session, then a plan that names components
process.description: One trial session per family at no charge follows the consultation. Ask for the plan in writing afterwards: it should name papers, components and a sequence. A plan written in terms of confidence and motivation cannot be measured against the next marked script.

process.title: Review at the next school assessment
process.description: Set the review point at the school's next assessment rather than after a number of weeks, and judge it on whether marks moved in the components the plan targeted. If they did not, the aim was wrong and should change. That is a normal event in a two-year programme.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level, not by distance
whyPoints.description: The pool is everyone who teaches your child's Diploma subject at your child's level, rather than everyone willing to drive the mountain road. In an emirate where a Higher Level cohort can be eight students, that is the difference between a specialist and a second generalist.

whyPoints.title: Component-level teaching from the first session
whyPoints.description: Work starts from the marked script and the published weightings: which paper, which section, which criterion. Sessions aimed at a named component are the reason one-to-one teaching can be worth several times a group revision class per hour.

whyPoints.title: Continuity the mountain road cannot interrupt
whyPoints.description: Nothing about the arrangement depends on the Hajar road being open or on a two-hour round trip staying attractive in February. Slots move inside the same week at no cost, which over a two-year Diploma is worth more lessons than any difference in hourly rate.

whyPoints.title: Published rates belong to the market, with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it and dated October 2026. Three of the main competing sites in this market publish no hourly figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down before you ask
whyPoints.description: Coursework support is teaching, criteria reading and feedback on the student's own draft. Board papers and mark schemes are linked at source rather than handed over. Those limits are published so a family never has to discover them during an assessment week.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and specific about what that means
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority, and no school named on this page is a client. Delivery is online; visiting tuition is offered only in India.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor need to know that a strong maths teacher does not?
faqs.answer: The machinery around the content. A capable maths teacher from any system can teach Diploma mathematics, but they may never have taught Paper 3, which exists only at Higher Level and carries 20 per cent of the grade as two long structured investigations. They may not know that the mathematical exploration is marked on presentation, communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics with published mark allocations, so a technically sound piece with no stated aim loses the top band. Command terms are the third gap: deduce, outline and explain are marked differently, and a student answering them all the same way is losing marks they already earned.

faqs.question: My son's school has one teacher per Diploma subject. Is outside teaching the right fix?
faqs.answer: Often, but check the cheaper option first. If the problem is a missed sequence of lessons or confusion about the teaching order, the subject teacher is the fastest and least expensive route and knows the cohort and the internal deadlines. Outside teaching earns its cost when the bottleneck is the input itself: a single-figure cohort with one teacher has no colleague to swap to, and more of the same explanation will not move a student who has already not understood it twice. The test is diagnostic rather than emotional. Ask what the last two marked scripts show, and whether the gap is content, technique or pacing.

faqs.question: Is the school's own after-school support enough to get through DP2?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes. School support has advantages nobody outside can match: it is close to the teaching order, cheap or included, and the person giving it knows the internal deadlines. It runs out in three situations. The subject has one teacher and that teacher is the reason the student has stalled. The need is Higher Level depth the school does not routinely teach, such as a third paper or an option topic. Or the core has slipped and the student needs sustained process coaching the school cannot give to one individual. Outside the first case, more school support is usually the right next step.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is content or examination technique?
faqs.answer: Read the marked script rather than the grade, and look for the pattern. Marks lost where the final answer is correct point at working and presentation, not understanding. Marks lost steadily through the last third of a paper point at pacing. Marks lost on answers that are factually right but score below band almost always point at command terms. Content gaps look different: whole questions untouched, or working that goes wrong at the same step every time. The distinction matters financially, because a technique problem can often be fixed in a short block while a content gap needs sustained weekly teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor based in Dubai realistically teach my daughter in Fujairah every week?
faqs.answer: In person, rarely for long. The round trip from the Dubai school belt to Fujairah City runs two to three hours around a sixty-minute lesson, so either the lesson gets long enough to justify the drive or the drive gets priced into the fee, which pushes the hour towards the upper end of the AED 180-500 visiting band. The arrangement then becomes fragile: the mountain road closes after heavy rain, slots stop moving because rescheduling costs the tutor a round trip, and by February the weekly lesson has become occasional. Over video the same specialist teaches the same hour with none of that attached.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Diploma tuition cost a family on this coast?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300 per hour, visiting one-to-one tuition at AED 180-500 with travel inside the fee, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium or examiner-experienced tutors at AED 500-650 and above. Monthly packages seen in this market ran around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, not a price list. For a specific subject, level and session length the honest answer is a short consultation, then one trial session per family at no charge.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level subjects can one student sensibly have support in at once?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and two at the outside. The constraint is not money but the student's week. A Diploma year already contains six subjects, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, and adding three weekly sessions to that usually means homework gets done worse rather than better. The productive pattern on this coast is to start with the subject where the marked scripts show the largest recoverable mark total, hold it for a term, and add a second only if the first has moved. A short pre-session block in a third subject is a different thing and can sit alongside.

faqs.question: How many points does the Diploma core contribute to the final score?
faqs.answer: They contribute points on top of the six subject grades, and they are awarded together rather than separately, which is why a weak Extended Essay cannot be fully offset by a strong Theory of Knowledge essay. The more important point for a Fujairah family is that both run to deadlines the school sets rather than to the examination timetable. Confirm the exact point allocation and the current core requirements with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the IB's own published documentation is the authority on it and this page does not restate figures it could not verify from the source.

faqs.question: Does a tutor really need to see my child's school deadline list?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most useful document a parent can send. The Diploma core and every internally assessed component run on dates the school chooses, and those dates differ between schools sitting the same session. Without the list, a tutor works to the examination timetable and discovers an internal deadline after it has passed, which is the commonest way a term of sessions gets aimed at the wrong thing. With it, the plan can put the exploration or the Extended Essay draft ahead of content revision in the weeks where that is genuinely the priority.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to staff from inside the UAE?
faqs.answer: The smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options, Higher Level physics, and Further Mathematics where a school offers it. The pattern is simple: a subject taken by few students nationally is taught by few teachers, and those teachers are already fully committed during the hours a Gulf Standard Time family wants. When that happens the options are a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait for a slot to open. None of those is hidden behind an enquiry form, and no provider in this market publishes its coverage limits, which is why they are stated here.

faqs.question: We may move west of the mountains next year. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the school and the regulator, and it need not change the teaching at all. A move from Fujairah into Dubai moves your child from federal Ministry of Education supervision to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with a different inspection cycle and term calendar; a move to Sharjah or Kalba puts them under the Sharjah Private Education Authority instead. What usually causes trouble in a mid-course move is coursework in progress, because internal deadlines and supervisor arrangements differ between schools. Settle the Extended Essay question and any assessed component before the transfer rather than after it.

faqs.question: Which authority supervises my child's school in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge. The practical consequence for a Fujairah parent is that there is no emirate-level inspection portal of the kind Dubai families use, so school-level information comes from the school itself and from ministry circulars rather than from a public dashboard.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma student allowed to use a tutor for the exploration at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits, and the limits are the point. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, read the criteria with the student and explain what each one rewards, discuss the student's own ideas, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it to completion, or supply a model to adapt. The work must be the student's own, and the consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate rather than on the tutor. Any provider offering to supply a finished internal assessment is offering an academic-honesty exposure rather than a grade.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 is it still worth starting with an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, provided the aim narrows as the time shortens. With two terms left, content teaching is still viable in a subject with identifiable gaps. With one term left, the productive work is technique: timed papers, mark scheme reading and command-term precision, aimed at the one or two components carrying the largest recoverable marks. With six weeks left, the honest answer is triage on a single paper rather than a broad programme. What does not work at any stage is starting from chapter one, which is why the first session reads the marked scripts instead of the textbook.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a Diploma specialist actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written plan that names components. Not a reassurance, not a general impression, but a short document saying which papers and criteria the marks are sitting in, which two or three topics come first and in what order, and when the plan will be reviewed against the next school assessment. Ask for it after the trial session and read it for nouns. A plan describing attitude and engagement cannot be measured against anything, and an unmeasurable plan is how two years of weekly sessions pass on the east coast without the component scores moving.

fujairah/ib-tutor.closingHeading: Send the subject, the level and the deadline list
fujairah/ib-tutor.closingBody: The useful first message is short: which Diploma subjects your child takes, which are at Higher Level, the school's internal deadlines for the core and the assessed components, and a weekday window that survives clubs and prayer timings. Attach the last two marked scripts and the consultation can start on a diagnosis instead of an introduction. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Fujairah address, holds no regulator or examination-board approval, and names no school as a partner. What it does is reach past the mountain road to someone who teaches your child's subject at your child's level.

intro.heading: The nearest specialist is further away than the map suggests
paragraphs: Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman, behind the Hajar mountains, which is the single fact that governs this search. The emirate has a small private school set and small subject cohorts inside it. A Higher Level science group may be eight students taught by someone who also covers two other sciences. When a parent types a proximity query, the map answers with a handful of results that are either general tutors or businesses west of the mountains quoting a national service area. Neither is what the query was asking for.

So it is worth being exact about what distance means here rather than trading in impressions. From Fujairah City the Dubai school belt is a two-to-three-hour round trip by road. Khor Fakkan and Kalba are minutes up the same coast but are Sharjah exclaves under a different regulator. Dibba is an hour north with almost no school choice in range. Masafi sits on the inland route west, which closes after heavy rain. None of those numbers is a complaint about the roads; they are the figures that decide whether a weekly appointment survives to February.

The next thing to establish is what proximity would actually buy. For a nine-year-old who needs reading practice and a routine, a nearby adult is genuinely valuable and the right answer. For a Diploma Higher Level subject, proximity buys almost nothing that matters and costs the thing that matters most, which is access to someone who has marked that subject's papers repeatedly. In a cohort of eight, the local pool of people who have done that is frequently zero, and no amount of driving changes it.

There are questions where being near home is decisive, and this page covers them rather than brushing them aside. Where the papers are physically sat, and whether a student can enter as a private candidate for a subject their school does not teach, are both local questions with local answers. So is which authority supervises the school, which changes within a few minutes' drive on this coast. So is the practical business of a school run, a bus timetable and the hour at which a session can start. Those are the parts of the search that proximity really does answer.

The delivery position is stated so nothing is assumed. Tuition arranged through IB Gram is one-to-one and delivered live over video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Fujairah and will not send anyone to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is offered only in India. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform holding no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority. What follows is the geography, measured, and the decisions that follow from it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level courses add components Standard Level students never meet, including a third paper in mathematics and the sciences. Every subject carries internally assessed work marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision within reach of the east coast is limited, so a Fujairah student's subject combination is often determined by what a school can staff rather than what the student wants. programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, reported on a 1-7 scale. Continuous assessment means there is no single point at which everything is decided, and the Personal Project in the final year is the first long self-managed piece a student writes.
programmes.countryNote: The nearest continuum campuses to the east coast sit in Sharjah and the northern emirates rather than in Fujairah itself, so an MYP family here is frequently already commuting or boarding. Where a student moves between the MYP and an IGCSE cohort, the gap is assessment language rather than content difficulty.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The qualification most east-coast students actually hold. Four-digit syllabus codes govern papers, tier and practical arrangements. Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones; it states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version of the timetable for their zone.
programmes.countryNote: This is where proximity genuinely matters, because the exam centre is a physical place. A Fujairah candidate sits Cambridge's June or November series, or Pearson's May/June or November window, and nothing in between. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and those results reached students in the new year. Cambridge entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, with June entries closing in the spring, and the exact date for your series is on the statement of entry the centre issues.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Available in a May or June window and again in November, with some subjects modular in structure. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: The November window is the practical fallback for east-coast families, because repeating a year is rarely viable where school choice is thin. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series, so plan from the board's live timetable rather than from any restatement of it, including this page.

fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects east-coast families ask for, listed with an honest note on how easy each is to find within reach. Scarcity rather than difficulty is what usually sends a Fujairah family looking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Widely taught, so the local pool is better here than anywhere else in the Diploma. The scarcity appears at Higher Level, where Paper 3 and its long structured investigations need somebody who has marked them rather than somebody who has read about them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Newer in most schools' teaching memory, which thins the pool of people confident in the modelling and statistics units. Local generalists frequently teach it as though it were Analysis and Approaches with a calculator, which misses where the marks are.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Commonly offered and commonly under-staffed at Higher Level. On the east coast one teacher frequently covers chemistry, physics and biology, so the organic mechanisms that separate the top grades get less specialist attention than they need.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The hardest Diploma science to find within reach, and consistently the hardest to staff nationally. Fields, circuits and uncertainty treatment are the components where east-coast students lose ground, and they are precisely the ones a generalist handles least well.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The easiest to find locally and the easiest to teach unproductively. Content re-explanation feels like progress and changes nothing; the recoverable marks sit in extended-response structure and in the data-analysis items.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Taught in fewer east-coast schools than the sciences, so the local pool is thin. Higher Level Paper 3, with its quantitative questions and policy evaluation, is the component most often left to general revision rather than practised directly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Popular and reasonably well covered, with the assessed research project as the real gap. A question too broad to answer inside the word limit is the commonest failure, and it is chosen before anybody outside the school sees the work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Generally available locally. The component families struggle to prepare for is the Individual Oral, which needs an unscripted spoken exchange rather than a rehearsed presentation, and which is rarely practised enough in a small cohort.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Well covered across the emirate's mixed-language intakes. Improvement comes from frequency rather than intensity, which makes this one of the few subjects where a long, low-intensity arrangement genuinely beats a short block.

subjects.name: Group 3 and Group 6 options
subjects.description: Psychology, global politics, visual arts, music and the smaller humanities. These are the subjects where a Fujairah student is most likely to be the only candidate in the emirate, and where no local specialist exists at any price.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: Required study alongside the licensed curriculum
subjects.description: Locally well staffed, since every school must provide it. First-language and additional-language streams are taught separately and material may not be substituted without ministry approval, so support is about assessment language and written structure.

sections.heading: What a proximity search actually returns here, and why
paragraphs: Three kinds of result come back from this query on the east coast, and it is worth knowing which is which. The first is general local tutors: real people, often very good with younger children, usually covering a phase rather than a Diploma subject. The second is national agencies declaring a service area that includes Fujairah, which in practice means a tutor would travel from west of the mountains or, more commonly, that the lesson would be delivered remotely without the page saying so. The third is marketplace listings with no local content at all.

None of those is dishonest exactly, but the aggregate effect misleads, because the thing the parent is implicitly asking for is a Diploma subject specialist within a short drive, and that is the one category the results do not contain. The reason is arithmetic. Specialists concentrate where cohorts are large. Fujairah's cohorts are small, so a teacher here covers breadth rather than depth, and the depth a Higher Level student needs sits where the student population is.

The useful reframe is to split the search in two. There are things only proximity can answer: where the papers are sat, which authority supervises the school, what time the bus gets home, whether a local centre will accept a private candidate. And there are things only subject matching can answer: who has marked this paper, who knows what criterion A actually rewards, who can tell a pacing problem from a content gap. Treating one question as if it were the other is the mistake that costs an east-coast family a term.

sections.heading: Drive times from the east coast, measured rather than estimated
paragraphs: Straight-line distance is misleading here because of the mountains, so the figures worth planning against are round trips at the hour a lesson would actually run. A tutor travelling from the Dubai school belt to Fujairah City is committing two to three hours of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. Nobody sustains that at an online rate, which is why published visiting rates in the UAE run AED 180-500 per hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

The second number that matters is reliability rather than duration. The inland route through Masafi closes after heavy rain, which in a visiting arrangement means a missed week rather than a late start. A missed week in February, with mocks marked and the papers approaching, is not recoverable by doubling up in April. And there is a slower failure that families only notice after a term: when a lesson is a round trip, rescheduling is expensive for the tutor, so slots stop moving, and a slot that cannot move is a slot that gets cancelled when a fixture or a school event lands on it.

sections.heading: The nearest three alternatives, ranked by what they stop short of
paragraphs: Set out in order of distance, the options a Fujairah family can reach are the school's own subject teacher, a local general tutor, the nearest tuition provision in the city, and a provider in the Sharjah exclaves or beyond the mountains. Each covers something real, and each stops at a specific point. Knowing where it stops is more useful than knowing how far away it is.

The school's own teacher is nearest and often best for the first move. They know the cohort, the teaching order and the internal deadlines, and an extra hour from them costs little or nothing. The stopping point is structural rather than a judgement: in a single-figure Higher Level cohort with one teacher, if that teacher's explanation is the thing the student has already not understood twice, more of it will not move the grade and there is no colleague to swap to. A local generalist stops earlier still on a Diploma subject, for the component-level reasons set out across this page.

Provision in the city and in the Sharjah exclaves extends the range without changing the fundamental problem: these are places with small cohorts too, so the pool they draw from has the same shape. The provider beyond the mountains has the specialists and cannot reliably deliver them to an east-coast address week after week. That is the gap the online option fills, and it is worth being precise that it fills a coverage gap rather than a price gap. The table puts the four side by side.

sections.heading: Why scarcity beats proximity in a cohort of eight
paragraphs: A small cohort changes more than the class size. It changes how much a teacher's time is divided across subjects, how many past papers the group has worked through collectively, how much peer comparison a student gets, and how quickly an individual gap is noticed. None of that is a criticism of small schools, several of which get excellent results. It is a description of the conditions under which an individual student can quietly drift for a term.

The most consequential effect is on specialism. Where a school runs one Higher Level science group, the teacher almost certainly also teaches the other sciences and probably the Middle Years Programme below. Their subject knowledge may be strong, but their accumulated experience of this specific paper, this specific mark scheme and this specific internally assessed component is spread across three syllabuses rather than concentrated in one. The gap that produces is not about intelligence or effort. It is about repetitions.

This is why subject matching rather than proximity is the right filter on this coast, and why the argument holds even for a family in Fujairah City with a tuition centre ten minutes away. The question to ask of any prospective tutor is how often they teach your child's subject at your child's level, and what they can tell you about the component where the marks are currently going. A specialist answers in the language of papers and criteria. Somebody covering it as a second subject answers in the language of topics. On the east coast the first answer is almost always further away than the second, and almost always worth the distance that no longer has to be driven.

sections.heading: What proximity genuinely does settle, and where to get it locally
paragraphs: It would be dishonest to spend a page arguing against proximity without listing the things it decides. The first is the exam centre: papers are sat at a physical place, under a centre number, with a timetable determined by Cambridge's administrative zone or Pearson's series. That is entirely local and worth confirming early rather than in the final fortnight. The second is peer study. A student who has two classmates to work through past papers with has something no remote arrangement supplies, and on this coast that is worth organising deliberately rather than leaving to chance.

The third is the school relationship. Internal deadlines, predicted grades, subject changes, access arrangements and any conversation about the Extended Essay supervisor all happen locally, in person, with people who know your child. No outside tutor substitutes for that, and a good one will keep pointing you back to it. The fourth is pastoral: a student under real pressure in DP2 needs adults who can see them, and a video session for one hour a week is not that.

The fifth is simply logistics, and it is why the school run and the bus timetable appear repeatedly on this page. A session has to fit into a real evening in a real household. Dibba's late bus arrivals push the first workable slot past five. Al Faseel's fixtures collide with the four o'clock hour. Port shift patterns mean some households need a slot that moves between weeks. Those are local facts, they decide whether a plan survives, and they are the part of a proximity search that deserves a straight answer rather than an argument.

sections.heading: Sitting the papers near home: centres and private candidates
paragraphs: This is the local question with the most consequences and the one families leave latest. Where a student's school is an exam centre, entries are handled by the school and the only thing to confirm is which series and which timetable version apply. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version of the timetable for their zone, so the zone is worth knowing in writing rather than by assumption.

Where a student wants a subject the school does not teach, the private-candidate route exists and it is genuinely local: the entry has to be made through a centre that accepts private candidates, within that series deadline, and the student travels to that centre to sit the papers. The deadlines sit months before the exams. A private-candidate entry for Cambridge's June series has to be lodged in the spring, and for the November series over the preceding summer, and a centre taking outside candidates often sets its own cut-off earlier again, so ask for that date in writing rather than working back from the board's. Pearson examines International GCSE subjects in a May or June window and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

For Diploma subjects the position is different and more restrictive, because the programme is delivered by authorised schools rather than entered privately in the way an International GCSE subject can be. That means a Fujairah student whose school cannot staff a Higher Level subject has school-level options rather than exam-entry options: a different subject, a different school, or in some cases a distance-learning arrangement through a provider that is itself an authorised school. A tutor does not solve that problem and should say so. What a tutor can do is make sure the subjects the student is actually entered for are taught to the level of the paper.

sections.heading: Which authority supervises the school nearest you
paragraphs: On this coast the regulator changes within a short drive, and it changes more than a logo on a letterhead. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. A few minutes down the same road, in the Sharjah exclaves of Kalba and Khor Fakkan, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education, and Sharjah's authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge with the same approval powers.

West of the mountains, Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, while Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools, and it is worth noting how rarely the competing pages in this market name any of them beyond Dubai's.

The practical consequences for a family near Fujairah are three. There is no emirate-level inspection portal for Fujairah of the kind Dubai parents use, so school information comes from the school and from ministry circulars. Term dates and fee rules differ across a boundary that may be ten minutes from your front door. And the federal baseline applies throughout: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations, which is the rule behind those subjects running alongside any international programme.

sections.heading: Checking the person who is near you, and what happens when nobody is
paragraphs: If you do hire locally, two checks are worth making before the first lesson. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated: individuals giving private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. MoHRE states that anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and publishes no fine schedule, so treat any amount quoted online as unverified. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason not to hold one.

The second check concerns your child's own school. A teacher at the school your child attends is generally not an appropriate choice for paid private tuition of that child. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That has been press-reported rather than read from the current policy text, so verify the exact wording with the authority, but do not treat the arrangement as routine simply because it is convenient and nearby.

And sometimes nobody is available near or far, which is the part of this search no competing page admits to. Higher Level physics, Further Mathematics where a school offers it, and the smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options regularly have no UAE-based specialist free at the hour a Fujairah family needs. The options then are a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait for a slot to open. That gets said rather than concealed. On the same principle: coursework support is teaching and feedback on the student's own work, never a draft supplied; board papers and mark schemes are linked at source rather than redistributed; and no tutor can promise a grade.

process.title: Separate the local questions from the subject ones
process.description: Write down two lists. Local: exam centre, Cambridge zone, bus times, school deadlines, who supervises the school. Subject: which papers, which level, where the marks are going. The first list goes to the school. The second decides who should teach your child.

process.title: Try the nearest option first, properly
process.description: An extra hour a week from your child's own subject teacher is the cheapest and best-informed help available, and for a content gap caused by absence it is usually sufficient. Establish whether it has been genuinely tried before paying for anything further.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the marked scripts
process.description: Which Diploma subjects, which are at Higher Level, and the last two marked pieces of work. Those three things let a first session start on a diagnosis. A proximity search cannot be answered usefully without them, because the answer depends on the subject rather than the postcode.

process.title: Set a slot that fits the real evening
process.description: Account for the bus from Dibba, the fixtures in Al Faseel, prayer timings and any shift pattern at home, and agree that the slot can move inside the same week. On this coast that single term saves more lessons across a year than any hourly saving.

process.title: Confirm the exam-centre details in writing
process.description: Ask the school for the centre, the Cambridge administrative zone, the series it enters and its own internal entry deadline, in writing. These are the genuinely local facts, and they are the ones most often discovered too late to act on.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the subject, which is where the scarcity is
whyPoints.description: The constraint on this coast is not distance but repetitions: how often a tutor has taught and marked your child's specific paper. Matching starts there, which is why a specialist for a cohort of eight is reachable at all.

whyPoints.title: The local questions get local answers
whyPoints.description: Exam centre, Cambridge zone, entry deadlines, which authority supervises the school after a move. Those are set out here with the boards' own published dates rather than waved away as details somebody else will handle.

whyPoints.title: Distances given as round trips, not map lines
whyPoints.description: Two to three hours from the Dubai school belt, an hour each way from Qidfa to the city, and a route through Masafi that closes after heavy rain. Those figures are the honest basis for deciding whether a visiting arrangement survives to February.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed to whoever published them
whyPoints.description: AED 150-300 online and AED 180-500 visiting with travel inside the fee, published October 2026 and credited. Three of the main competing sites in this market publish no hourly figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published, not concealed
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics, Further Mathematics and the smaller option subjects regularly have nobody free at a workable hour. That is stated with the alternatives named. No provider in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere on its site.

whyPoints.title: Independent, online, and specific about both
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no approval, accreditation or partnership from any board or regulator, and no school named here is a client. Lessons are one-to-one over live video; visiting tuition is offered only in India.

faqs.question: Why does a search for a tutor near me return so little in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Because specialists concentrate where cohorts are large, and Fujairah's are small. The emirate has a modest private school set, and inside it a Higher Level subject group may be eight students taught by someone who also covers two other subjects. What the search does return is general local tutors, who are often genuinely good with younger children, and national agencies declaring a service area that includes the east coast. The category the query is implicitly asking for, a Diploma subject specialist within a short drive, is the one the results do not contain, and no amount of searching changes that arithmetic.

faqs.question: How far away is the nearest Diploma subject specialist from Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: For a widely taught subject such as mathematics or biology, there may be somebody within the city or in the Sharjah exclaves down the coast. For Higher Level physics, Further Mathematics or a smaller Group 3 or Group 6 option, the nearest person who teaches that course regularly is usually west of the Hajar mountains, which is a two-to-three-hour round trip from Fujairah City. That distance is why a visiting arrangement at an online rate does not hold: the travel either enters the fee, pushing it towards the AED 180-500 visiting band, or it quietly erodes the frequency of the lessons.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in Khor Fakkan or Kalba nearer than one in Sharjah city?
faqs.answer: Much nearer, and that is worth knowing because the two are in the same emirate. Kalba and Khor Fakkan are Sharjah exclaves minutes down the east coast road, so for some Fujairah households they are closer than Fujairah City itself. What travels with them is the regulatory system: schools there come under the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than the federal Ministry of Education, with their own term dates, fee rules and inspection cycle. Proximity on this coast does not line up with emirate boundaries, which catches out families who plan on a map.

faqs.question: Does hiring someone nearby make the arrangement more reliable?
faqs.answer: Within a district, yes. Across the mountains, the opposite. A tutor five minutes away can turn up in most weathers and reschedule cheaply. A tutor committing to a two-to-three-hour round trip cannot reschedule cheaply, so slots stop moving, and a slot that cannot move is the one that gets cancelled when a fixture or a school event lands on it. Add the inland route closing after heavy rain and the arrangement becomes fortnightly by February. Reliability is really about the cost of moving a lesson, and that cost is zero for a video session.

faqs.question: Our neighbour tutors maths. Is that enough for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the component. For algebraic fluency, confidence and the habit of working consistently, a strong nearby mathematician can be excellent value. For Higher Level specifically, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent of the grade and consists of long structured investigations that do not exist at Standard Level, and the mathematical exploration is marked against criteria with published mark allocations where presentation and communication each carry four marks. Ask your neighbour directly how often they have taught Paper 3 and what criterion A of the exploration rewards. The answer will settle it either way.

faqs.question: Where is the nearest centre for a private candidate entry?
faqs.answer: That has to come from the centres themselves, because accepting private candidates is each centre's own policy rather than a board-wide rule, and the nearest accepting centre may not be in Fujairah. The practical route is to ask your child's school first, since many schools will host an entry for a subject they do not teach, and to ask for the centre number and administrative zone in writing. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone's timetable, so the zone matters as much as the location.

faqs.question: Can my child be entered for a Diploma subject the local school does not teach?
faqs.answer: Not in the way an International GCSE subject can be. The Diploma is delivered through authorised schools rather than entered privately, so a student whose school cannot staff a Higher Level subject has school-level options rather than exam-entry ones: choose a different subject, move school, or use a distance-learning arrangement through a provider that is itself an authorised school. A tutor cannot solve that and should say so plainly. Confirm the current position with your child's Diploma coordinator, who is the person with access to the authoritative answer for your school.

faqs.question: What does being near home genuinely help with?
faqs.answer: Five things. Where the papers are physically sat, including the centre number and timetable version. Peer study, which is worth organising deliberately on a coast with small cohorts. The school relationship, covering internal deadlines, predicted grades, subject changes and the Extended Essay supervisor. Pastoral support for a student under real pressure, which one hour a week over video does not provide. And logistics: the bus from Dibba, fixtures in Al Faseel, prayer timings and shift patterns all decide whether a plan survives. Those are the parts of this search where proximity is the right answer.

faqs.question: Which authority covers a school in Kalba or Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, because both are Sharjah exclaves on the east coast despite being minutes from Fujairah. Fujairah's own private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which also covers Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and Abu Dhabi and Al Ain the Department of Education and Knowledge. Those five are the complete map. The practical effect of crossing that boundary is different term dates, different fee rules and a different inspection cycle, on the same stretch of road.

faqs.question: Is a local tutor cheaper than one further away?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for a general tutor, and not necessarily for a specialist. Published market rates in October 2026 put visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE at AED 180-500 per hour with travel inside the fee, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium or examiner-experienced tutors at AED 500-650 and above. On this coast the travel component dominates the visiting figure. Those are other providers' published rates rather than a price list; a specific subject and level is a consultation, followed by one trial session per family at no charge.

faqs.question: How do we check that a nearby tutor is permitted to teach for money?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and appears on MoHRE's own site as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services system. Eligibility covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and publishes no amounts, so disregard figures circulating online.

faqs.question: My son is one of five students in his Higher Level group. Does that affect his grade?
faqs.answer: It affects the conditions rather than the ceiling. Small groups often get more attention per student, which is a real advantage. What they get less of is specialism and volume: the teacher probably covers other subjects too, the group has collectively worked through fewer past papers, and there is less peer comparison to reveal that an individual has drifted. The practical fix is volume of marked timed work against the published scheme, which is exactly what a subject specialist outside the school can supply without anyone changing school or driving anywhere.

faqs.question: Would weekly boarding west of the mountains be better than arranging tuition?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the deciding question is whether the problem is the subject or the provision. If your child wants a Higher Level combination the local school cannot staff at all, tuition does not fix that and a move or a boarding arrangement is the honest answer. If the subjects are available locally and one of them has stalled, boarding is an expensive solution to a problem a specialist can address in a term. Settle which situation you are in by asking the school directly what it can and cannot offer next year, in writing, before costing anything else.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who actually live in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: The question to ask is which subject, because residence is not how the matching works. Every session is one-to-one over live video and scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so a tutor's location affects their own working hours rather than your child's lesson time. IB Gram does not send anyone to a Fujairah address; visiting tuition is a service offered only in India. What that buys an east-coast family is the pool: instead of choosing among people willing to drive the mountain road, you are choosing among people who teach your child's subject at your child's level.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is available, near or far?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the alternatives named. Higher Level physics, Further Mathematics where a school offers it, and the smaller Group 3 and Group 6 options regularly have no UAE-based specialist free at the hour a Fujairah family needs. The options at that point are a specialist in another time zone teaching into a Gulf Standard Time slot, a fortnightly longer session, or a wait until a slot opens. None of that sits behind an enquiry form. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit anywhere, which is precisely why it is written on this page.

fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Two lists, and one email to the school
fujairah/ib-tutor-near-me.closingBody: Make the local list and the subject list, then send the local one to the school: exam centre, Cambridge administrative zone, the series it enters, its internal entry deadline, and the bus times that decide your evening. Send the subject list here instead: which Diploma subjects, which are at Higher Level, and the last two marked scripts. Those are different questions with different answers, and separating them is what turns a proximity search into a plan. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram holds no board or regulator approval, names no school as a partner, and does not send anyone to a Fujairah address.

intro.heading: Where your child is now, where the grade needs to be, and the weeks in between
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IGCSE home tutor in Fujairah rarely want a discussion of pedagogy. They want to know whether there is still time. A mock came back two grades below target, or a subject that was fine in Year 10 has quietly stopped working, and the real question is arithmetic: how many teaching weeks remain before the papers, how much of the gap those weeks can close, and what it costs per week to find out. Almost nothing written about tutoring in this market answers that, because answering it honestly sometimes means telling a family to buy less.

The arithmetic on the east coast has an extra term in it. Fujairah is on the far side of the Hajar mountains, roughly an hour and a half of driving from Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah and often closer to two from Dubai. A visiting tutor taking a two-hour lesson in Fujairah city from a base in Sharjah is away from that base for around five hours. That time is real and somebody pays for it, which is why visiting rates in the UAE sit in a higher band than online rates and why visiting availability on this coast is usually weekends, a two-hour minimum, or both. The first table on this page sets that out properly rather than leaving it as a vague note about convenience.

IB Gram's answer to it is to remove the drive. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so a session sits in a Fujairah evening after the bus and a meal. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. That is a limitation and it is stated here rather than implied. What it buys is a subject match chosen from everyone who teaches the specification rather than from whoever is prepared to cross the mountains on a Tuesday.

The rest of the page is the timeline. There is a diagnostic stage, which should take one session and produce a document. There is the block of roughly twelve weeks in which a single subject genuinely moves, and the evidence for that movement is marked work rather than anybody's impression. There is the Year 11 year counted from October to results day, window by window, with what should exist at the end of each. There are the last six weeks, which are a different kind of work entirely and are mostly wasted on new content. And there is the conversation about Ramadan, term dates and what happens when the plan slips, which it usually does once.

One honest caveat before any of it. A grade is not a purchase. Nothing on this page promises a number, a jump or a result, because no tutor can deliver one and anyone offering it is selling something other than teaching. What a good plan offers is that the mark your child is capable of actually appears on the paper, which is a smaller claim and a far more achievable one. Most lost marks on IGCSE papers are not lost to ignorance. They are lost to unwritten working, misread command terms and time spent in the wrong order, and those are the things a term of structured weekly work reliably repairs.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: A home-tutoring question is really a question about which stage your child is standing in, because each stage has a different number of weeks attached and a different kind of work available inside them. The four below cover almost every enquiry that arrives from the east coast.

programmes.name: Year 10: the cheap year to fix things
programmes.description: The first year of the two-year course, examined by nobody, which makes it the least expensive year in which to repair a foundation. Work done here compounds: algebraic fluency secured in Year 10 pays into every science paper in Year 11, while the same work bought in March of Year 11 competes with revision for the same hours. A block of eight to twelve weekly sessions in Year 10 typically achieves more than twice that number bought later.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast families often wait, understandably, because nothing is being examined and the school report looks survivable. The practical argument for not waiting is the local subject list: if a Year 10 diagnostic shows that Extended tier is at risk in mathematics, there is still time to decide whether a tier change or a tuition block is the answer, and both of those decisions get harder once entries for the series are in.

programmes.name: Year 11: the run to the series
programmes.description: Around thirty-four teaching weeks, interrupted by mocks, holidays and Ramadan, ending in a series of written papers. The year divides naturally into content completion, mock analysis, whole-paper practice and final rehearsal, and the mistake families make most often is using the later windows for the earlier kind of work. Revising topics in April when the problem is timing produces a student who knows more and scores the same.
programmes.countryNote: Mock timing varies between schools in Fujairah, and the mock is the single most useful document a tutor can be given, because it shows where marks went rather than how the student seemed. Ask the school when mocks fall for your child's cohort in September, then plan the first tuition block to land immediately afterwards rather than before, when there is nothing to diagnose from.

programmes.name: The November series and resits
programmes.description: Both major boards run an autumn series as well as a summer one, which means a disappointing grade is not a lost year. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE examinations in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and Cambridge runs June and November series. A resit plan is short, narrow and built entirely around the papers that went wrong.
programmes.countryNote: For a Fujairah student the resit question is partly logistical, because the entry may need to go through a centre in another emirate if the school does not enter the autumn series. Settle where the paper will be sat at the same time as deciding to resit, and confirm which administrative zone that centre sits in before reading any timetable.

programmes.name: The summer bridge into sixth form
programmes.description: The six to eight weeks between the last paper and the start of Year 12, which almost nobody uses and which repays use more than any equivalent period in the school year. A short block here covers the content the A Level or Diploma course assumes rather than teaches: calculus notation, moles beyond the IGCSE treatment, and the reading load that sixth form drops on a student in week one without warning.
programmes.countryNote: The bridge matters more on the east coast because some students change school or emirate for sixth form, which means arriving in a new cohort with a different scheme of work and no shared history with the teacher. A student who has already met the first three weeks of content starts that term as a participant rather than as somebody catching up.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject below is about time: how long a block of weekly one-to-one work usually needs before the change shows in marked work. These are patterns from teaching the specifications, not promises, and a diagnostic replaces them with something specific to your child.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The fastest subject to move and the one where the first five weeks matter most, because almost every later topic rests on algebraic manipulation. A student whose arithmetic is fine and whose algebra is not will often show a measurable change within a month. A student missing number work from Year 9 needs a term, and saying so early saves a family from buying the wrong plan.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Moves in two stages. Numerical confidence arrives first, usually inside four or five weeks, because the calculations follow patterns. Circuit and field reasoning takes longer, because it has to be rebuilt rather than practised. A plan that treats physics as one subject with one timeline consistently underestimates the electricity topics and overestimates everything else.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: The most measurable subject on this list. Moles calculations either work or they do not, and the same is true of balanced equations and organic pathways, which makes progress visible in marked work faster than in biology. Six to eight weeks of weekly work usually converts a student who understands chemistry into one who scores it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The slowest of the three sciences to shift, because the problem is almost never comprehension. It is volume and recall under time. Progress comes from repeated retrieval and from marking long answers against the published criteria, which means the useful work happens between sessions and the session exists to set it up and audit it.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Responds quickly in directed writing and slowly in reading response. Teaching a student the shape of a strong directed-writing answer can change marks within three or four weeks. Teaching close textual analysis is a term's work, because it depends on reading habits that do not form in a fortnight. Honest sequencing matters more here than in any other subject.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: The speaking and listening components are the ones that move fastest, and they are the hardest for a student to rehearse alone, which makes them unusually good value in a weekly slot. Reading and writing improve steadily rather than suddenly. A term of weekly conversation practice with targeted correction is the standard shape of a plan here.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram discipline is a three-week job and it carries a surprising share of the available marks. Data-response technique takes longer because it is really a reading skill. A plan that starts with diagrams gets an early visible improvement, which also buys the student the confidence to do the slower work.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: The evaluative command terms are the whole ceiling, and they are teachable in about a month of weekly work on past questions. Content knowledge is rarely the limiting factor by Year 11. This is a subject where four well-used sessions can do more than a term of general revision, which is worth knowing before buying a longer block.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Two independent timelines in one subject. Theory recall responds to the same retrieval work as biology. The algorithms and pseudocode paper responds to writing code by hand against the board's own conventions, which a confident Python student may never have done. Diagnose which half is weak before committing to a number of weeks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Not a subject to start late. It assumes fluency the main mathematics course is still building, so a block bought in the final two terms usually turns into remedial work on 0580 content under a different name. Started in Year 10 alongside the main course, it is the best preparation available for sixth-form mathematics.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Fujairah changes the weekly rhythm a plan has to fit inside: when the bus arrives, when a quiet room is free, and which evenings are already gone. The notes below are about that rhythm, because a slot nobody can keep is worse than no slot at all.

regions.name: Fujairah city
regions.note: Shortest journeys home and the widest choice of school, which usually means the earliest workable weekday slot in the emirate. Families here are also the most likely to have an activity already booked on two weekday evenings, so the useful question is not when a lesson could start but which evening is genuinely free for a whole term.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: The bus run rather than the distance sets the clock here. A realistic first slot sits after arrival and a meal, which in most households means an hour later than parents expect when they first pick a time. Picking a slot thirty minutes later than seems necessary is the single best way to stop a plan from quietly collapsing in week four.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Households here are frequently running more than one school timetable, with siblings finishing at different times. Where two children both need a weekly slot, putting them in consecutive hours on the same evening protects the rest of the week and means one quiet room is prepared once rather than twice.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Close enough to the city that an evening out is plausible, which in practice means the calendar fills. The families here who keep a plan going for a full term are the ones who treat the weekly session as fixed rather than movable, and who agree at the outset which two weeks of the year it will be skipped.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Quieter and further from the city's activity schedule, which tends to make the weekly slot easier to protect and the plan easier to sustain across a whole term. The constraint here is usually one shared study space, so a paired sibling booking in consecutive hours works better than two separate evenings.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The longest journey to anything in-person and the smallest local subject list, which means a plan here is normally built for the whole year rather than bought in short blocks. Families in Dibba also need term dates confirmed from the specific school rather than assumed, because the wider area is served by more than one administration.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Highway villages where the school journey is already long, so an evening slot competes directly with the student's remaining energy. A mid-evening session of fifty minutes with a marked set to follow usually works better here than a longer sitting, and the plan should say so rather than defaulting to a full hour.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: At the mountain pass, with some students attending school in another emirate entirely. That matters for a timeline because term dates, mock weeks and holiday patterns can differ from their neighbours', so the Year 11 calendar below has to be rebuilt against the actual school rather than against the emirate.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The schools inside the emirate itself, where mock timing and term dates set the shape of any tuition plan. Students we support attend schools in this group. No school named here is a partner, client or sponsor of IB Gram, and none has endorsed this page or anything on it.
schools: Our Own English High School, Fujairah

schoolClusters.note: Where some Masafi and Dibba students attend school, and where east-coast families look for a subject the local list cannot carry. Different regulator, sometimes different term dates, and therefore a different Year 11 calendar from the one a neighbour's child is working to.
schools: Scholars Indian School, Ras Al Khaimah

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for term dates, mock timing and the curriculum mix on the east coast. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement arrangement with any of them.
fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of booking, each defined by how many weeks it has to work in. The honest version of this choice starts with the calendar rather than with a preference, because a format that suits a year does not suit a fortnight.

modes.title: The twelve-week block
modes.description: The standard shape when a term is available. One weekly hour, the same tutor, the same slot, working through the specification in sequence with a marked question set between sessions. A review falls at week five, when a recurring error should have stopped appearing, and again at week eleven, when the decision is whether to extend, change subject or stop.
bullets: A stated number of sessions with an end date, not a rolling booking
Review points at week five and week eleven, both against marked work
Specification-order coverage rather than homework rescue
Two agreed skip weeks built in before the term starts

modes.title: The six-week pre-series run
modes.description: Bought for the weeks immediately before the papers and built entirely around whole papers and the published mark schemes. No new content unless a diagnostic finds a gap that is genuinely cheap to close. The work is timing, command terms, the order answers are attempted, and the five errors that keep recurring in that student's own scripts.
bullets: Whole papers to time from week one, not topic revision
Errors tracked by frequency across the student's own marked scripts
A per-paper plan the student can state back without prompting
A clear early answer if six weeks is not enough for what is being asked

modes.title: Paired sibling or paired subject slots
modes.description: Two consecutive fifty-minute sessions on one evening, either two subjects for one student or one subject each for two children in the same house. It protects the rest of the week, uses one prepared quiet room, and keeps both plans visible to the same parent in the same written record.
bullets: Consecutive slots rather than one long sitting
Separate written records, reviewed together at the same points
Works best where the two needs are different; two identical plans rarely are
Reviewed after a month to check neither half is being starved

sections.heading: What a visiting IGCSE tutor on the east coast actually costs per teaching hour
paragraphs: Visiting tuition is priced per hour, which is the least informative way to price it. The number a Fujairah family should be comparing is cost per teaching hour, and on this coast those two figures diverge sharply because of the mountains. A tutor based in Sharjah who teaches a two-hour lesson in Fujairah city is committed for roughly five hours door to door. Whoever absorbs that time pays for it: either the rate sits at the top of its band, or there is a travel surcharge, or there is a two-hour minimum booking, or the availability is weekends only.

Published market bands in the UAE put visiting one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table sits at the lower end of the visiting range, at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reported up to AED 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits, and those two numbers only become comparable once both are divided down to a per-hour figure.

None of this makes visiting tuition the wrong choice. For a younger student who genuinely needs an adult sitting beside them, or for a family that wants a person in the house, it can be worth every dirham. What it does mean is that the honest comparison is not AED 250 against AED 250. It is a narrower subject list, a narrower availability window and a higher real rate against a wider tutor pool and a fixed weekday slot. The table below sets out the drive-time arithmetic from the five bases a Fujairah family is most likely to be quoted from.

A note on what IB Gram does and does not do here, stated plainly rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; tutors arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The reason this page costs out visiting tuition anyway is that a parent comparing options deserves the real numbers for both, including the option we do not sell.
