sections.heading: Finding out where your child actually is, in one session
paragraphs: A timeline needs a starting point, and a report comment is not one. Reports describe how a student seemed across a term. A marked paper shows where the marks went, which is a completely different document and the only one from which a plan can be written. The single most useful thing a Fujairah parent can do before any tuition is bought is to photograph two or three pages of the most recent marked mock and send them with the enquiry.

The diagnostic session itself should take forty-five minutes and should produce something written. In that time a specialist can watch a student attempt a timed question, see what they do when they are stuck, check two or three foundational skills the specification assumes, and read one marked script. What comes out is a statement of which topics are secure, which are not, whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and a realistic number of weeks. It should name the syllabus code and the tier it is planning against.

The distinction between content, technique and timing is the one that decides everything afterwards, and it is the one most plans never make. A student who does not know the topic needs teaching, which takes weeks. A student who knows it and writes it badly needs mark-scheme work, which takes sessions. A student who knows it, writes it well and runs out of time needs whole-paper rehearsal, which takes practice rather than instruction. Buying twelve weeks of teaching for a timing problem is the most common way families waste money in this market.

If the diagnostic concludes that tuition is not the right purchase, that is a legitimate outcome and it gets written down. Sometimes the honest answer is that the student needs to use the school's own clinic properly for a term, or that the problem is sleep and screen hours rather than chemistry, or that one subject is being carried at the expense of three others and the choice is a timetable decision for the school. A diagnostic that can only ever conclude in favour of buying lessons is a sales call with a worksheet attached.
bullets: Send photographs of marked mock pages, not the report
Expect a written statement after the diagnostic, naming code and tier
Content, technique and timing need different numbers of weeks
A diagnostic that cannot conclude against tuition is not a diagnostic

sections.heading: What twelve weeks of weekly one-to-one work actually changes
paragraphs: Twelve weeks is the shortest block in which a subject reliably moves and the longest a family should commit to before a review. The shape is consistent across subjects. The first two sessions are foundation repair, which feels like going backwards and is the part students resist. Sessions three to five introduce the specification content in order with a marked question set between each. Around week five, a recurring error either stops appearing in the marked sets or it does not, and that binary is the first honest review point.

From week six the work changes character. Content coverage continues, but whole questions replace individual skills and the marking starts naming mark-scheme points rather than right and wrong. By week nine most students can attempt a full past question in the subject under time, and the sessions become about reading their own scripts critically. Week eleven is the second review: extend, switch to a different subject, or stop because the subject is now self-sustaining. All three are real outcomes and the third is not a failure.

The part of this that families underestimate is what happens outside the hour. A weekly session with no work between sessions is a conversation, and it moves marks very little. Twenty targeted questions on the one error that keeps recurring will do more for a grade than an extra hour of teaching, which is why every session here ends with a set and the next one starts by marking it. Parents do not need to teach anything; they need to know whether the set was done, and the written record tells them.

Measured honestly, a twelve-week block in a single subject usually produces a student who writes the marks they already deserved, plus some of the content they were missing. Whether that is one grade or two depends entirely on how much of the original gap was technique rather than knowledge, which is why the diagnostic comes first. Anybody quoting a grade improvement before seeing a marked paper is guessing, and anybody quoting one afterwards is still guessing with better information.

sections.heading: The Year 11 year, counted window by window from October
paragraphs: Roughly thirty-four teaching weeks separate the start of Year 11 from the summer papers, and they are not interchangeable. Each window supports a different kind of work, and the commonest planning error is using a late window for early work: revising topics in April when the problem is paper timing produces a student who knows more and scores exactly the same. The table below assigns each window its job and says what should exist at the end of it.

The first window, September to late November, is the one that carries the tier decision, and it sits early on purpose. Cambridge publishes a final entry date for each series months ahead of the papers, and once entries are submitted the tier is fixed on the statement of entry. For the June series a Fujairah candidate actually sits, that closing date falls in the spring term, well before the first paper and often before the evidence from a second mock exists, so the tier gets argued from whatever is on paper by then rather than from how the year finishes. Rather than trusting a date restated on a tutor's page, ask the exam officer in September for the final entry date that applies to your centre and treat it as the deadline for every tier conversation.

The middle windows belong to the mock. A mock paper is the most valuable document of the year because it converts a vague worry into a list, and the list is short: most students lose marks in three or four identifiable places, repeatedly. December to mid-February is for closing those. Mid-February to the end of March is for whole papers under time, which is a different skill and needs practising rather than learning. April onwards is rehearsal, logistics and sleep.

Two practical items that belong in the same calendar. Pearson publishes its International GCSE timetables for each series and also issues provisional timetables in advance, so any date should be checked against the live page rather than a restatement. And Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Confirm your centre's zone before printing anything.

sections.heading: The last six weeks, and what they can honestly fix
paragraphs: The six weeks before a series are the most commonly misused period in the whole timeline. Families buy teaching and students want reassurance, when what the weeks can actually deliver is a higher mark for knowledge the student already has. Almost every script in this window loses marks to the same small set of causes: working not shown, command terms misread, time spent in the wrong order, and one or two genuinely weak topics that keep appearing. Those are repairable in six weeks. A missing year of content is not, and saying so in week six is kinder than discovering it in week two of the papers.

The method is unglamorous. Week six is a diagnostic on the two weakest papers, sat to time, marked properly, and reduced to a written list of the errors that recur by frequency rather than by how annoying they are. Weeks five and four take the top two errors and rebuild them with targeted question sets. Week three moves to mark-scheme language, because a student who can name the criterion they are meeting writes differently from one who is hoping. Weeks two and one are whole papers, timing plans and logistics.

What the student does alone matters more in this window than at any other time, and it is where a plan either works or quietly fails. Twenty questions on one recurring error beats an extra hour of teaching, every time. A full paper attempted to time and then marked by the student against the published criteria, with the tutor auditing the marking rather than redoing it, teaches more about the examiner's expectations than a term of explanation. Parents do not need to understand the chemistry; they need to know the paper was attempted and marked.

The last item on the list is not academic. Confirm the statement of entry, the correct zone timetable, the centre and the room in the final week, not on the morning. Cambridge is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after using the wrong zone version of the timetable, and that is an avoidable way to lose a grade that no amount of tuition can repair afterwards.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holiday weeks and the weeks a plan has to survive
paragraphs: A thirty-four week plan written in September will meet at least three interruptions, and the ones that break plans are the predictable ones. The UAE academic year carries a shortened school day during Ramadan, a set of public holidays that move with the lunar calendar, and a mid-year break whose dates differ between schools and sometimes between emirates. A plan that pretends otherwise collapses in its sixth week and takes the family's confidence with it.

The practical approach is to decide the skip weeks before the block starts rather than negotiating them one at a time. Two agreed weeks in a twelve-week block is realistic and keeps the rest of the schedule intact. During Ramadan the usual answer is not to pause but to move: a shortened school day frees the afternoon, and a session after Iftar works well for older students who are revising late anyway. Either way, the time changes once for the month rather than drifting weekly, because a slot that moves every week is a slot that gets missed.

Holidays themselves are worth using rather than avoiding, particularly the winter break in a Year 11 year. Three sessions in a week with nothing else competing for the hours can do what six weekly sessions do during term, which makes a holiday block the cheapest acceleration available in the calendar. The limit is the student, not the subject: a child who has just finished a term of mocks may need the first week of a break to be a break.

For Masafi and Dibba families there is an extra step, because a student attending school in another emirate may be working to different term dates and mock weeks from their neighbours. Build the plan against the school's published calendar rather than against the emirate's general pattern, and confirm the mock weeks in September when the school sets them, since those weeks are the anchor for everything the plan does afterwards.
bullets: Agree two skip weeks at the start of a block rather than negotiating weekly
During Ramadan, move the slot once for the month instead of rescheduling each week
A three-session week inside a holiday break accelerates more than the equivalent term weeks
Build against the specific school's calendar, not the emirate's general pattern

sections.heading: What a parent does between the sessions
paragraphs: Parents repeatedly ask what they should be doing, and the honest answer is less than they fear and more than nothing. Nobody needs to learn the chemistry. What a plan needs from a parent is three things: that the weekly slot is protected, that the question set between sessions is attempted, and that the written record is read rather than filed. Those three are the difference between a plan that works and an identical plan that does not.

Protecting the slot sounds trivial and is the hardest of the three. A session that moves twice becomes a session that is missed, and a missed session in a twelve-week block is eight per cent of the plan. The practical trick is to choose a slot thirty minutes later than seems necessary, so the bus, the meal and the inevitable delay all fit inside the margin rather than eating into the lesson. Families who do this keep plans going for whole terms; families who optimise for the earliest possible start tend not to.

Reading the record matters because it is the only window a parent has into a lesson they were not in. A useful record says what was covered, which question set was issued, and which mark-scheme points the previous set lost. Over five weeks a pattern becomes visible without any technical knowledge at all: either the same loss keeps appearing or it stops. If it keeps appearing for five weeks and nothing in the plan changes, that is the moment to ask the question rather than to wait politely for the next review.

One thing a parent should not do is become the enforcer of the between-session work in a way that turns the subject into a battleground. If the set is not getting done, the useful conversation is with the tutor about whether it is the wrong length, the wrong difficulty or the wrong time of day. A set that takes forty minutes and is attempted is worth more than one that takes two hours and is not.

sections.heading: When the weeks are not enough, and what to buy instead
paragraphs: Sometimes a family arrives eight weeks before a series asking for two subjects rebuilt and a tier change, and the honest answer is that the hours do not exist. Saying so loses the booking. It also saves several thousand dirhams from being spent on a plan that was never going to land, and it keeps the family's trust for the resit or for the sibling behind them. No tutoring provider in this market publishes that limit, which is one of the stranger silences in the whole set of pages competing for this search.

When the weeks are short, the right purchase changes rather than disappearing. Narrowing to one subject rather than three concentrates the hours where they can still move a grade. Narrowing further to the two papers with the most recoverable marks concentrates them again. In some cases the best advice is to protect the subjects that are already working, because a student spending every evening rescuing chemistry can lose two grades elsewhere without noticing, and a timetable triage conversation is worth more than any number of lessons.

The autumn series is the other honest option, and it is routinely forgotten. Both major boards run a November or autumn series as well as a summer one, so a grade that goes wrong in June is a delay rather than a year. A resit plan is narrow, cheap relative to a full year, and built entirely around the specific papers that went wrong. For a Fujairah student the logistics need settling early, because the entry may need to go through a centre in another emirate and the administrative zone must be confirmed with that centre.

All of this gets said in the trial lesson, before money changes hands. One free 45-minute session per family, no card details required, ending in a written statement of what the subject needs and how many weeks that is. If the statement says the weeks are not there, it says so in writing, with a recommendation for what to do instead. That is the only version of this conversation worth having, and it is better had in October than in May.
bullets: Short weeks mean fewer subjects, not more sessions
Triage the timetable before adding hours to the weakest subject
The autumn series turns a lost grade into a delay, not a lost year
The written diagnostic says plainly when the hours do not exist

process.title: Say which series your child is entered for
process.description: The series fixes the number of teaching weeks available, and the number of weeks decides what kind of plan is honest. Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series in the first message. All five sit on the option booklet or the statement of entry, and with them a plan can be written in one conversation instead of three.

process.title: Send the marked mock, not the report
process.description: Photographs of two or three marked pages tell a specialist where the marks went, which a report comment cannot. If no mock exists yet, say when the school has scheduled them, because the most useful first tuition block usually starts the week after a mock rather than the week before it.

process.title: Take the 45-minute diagnostic
process.description: One free trial session per family, no card details required. Your child attempts a timed question while the tutor watches what happens when they get stuck, and the session ends in a written statement: topics secure, topics not, whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and a realistic number of weeks. If tuition is the wrong purchase, the statement says so.

process.title: Fix a slot with margin and two skip weeks
process.description: Choose a weekday slot thirty minutes later than seems necessary, so the bus, the meal and the usual delay fit inside the margin. Agree the two weeks in the block that will be skipped before the block starts. Both of these sound administrative and both are the reason plans survive a full term.

process.title: Review at week five and week eleven, against marked work
process.description: At week five a recurring error has either stopped appearing in the marked sets or it has not, and that is the review. At week eleven the decision is to extend, switch subject or stop because the subject is now self-sustaining. Stopping is a legitimate outcome, and a review that consists of asking whether everyone is happy is not a review.

whyPoints.title: Plans with an end date
whyPoints.description: Every block is a stated number of sessions with a review point and a finish, not a rolling monthly charge. Families know at the outset what they are buying and when the decision to continue falls. Open-ended bookings are how a term becomes a year without anybody producing an account of what changed.

whyPoints.title: Marked work as the only evidence
whyPoints.description: Progress is read from question sets marked against the board's published criteria, with the mark-scheme point named against each loss. A parent who was not in the lesson can still see whether a specific error has stopped appearing. Nothing here is reported as a general sense that things are going well.

whyPoints.title: Travel priced honestly, including the option we do not sell
whyPoints.description: This page costs out visiting tuition from five bases with the drive counted, because a parent comparing options needs the real figure for both. IB Gram delivers online only in the UAE, with no home visits anywhere in the country, and says so rather than letting a parent assume otherwise.

whyPoints.title: A slot built around the school bus
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time with deliberate margin after the bus and a meal, because a slot that is thirty minutes too early is a slot that gets missed. The tutor pool is wide enough to make an east-coast evening slot a normal request rather than a favour.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, at any point
whyPoints.description: Nothing on this page promises a number, a jump or a result. What a plan can honestly offer is that the mark your child is already capable of appears on the paper, which is where most lost IGCSE marks actually are. Any provider promising a specific number in advance is selling something that is not teaching.

whyPoints.title: The limits said first
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no group classes, no tutor for a syllabus code nobody teaches, and a written no when the weeks remaining are too few. Those statements cost bookings and they are the reason what is described on this page is what arrives in the lesson.

faqs.question: How much does a visiting IGCSE tutor charge to drive out to Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Published market bands for visiting one-to-one tuition in the UAE run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Bestimate's Dubai rate table sits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reported up to AED 500. For the east coast the number matters less than the structure: a tutor coming from Sharjah is committed for about five hours to teach for two, so expect a two-hour minimum, a surcharge, weekend-only availability, or a rate at the top of the band.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Fujairah cost per actual contact hour?
faqs.answer: Divide everything down before comparing. A monthly package of four two-hour home visits quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799 works out around AED 200 to 225 per teaching hour, while eight online sessions quoted around AED 799 works out near AED 100. Neither figure includes what the family absorbs in rearranged evenings or in a narrower subject list. The comparison that matters is cost per teaching hour against subject match, because a cheaper hour teaching the wrong specification is not cheap at all.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to homes anywhere in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and tutors arriving at a family's door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so the slot sits in a Fujairah evening after the school bus and a meal. This page prices visiting tuition anyway, because a parent weighing the options deserves real figures for the option we do not sell as well as the one we do.

faqs.question: How many weeks of tuition does my son need before the June series?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the losses are content, technique or timing, and that cannot be answered from a report. Broadly: a timing problem responds to four to six weeks of whole-paper work, a technique problem to six to eight weeks of mark-scheme work, and a genuine content gap to a term or more. A diagnostic session that watches your son attempt a timed question and reads one marked script will give a specific number, in writing, along with what happens if that number is not available.

faqs.question: We are starting in January with papers in May. What can realistically change?
faqs.answer: A great deal, provided the plan accepts what January means. There is time to close the three or four errors a mock exposed, time to build whole-paper timing, and time to rehearse command terms properly. There is not time to rebuild a missing year of content in three subjects at once. The realistic January plan narrows to one or two subjects, works from marked scripts rather than from the textbook, and spends March and April on whole papers rather than on topic revision.

faqs.question: My daughter is at a grade 4 and needs a grade 6. Is that jump realistic?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise it and anybody who does is selling something other than teaching. What can be assessed is how much of the current gap is technique rather than knowledge, because that fraction is what moves fastest. A student sitting at a 4 who understands the content and writes it badly has a very different ceiling from one who is missing half the specification. The diagnostic exists to tell you which of those is true before you commit a term of evenings and several thousand dirhams to finding out.

faqs.question: How do I know the plan is working after the first month?
faqs.answer: Read the marked sets rather than asking how things are going. By about week five a specific recurring error has either stopped appearing in your child's own written work or it has not, and that is a binary you can check without knowing the subject. A useful record names the mark-scheme point lost against each question, so the pattern is visible across four or five weeks. If the same loss is still there at week five and nothing in the plan has changed, ask then rather than waiting for a review.

faqs.question: What should my child be doing between the weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: One targeted set, finished. Twenty questions on the single error that keeps recurring does more for a grade than an extra hour of teaching, because the hour explains and the set embeds. Later in a plan the set becomes a full paper attempted to time and marked by the student against the published criteria, with the tutor auditing that marking rather than redoing it. If the set is not getting done, the fix is usually its length or its timing rather than more pressure.

faqs.question: Do lessons continue through Ramadan, and at what time of day?
faqs.answer: They continue, with the time moved once for the month rather than renegotiated weekly. The shortened school day frees the afternoon, which suits younger students, while older students revising late often do better in a slot after Iftar. The important part is making a single change for the month: a slot that drifts every week is a slot that gets missed, and a missed week in a twelve-week block is a meaningful fraction of the plan. Agree the Ramadan timing when the block is first set up.

faqs.question: Can we pause tuition over the school holidays and pick it up again?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families pausing is sensible. The alternative worth considering in a Year 11 year is using part of a break as a short intensive block instead: three sessions in a week with nothing else competing for the hours achieves roughly what six weekly term-time sessions achieve, which makes it the cheapest acceleration in the calendar. The limit is the student rather than the subject. A child who has just finished mock weeks may need the first week of a break to actually be a break.

faqs.question: What happens in the last fortnight before the first paper?
faqs.answer: Almost no new content. Week two is whole papers under strict timing, a plan for the order answers will be attempted, and a decision about how the first ten minutes of each paper will be spent. The final week is short retrieval bursts, early nights and logistics. That last item is not trivial: confirm the statement of entry, the centre, the room and the correct zone version of the timetable, because Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in Year 10 rather than waiting until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest year in which to fix anything, because nothing is being examined and the work compounds. Algebraic fluency secured in Year 10 pays into every science paper the following year, while the same work bought in March of Year 11 competes directly with revision for the same evenings. A block of eight to twelve sessions in Year 10 typically achieves more than twice that number bought in the final two terms, which is an argument about timing rather than about effort.

faqs.question: What happens when a visiting tutor cancels during exam term?
faqs.answer: This is the structural risk of a long drive and it is worth asking about before booking rather than after. A tutor crossing the Hajar mountains has weather, traffic and their own commitments between them and your child, and a cancellation in the final six weeks is a week of the plan gone with no easy replacement nearby. Online sessions carry the same risk of illness and none of the travel risk, and a wider tutor pool means a cover session is a realistic option rather than a theoretical one.

faqs.question: Who writes the revision timetable, the family or the tutor?
faqs.answer: The tutor should draft it, the student should own it, and the parent should be able to read it. A plan written by a tutor who has seen marked scripts will prioritise by where the marks actually are, which almost never matches what the student feels worst about. A plan the student has not agreed to will not survive February. The practical version is one page: which papers, in which order, which errors are being tracked, and what happens in each of the remaining weeks.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors part way through a block if the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be raised early rather than endured politely. A mismatch usually shows up in the first three sessions as a student who is working but not being stretched, or who is being taught above the level the diagnostic found. Because the written record travels with the plan, a new tutor starts from the marked sets rather than from scratch. Changing tutor at week two costs a session of continuity; changing at week ten costs most of the block.

faqs.question: How late in Year 11 is it still worth paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: Up to about six weeks before the first paper, with the plan narrowed and the goal changed. In that window tuition cannot repair a missing year of content, but it can reliably recover marks lost to unwritten working, misread command terms and poor time allocation, and those account for a surprising share of the gap on most scripts. Inside six weeks the honest answer is sometimes no, and it should come in writing from a diagnostic rather than after the first invoice.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the number of weeks you have left
fujairah/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: Everything on this page follows from one figure: the teaching weeks between today and your child's series. With a term available, a twelve-week block in one subject with marked work between sessions is the shape that reliably moves a grade. With six weeks, the plan narrows to the papers where marks are most recoverable. With fewer than that, the honest answer may be the autumn series and a short, specific plan instead. One free 45-minute diagnostic, no card details, gives you that number in writing, along with what it can and cannot buy, before anyone asks you for money.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tier. Each one is matched to a single subject and a single syllabus code, because a Physics 0625 paper and a 4PH1 paper are marked against different rules.

intro.heading: Start with the date, not the tutor
paragraphs: Al Faseel sits on the Fujairah coast, a short drive from the corniche and the port, and the families who live there have a narrower set of school choices than families in Dubai or Sharjah. Fujairah's private-school list is short. That has one practical consequence for IGCSE: the number of adults within driving distance who have actually marked a Cambridge Extended paper or a Pearson Edexcel Higher tier paper is small, and in a subject like Chemistry or Economics it may be zero. The search for a home tutor in Al Faseel usually ends with a parent discovering that the nearest person advertising the subject teaches something adjacent to it.

So the honest answer is to invert the question. Do not start by asking who lives nearby. Start by asking what date your child is working to, what that date requires, and who in the world can teach it. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Al Faseel as one-to-one online lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, which means the pool of candidates is the pool of qualified subject teachers rather than the pool of qualified subject teachers who happen to live within twenty minutes of your villa. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India; there are none anywhere in the UAE, and no page on this site will tell you otherwise.

That framing matters because IGCSE is a calendar qualification. The grade is not set by how much work happens across two years; it is set by what a student can do inside a two-hour paper on a fixed morning. Cambridge International runs its International GCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Entries close months before the paper. Coursework and practical components close earlier still. A family that starts tutoring in the week the timetable lands has already lost the part of the year where tutoring is cheapest and most effective.

The sections below are built around that calendar. There is a table that counts the year backwards from results day to the entry deadline, a second that sets out what an eight-week run before a paper should contain and what evidence proves it worked, a third on the Core and Extended decision that Year 10 families in Fujairah make without much guidance, and a fourth on what tutoring actually costs around the emirate, with each figure attributed. The permit question gets its own section, because a parent in Fujairah can check a tutor's legal position in a way that most parents do not know is available to them.

One more thing before the detail. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level regulator, which is a genuine difference from Dubai's KHDA or Abu Dhabi's ADEK. It changes where a parent looks things up, and it changes what an inspection report means. That is covered too, because a page that answers the tutoring question and leaves the regulatory question unanswered has only done half the job.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.programmesIntro: Al Faseel students arrive at IGCSE from several directions: a Cambridge Lower Secondary pathway, an Indian middle school, or a move from another emirate. The four stages below are the ones that matter to a Fujairah family planning backwards from a June paper.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, ending in Checkpoint tests that schools use for setting rather than for university entry. Checkpoint is diagnostic: it tells a school whether a student is on the Core or Extended track in maths and science, and it is the last low-stakes evidence anyone gets before the real thing. Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October windows.
programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah the Checkpoint result often decides whether a student is entered for Core or Extended in Year 10, and that decision is harder to reverse than parents expect. A Year 9 student in Al Faseel who is capable of Extended maths but has been placed on Core has a grade ceiling of C before the course has started. Two terms of targeted work in Year 9 is the cheapest intervention available.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by written paper. Cambridge syllabuses split into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel splits maths into Foundation and Higher tier. Grades come as 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus version your child's school entered. Coursework exists in some subjects and not others, and the school chooses.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, a British-track student must pass five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. One competitor page ranking for this query states six subjects. Five is the sourced figure, taken from the UAE clarification reported in July 2026, and it changes which subjects a Fujairah family should protect.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two-year route most Fujairah British-curriculum students take after IGCSE, in three or four subjects. AS sits at the end of the first year in some schools and is cashed in as a standalone qualification; A2 completes the full A Level. Subject prerequisites are set at IGCSE grade level, which is why Year 11 grades matter beyond the certificate itself.
programmes.countryNote: The equivalency requirement for the British track also names the post-16 stage: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A Fujairah student who drops to two AS subjects without checking that rule can finish Year 13 with a certificate that will not attest cleanly. Verify on the Ministry of Education's own channel.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme as the alternative at 16
programmes.description: Six subjects plus the core of Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, graded out of 45 points with 24 as the diploma minimum. Students who finish IGCSE in Fujairah and want the DP generally move school or move emirate, because the local DP offer is limited. The jump from Extended IGCSE to Higher Level DP is real but navigable with a term of bridging work.
programmes.countryNote: No IB points threshold for UAE equivalency is published in a source this project could verify, so none appears on this page. The British-track numbers above were read from a named news report; the IB figure was not. A Fujairah family weighing DP against A Level should ask the Ministry of Education directly rather than trust a figure on a tutoring site, including this one.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with the Cambridge syllabus code and, where relevant, the Pearson Edexcel equivalent. Ask your child's school which code it entered; the two boards assess the same subject differently, and a tutor working from the wrong one wastes the hours you are paying for.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980; Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Cambridge splits the paper set between a non-calculator and a calculator paper, each carrying half the grade; Edexcel 4MA1 runs two calculator papers at 50% each across Foundation and Higher tier. Marks go missing on algebraic fractions, bounds, vectors and the last two parts of a structured question. Check the current paper structure for your child's entry year on the board's own syllabus page.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 0972; Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Cambridge runs a multiple-choice paper worth 30%, a theory paper worth 50% and a practical component worth 20% taken either as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Edexcel 4PH1 has two written papers and no separate practical exam, with practical skills examined inside the theory. Electricity and circuit calculation lose the most marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 0971; Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Same 30/50/20 split as Physics on the Cambridge syllabus. Students lose marks on mole calculations that require two conversions, on the exact wording of tests for ions and gases, and on writing ionic equations with charges balanced as well as atoms. Organic reaction conditions are pure recall and are the fastest marks to recover in a short run of lessons.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 0970; Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest-content syllabus in the science group and the one where students most often confuse revision with reading. Extended candidates lose marks on osmosis and water-potential language, on genetic-cross notation, and on the command term 'explain' where they have described instead. Data-handling questions on an unfamiliar graph reward practice more than memorisation.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500 / 0990; Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading and writing papers rather than literature. The directed-writing and composition tasks are marked against a style and audience rubric, so a technically clean essay can sit two grades below its potential if the register is wrong. Summary questions reward precision in the student's own words and punish lifted phrasing from the passage.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 / 0987; Edexcel 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries disproportionate weight: an unlabelled axis or a shift drawn in the wrong direction costs marks that the surrounding prose cannot recover. Extended candidates are assessed on evaluation, which means a judgement supported by the diagram rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages. Past-paper work with a marked script is the only reliable route.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 0986; Edexcel 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study based, so the context in the insert decides the answer. The common failure is a correct textbook point applied to a business the insert does not describe. Calculation questions on break-even, cash flow and ratios are the most predictable marks on the paper and the most frequently dropped through arithmetic rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 / 0984; Edexcel 4CP0)
subjects.description: Two papers: computer systems theory and algorithms with programming. Pseudocode questions are marked on logic, not on syntax, which students find counterintuitive after a year of writing Python. Binary, hexadecimal and two's complement conversion appear every series and are worth drilling to automatic accuracy early.

subjects.name: Geography (0460 / 0976; Edexcel 4GE1)
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, graphs and photographs are the dependable marks; case-study questions are where grades are made or lost, because a named example with figures scores and a generic example does not. Students in Fujairah often have strong local material on coastal processes and water scarcity that they never think to use.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and International Mathematics (0606 / 0607)
subjects.description: 0607 International Mathematics is the syllabus IB-feeder schools often choose, and it includes an investigation paper that no other maths syllabus has. 0606 Additional Mathematics is a bridge to A Level for strong Extended candidates. Both reward students who can write a method out in full; both punish answers that jump to a result.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 first language / 0544 foreign language)
subjects.description: Fujairah students sit Arabic alongside the international curriculum because the federal rules require Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies in private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. First-language and foreign-language syllabuses are separate qualifications with different papers, and being placed on the wrong one is a common and fixable problem.

subjects.name: History (0470 / 0977; Edexcel 4HI1)
subjects.description: Source-based papers where the mark scheme rewards use of provenance over summary of content. Students who can say why a source was produced, by whom, and for which audience move up a level without learning more facts. Essay questions need a line of argument stated in the first sentence and then defended, not discovered on the way.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.regionsIntro: Fujairah's districts sit between the Gulf of Oman and the Hajar mountains, and the distances between them are short but the school options are not evenly spread. regions.note: Coastal district close to the corniche and the port, with a mix of villa compounds and apartment blocks. Families here are usually within fifteen minutes of Fujairah city schools, which makes an after-school session at 16:30 or 17:00 realistic without a long drive first.

regions.name: Fujairah City centre
regions.note: Where most of the emirate's private-school capacity sits, along with the Ministry of Education's own secondary provision. A student living in Al Faseel and schooling here has the shortest commute in the emirate and the widest subject choice available locally.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland residential district north-west of the city centre, closer to the mountain edge. The drive to the coastal schools adds time in the afternoon, which pushes realistic session starts later and makes a fixed online slot easier to hold than a travelling tutor's arrival time.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Established residential area with a high proportion of long-term resident families. Subject demand here skews towards IGCSE sciences and maths at Extended tier, which is also where the local specialist supply is thinnest across the emirate.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South of the city along the coast road, quieter and more spread out. The practical effect on tutoring is scheduling: a family in Al Gurfa with two children at different schools rarely has both home before 16:00, so sessions tend to run in the 17:00 to 20:00 window.

regions.name: Dibba Al Fujairah
regions.note: At the northern end of the emirate, around ninety minutes from Al Faseel by road. Students here have the fewest local IGCSE options of anywhere in Fujairah, and online delivery is less a preference than the only way to reach a subject specialist at all.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: A Sharjah enclave on the Fujairah coast, which means its private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than the federal Ministry of Education. Families who move between Khor Fakkan and Fujairah city change regulator without changing emirate coastline.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Small coastal settlements between Fujairah city and Dibba. Secondary provision is limited and boarding or long commutes are common, so families here plan tutoring around travel days as much as around school deadlines.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the coastal districts
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private schools are concentrated in and around Fujairah city, within reach of Al Faseel, Sakamkam and Merashid. The list is short and changes, so check the Ministry of Education's own directory for the currently licensed set rather than trusting any third-party list, including this one.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the Khor Fakkan corridor
schoolClusters.note: Families who want a wider IGCSE or IB offer within commuting range often look to Sharjah, whose private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. That authority approves fees, curricula and assessment methods, not just inspection outcomes, which makes it worth reading before a mid-year move.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools Fujairah families follow online
schoolClusters.note: Some Al Faseel families keep a child at a Dubai school through boarding or a weekly commute, and others simply want a tutor familiar with the syllabus choices Dubai schools make. Dubai private schools are licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority.

The tutor works a term ahead of the school's scheme of work where possible, so the student meets each topic twice: once in the lesson before school covers it, once in the week after. This is the cheapest version of tutoring per grade gained, because nothing is being repaired.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Faseel can actually be booked for this term
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Faseel, through IB Gram, means a named subject specialist teaching your child one-to-one over live video at a fixed time each week, on Gulf Standard Time. It does not mean somebody arriving at the door. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and that has been the position on every country page this site publishes.

The reason to say that in the first paragraph rather than the tenth is that it changes what you should compare. A travelling tutor in Fujairah is priced partly on distance. The market quotes in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and a good part of that gap is the drive. In Dubai the drive buys convenience. In Fujairah, where the private-school set is small and the specialist pool smaller, the drive buys a shorter list of candidates as well. A family in Al Faseel paying the travel premium is often paying more for less subject match.

What you can book this term is specific. A single subject, a named syllabus code, one or two sessions a week, starting after a free trial lesson where you and your child meet the tutor and decide. If the subject is one where Fujairah has no local specialist at all — Extended Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science — online is not the compromise option, it is the only route to someone who has marked that paper. If no specialist is free in the slot you need, you will be told that rather than offered the nearest available generalist.

The rest of this page assumes you have a date in mind. If you do not, the next section will give you one: the Cambridge and Pearson year laid out backwards, so you can see which deadline is nearest and work from it.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Pearson year, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names an exam session, an entry deadline or a results date. That is the single largest gap in the whole cluster, and it is the one a parent actually needs filled. So here is the shape of the year, built from the boards' own published guidance, with the structural point stated first: the exam is the last event in the sequence, not the first, and almost every decision that affects the grade is made before it.

Cambridge International runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October windows. The February/March series exists, but it is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate does not sit it — a point worth checking against any advice your child has been given, because it circulates incorrectly. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year.

One Cambridge detail deserves its own sentence, because it has cost candidates whole papers. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If your child has printed a timetable from a forum rather than from the school, that is worth an evening's attention. Always work from the live official timetable rather than from any date restated on a third-party page, including this one.

The milestones below are ordered by how far ahead of the paper they fall. Dates that have already happened are cited with their year because that is what makes them checkable; future sessions are named by month, because a month stays true and a month-plus-year goes stale.

sections.heading: Eight weeks before a paper: what the run actually contains
paragraphs: Most families in Al Faseel start looking for a tutor somewhere between eight and twelve weeks before a paper. That is late for building knowledge and about right for converting knowledge into marks, so the shape of the work should change accordingly. An eight-week run that teaches the syllabus from the start will not finish it. An eight-week run that attacks the specific causes of lost marks usually moves a grade, sometimes two from a low base, and occasionally not at all — which is why the first session has to be a measurement rather than a lesson.

The measurement is a full past paper, sat under timed conditions, marked against the official scheme, and then analysed by cause. A lost mark has a cause: content not known, content known but not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method correct and arithmetic wrong, or time ran out. Those six causes need completely different remedies, and a tutor who starts teaching before knowing the mix is guessing. Parents can ask for that analysis in writing after the first session; it is the single most useful document in the whole engagement.

From there the weeks have a pattern. The first half of the run goes after the largest causes one at a time, with a short timed section at the end of each session to check the fix held. The second half shifts to full papers under exam conditions, because stamina and timing are separate skills from content and are usually the last thing to be fixed. The final fortnight should contain no new content at all. If something has not been learned by then, learning it costs more marks elsewhere than it gains.

The table below is the version used for a single Extended science or maths subject. It is a template, not a promise: a student starting from a D with gaps across the syllabus and a student starting from a B with two weak topics need different weeks two through five, and the plan should be rewritten after the diagnostic rather than before it.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the Year 10 decision Fujairah families make too quickly
paragraphs: Cambridge splits several of its most-entered syllabuses into a Core and an Extended tier, and the practical consequence is a grade ceiling. A Core candidate is assessed on a narrower syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade C. An Extended candidate sits harder papers and can reach A*. Pearson Edexcel does the same thing in maths with Foundation and Higher tier. The decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10, often on the basis of a Year 9 Checkpoint result and a teacher's judgement, and it is frequently not explained to the parent in those terms.

That matters more in Fujairah than in Dubai, for an unglamorous reason: class sizes in a small private-school market make setting coarser. A school with one Year 10 maths set per tier has to place borderline students somewhere, and the safe placement from the school's point of view is Core. From the family's point of view, a capable student placed on Core has lost access to grades A* to B before the course begins, and lost the A Level and university routes that depend on them.

If your child is borderline, the useful move is not an argument with the school but evidence. Two terms of Year 9 or early Year 10 work on the Extended-only content, with a timed Extended paper as the proof, gives a teacher something concrete to re-set on. That is a far cheaper intervention than a Year 11 scramble, and it is the clearest example of why starting from the calendar rather than from the crisis saves money. Check also which grading scale your child's syllabus uses: some Cambridge subjects report 9-1 and others A*-G, and the two are not interchangeable on a university application.
The comparison below is written for a parent deciding whether to push for a re-set. Ask the school which tier has been entered, in writing, well before the entry deadline — not after the mock.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Fujairah, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a family budgets against. A single weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor, priced at the middle of the online band, lands somewhere around AED 600 to 1,200 a month on the published market estimates, and an exam-year plan with two subjects or two sessions a week runs higher. Bestimate's rate work for Dubai puts budget weekly sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. The figures come from competitor pages and from published rate tables read in October 2026, and they are here because almost nobody in this search result publishes a number in dirhams at all. Three of the six pages that rank for queries like this one publish no price; the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family pays school fees in. A parent who cannot see a number cannot compare, which is the point of the table below.

The interesting line in that table is the in-home one. The market quotes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for a travelling tutor, with the upper end for a named specialist. Part of that spread is seniority and part of it is the car. In a dense city the car buys genuine convenience. In Fujairah it buys a smaller candidate list, because the set of people who will drive to Al Faseel on a Tuesday evening and who have also marked Extended Chemistry is close to empty. If you are weighing the premium, weigh it against subject match rather than against convenience alone.

For context on the wider cost picture: the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Fujairah schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision rather than KHDA, so that freeze does not apply here — but it does tell you something about where tutoring sits in a family budget when the larger line item is held flat.

sections.heading: Why Al Faseel runs short of local IGCSE specialists, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Fujairah is the only emirate on the Gulf of Oman coast, separated from Dubai by the Hajar mountains, and that geography shapes the tutoring market more than anything else. The emirate's private-school sector is small. A small sector employs a small number of subject teachers. A small number of subject teachers means that for any given syllabus code at Extended tier, the number of people within driving distance of Al Faseel who have taught it recently may be one, or none.

This is not a judgement about Fujairah schools. It is arithmetic, and the same arithmetic applies in Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain, which is why none of the three appears anywhere in the competitor pages researched for this market. Those pages are written for Dubai and Abu Dhabi and reach the smaller emirates by changing a place name. A Fujairah family reading them is being sold a Dubai supply picture that does not exist on this coast.

What follows practically is a different search strategy. Stop looking for proximity and start looking for coverage: which subjects at which tier can actually be staffed, how quickly, and what happens when they cannot. The table in the next section covers the permit question; this one is about availability, and the honest version is that a common subject at Core tier is easy, a common subject at Extended tier is straightforward, and a minority subject at Extended tier may take longer or may not be available in your preferred slot at all. You should be told which of those applies before you pay, not after.

The second practical consequence is scheduling. An online slot can be held at 17:00 every Tuesday for a year. A travelling tutor's 17:00 is a 16:30 departure and a 17:10 arrival, and over a Fujairah school term that drifts. For a student working to a June paper, consistency in the slot is worth more than almost anything else, because the homework cycle between sessions only works if the sessions land where they are meant to.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and how would you know?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and most parents do not know that. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Two things follow. First, anyone who tells you the permit costs money, or that it is optional, is wrong on a point of federal regulation: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here; a number circulating online could not be verified against any official source and is left out deliberately. Second, because the permit is free and takes two working days, there is no good reason for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one.

There is a separate rule parents should know about before asking a school teacher for private lessons. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as the regulator's exact wording, and check the current policy document before relying on it. The underlying point is sound everywhere in the country: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay privately.

A note on what IB Gram is and is not. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. It holds none of those relationships and claims none. An operation running a physical tuition centre in Dubai would need a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute; IB Gram runs no UAE premises and should never be described that way. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is useful to a parent. Implying an endorsement is not.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may do with coursework, and what must be refused
paragraphs: This market has a real problem with assessed work, and a parent in Al Faseel should know what it looks like before encountering it. Pages in this search result sell finished Internal Assessments. One advertises completed IA work at a fixed price. That is not a grey area and it is not a service: it is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's qualification at risk, not the seller's. A board that identifies submitted work as not the candidate's own treats it as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the child.

The boundary is actually quite clear once stated. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, model how a similar question is approached, read a draft the student has written and say where it does not meet the criteria, and show the student how to improve it themselves. A tutor may not write the coursework, may not draft the assignment, may not edit a piece to completion so that the words are the tutor's, and may not supply a finished piece for submission. The distinction is who produced the sentences.

There is a related rule about materials. Boards publish syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and those documents are theirs. A tutoring provider that offers them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and in the case of unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct approach is to reference them, cite the official address, and link out so that a parent reads the real thing. Everything factual on this page about Cambridge and Pearson sessions comes from the boards' own published guidance, and the boards' own sites are where you should confirm it.

For an Al Faseel family this is a selection criterion rather than a disclaimer. Ask any prospective tutor what they would do if your child asked them to write a coursework paragraph. The right answer is a refusal and an explanation of what they would do instead. An answer that treats the question as a negotiation tells you what will happen the week before the deadline.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the syllabus code and the date
process.description: The three things that determine whether a match is possible. Subject alone is not enough: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are different papers with different practical arrangements, and a tutor should be matched to the code your child's school actually entered. Ask the school if you are unsure; the code sits on the entry confirmation.

process.title: We check coverage honestly before promising anything
process.description: Common subjects at Core and Extended tier staff quickly. A minority subject at Extended tier in a specific evening slot may not be available at all. You will hear which of those applies to your request, with a realistic timeframe, rather than being offered the nearest available generalist and left to discover the mismatch in week three.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with you able to watch
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor before anything is paid. The point is not a sales call: it is for your child to find out whether they can follow this person's explanation, and for you to hear whether the tutor talks about the mark scheme or about enthusiasm. If the fit is wrong, say so and the match changes.

process.title: A diagnostic paper in the first fortnight
process.description: A past paper sat under timed conditions, marked against the official scheme, and returned with the lost marks grouped by cause. This is what the plan is built from, and it is the document to ask for if you want to know what you are buying. Without it, a tutoring plan is a guess dressed as a schedule.

process.title: Fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are held online at the same time each week, after the Fujairah school day. Consistency is the part that makes the homework cycle between sessions work. During Ramadan the slot usually shifts later, often to a post-Iftar time, and that is arranged in advance rather than improvised week to week.

process.title: Written progress against the topic list, not vibes
process.description: Progress is reported as marks on marked work and as topics closed on the risk list from the diagnostic. If a topic has not moved in three weeks, that is the conversation to have. Ask for the updated risk list before each half-term; it is the clearest signal of whether the hours are converting into grades.

whyPoints.title: The specialist is matched to the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Not to the subject in general. A tutor who has taught 0580 Extended maths to a UAE cohort knows which questions the board returns to and where the method marks sit. The same tutor may be the wrong choice for Edexcel 4MA1 Higher tier, and saying so is more useful to an Al Faseel family than claiming to cover everything.

whyPoints.title: Geography stops limiting the shortlist
whyPoints.description: Al Faseel's local pool of Extended-tier subject specialists is small, and in some subjects it is empty. Online one-to-one delivery replaces the question of who lives nearby with the question of who can teach this paper. That is the whole argument, and it is strongest precisely in the emirates competitor pages ignore.

whyPoints.title: Dirham figures, with their source attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is a market figure read from a published source in October 2026 and attributed as such, never presented as an IB Gram price. Three of the six pages ranking for searches like this one publish no price at all, and two quote in dollars. A parent who cannot see a number in dirhams cannot compare anything.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is treated as the real constraint
whyPoints.description: Entries close months before the paper, coursework closes earlier, and the Cambridge zone timetable decides the exact morning. A plan built backwards from results day finds the deadlines that are actually near. No competitor page in this market names a session or a deadline at all, which is why that gap is worth filling properly.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help stays on the right side of the line
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criteria, feedback on the student's own draft. Not writing, not completing, not supplying. This market contains pages selling finished Internal Assessments, and the risk of that lands on the student's qualification rather than on the seller's business. The boundary is stated here so you can test anyone else against it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for your subject, tier and slot, you are told. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several route UAE parents to a phone number in another country without saying so. Knowing the limit before you pay is worth more than a promise that unravels in week two.

faqs.question: Can I actually get an IGCSE home tutor in Al Faseel who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons for Al Faseel families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. There is a local in-home market, and the published rates for it run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. Before paying that premium, check what it buys in Fujairah specifically. The emirate has a small private-school sector, so the number of travelling tutors who have actually taught your child's syllabus at Extended tier may be very small.

faqs.question: Which exam series do IGCSE students in Fujairah sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs its International GCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and those are the two a UAE candidate sits. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The February and March series does exist in the Cambridge calendar but it is offered to India only, so it is not a UAE option, and advice to the contrary circulates more often than it should. Checkpoint tests for the lower secondary years sit in March, May and October windows. Confirm the exact dates for your child on the board's live official timetable through the school.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The practical risk is a timetable printed from a forum or a revision site rather than obtained from the school. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work only from the timetable that officer provides, checked against the board's own site.

faqs.question: How much should a family in Al Faseel expect to pay per month for one subject?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for a single weekly hour put a mid-range qualified tutor at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with budget options from around AED 240 to 600 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Advertised packages in the market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are market figures read in October 2026 from published rate tables and competitor pages, not IB Gram prices. For an actual quote, take the free trial lesson and discuss the subject, tier and number of sessions you need.

faqs.question: My child was put on Core maths but I think Extended is right. Can that change?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window is Year 10 rather than Year 11. A Core entry caps the grade at C, so the decision removes the top four grades before teaching begins. Schools in a small market often place borderline students on Core because the sets are coarser. What reopens the conversation is evidence: Extended-only content taught, then a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme and shown to the teacher. Ask the school in writing which tier has been entered and when the entry deadline falls, well before that deadline rather than after the mock.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks before the paper too late to start tutoring in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: It is late for building knowledge and about right for converting knowledge into marks, provided the run is built correctly. The first session should be a full past paper under timed conditions, marked against the official scheme, with every lost mark attributed to a cause: content not known, content not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, arithmetic error, or time. The remedies for those six are different. Weeks two to five attack the largest causes, weeks six and seven run full papers to time, and the final week adds nothing new.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Fujairah students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. It is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service, with a stated two working days to complete. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine amount is published, so none is quoted here.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Fujairah, and how is that different from Dubai?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah's to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's to its Department of Knowledge. The difference is practical: a Fujairah parent looking up inspection outcomes or curriculum approvals goes to the federal ministry rather than an emirate authority, and a family moving from Fujairah to Sharjah changes regulator as well as school.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does an Al Faseel student need for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Post-16, the requirement names one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page ranking for these searches states six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the sourced figure. Verify your own case through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam for IGCSE sciences in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and on what the school entered. Cambridge science syllabuses carry a practical component worth 20% of the grade, taken either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school decides which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam; practical skills are examined inside the written papers instead. Those are genuinely different pieces of preparation, so ask the school which component your child is entered for before booking any tutoring around it.

faqs.question: What may an Al Faseel tutor do with an IGCSE coursework draft, and what must they refuse?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written, and say where it falls short of the criteria. A tutor may not write the coursework, draft the assignment, or edit a piece to completion so that the sentences are the tutor's. Pages in this market sell finished assessed work outright. The risk of that falls on the student's qualification, which is why the line is stated plainly here.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for my subject at Extended tier?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay rather than after. Common subjects at Core and Extended tier staff quickly. A minority subject at Extended tier in one specific evening slot sometimes cannot be filled, and in that case the honest answer is a realistic timeframe or none at all, not the nearest available generalist. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several route UAE parents to a phone number in another country. Ask the question directly of anyone you are considering.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around travel between Fujairah and abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the shift is usually planned rather than improvised. During Ramadan most families move the slot later, often to a post-Iftar time, and because lessons are online the arrangement does not depend on anybody's drive home. Travel is the same: a fixed online slot follows the student to another time zone with a one-off adjustment rather than a cancelled term. What matters is agreeing the change a week ahead so the homework cycle between sessions is not broken in the process.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic studies affect IGCSE planning for Al Faseel students?
faqs.answer: They affect the timetable rather than the IGCSE grades. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must follow the ministry's general regulations, so those subjects run alongside the international curriculum. The result is a fuller week than an equivalent UK timetable. For equivalency purposes, Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five-subject IGCSE count, so a family should be clear which subjects are carrying that requirement.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective for a Fujairah student as someone in the room?
faqs.answer: The honest answer is that format matters less than match and consistency. A travelling generalist in the room who has never taught Extended Chemistry will not move the grade; a specialist on screen working from marked past papers usually will. In Al Faseel the comparison is rarely between an equally qualified local and an equally qualified online tutor, because the local specialist often does not exist. Online also holds the slot: the same time every week, which is the condition the homework cycle between sessions depends on.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.closingHeading: Work out your nearest deadline, then book one trial lesson
fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-faseel.closingBody: The useful next step for an Al Faseel family is not choosing a tutor. It is finding out which deadline is nearest: the entry confirmation, the coursework submission, the mock window, or the paper itself. Ask your child's school for the syllabus code, the tier entered, and the exams officer's timetable for your Cambridge zone. Then book a free trial lesson with a matched specialist and ask for a diagnostic paper in the first fortnight.
