intro.heading: Knowing the subject and knowing the specification are different jobs
paragraphs: Al Gurfa stretches south of Fujairah city along the coast road, and most students here travel in to the city-centre schools. The tutoring question families end up asking is not geographical. It is whether anybody they can reach actually knows the thing their child is sitting, because a graduate chemist and a person who has marked Cambridge 0620 Extended scripts are not the same professional, and only one of them can tell you where the marks are going.

The distinction has a test. Somebody who knows the specification can name the papers and their weightings without pausing, say whether a practical component exists on that board, map a topic to the paper it appears in, explain why a raw mark is not a grade until the board sets boundaries after marking, and tell you what a November resit is worth component by component. Somebody who knows the subject in general can do none of those and will instead talk about confidence, potential and the importance of past papers. Both sound equally reassuring on a phone call, which is why the test matters.

This page is built around those checkable things. Grade boundaries, explained properly rather than guessed at. Topic-to-paper mapping, which schools rarely hand out and which turns a vague revision plan into a targeted one. What progress evidence looks like when it is real. How resits actually work, since both boards run a November series and most families treat it as a last resort rather than a plan. And the three documents to extract from the school before paying anybody.

IB Gram delivers to Al Gurfa as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, stated the same way on every country page here. The in-home market is real and publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In a small emirate the premium buys a shorter list of specifications somebody has actually taught, which is the opposite of what a family is trying to buy.

One structural anchor to carry through. Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series, and those are the two a UAE candidate sits; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Every date specific to your child should come from the exams officer's own timetable rather than from any third-party page, this one included. Where this page cites a date it is a past one, kept with its year because that is what makes it checkable, and where a session is still ahead it is named by month only so the page does not go stale without anybody touching it. No grade boundary figure appears anywhere here, for the same reason: boundaries belong to the boards, they move every series, and a number quoted second-hand will eventually be wrong.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-gurfa.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the topic-to-paper detail that a tutor who has taught the specification will know and a general subject graduate usually will not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980; Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Cambridge splits the entry between a non-calculator and a calculator paper at half the grade each; Edexcel 4MA1 runs two calculator papers at 50% apiece across Foundation and Higher tier. The method-mark structure is the thing to know: a written method earns marks even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Physics (0625; Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: On Cambridge, a multiple-choice paper at 30%, theory at 50% and a practical component at 20% sat as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Edexcel has no separate practical exam. Circuit behaviour under load and sign conventions carry the predictable losses.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620; Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations needing two conversions sit on the theory paper; the exact wording of ion and gas tests appears across both theory and the practical component. Organic conditions are pure recall and recoverable in two sessions, which is why a specialist goes there first.

subjects.name: Biology (0610; Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content load in the sciences. The highest-volume avoidable loss is answering describe where the question said explain, which appears on every paper and is a notation habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500; Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading and writing papers rather than literature. The summary question penalises phrasing lifted from the passage because the marks are for the student's own words, and directed writing is marked against register and audience as much as accuracy.

subjects.name: Economics (0455; Edexcel 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram marks are awarded individually: labelled axes, correct initial position, correct direction of shift, new equilibrium identified. Prose cannot recover a wrong diagram, which makes diagram drilling unusually efficient per hour spent.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450; Edexcel 4BS1)
subjects.description: One paper is built on a case-study insert and the insert decides the answer. The dominant error in scripts is a correct textbook point applied to a business the insert does not describe, which is a reading failure rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478; Edexcel 4CP0)
subjects.description: Two papers: systems theory, and algorithms with programming. Pseudocode is marked on logic rather than syntax. Binary, hexadecimal and two's complement conversion appear every series and should be drilled to automatic accuracy early.

subjects.name: Geography (0460; Edexcel 4GE1)
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, graphs and photographs are the dependable marks; case studies decide the grade. A named example with figures scores where a generic description does not, and Fujairah's own coastline and water scarcity are usable material.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics (0606 / 0607)
subjects.description: 0607 International Mathematics carries an investigation paper no other maths syllabus has, and is often the choice at schools feeding into the IB. 0606 bridges to A Level. Both reward a fully written method and punish an answer that arrives without one.

sections.heading: What knowing the specification means, in testable terms
paragraphs: Through IB Gram, an IGCSE home tutor for an Al Gurfa student means a specialist matched to one syllabus code, teaching one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to the door: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and home visits exist only in India. What makes the match worth anything is the code, so it is confirmed in writing before the first session rather than assumed.

The reason to insist on that is that the two boards diverge in ways a general subject teacher will not anticipate. On Cambridge science syllabuses a practical component carries twenty per cent of the grade, sat either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam; the same skills are examined inside the written papers. A term spent preparing for a component your child is not sitting is a term gone, and the mistake is invisible until results.

Four questions settle competence quickly and none of them requires you to know the answers. What are the components and what is each worth. Does a practical exam exist on this specification. Which paper does this topic appear in. And what does a raw mark of, say, fifty-two actually mean before the board sets boundaries. A person who has taught the course answers each in a sentence. A person who has not describes their approach, which is a different kind of answer and is itself the information.

Everything below expands those four. The grade-boundary section is the one most families have never had explained, and it changes how a mock result should be read. The topic-to-paper section is the one that changes how revision is planned. Both are free to ask about and neither appears on any competitor page researched for this market.

sections.heading: Why a raw mark is not a grade, and what a mock result really tells you
paragraphs: Parents read a mock percentage as if it were a grade, and tutors who do not know better encourage it. It is not one. On both boards the grade boundaries for a series are set by the board after that series has been marked, taking account of how the cohort performed and how the paper behaved, and they are published after results. A raw mark therefore has no fixed grade attached to it until that happens. The same mark can fall either side of a boundary in two different series.

That has three practical consequences for an Al Gurfa family. First, a mock graded against last year's boundaries is an estimate, not a result, and should be described that way. Second, a student sitting two marks below a boundary is not two marks from a grade in any reliable sense, because the boundary will move. Third, the useful number out of a mock is not the percentage at all. It is the distribution of lost marks across causes and topics, which is stable information and can be acted on.

This is also why a tutor who talks only in predicted grades is giving you less than one who talks in marks. A grade prediction compresses everything into one letter and hides where the marks went. A marked script with losses attributed to six causes — content not known, content known but not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method correct but not written out, time ran out — tells you what to do next, and the remedies for those six are genuinely different from one another.

A note on the documents themselves: grade-boundary tables, mark schemes and past papers belong to Cambridge and Pearson. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material. The right practice is to reference them and point a parent to the official source, which is also where the actual boundaries for a past series can be read. No boundary figures appear on this page for that reason, and because a figure quoted second-hand is a figure that will eventually be wrong.

sections.heading: Topic-to-paper mapping: the thing schools rarely hand out
paragraphs: Revision plans usually list topics. Papers do not. A topic appears on a particular paper, in a particular question style, worth a particular number of marks, and the same topic can be worth four marks on one paper and twelve on another. A student revising a topic without knowing where it lands is revising for an unspecified audience, which is why so much revision produces familiarity rather than marks.

Mapping fixes this and takes one session. The tutor takes the student's weak topics from the diagnostic, places each on the paper it appears in, notes the typical question style and mark allocation, and ranks them by marks at stake rather than by how uncomfortable the student feels. The output is a list in which the top item is worth doing first for a reason the student can see, which also solves most motivation problems without a conversation about motivation.

The ranking frequently surprises families. A topic the student hates may be worth six marks across the whole entry, while a topic they are mildly shaky on carries thirty. On the Cambridge sciences, where a multiple-choice paper carries thirty per cent, elimination technique is itself worth more than several individual topics and is almost never taught. On mathematics, the discipline of writing out a method earns marks across every structured question on both papers, which makes it the highest-value single behaviour change available.

Schools do not usually produce this document, not out of reluctance but because it is per-student work. It is exactly the kind of thing a tutor should produce in the first fortnight, and exactly the kind of thing to ask for when deciding whether somebody knows the specification. A tutor who cannot map a topic to a paper has not taught the course, whatever else they know about the subject.

sections.heading: What real progress evidence looks like after a month
paragraphs: Four weeks in, an Al Gurfa family should be able to see whether the hours are converting. The evidence is not a report and not a feeling. It is the diagnostic's topic list, updated, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged, and the marked work that justifies each marking. That document takes a tutor ten minutes to produce if they have been working from it, and cannot be produced at all if they have not.

An item marked closed should have evidence attached: the same question type answered correctly twice in a row under timing, in two different weeks. One correct answer is luck. Two under timing a fortnight apart is a closed topic. An item marked improving should show a mark that moved on comparable questions. An item unchanged after three weeks is a conversation, not a failure, and the conversation is about method rather than effort.

What should not count as progress evidence, however sincerely reported: improved confidence, better engagement, a willingness to attempt harder questions, or a completed stack of past papers. All four are pleasant and none is a grade. They are often genuine precursors to improvement and they are also exactly what a tutor says when there is nothing measurable to report, which is why a parent needs the marked work rather than the summary.

The review cadence that works is monthly, not termly. A term is long enough for an arrangement to drift entirely, and by the time a term-end report arrives the remaining time has shrunk. Monthly, with the list and the scripts, catches both failure modes early: the wrong content, and the wrong slot. In an Al Gurfa household where the coast road and two school runs compress the evening, the second is at least as common as the first.

sections.heading: Resitting properly: whole subject, one component, or wait
paragraphs: Most families treat a resit as a failure and a last resort. It is better treated as one of several planned options, because both boards run a November series alongside the main summer one, which means a single-subject resit costs months rather than a year. Cambridge runs June and November for International GCSE; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. Deciding in advance what you would do if one subject goes wrong removes the panic from August.

The real question is what has to be retaken. Depending on the board's rules for the specification, a candidate may be able to resit a single component or may have to retake the whole subject, and that distinction completely changes the cost and the preparation. The exams officer can confirm it for your child's specification in one conversation, and it is worth having that conversation before results rather than after, when every family is asking at once.

Three things then decide whether a resit is worthwhile. First, whether the grade is actually blocking something: a post-16 subject prerequisite, or one of the five passes needed for British-track equivalency, where Arabic and Islamic education do not count towards the five. Second, whether the diagnostic shows a short specific list of causes or gaps across the syllabus, because the first is fixable in a November window and the second usually is not. Third, whether the student has the appetite for it alongside starting a post-16 course.

For a sense of the timetable shape, the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Those are backward-looking citations kept with their dates because that is what makes them checkable. For any upcoming series, use the live official timetable through the exams officer, and remember that Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones with its own timetable version.

sections.heading: The three documents to get from the school before booking anybody
paragraphs: Everything on this page becomes actionable with three pieces of paper, all free, all obtainable with two emails to the school. Families routinely book a tutor first and collect these later, which is the wrong order, because two of the three can invalidate a match.

The first is the entry confirmation, which carries the syllabus code per subject and the tier. This is the document that prevents the expensive mistake: booking a Cambridge 0625 tutor for a child entered on Pearson 4PH1, or an Extended specialist for a Core-tier candidate. It also tells you, for the Cambridge sciences, whether the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper has been entered, which are two different pieces of preparation.

The second is the dates sheet: the final entry deadline, the mock window, and the exams officer's own copy of the timetable for the correct Cambridge zone. Entry deadlines fall months before the papers and are not published anywhere a parent naturally looks, and a subject never entered cannot be sat however well prepared the student is. The timetable matters because Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The third is the last marked assessment with the mark scheme, or at least the mark breakdown. This is what lets a tutor map topics to papers in the first session instead of the third, and it is also the document against which a diagnostic can be compared. Together the three take ten minutes of a parent's time and save several sessions of discovery, which at market rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor is a worthwhile trade.

sections.heading: When Al Gurfa's local supply runs out
paragraphs: Sometimes the honest answer to a near-me search is that nobody locally has taught the specification. Fujairah's private-school sector is small, and for Extended-tier Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science or Business Studies the number of people within a reasonable drive of Al Gurfa who have taught that course recently can be zero. The in-home premium of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour does not change that number, and it is worth saying so plainly because no page researched for this market does.

Removing geography from the problem is the only move that changes the outcome rather than the convenience. Online one-to-one delivery replaces who lives nearby with who has taught the specification. That argument is strongest exactly where this market's pages are silent: Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain are named by none of the sixty-odd competitor pages read for this research, which were written for Dubai and Abu Dhabi and extended elsewhere by substituting a place name.

Even with geography removed, availability is finite and should be disclosed rather than implied. Core and Extended mathematics, the separate sciences, and English as a first language staff quickly. Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science at Extended tier take longer. A minority subject in one specific evening slot sometimes cannot be filled, and the correct response then is a realistic timeframe, a different slot, or a straight no with the reason attached.

Ask every provider what happens if the slot cannot be filled, this one included. An answer that promises everything always and immediately, in a market this size, has answered a different question. The useful answer names a limit, and a limit is information a parent can plan around.

sections.heading: Materials, coursework and the position of this site
paragraphs: Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the property of Cambridge and Pearson. A provider handing them out as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and where a paper is unreleased it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct practice is to reference the document, cite the official address and link out, so a parent reads the authoritative version rather than a summary. That applies to everything factual on this page.

Where a school has entered a coursework component, the line is authorship. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name where it falls short, and teach the student to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the coursework, draft the assignment, or edit a piece to completion so that the sentences become theirs. A page in this search result sells finished assessed work outright, and the consequence of that lands on the candidate.

There is one more rule a parent in Al Gurfa should know before approaching a teacher privately. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition work permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as press-reported rather than exact regulatory wording and check the current policy, but the principle holds nationally.

And the position of this site, stated because the claim circulates in this market and because every check on this page should be applied here too. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by Cambridge International, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, runs no premises in the UAE, publishes no star rating, and quotes no statistic without its sample and date.

process.title: Test specification knowledge in four questions
process.description: Components and weightings. Whether a practical exam exists on this board. Which paper a named topic appears in. What a raw mark means before boundaries are set. You do not need the answers; you need to notice the difference between a sentence and a paragraph about approach.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep
process.description: Not a convenient demonstration hour. The real weekday and time, with you able to listen in, because an Al Gurfa evening compressed by the coast road and two school runs is the actual constraint. Watch whether the tutor asks which board before teaching anything.

process.title: Diagnostic and a topic-to-paper map in the first fortnight
process.description: A paper sat to time, marked against the official scheme, losses attributed to six causes, then each weak topic placed on the paper it appears in and ranked by marks at stake. A tutor who cannot produce that map has not taught the specification.

process.title: Review monthly with the list and the scripts
process.description: Each topic marked closed, improving or unchanged, with the marked work behind it. Closed means the same question type correct twice under timing in two different weeks. Unchanged after three weeks is a method conversation rather than an effort one.

process.title: Decide the resit position before results, not after
process.description: Ask the exams officer now whether your child's specification allows a single-component resit or requires the whole subject, and note the November entry deadline. Deciding in advance what you would do if one subject goes wrong removes the panic from the week results arrive.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, confirmed in writing
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are both International GCSE Physics and differ on practical assessment entirely. The code is confirmed before the first session, which is how a mismatch surfaces in week one rather than at results, when it is unfixable.

whyPoints.title: Grade boundaries explained rather than implied
whyPoints.description: Boundaries are set per series by the board after marking, so a raw mark carries no fixed grade and a mock percentage is an estimate. That changes how a mock should be read, and no competitor page researched for this market explains it at all.

whyPoints.title: Topic-to-paper mapping, ranked by marks at stake
whyPoints.description: A topic can be worth four marks on one paper and thirty across an entry, and the ranking frequently surprises families. Mapping turns revision into targeting and solves most motivation problems without a conversation about motivation.

whyPoints.title: Progress reported as marks, not as confidence
whyPoints.description: A closed topic means the same question type correct twice under timing in two different weeks, with the scripts attached. Improved confidence and a stack of completed papers are pleasant and are not evidence that a grade is moving.

whyPoints.title: The resit treated as a plan, not a failure
whyPoints.description: Both boards run a November series, so a single-subject resit costs months rather than a year, and whether one component or the whole subject must be retaken depends on the specification. That is a question for the exams officer before results, not after.

whyPoints.title: Every check on this page applies to us
whyPoints.description: Ask for the permit. Ask the four questions. Ask what happens if the slot cannot be filled. This site claims no regulator or board accreditation, holds no school partnership, runs no UAE premises, and publishes no figure it cannot source.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows my child's IGCSE specification?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions and listen for specificity rather than for the answers. What are the components and what is each worth. Does a practical exam exist on this board. Which paper does this topic appear in. What does a raw mark mean before the board sets boundaries. Somebody who has taught the course answers each in a sentence; somebody who knows only the subject describes their teaching approach instead. That difference is observable without any subject knowledge of your own.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor come to our house in Al Gurfa?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. A local in-home market does exist, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In a small emirate the premium tends to buy a shorter list of specifications somebody has actually taught, which is the reverse of what a family wants.

faqs.question: Why is my child's mock percentage not a grade?
faqs.answer: Because grade boundaries are set by the board after each series has been marked, taking account of how the cohort and the paper performed, and are published after results. A raw mark therefore has no fixed grade attached until that happens, and the same mark can fall either side of a boundary in different series. A mock graded against a previous series' boundaries is an estimate. The useful output of a mock is the distribution of lost marks across causes and topics, which is stable.

faqs.question: What is topic-to-paper mapping and why should I ask for it?
faqs.answer: It places each of your child's weak topics on the paper it appears in, notes the question style and typical mark allocation, and ranks them by marks at stake rather than by how uncomfortable they feel. A topic can be worth four marks on one paper and thirty across an entry, and the ranking often surprises families. It takes one session, schools rarely produce it because it is per-student work, and a tutor who cannot do it has not taught the specification.

faqs.question: What should count as progress evidence after four weeks?
faqs.answer: The diagnostic's topic list, updated, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged, and the marked work that justifies each marking. Closed means the same question type answered correctly twice under timing in two different weeks; one correct answer is luck. Improved confidence, better engagement and a stack of completed past papers are pleasant and are not evidence. Review monthly rather than termly, because a term is long enough for an arrangement to drift entirely.

faqs.question: Which three documents should I get from the school before booking a tutor?
faqs.answer: The entry confirmation, which carries the syllabus code and tier per subject and, for the Cambridge sciences, which practical component was entered. The dates sheet with the final entry deadline, the mock window and the exams officer's own timetable for the correct Cambridge zone. And the last marked assessment with its mark breakdown. Ten minutes of emailing replaces two or three sessions of discovery, and two of the three can invalidate a match outright.

faqs.question: Can my child resit only one paper rather than the whole IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board's rules for that specification, and the exams officer can confirm it in one conversation. Both boards run a November series alongside the main summer one, so a resit costs months rather than a year. Whether a single component or the whole subject must be retaken completely changes the preparation and the cost, which is why the question is worth asking before results arrive rather than in the week when every family asks at once.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth it for an Al Gurfa student?
faqs.answer: Three things decide it. Whether the grade actually blocks something: a post-16 subject prerequisite, or one of the five passes needed for British-track equivalency, in which Arabic and Islamic education do not count. Whether the diagnostic shows a short specific list of causes, which a November window can close, or gaps across the syllabus, which it usually cannot. And whether the student has appetite for it alongside starting a post-16 course, which is a real constraint.

faqs.question: Why does multiple-choice technique matter on the Cambridge sciences?
faqs.answer: Because the multiple-choice paper carries thirty per cent of the grade, which is more than many individual topics are worth across the whole entry, and elimination technique is a teachable skill that is almost never taught explicitly. A student who can rule out two plausible distractors reliably converts guesses into marks across the entire paper. Ranking it against individual topics by marks at stake usually puts it near the top, which surprises families and the students themselves.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody has taught my child's specification locally?
faqs.answer: That is the honest situation for Extended-tier Chemistry, Economics, Computer Science and Business Studies in a small emirate, where the number of people within a drive of Al Gurfa who have taught the course recently can be zero. Paying an in-home premium does not change that number. Removing geography is the only move that changes the outcome rather than the convenience, which is the argument for online delivery and is strongest precisely where this market's pages are silent.

faqs.question: How do method marks work in IGCSE mathematics?
faqs.answer: Marks are allocated to steps as well as to the final answer, so a written method earns marks even when the arithmetic at the end goes wrong, and an unwritten method loses marks the student had already earned. That asymmetry is the highest-value single behaviour change available in the subject, because it applies across every structured question on both papers. Teaching it explicitly changes a script faster than any amount of additional content revision does.

faqs.question: Do I need to tell the tutor which Cambridge zone our centre is in?
faqs.answer: Not for teaching, but you need to know it yourself. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The failure mode is a timetable printed from a revision forum. Use the exams officer's copy and nothing else, checked against the board's own site.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an IGCSE coursework component in Al Gurfa?
faqs.answer: Teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name where it falls short of a criterion, and teach the student to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the coursework, draft the assignment, or edit a piece to completion so that the sentences become theirs. A page in this search result sells finished assessed work, and the consequence of that falls on the candidate rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Can I buy only a diagnostic without committing to lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for an undecided family it is often the best first purchase. One or two sessions produce a document about your child that you keep whatever happens next: a paper sat to time, marked against the official scheme, with losses grouped by cause and topics mapped to papers. It can be taken to any other tutor, and its specificity is the clearest available evidence of whether this tutor knows the specification at all.

Email the school for the entry confirmation, the dates sheet with the entry deadline and zone timetable, and the last marked assessment. Then run a free trial lesson in the slot you actually intend to keep, and ask for a diagnostic with a topic-to-paper map in the first fortnight. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to an Al Gurfa address, and no grade boundary figure is quoted here.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-dibba.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tier. Work is organised as a countdown to a named paper date rather than as an open weekly slot, and the week number is written on every session note.

intro.heading: Twelve weeks, counted one at a time
paragraphs: Dibba sits at the northern end of the Fujairah coast with the Hajar mountains behind it and the Gulf of Oman in front. The private-school provision on this coast is small, which means an IGCSE cohort in any one subject is small too, and a student who needs a specific paper fixed in a specific number of weeks has a narrow local market to work with. That is the situation this page is written for.

Most families arrive with a number of weeks rather than a diagnosis. Twelve weeks is the common one: the mock has come back, the paper date is known, and the question is what can be done in the time that remains. The answer is quite a lot, provided the weeks are used in a particular order, and almost nothing if they are used as twelve interchangeable hours of general revision.

So this page is a countdown. It sets out the final twelve weeks one at a time, with what should happen in each and what you should be able to see at the end of it. It also sets out the entry chain, because the single most expensive mistake available in an IGCSE year is a missed entry decision, and the chain has five participants of whom the parent is only one.

Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Dibba is also next to Dibba Al-Hisn, which belongs to Sharjah and therefore to a different authority. Neither fact changes the papers your child sits, but both change who you ask when something administrative needs resolving.

IB Gram matches Dibba students to subject specialists and delivers every lesson one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. On this coast that is less a restriction than the only route to a tutor who has taught the exact syllabus code your child is entered for.

One date discipline before the detail. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June and November series, and the February and March series Cambridge offers is for India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates are in the past deliberately, so they stay checkable.

A final practical point. Agree the two weekly slots before the countdown starts rather than negotiating them week by week. In Dibba that usually means one fixed weekday evening after the school run and one weekend morning, chosen around whatever already occupies the week. A slot that has to be renegotiated every week is the slot that disappears around week six, and in a twenty-four session plan two lost sessions is nearly a tenth of what the countdown was supposed to deliver.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-dibba.programmesIntro: Three qualifications and one diagnostic stage produce the countdown questions on this page. Which one applies depends entirely on the entry your child's school has already submitted.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Linear courses assessed by terminal papers, with Core and Extended tiers in most subjects. Core caps at grade C and Extended runs the full A* to G range. Syllabus codes govern the preparation: 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, and each has its own paper count, duration and mark-scheme vocabulary.
programmes.countryNote: Dibba candidates sit the June and November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct zone version of the timetable, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. On a small coast with few centres that question goes to your exams officer early, not late.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same certificate name reached through different papers, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry on a 9 to 1 grading scale. Mathematics uses Foundation and Higher tiers rather than Core and Extended, and several sciences are untiered, which changes what a mock result means.
programmes.countryNote: Available in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November entry produces a certificate in the following January rather than the following summer. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so plan from the live official file.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The early-warning system almost nobody uses as one. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and produce a diagnostic report rather than a certificate. A Year 9 report showing weak algebraic fluency predicts a difficult 0580 Extended two years ahead, at a point when eight weeks of work would fix it entirely.
programmes.countryNote: In Dibba this matters more than in a city, because remediation later is harder to arrange locally. A family who acts on a Year 9 Checkpoint report spends one short block in a quiet year. A family who waits until the Year 11 mock spends an exam-year budget on the same gap, at a point when every other subject is competing for the same evenings.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual next step on this coast for a student who does not move to an IB school. AS sits at the halfway point and can be carried forward to the full A Level. Subject availability is constrained by IGCSE grades, so what comes out of Year 11 decides what is open in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: It also matters to the Ministry of Education equivalency file. The published British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than E or grade 3.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-dibba.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names what twelve weeks can realistically move in it, which is a narrower and more useful claim than a list of topics covered.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Twelve weeks can fix method-mark discipline, timing across the longer paper, and three topic clusters. It cannot rebuild two years of algebra. The highest-yield single change is writing the substitution line every time, which is a habit rather than a piece of knowledge.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Twelve weeks is enough for electricity, the practical or alternative-to-practical component, and timing. Potential dividers and series-parallel circuits respond quickly to redrawing every circuit before calculating, and the experimental vocabulary is pure learning rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic, the qualitative analysis table and organic pathways, in that order of return. The analysis table is recall and the cheapest marks in the paper; students skip it in revision because it feels less like chemistry than a calculation does.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The widest content of the three sciences, so twelve weeks means triage rather than coverage. Genetics crosses, osmosis write-ups and command-term discipline on the extended responses are where the recoverable marks sit, and the mark scheme accepts a short list of specific phrases.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Twelve weeks is tight here because the calculus arrives early and compounds. Differentiation of composite functions and the proof-shaped command terms are the two targets worth taking, and the rest is best left to the main mathematics entry.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The most improvable paper on this list inside twelve weeks, because the summary question is scored on content points within a word ceiling and that is a technique. Students who paraphrase elegantly lose the lifted detail the scheme requires, and the fix takes about three sessions.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response reward control of register and answering the question asked about the text rather than the text itself. Past papers with the published scheme open is close to the entire intervention and it works quickly.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is worth a grade on its own and takes about a week to fix. A labelled axis, a shifted curve and a marked new equilibrium score where prose does not, and the evaluation sentence must reach a judgement rather than list both sides.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case study separates the grades, and it is learnable fast: name the business in the stem, use its figures, answer the command term. Break-even and cash-flow calculations are reliable marks that revision routinely skips.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Data representation and networking are heavily recalled and heavily mis-remembered, especially hexadecimal conversion. Pseudocode consistency is built by writing code under time, so twelve weeks is enough if the student actually writes rather than reads.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity carries the top band, and a named place with a figure and a date can be learned in a fortnight. Map and graph skills are the most teachable part of the syllabus and routinely the least practised, which makes them a reliable twelve-week target.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in two awards means breadth beats depth, and twelve weeks forces the triage that students resist. The work is identifying which topics are examined thinly and which carry weight, then ignoring the former without guilt.

sections.heading: The final twelve weeks, one week at a time
paragraphs: Twelve weeks is the most common amount of time a family in Dibba has when they start looking, and the order the weeks are used in matters more than the number of hours in them. The first week is deliberately unpleasant: a full past paper sat to time, before any teaching. A conversation about which topics feel hard is the least reliable diagnostic available, and a script is the most reliable.

Weeks two to six are topic work driven by that script, using questions rather than explanations, because a student who attempts and fails and is corrected retains more than one who watches a worked example. Three clusters is what the time holds. A fourth is possible only by shortening the timed work, which is a bad trade in the second half of a countdown.

Weeks seven to ten alternate content and timed components, then hand the marking over. By week nine the student should be marking their own work against the published scheme with the tutor present, because that skill outlasts the block and applies to every remaining subject. Week ten is a comparable paper under time, marked, and set beside week one so the movement is a number.

Weeks eleven and twelve contain nothing from us. The block stops two weeks before the paper by design, so the final fortnight belongs to the student. Families ask to extend into it and the answer stays no: a student still being taught in the last fortnight arrives tired and uncertain, and fatigue costs more marks than late teaching adds. If a gap appears then it gets a note and a two-minute recap, not a lesson.

sections.heading: The entry chain, and who actually controls each step
paragraphs: Parents assume they control more of the IGCSE process than they do, and the gap produces the single most expensive mistake available in an exam year. The entry is submitted by the school to the board, months before the paper. The tier is part of it. The subject list is part of it. By the time most families start thinking about tuition, two of the three decisions that matter are already fixed.

The chain has five participants and the parent controls one step of it directly. The student chooses subjects, within what the school offers. The school confirms the tier and submits the entry to the board. The board publishes the timetable by zone. The centre administers the sitting. The parent's one controlling step is asking the right question at the right time, which is why the table below names the question rather than just the stage.

The question that matters most is the internal entry deadline, in writing, from the exams officer. It is the only point in the chain where a missed date cannot be recovered without an extra fee and sometimes cannot be recovered at all. Everything after it is administrative and fixable. Everything before it is a decision and is cheap to change.

For a family in Dibba there is a second question worth asking early: which zone the centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a different timetable for each, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. On a coast with few centres, nobody is going to repeat that in a school assembly.

sections.heading: Private-candidate entry when the school does not run the subject
paragraphs: This comes up more on the east coast than anywhere else in the country, because the local school offer is narrower. A student who wants a subject the school does not enter candidates for, or who has left school and needs a resit, becomes a private candidate. That means finding a centre willing to accept private entries, paying its fees, and managing the logistics yourself.

The practical steps are the same everywhere and the distances are not. A private candidate needs an accepting centre, an entry inside that centre's own deadline, and a plan for getting to it on each paper day. From Dibba the nearest accepting centre may be in Fujairah City or further, which turns each paper into a half-day with travel at both ends and makes the exam timetable a logistics document as well as an academic one.

Two cautions worth carrying. First, centre deadlines for private entries are often earlier than a school's internal deadline, because the centre is batching its own submission. Second, not every centre accepts every subject or every component; a subject with a practical examination may be refused by a centre without the facilities, which is a conversation to have before planning five months of work.

What tuition can do here is narrow and useful. A private candidate has no form tutor repeating the dates and no class to pace against, so the plan has to supply both. A countdown block with the week number on every note, a diagnostic paper at the start and a comparable one at the end gives a private candidate the structure a school cohort gets for free. The entry logistics remain the family's own, and no tutoring service should imply otherwise.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson, when the question is a resit
paragraphs: After a disappointing result, the resit question has a board dimension that families rarely consider. Both boards offer a November window, so a UAE candidate has a defined next opportunity either way, but the routes differ in what they let a student carry and in when the certificate arrives.

Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and November results arrive in the following January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That timing matters if a sixth-form place depends on the grade, because a January certificate lands after most offers are settled. Cambridge's November series sits similarly, with the June series as the main route and November as the resit window for UAE candidates.

The other dimension is what gets repeated. A linear qualification means resitting the whole subject, including components that went well, which is both a cost and a risk if a strong component is re-sat and performs worse. Where a board and subject allow a carry-forward of an assessed component, that should be confirmed in writing with the exams officer rather than assumed from a forum post.

The decision should rest on component evidence, not on a feeling about the grade. A statement of results showing a strong long paper and a weak short one points at timing and arithmetic under pressure, which five focused months will move. An even spread of low marks points at content coverage, which takes longer and may be better served by a different route entirely. The table sets the options against each other.

sections.heading: Year 9 is the cheapest place to spend money
paragraphs: Everything else on this page is remedial. This section is not, and it is the one most likely to be ignored, because nothing has gone wrong yet. Cambridge Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and produce a diagnostic report rather than a certificate. That report is the earliest external signal a student generates, and it arrives roughly two years before the IGCSE papers it predicts.

The signal most worth acting on is algebraic fluency. A Year 9 report showing weak manipulation predicts a difficult 0580 Extended, a difficult 0625 and a difficult 0606, because all three assume the algebra rather than teach it. Eight weeks of focused algebra in a quiet Year 9 removes a problem that otherwise consumes most of an exam-year tuition budget two years later.

The arithmetic is stark when written down. One short block in Year 9 costs a fraction of a twelve-week countdown in Year 11, and it also buys something the countdown cannot: a student who enters Year 10 believing they can do mathematics. Confidence in Year 10 decides how much a student volunteers, and how much they volunteer decides how quickly a teacher notices a gap.

For families in Dibba there is an additional reason. Remediation is harder to arrange locally at short notice, so acting early is worth more here than in a city where a replacement option is twenty minutes away. A quiet Year 9 block, booked when nothing is urgent, is the single best-value decision available on this whole page.

sections.heading: What a twelve-week countdown costs from published rates
paragraphs: Because this page recommends a countdown rather than an open slot, the useful figure is the block total. Twelve weeks at two sessions a week is twenty-four hours. Run that through the published UAE market bands and the cost becomes a comparable number instead of an hourly rate that could mean anything.

The bands with their publishers: budget online and university-student tutors from roughly AED 45-150 per hour, with one content platform publishing from AED 45-65 and one learning platform from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150-300, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with a UK agency quoting AED 270. Premium named tutors at AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650.

Monthly comparisons for context: UAE surveys put a weekly hour at roughly AED 240-600 for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include online bundles from around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits.

None of those figures is an IB Gram price and nothing here is a quote. The free trial lesson comes before any payment, with no card needed. For a Dibba family the comparison worth running on any quote is the block total against a named paper date and a named component, because an hourly rate with no session count and no endpoint is the easiest thing in this market to advertise and the least useful to compare.

sections.heading: Will the countdown actually finish?
paragraphs: A twelve-week countdown contains twenty-four sessions, and the question that decides whether it works is how many of them happen. Each lost session is about four per cent of the plan, and losses are not random: they cluster in the weeks when something else is happening, which on this coast means travel, road conditions and the longer journeys a family here makes routinely.

An online session needs a student and a connection. An in-home session on the Fujairah coast needs a tutor able to make the journey on that specific evening, roads that cooperate, and a household at home. Over twenty-four sessions that difference reliably costs a countdown one or two sessions, and in a plan that deliberately keeps the last fortnight empty there is nowhere to reschedule them to.

The honest counterpoint is worth stating. A tutor in the room reads handwritten working upside down and interrupts mid-line, which is the main thing physical presence buys. Online that needs a document camera or a phone propped over the page, set up in session one rather than discovered in session eight. Families who arrange it get most of the benefit and families who do not lose something genuine.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so this is settled for us rather than open. The comparison is printed because a parent weighing two formats deserves the trade-offs including the one that favours the option we do not sell, and because on this coast the session-completion argument is the strongest one available.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and the two things to check
paragraphs: Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. In Dibba the boundary is unusually close, because Dibba Al-Hisn next door is Sharjah.

Those bodies regulate schools, not tutors. Tutors are covered by a permit: the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

So there are two things to check with any prospective tutor. Whether they hold the MoHRE permit, which is a direct question with a direct answer and the application route is the ministry's own private tutor licensing service, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time. And whether they are being honest about status: individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has published no amounts, so any figure quoted to you is invented.

One claim to treat sceptically whoever makes it. No UAE regulator or examination board accredits a tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and this page claims none. A permit for a training institute with premises is a specific KHDA instrument and no online platform should borrow its language.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or an assessed practical component, and the boundary around them is worth printing rather than assuming. A tutor teaches the skills, explains the assessment criteria, and gives feedback on work the student has written. Nobody here produces assessed work on a student's behalf, at any price.

That is not squeamishness. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under board rules and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. Services in this market do sell completed assessed work, including at IB level, which is precisely why the line belongs on the page where a parent can see it before paying rather than in terms afterwards.

There is a parallel rule about materials that parents are rarely told. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. They are cited and linked here rather than reproduced or supplied, because redistributing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure as well. Your school's subject teacher is the right route to the material your child is entitled to use.

The same caution covers examiner claims. Current examiner status is either evidenced or it is not, and it grants no access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. A tutor who has taught a syllabus for years is worth hiring on that basis, and one whose main selling point is proximity to a board deserves a direct question about what is actually being claimed.

process.title: Give us the paper date
process.description: Everything on this page counts backwards from it, so it is the first thing we need. With the date, the board, the syllabus code and the tier, a countdown can be written before the first lesson rather than after the third. The exams officer has all four.

process.title: Send the marked mock
process.description: The script, not the grade. It shows within minutes whether marks are being lost to timing, to unwritten method lines, to command terms or to missing content, and those four have very different timescales. Component-level mock marks are better still where the school can release them.

process.title: Free trial lesson before anything is paid
process.description: A real lesson on your child's own material, with no card needed and you welcome to watch. What you are judging is how the tutor responds when your child is stuck, because that moment repeats twenty-four times across a countdown and no description can show it to you.

process.title: Week numbers, not vague progress
process.description: Every session note carries the week number and the distance to the paper. That sounds small and it is the thing that keeps a twelve-week plan honest, because in week six it is obvious whether the plan is where it should be or two weeks behind.

process.title: A comparable paper at week two
process.description: Ten weeks after the diagnostic, your child sits a comparable paper under the same conditions, marked to the published scheme. The result is a number set against week twelve, which is the only way to know whether twenty-four hours of work moved anything.

process.title: A straight answer about availability
process.description: In a thinly taught subject at Extended tier there may be nobody suitable free this month. You will hear that with a date or an alternative rather than being matched to somebody adjacent. Six wasted sessions inside a twelve-week countdown is half the plan.

whyPoints.title: A countdown, not an open slot
whyPoints.description: Twelve weeks with a week number on every note, a diagnostic at the start and a comparable paper at the end. The alternative, an indefinite weekly hour, is what this market mostly sells and the arrangement where nobody can say afterwards what changed.

whyPoints.title: The entry chain explained, with the questions
whyPoints.description: Five participants hold the IGCSE process and the parent controls one step. This page names the question to ask at each stage, including the internal entry deadline, which is the only point where a missed date cannot be recovered.

whyPoints.title: Private-candidate reality, not glossed over
whyPoints.description: On this coast the local offer is narrow, so private entry comes up often. Centre deadlines are earlier than school ones, not every centre accepts every subject, and each paper day is a half-day with travel. We say so rather than implying we handle it.

whyPoints.title: Year 9 named as the cheapest intervention
whyPoints.description: Checkpoint runs in March, May and October and the report predicts IGCSE difficulty two years ahead. Eight weeks then costs a fraction of twelve weeks in Year 11, and no page in this market recommends spending money when nothing is yet wrong.

whyPoints.title: Rates costed as a block
whyPoints.description: Twenty-four hours priced from each published market band, with every figure attributed to whoever published it. An hourly rate with no session count is the easiest number in this market to advertise and the least comparable.

whyPoints.title: One format, disclosed before booking
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run in India only. On a coast with long roads, session completion is the strongest argument available.

faqs.question: Can anyone actually come out to Dibba for weekly IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, and on this coast it is difficult through anybody. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson here is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. Published in-home rates of roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel assume city distances; from Dibba the premium buys more road and the choice of tutor narrows to whoever is willing to make an hour's drive each way on a school evening.

faqs.question: Is twelve weeks genuinely enough to change a grade?
faqs.answer: It is enough to change timed-paper technique, method-mark discipline, command-term handling and three topic clusters, which between them hold a large share of recoverable marks. It is not enough to re-teach two years of content, and a tutor claiming otherwise is selling hours. The order matters more than the total: a full paper to time in week twelve, topic work driven by that script, timed components from the midpoint, and nothing new in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Who decides which tier my child sits, and can we still change it?
faqs.answer: The school decides it with the family, and it forms part of the entry submitted to the board roughly five months before the paper. Inside that window a change is a conversation with the exams officer. Outside it, the tier is fixed for that series and a Core entry caps the grade at C however well your child performs. That is why the tier question deserves attention in the autumn rather than in the spring, when it feels urgent and is no longer movable.

faqs.question: What is the one date I must get from the school in writing?
faqs.answer: The internal entry deadline. It is the only step in the whole chain where a missed date cannot be recovered without an extra fee and sometimes cannot be recovered at all. Everything after it is administrative and fixable; everything before it is a decision and cheap to change. Ask the exams officer for it in writing, along with confirmation of which tier each subject has been entered at, and keep the reply.

faqs.question: My child wants a subject the school does not enter. What now?
faqs.answer: That makes them a private candidate, which means finding a centre willing to accept private entries, meeting that centre's own deadline, which is often earlier than a school's, and getting to it on each paper day. Not every centre accepts every subject, and one with a practical examination may be refused where facilities are lacking. From Dibba each paper becomes a half-day with travel at both ends, so confirm the centre before planning five months of work.

faqs.question: When would results from a November entry actually arrive?
faqs.answer: Early in the following year. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, so the pattern is an exam window ending in November and results in January. That timing matters if a sixth-form place depends on the grade, because a January certificate lands after most offers are settled. Check the live official timetable, since provisional versions can be revised.

faqs.question: Does my child's exam centre zone affect anything?
faqs.answer: It decides which timetable you should be reading. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct one and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre is in, then take the timetable from the board's own site and plan revision in the paper order it shows.

faqs.question: Should we spend money in Year 9 if nothing has gone wrong?
faqs.answer: It is the best value decision on this page and almost nobody takes it. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and produce a diagnostic report two years before the IGCSE papers it predicts. A report showing weak algebraic fluency predicts difficulty in 0580 Extended, 0625 and 0606, all of which assume the algebra rather than teach it. Eight weeks then costs a fraction of a twelve-week countdown later, and the student enters Year 10 confident.

faqs.question: What does a twenty-four hour block cost in this market?
faqs.answer: From published bands, roughly AED 1,080-3,600 with a budget online tutor, AED 3,600-7,200 with a qualified subject tutor, and AED 4,800-10,800 or more with a specialist. Those come from providers and surveys that published them, including EdFlik at AED 45-65, Tutopiya at AED 33-52, Unitors from AED 150 for International GCSE, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate at AED 200-450 and above. None is our price and nothing here is a quote.

faqs.question: How many sessions can we expect to lose over three months?
faqs.answer: Online, usually none or one, because the only requirements are a student and a connection. In-home on this coast, reliably one or two across twenty-four sessions, since the tutor has to make the journey on a specific evening and the roads are long. Each lost session is about four per cent of a twelve-week countdown, and because the final fortnight is deliberately kept empty there is nowhere to reschedule them into.

faqs.question: Which paper usually gives the fastest improvement?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge sciences, the alternative-to-practical component, by a clear margin. Its mark scheme accepts a defined vocabulary about controlling variables, repeating readings, improving precision and identifying anomalies, plus reading and completing a results table. Five past papers with the scheme open typically moves it further than the same hours spent on theory. Across subjects, English as a Second Language's summary question and Economics diagram accuracy are the next fastest, both about a week of focused work.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go on an assessed coursework component?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor teaches the skills, explains the assessment criteria and gives feedback on work the student has written. Nobody here produces assessed work for a student at any price, because submitting work that is not your own is malpractice under board rules and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. Services in this market do sell completed coursework, which is exactly why the line is printed here.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list Cambridge February or March dates?
faqs.answer: Because that series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November Cambridge series, and a page quoting a February or March entry deadline to a Fujairah family would be handing them a date they might act on for a country they do not live in. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A UAE tutoring page quoting the India-only February and March window has not checked its own dates, so treat the rest of them with equal suspicion.

faqs.question: Do we need a permit to employ a tutor privately?
faqs.answer: The permit belongs to the tutor, not to you, and it is reasonable to ask whether they hold it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan without losing the countdown?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one adjustment. School days shorten and the useful study window moves to the late evening, so sessions typically shift to a post-Iftar slot, which works because there is no travel to schedule around prayer times or the family meal. Move content-heavy weeks out of Ramadan and keep the lighter work inside it: timed paper sections, mark-scheme reading, a command-term drill. Plan it a month ahead and a countdown loses almost nothing.

faqs.question: What happens in week two of the countdown?
faqs.answer: Your child sits a comparable paper under the same conditions as the week twelve diagnostic, and it is marked against the published scheme. The two scripts side by side give component-level movement rather than an impression, which is the only honest answer to whether twenty-four hours of work achieved anything. After that the block stops: weeks one and zero belong to the student, with no new content introduced by anybody.

intro.heading: Fujairah City, the coastal villages, and the drive nobody wants to make
paragraphs: An IGCSE search on the east coast runs through the same four options in the same order. First Fujairah City, because that is where the private schools are. Then the villages: Sakamkam, Al Faseel, Merashid, Al Gurfa, Dibba. Then the Sharjah enclaves up the coast, Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn, on the theory that a different emirate might hold a different teacher. Then, reluctantly, the mountain road to Sharjah or Dubai for a weekend session. This page is that comparison, worked out, with the figures attached.

Here is the short version. Fujairah City is the only one of those options with a meaningful concentration of private-school teaching staff, and that concentration is small. The emirate's private schools run British, Indian and bilingual curricula with modest year groups, which means narrow option blocks and very little spare teacher capacity. Move out to the villages and you lose even that. Move up to Khor Fakkan or Dibba Al-Hisn and you change regulator without changing the labour market, because those towns are Sharjah territory under the Sharjah Private Education Authority while Fujairah sits under the federal Ministry of Education.

The Dubai option is the one families take most seriously and regret most often. A weekend session in Sharjah or Dubai costs two to three hours of driving on top of the hour of teaching, and the mountain road in the dark is not a trivial journey. Parents do it for one term and then stop, usually in the middle of the term that mattered.

What makes all four comparisons collapse into one answer is that the scarce thing is not proximity. It is a person who has marked the specific paper your child is entered for. Cambridge 0620 Paper 4 and Pearson 4CH1 Paper 1 are different instruments. A tutor who is strong on one is not automatically useful on the other, and the number of people on this coast who are strong on either is small enough to count. Driving further does not create one. A parent in Sakamkam and a parent in Al Faseel will be handed the same three or four names, because those names come out of the same staff rooms, and the schools those staff rooms belong to serve every district on this list.

So IB Gram's answer for Fujairah City is online, one-to-one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor matched to the syllabus code rather than to the distance from your street. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and a page that implied otherwise for the east coast would be selling something nobody can deliver. The rest of this page gives you the district-by-district comparison, the AED figures with sources, the online-against-in-home trade-off, and the exam calendar a Fujairah family has to track.
