fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-fujairah-ci.programmesIntro: An IGCSE enquiry in Fujairah City usually concerns one of three stages, and each needs something different from a tutor. The village pages on this site cover the same stages from their own angles.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary (Years 7-9)
programmes.description: No external exam, which is why weak foundations travel forward unnoticed. The Year 10 repair work is almost always Year 8 content: indices and fractions in maths, rearranging formulae in science, paragraph control in English. Intervening here is cheaper than intervening in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah City year groups are small, so a student who is quietly behind is visible to the teacher but there is rarely a parallel set to move them into. That makes external support at this stage more useful here than in a larger market, where the school itself can absorb the problem.

programmes.name: International GCSE (Years 10-11)
programmes.description: Two years, examined entirely at the end by Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel. Each subject has its own paper structure and its own tiering. The grade on the certificate is what MoE equivalency and university admission read, so a near-miss in Year 11 has consequences a mock does not.
programmes.countryNote: Option blocks on this coast are narrower than in Dubai, so Fujairah City students sometimes take a subject because it is timetabled rather than because it was chosen. That is a specific reason to check tier and board early, since a Core entry made for timetabling reasons caps the grade available.

programmes.name: A Level and Diploma routes after Year 11
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide which post-16 courses are open. Most A Level sciences expect a grade 6 or 7 in the same subject, and Higher Level IB expects comparable attainment. A grade missed in June closes a door that was open in March.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 choice is where east-coast families most often leave the emirate, sometimes for weekly boarding in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah. That makes the Year 11 grade profile unusually decisive in Fujairah City, because it determines whether staying local is even an option.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-fujairah-ci.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Fujairah families ask about, each described by where marks actually go missing. Codes are named because paper structure follows the code, not the subject name.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 / 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended candidates lose most on functions, graph transformations and conditional probability in tree diagrams. Method marks sit on nearly every question, so unshown working is the biggest avoidable loss. Pearson supplies a formula sheet; Cambridge does not, which changes what has to be memorised.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 / 4PH1
subjects.description: Circuits are the reliable failure point: potential dividers, and distinguishing potential difference across a component from current through it. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards writing a method with a named control variable, which students rarely practise.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 / 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles calculations and the qualitative-analysis tables carry a disproportionate share of lost marks. Electrolysis half-equations must balance charge as well as atoms. Organic answers are usually fine on naming and weak on reaction conditions, which is what the longer questions ask for.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 / 4BI1
subjects.description: Content volume rather than difficulty. Enzymes, transport and inheritance reward defined vocabulary used precisely, and examiners reject loose paraphrase of terms like active transport. Six-mark answers need a mechanism in sequence, not a list of facts.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510 / 0511
subjects.description: Comprehension marks are lost by lifting whole sentences when the question asks for two specific details. The summary task has a marked word limit. Speaking is assessed separately and is rarely practised under timed conditions until the final fortnight.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450 / 4BS1
subjects.description: Case-study application separates grades. Students know break-even and cash flow and then answer in the abstract when the scheme wants the figures from the stimulus used. Evaluation marks need a judgement with a stated condition.

subjects.name: Economics 0455 / 4EC1
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked on labelled axes, labelled curves, the shift drawn and the new equilibrium identified. Fluent prose above an unlabelled diagram earns nothing for the diagram. Data-response answers must use the figures in the extract.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: The board's own pseudocode conventions are examinable, so fluent Python coders still lose marks. Trace tables under timed conditions and the validation-versus-verification distinction are the two most reliable mark earners on the paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and the binomial theorem at a depth 0580 never reaches, taken as a bridge to A Level. Teaching capacity for this paper on the east coast is effectively nil, which is the clearest single case for online delivery in this emirate.

sections.heading: Fujairah City against the villages, the enclaves and the Dubai drive
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search implies, so here it is in full. Four options, priced in time as well as money, with the variable that decides the outcome in the last column.

The pattern in the table is worth stating in words. Travel time rises steeply as you move out of Fujairah City, and the local teaching pool falls at the same time, because the schools and therefore the teachers are concentrated in the city. The Sharjah enclaves change the regulator and the school calendar without adding specialists, since Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn draw on the same regional labour market. The Dubai weekend option adds a genuinely larger pool and a journey most families abandon within a term.

What does not appear in any row is the thing a Year 11 student actually needs: somebody who has marked their specific paper. There is no district on this coast where you reliably find a Pearson 4CH1 specialist, or anybody at all who teaches Additional Mathematics 0606. Moving along the coast rearranges the driving. It does not change the supply.

Use the table to see how much of what you are about to pay for is teaching and how much is transport. Then decide whether the transport is buying anything. For a Year 7 student who needs supervision, it may be. For a Year 11 student who needs paper-level diagnosis, it is money leaving the thing you are trying to buy.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, read from the bottom up
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. Here are the AED bands with the source for each, so you can place any quote you receive on this coast.

Start at the cheap end, because that is where most families start. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 on their own sites. That buys content re-teaching from a capable graduate. It is the right purchase if your child missed a fortnight of school and the wrong one if the problem is converting knowledge into marks under a mark scheme.

Above that, a qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Exam-year specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270, and the premium end is quoted at AED 650 by BartyED.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of those figures is an IB Gram price. Ours is confirmed in the conversation after the free trial lesson, with the session length and format stated first.

sections.heading: The travel premium, and what it is actually buying
paragraphs: The gap between the online band and the in-home band is not margin. It is the tutor's journey, and on this coast the journey is long enough to change the arithmetic of the whole evening.

A tutor driving from Fujairah City out to Al Gurfa or up to Dibba spends forty to ninety minutes in the car for one ninety-minute session. At AED 300 for the visit, they are being paid for roughly three hours of their evening. Nobody is overcharging. The travel is real and somebody has to pay for it, and in a small market that somebody is always the parent.

The question is therefore not whether in-home is more expensive but what the extra money buys. It buys a person in the room, which is genuinely valuable for a younger student who needs supervision as much as teaching, and for a student who will not engage with a screen. It does not buy subject expertise. If the choice on this coast is between an in-home generalist and an online specialist in your child's actual paper, the money spent on the car is money not spent on the thing that moves the grade.

IB Gram's position is stated rather than hedged: we run no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and Fujairah City students are taught one-to-one over live video. The comparison is published because the trade-off is real and a parent should see it, not because the conclusion is automatic.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from a June series
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for these searches names an exam session, a registration deadline or a results date. That is the single most useful thing a tutoring page can give a Year 11 parent, so here it is, with the caveat that live dates must come from the board.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March sitting is offered to India only: a Fujairah candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your school's exams officer knows the zone.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results timing drives the resit decision: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so build a plan against the live official timetable rather than against dates restated on a tutoring page.

Counted backwards, the year has a consistent shape and the table sets it out as milestones rather than dates. Entries are confirmed by the school months ahead. Mocks fall in the winter term. Content coverage finishes in spring. The last six to eight weeks are whole papers under timed conditions. Confirm each specific date with your school.

sections.heading: Two regulators on one coastline, and what that means for you
paragraphs: Fujairah families get a regulatory question nobody else in the UAE gets, because the coastline is not all one emirate. Understanding it saves confusion when comparing schools.

The UAE has five bodies regulating private schools. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those three emirates.

So a school in Fujairah City is supervised federally, and a school half an hour up the same road in Khor Fakkan or Dibba Al-Hisn is regulated by Sharjah. The Sharjah authority's remit is broad: it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A family comparing two schools across that line is comparing two different approval regimes, two different reporting formats and two different internal calendars. If your household has children in both, you are running two school calendars in parallel, and that is worth putting on one sheet in September.

A caution belongs here because the opposite is commonly implied. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by the Ministry of Education, SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, Cambridge International, Pearson or the IB. Naming a regulator and explaining its remit is information. Suggesting a regulator has blessed a tutoring company is not, and any provider making that claim should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a reasonable question and the UAE answer is specific. Private tutoring is permitted, and it is regulated by permit.

The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so anyone who tells you it is expensive to obtain is mistaken. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website and e-services system, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so the amounts circulating on tutoring blogs should be disregarded. There is also a professional boundary worth asking about: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from policy, so treat it as a question to ask rather than settled wording.

Organisations are treated differently from individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific permit for institutes with premises, and nobody should describe themselves as KHDA approved without holding it.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule, and the figure a competitor gets wrong
paragraphs: Families on the east coast planning a UAE university route need the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements, and this is an area where a ranking page in this market publishes the wrong figure.

On the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five, and the exclusion of Arabic and Islamic Education from the count is the detail that changes an option-choice conversation in Year 9.

On the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics as at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so no IB equivalency figure should be stated without a Ministry of Education page behind it. Diploma families should ask the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly.

Two honest caveats close this. Equivalency and attestation are run by the authority and not by any tutoring company; IB Gram can describe the requirement and point you to the official channel, and that is all. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Anyone telling a Fujairah City parent otherwise has turned a regulatory process into a sales argument.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not just the subject
process.description: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, 0620 or 4CH1. The statement of entry carries it, and your school's exams officer can confirm it before that arrives. This one detail decides whether a formula sheet applies and prevents a term spent coaching the wrong paper on the wrong board.

process.title: Use the free trial as a diagnosis
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and is not a sales call. Your child brings marked work, ideally a mock, and the tutor works through the questions that lost marks to establish whether the gap is content, method, command term or timing. You get that in writing, naming the questions.

process.title: Set the slot against the real east-coast evening
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time around the actual school run, Arabic assessments, sport and prayer times. Central Fujairah City households usually manage 4.15pm; families in Al Gurfa or Dibba settle later. Nothing is scheduled before your child is home and fed.

process.title: Work in blocks with a named target
process.description: Each block closes one specific gap: circuit questions in 0625, or data application in 0455. Progress is judged on marked past-paper questions rather than on how the hour felt. When the gap closes you can stop, change subject, or move into the timed-paper phase.

process.title: Rematch or hear the truth about availability
process.description: If the subject fit is right and the relationship is not, ask for a different tutor and the written diagnosis travels with you. If no specialist is free for a scarce paper such as Additional Mathematics 0606, you will be told rather than offered a near-enough substitute learning the paper alongside your child.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is published, not hidden
whyPoints.description: This page lays out the city, the villages, the Sharjah enclaves and the Dubai drive side by side with travel times attached. You can disagree with the conclusion and still use the table, which is more than the pages currently ranking for this search offer.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 differ on structure, tiering and what has to be memorised. Tutors are assigned by board and paper, which is the difference between an hour that moves marks and an hour that feels productive.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The rates above are the market's, attributed to the provider or rate table that published them. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. Check ours against theirs and ask anyone else for the same.

whyPoints.title: Distance is removed as a filter
whyPoints.description: On this coast the local pool is tiny once you specify a paper and a time. Teaching over live video lifts the only filter a family can lift, so the shortlist becomes people who teach that paper rather than people who can reach Fujairah City by evening.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is explicit
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. Nobody writes coursework for a student, and no mark schemes or past papers are redistributed, because they belong to the boards. That protects the qualification your child is working for.

whyPoints.title: No regulator is claimed as a sponsor
whyPoints.description: The Ministry of Education, SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, Cambridge, Pearson and the IB are described here because east-coast families need to understand them. None of them approves or endorses IB Gram, and we do not imply otherwise.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE home tutor come to our house in Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: Tutors who travel to homes do work in Fujairah City, and market rates for that service run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting in-home at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. IB Gram is not one of them. We teach Fujairah City students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Better to know that before booking than after.

faqs.question: Is it worth driving to Sharjah or Dubai for a better IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and families who try it usually stop within a term. The mountain road adds ninety minutes to two and a half hours each way to a one-hour session, in the dark, after a full school day. The larger emirates genuinely do have a bigger tutor pool, which is the honest part of the argument. The dishonest part is pretending the journey is sustainable through a Year 11 winter. Live video gives you the same pool without the road.

faqs.question: Do Sakamkam, Al Faseel or Merashid have more tutors than Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: No. Those districts send children to the same Fujairah City campuses, and the teachers in those staff rooms are the local tutoring pool. Moving the search between them changes the length of the tutor's drive and nothing else. Al Gurfa and Dibba are further out again, which raises the travel premium without raising supply. The only variable that changes materially across these districts is what time a session can realistically start.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees schools in Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That differs from Dubai, which sits under KHDA, Abu Dhabi under ADEK, Sharjah under SPEA and Ras Al Khaimah under its own Department of Knowledge. It matters on this coast because Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn are Sharjah territory, so a school half an hour up the road is approved and inspected under a different authority with its own calendar.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tutors charge on the east coast?
faqs.answer: The figures published in this market are UAE-wide rather than Fujairah-specific. Budget online runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table. Exam-year specialists reach AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. IB Gram's rate is confirmed after the free trial.

faqs.question: When will my child in Fujairah City actually sit the IGCSE papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March sitting is offered to India only, which several tutoring sites get wrong for Gulf families. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Work from the board's live official timetable and your school's exams officer, since provisional timetables get revised.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in Fujairah need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own e-services, which list no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject is hardest to get help with in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606. The cohort anywhere is small, the content reaches calculus and logarithms that 0580 never touches, and on this coast the number of people who have taught the paper is effectively zero. Computer Science 0478 is close behind, because the board's own pseudocode conventions and trace tables need someone who has marked it. Pearson science codes are thinner than Cambridge ones locally, simply because fewer east-coast schools use that board.

faqs.question: My child is on Core and wants a higher grade. Can the tier be changed?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is worth asking the school early. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade available, and tiering decisions are sometimes made in Year 10 on the basis of a weak term or a timetabling constraint rather than on current ability. If your child has since improved, ask whether an Extended entry is still possible and what the school needs to see. Extended questions are harder on the same topics, so the switch needs a plan behind it rather than optimism.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Fujairah student need for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The sourced British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A ranking competitor page states six, which is wrong. Equivalency is administered by the Ministry of Education, so confirm the current requirement through the official channel rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can online lessons work for IGCSE Chemistry practical skills?
faqs.answer: For the written assessment of practical skills, yes, and that is where the marks are. The paper asks candidates to identify variables, describe a method with a named control, read apparatus correctly, spot anomalous results and comment on reliability. All of it is taught with the student's own paper on screen. Laboratory handling itself stays with the school. The tutor's job is converting the practical time your child has already had into marks on the written paper, which is a different skill.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session start for a family in Fujairah City?
faqs.answer: Central households usually manage 4.15pm once the ten to fifteen minute run home is done. Sakamkam and Al Faseel are similar. Al Gurfa adds time, and families travelling from Dibba or the northern coast rarely start before 6pm. Because lessons run over live video, the only limit is when your child is home and ready rather than when a tutor could reach your street. Flag Arabic assessment weeks and sport fixtures when the slot is agreed.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two IGCSE subjects for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Maths and Physics pair naturally, as do Business Studies and Economics. Chemistry and Biology look adjacent but are often taught by different specialists, because their mark schemes reward different skills. The real test is whether the tutor has taught both papers to a scheme, not whether they feel confident in both subjects. Where the answer is no, two tutors in alternating weeks beats one tutor stretched across both.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do about coursework without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the method, models a worked example on a different question, marks your child's own attempt against the published criteria and explains where the marks went. A tutor does not write, draft or complete assessed work. At least one provider ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments, which puts a student's qualification at risk rather than saving them time. Tutors should also reference rather than redistribute syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes, which belong to the boards.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You will be told. For a scarce paper there may be nobody free in the week you ask, and the honest options are to wait for the right match, to start on a related paper where the diagnosis still helps, or to look elsewhere. Being quietly handed a near-enough tutor on a scarce code is how a family loses a term they cannot get back, so availability is disclosed up front rather than smoothed over in a booking confirmation.

intro.heading: The slot is the decision nobody plans
paragraphs: Families in Merashid choose a tutor carefully and choose a time casually, which is the wrong way round. Over a two-year IGCSE course the slot decides more than the shortlist does, because the slot is what makes the weekly cycle possible: work set, work done, work marked, next session built on the marking. Break the slot and the cycle stops. A session that starts late is not a delayed session; it is a shorter one, and the part that gets cut is always the end, which is where the review and the next week's work are set.

Merashid is an established residential district of Fujairah, with a high share of long-term resident families and a school run into the city-centre schools that is short in distance and unreliable in duration. Add a second child at a different school and the household's earliest workable hour moves back by thirty or forty minutes. None of that is dramatic, and all of it is the difference between an arrangement that holds through February and one that quietly becomes fortnightly.

This is also where online delivery earns its keep in a way that has nothing to do with teaching quality. IB Gram teaches Merashid students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the slot does not depend on anybody's journey across Fujairah in the evening. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, stated the same way on every country page here. The in-home market exists and publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour; part of what that buys is an arrival time rather than a start time.

So the sections below are operational rather than aspirational. Which schools Merashid feeds and when their days realistically end. Which slot suits which year group, because a Year 10 student and a Year 11 student in the spring need different hours of the evening. How to read a school inspection report, band by band, since that document is free, public and almost never used by the families it was written for. What the Year 9 options form actually commits a child to. And the exam-season logistics that catch families out every single series.

One factual anchor to carry through all of it. Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series, and those are the two a UAE candidate sits; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Entries close months ahead of the papers, which is why the Year 9 and Year 10 sections of this page matter more than the revision advice. Everything else here can be obtained from your child's school with two emails and a week of writing down arrival times, which is a cheaper investigation than any tutoring you will buy.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-merashid.programmesIntro: Three stages, and at each one the decisions that matter are made on a form rather than in a lesson. Knowing when those forms land is most of the planning a Merashid parent needs to do.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, before the options form
programmes.description: Cambridge Lower Secondary or an equivalent middle-school programme, ending in Checkpoint tests in March, May and October windows. Checkpoint certificates do not count towards anything external; schools use them for setting and for tier placement, which is the function parents should care about.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 9 options form is the most consequential piece of paper in a Merashid student's school career and is usually filled in during a single week. Subject choice, tier placement and in the sciences whether separate subjects or a combined award is taken all get settled there. Ask for the form, the deadline and the tier implications in writing before it comes home.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years, assessed by terminal paper. The timetable is at its fullest here because the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the international ones, which is why Year 10 evenings are shorter than families expect when they plan tutoring.
programmes.countryNote: In Fujairah the Year 10 school week is long and the drive home is variable, so a realistic session slot for a Merashid student usually sits between 17:00 and 20:00 rather than straight after school. Two subjects at once in Year 10 is rarely a good purchase for that reason alone, regardless of what either subject needs.

programmes.name: The final IGCSE year
programmes.description: Mocks, coursework deadlines where entered, the final entry confirmation, then the series. The shape of the year is front-loaded: almost every decision that affects the grade has been taken by the time the revision feels urgent.
programmes.countryNote: The two dates to extract from the school in the autumn of Year 11 are the final entry deadline and the mock window, not the exam dates. Entries close months before the papers, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones with its own version of the timetable, so the exams officer's copy is the only one worth working from.

programmes.name: What comes after, and why Year 10 decides it
programmes.description: A Levels or the IB Diploma, both gated on IGCSE grades in the same subject and usually at a B or better. A Core-tier entry caps the grade at C, so a tier decision taken in Year 10 can close a post-16 route two years before the student reaches it.
programmes.countryNote: Local Diploma provision in Fujairah is limited, so a Merashid student choosing that route often moves school or emirate. Either way the Ministry of Education's sourced British-track equivalency rule applies downstream: five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-merashid.subjectsIntro: Subjects below are listed with both boards' codes and with the practical note a Merashid parent needs: how much homework the subject generates, since that is what competes with a tutoring slot.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 0980; Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: The highest regular homework load of any IGCSE subject and the one most families tutor first. A session placed immediately after a maths homework night wastes half its time on work the student has already attempted badly. Ask which nights maths is set.

subjects.name: Physics (0625; Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Cambridge carries a practical component worth twenty per cent, taken as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Edexcel has no separate practical exam. Practical write-ups cluster around the same weeks, which is when a session should be moved rather than cancelled.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620; Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Organic reaction conditions and ion tests are pure recall and can be drilled in short bursts, which makes Chemistry unusually tolerant of a shorter forty-minute session on a busy evening. Mole calculations need a full hour and a clear head.

subjects.name: Biology (0610; Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content load in the sciences, so the work between sessions matters more than the session itself. Retrieval practice in ten-minute blocks on three evenings beats one long revision sitting, and that is a scheduling decision rather than a teaching one.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500; Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Writing tasks need an uninterrupted stretch, so this is the worst subject to tutor in a compressed slot after a long school day. A weekend morning session often works far better for English than any weekday evening can.

subjects.name: Economics (0455; Edexcel 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram drills are short, repeatable and well suited to an evening slot. Extended-response evaluation needs more room, so a sensible pattern alternates: diagram and recall work midweek, extended writing at the weekend.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450; Edexcel 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study work needs reading time before the session, not during it. Sending the insert in advance converts a sixty-minute session into something closer to ninety minutes of value, and costs nothing.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478; Edexcel 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode is marked on logic rather than syntax. Conversion drills on binary, hexadecimal and two's complement are short and benefit from frequency, so they are ideal filler for a compressed evening when the drive home has run late.

subjects.name: Geography (0460; Edexcel 4GE1)
subjects.description: Skills questions are the dependable marks; case studies decide the grade, and a named example with figures scores where a generic one does not. Fujairah's coastline and water scarcity are local material Merashid students rarely think to use.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508 first language / 0544 foreign language)
subjects.description: Two separate qualifications with different papers. Because UAE private schools must teach Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, this subject sits inside the school day rather than beside it, and tutoring works from the school's own material.

sections.heading: What the Merashid school run does to a 16:30 session
paragraphs: Begin with the arithmetic nobody does. School ends; the bus or the car takes between fifteen and forty minutes depending on the day; a child needs food and a short break, which is not optional for a fourteen-year-old; and a second child at a different school adds another leg. A household that believes its earliest workable hour is 16:30 is usually working at 17:15. Booking the 16:30 slot anyway produces a session that starts late every week and ends on time, which means it loses its last fifteen minutes permanently.

That matters because of what sits at the end of a session. The review, the summary of what was understood, and the setting of the work for the coming week all happen in the final stretch. A session that is routinely truncated keeps the teaching and loses the follow-through, and the follow-through is where most of the gain lives. Families then conclude that tutoring is not working, when what is not working is the clock.

IB Gram teaches Merashid students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which removes one variable entirely: nothing depends on a tutor travelling across Fujairah at six in the evening. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are available only in India. Published rates for the in-home market here run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and part of the premium is paying for somebody else's journey as well as your own.

The practical instruction is simple. For one week, write down the actual time your child is at a desk with food eaten. Book the slot thirty minutes after the latest of those times. It will feel late. It will also still be running in March, which is more than can be said for most tutoring arrangements started with an optimistic hour.

sections.heading: Which schools Merashid feeds, and what their days actually look like
paragraphs: Fujairah's private-school capacity sits in and around the city, so most Merashid students travel in rather than walk. The schools differ less in curriculum than in operational detail — when the day ends, which nights homework is set, whether there is a bus and how long its route takes — and those details are what a tutoring slot has to fit around. None of them appear in a prospectus, and all of them can be had by asking the school office.

There is a second layer that catches families moving in from elsewhere. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, not by an emirate-level authority. Dubai's schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah's to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's to its Department of Knowledge. A family moving from Sharjah to Fujairah, or using a school in Khor Fakkan, changes regulator without changing coastline.

That distinction is practical rather than academic. It determines where inspection reports are published, who approves a curriculum change or a fee increase, and which complaints route exists. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection alone. The federal ministry plays the supervisory role for Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain.

sections.heading: Session timing by year group, because Year 10 and Year 11 differ
paragraphs: A Year 10 student and a Year 11 student in the spring should not be tutored at the same hour or in the same way, and treating them identically is one of the quieter mistakes in this market. The Year 10 student has a full timetable, moderate homework, and time. The Year 11 student in February has mocks behind them, a coursework deadline passed or looming, and a series approaching. What each can usefully absorb at seven in the evening is completely different.

For Year 10 the sensible pattern is one session a week, slightly ahead of the school's scheme of work so the student meets each topic twice, and a session long enough for proper teaching. The goal is development, the cost per grade gained is lowest here, and the slot can afford to be a little later because there is no immediate deadline pressure compressing the week.

For Year 11 in the autumn the work shifts to coverage and technique, still weekly. By the spring it becomes paper work: timed sections, marked against the official scheme, with each lost mark attributed to a cause. That is tiring in a different way, so an earlier slot or a weekend morning usually produces more than a late-evening one. A student doing timed papers at 20:00 after a school day is measuring their fatigue rather than their ability.

Younger students, where a Merashid family is tutoring in Year 8 or 9 before the options form, are better served by two short sessions than one long one. Attention at that age is the binding constraint, not content. Forty minutes twice a week on arithmetic fluency or written explanation does more than eighty minutes once, and it survives a late school run intact.

sections.heading: How to read a school inspection report, band by band
paragraphs: Inspection reports are free, public and written for parents, and almost no parent reads one. UAE inspection frameworks use a six-band scale running from outstanding at the top through very good, good and acceptable to weak and very weak, and the bands are applied separately to different aspects of a school rather than only to the school as a whole. That separation is the useful part and the part that gets lost when a rating is quoted as a single word.

What a Merashid parent should look for is not the headline band. It is the band awarded for teaching and assessment in the relevant phase, the band for students' attainment and progress in the specific subjects your child takes, and the inspectors' narrative on what the school has been asked to improve since the last visit. A school with a strong overall band can carry a weaker secondary science outcome, and that is exactly the detail a tutoring decision should be based on.

The second thing to check is the date. An inspection is a snapshot, leadership changes, and a report two or three years old describes a school that may no longer exist in that form. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so that is where a Merashid parent looks; families using schools in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah go to that emirate's own authority instead.

Nothing on this page states or implies a rating for any named school, and no tutoring provider should. Ratings belong on the regulator's own site, with their date attached, and quoting one second-hand is how errors propagate. The point of knowing the scale is to read the real document rather than to accept somebody's summary of it, including this one.

sections.heading: The Year 9 options form, and what it quietly commits a child to
paragraphs: One sheet of paper, filled in during a single week of Year 9, sets most of what follows. It fixes the subject list for two years. It usually fixes the tier — Core or Extended on Cambridge, Foundation or Higher on Edexcel mathematics. In the sciences it decides whether a student takes three separate subjects or a combined award, which affects what post-16 courses will accept them. And it is frequently sent home with a short deadline and little explanation of the consequences.

The tier line is the one to interrogate. A Core-tier entry is assessed on a narrower syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade C, which removes the top four grades before any teaching happens and closes A Level and Diploma routes that require a B. In a small school market the sets are coarser, so borderline students tend to be placed cautiously. That is a rational decision for the school and a costly one for a family that wanted the higher route.

What changes it is evidence rather than argument. Extended-only content taught in Year 9 or early Year 10, followed by a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme, gives a teacher something concrete to re-set on. That is a handful of sessions at the cheapest point in the whole course, and it is worth far more than the same money spent in Year 11. Ask in writing which tier is proposed, and when the entry deadline falls, before the form goes back.

The separate-versus-combined science decision deserves the same scrutiny. Three separate sciences is a heavier load and keeps the most doors open; a combined award is lighter and is accepted for fewer post-16 science courses. Neither is wrong, but a student who intends to take Higher Level Chemistry or A Level Physics should know which choice supports that before the form is signed rather than two years later.

sections.heading: Exam-season logistics that catch Merashid families every series
paragraphs: Three things go wrong in exam season and all three are administrative. The first is the entry deadline. Entries close months before the papers, and a subject not entered cannot be sat however well prepared the student is. Ask the exams officer for the final entry date in the autumn of Year 11 and write it down; it is a more important date than the exam itself, because the exam date is published everywhere and the deadline is not.

The second is the timetable. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The failure mode is a timetable printed from a revision forum rather than obtained from the school. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, so the same instruction applies: use the exams officer's copy.

The third is the resit route, which families treat as a last resort and should treat as a plan. Both boards run a November series alongside the main summer one, so a single-subject resit costs months rather than a year. For a worked sense of the shape, the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Those dates are backward-looking citations; for any upcoming series, use the live official timetable.

A Merashid-specific note on all three. In a small centre the exams officer is often also teaching, which means the answers come faster if you ask early and in writing. September and October are the right months for these questions. February is when everybody asks them at once.

sections.heading: Materials, coursework and what a tutor should decline to do
paragraphs: Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the property of Cambridge and Pearson. A provider that hands them out as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and where a paper is unreleased it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct practice is to reference the document, cite the official address and link out, so a parent reads the authoritative version. Everything factual here about papers and series comes from the boards' own published guidance.

On coursework, where a school has entered a component, the line is authorship. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name where it falls short, and teach the student to fix it. A tutor may not write the coursework, draft the assignment, or edit a piece to completion so the sentences become theirs. Pages in this search result sell finished assessed work, and the consequence of that lands on the candidate.

There is a UAE-specific rule worth knowing before approaching a school teacher privately. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition work permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. Treat that as press-reported rather than exact regulatory wording and check the current policy document, but the principle is sound nationally: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay.

And a statement of position, because the claim circulates in this market. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by Cambridge International, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge or the Sharjah Private Education Authority. It holds no such relationship, claims none, and runs no premises in the UAE.

process.title: Measure the real arrival time for one week
process.description: Write down when your child is actually at a desk with food eaten, every day for a week, including the slowest day. Then book the slot thirty minutes after the latest of those times. It will feel late and it will still be running in March, which is more than most arrangements manage.

process.title: Get the syllabus code, the tier and the homework nights
process.description: The code and tier from the exams officer, the homework nights from the form tutor. A session the evening after maths homework repeats work already attempted badly. These three facts cost two phone calls and shape both the match and the slot.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the slot you intend to use
process.description: Not a convenient demonstration hour. Run the trial at the real time on the real weekday, so you find out whether your child can work at 18:00 on a Wednesday before committing to a term of it. The tutor's explanation and your child's alertness are both being tested.

process.title: Diagnostic paper in the first fortnight
process.description: A full past paper under timing, marked against the official scheme, with every lost mark attributed to a cause. Ask for it in writing. It turns a vague worry into a list of four to seven items, which is what the remaining sessions should be spent closing.

process.title: Agree the Ramadan and midterm pattern in advance
process.description: The slot usually moves later during Ramadan, often post-Iftar, with shorter sessions at the same frequency and recall work rather than new content. Settling that a week ahead keeps the work set between sessions getting marked instead of being dropped in the reshuffle.

whyPoints.title: The slot treated as a decision, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: Over a two-year course the hour matters more than the shortlist, because the weekly cycle of work set, done and marked depends on sessions landing where they were booked. A late start is a shorter session and the end is always what gets cut.

whyPoints.title: Nothing depends on an evening drive across Fujairah
whyPoints.description: Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, so the start time is a start time rather than an arrival window. Part of the published in-home premium of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour is paying for somebody else's journey as well as your own.

whyPoints.title: Format matched to the subject and the year group
whyPoints.description: Writing tasks want a weekend morning; recall drills want forty minutes twice a week; timed papers want the earliest workable hour rather than 20:00. A student sitting a timed paper after a full school day is measuring fatigue, not ability.

whyPoints.title: The options form flagged while it still matters
whyPoints.description: One sheet in Year 9 fixes the subject list, usually the tier, and in the sciences separate against combined. A Core entry caps the grade at C and closes post-16 routes. Evidence from a timed Extended paper is what reopens it, and the cheapest point to produce that is Year 9.

whyPoints.title: Inspection reports explained rather than quoted
whyPoints.description: The six-band scale is applied aspect by aspect, not just overall, so the band for teaching in your child's phase matters more than the headline. No rating for any named school appears here; ratings belong on the regulator's own site with their date attached.

whyPoints.title: The administrative dates named before they bite
whyPoints.description: The entry deadline, the mock window and the correct Cambridge zone timetable are the three things that go wrong every series, and all three are obtainable in September with two emails. February is when every family asks at once.

faqs.question: What time should a Merashid family actually book an IGCSE session for?
faqs.answer: Thirty minutes after the latest time your child is genuinely at a desk with food eaten, measured over a week rather than estimated. For most Merashid households with a city-centre school run that lands between 17:00 and 18:00, and later with two children at different schools. Booking earlier produces a session that starts late every week and ends on time, which permanently removes the final stretch where the review happens and the next week's work gets set.

faqs.question: Does a tutor travel to Merashid for lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are not offered anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The local in-home market is real, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Part of that premium pays for a journey, and the practical cost of the journey is that an arrival time is not the same thing as a start time.

faqs.question: Why is a weekend morning better than a weekday evening for English?
faqs.answer: Because writing tasks need an uninterrupted stretch and a rested student. Directed writing and composition at IGCSE are assessed on register, audience and control, none of which a tired fourteen-year-old at seven in the evening can sustain for forty minutes. The difference shows up in marked writing within a month. Recall-based work is the opposite: Chemistry ion tests or Computer Science conversions survive a compressed evening slot perfectly well and benefit from frequency.

faqs.question: What does the Year 9 options form commit my child to?
faqs.answer: The subject list for two years, usually the tier, and in the sciences whether three separate subjects or a combined award is taken. The tier line is the consequential one: a Cambridge Core entry is assessed on a narrower syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade C, which closes post-16 routes requiring a B. Ask in writing which tier is proposed and when the entry deadline falls, before the form goes back rather than after.

faqs.question: How do I read a Fujairah school inspection report properly?
faqs.answer: Ignore the headline band first and look at three things: the band for teaching and assessment in your child's phase, the band for attainment and progress in the subjects they actually take, and the improvement points inspectors listed. Then check the date, because an inspection is a snapshot and leadership changes. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so that is the source. No tutoring page should be quoting a school's rating to you.

faqs.question: Which date matters more, the exam date or the entry deadline?
faqs.answer: The entry deadline, by a wide margin. Exam dates are published everywhere; entry deadlines fall months earlier and are not, and a subject that was never entered cannot be sat however well the student has prepared. Ask the exams officer for the final entry date in the autumn of Year 11 and write it down alongside the mock window. In a small centre the exams officer is often also teaching, so asking in September gets a faster answer than asking in February.

faqs.question: What are the Cambridge timetable zones and how do I avoid the mistake?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The way families get caught is printing a timetable from a revision forum. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre is in and work only from the copy they provide, checked against the board's own site.

faqs.question: Can my child resit one IGCSE subject in November?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is worth treating as a plan rather than a last resort. Both boards run a November series alongside the main summer one, so a single-subject resit costs months rather than a year. As a sense of the shape, the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The entry is made through the school, with a deadline well before the paper.

faqs.question: Should I book two subjects at once for a Year 10 student in Merashid?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is the week rather than the money. The Year 10 timetable is at its fullest because mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the international ones, the drive home from the city schools is variable, and two sessions plus two sets of homework compete with school homework for the same evenings. Sequencing works better: start with the subject whose diagnostic shows the shortest list of causes, bank the improvement, then move the hours across.

faqs.question: Why does the school run matter more in Fujairah than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the capacity is concentrated. Most of Fujairah's private-school places sit in and around the city, so students in Merashid, Sakamkam and Al Gurfa travel in rather than attending locally, and the return journey competes directly with the only usable hours of the evening. In a city with schools in every district, a family can often choose a school by commute. In Fujairah the commute is largely given, so the slot has to adapt to it.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions during Ramadan for a Merashid student?
faqs.answer: The slot usually moves later, often to a post-Iftar time, with shorter sessions at the same frequency and the content weighted towards recall and drills rather than new material. Shortened school days change what a student can absorb, so adding sessions during the month tends to backfire. Agree the change a week in advance so the work set beforehand still gets marked, and because lessons are online nothing depends on a tutor's evening journey.

faqs.question: How many separate sciences should a Merashid student take at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends on the post-16 intention rather than on current ability alone. Three separate sciences is a heavier load and keeps the most doors open, including Higher Level Chemistry in the Diploma and A Level Physics. A combined award is lighter and is accepted for fewer post-16 science courses. Neither choice is wrong, but it is made on the Year 9 options form and reversed with difficulty, so the intention should be discussed before the form rather than after results.

faqs.question: Do I need to tell the tutor which nights homework is set?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more useful things you can supply. A session the evening after maths homework spends half its time on work the student has already attempted badly and is now bored by, while a session the evening before it means the work gets done properly without the tutor present. The same applies to practical write-up weeks in the sciences, which cluster, and are better handled by moving the slot than by cancelling it.

faqs.question: Should the free trial lesson be at a convenient time or the real one?
faqs.answer: The real one. A trial at 15:00 on a Saturday tells you whether the tutor can explain; a trial at 18:00 on the Wednesday you intend to use tells you whether your child can work then, which is the question that decides whether the arrangement survives a term. Run it in the slot you actually plan to book, with you able to listen in, and judge both the explanation and the alertness together rather than separately.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-merashid.closingHeading: Fix the hour first, then the tutor
fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-merashid.closingBody: For a Merashid household the sequence that works is unglamorous. Measure the real arrival time for a week. Get the syllabus code, the tier and the homework nights from the school. Book the slot thirty minutes after the latest arrival, and run the free trial lesson in that exact slot rather than a convenient one. Ask the exams officer for the entry deadline, the mock window and the timetable zone in September. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, shifting later during Ramadan by agreement. Nobody is sent to a Merashid address, and no school rating is quoted anywhere on this page.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach a single IGCSE subject against a single specification. Ask your child's school for the code on the entry confirmation before matching, because the code decides the papers, the tiering and whether a practical exam exists at all.

intro.heading: Two boards, one subject name, different papers
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake a Sakamkam family makes with IGCSE tutoring has nothing to do with the tutor's ability. It is booking somebody for Physics when the school entered Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 and the tutor teaches Cambridge 0625. Both are International GCSE Physics. Both cover broadly similar content. But Cambridge examines practical skills in a separate component worth a fifth of the grade, taken as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and Edexcel has no separate practical exam at all, examining those skills inside its two theory papers instead. A term of preparation aimed at the wrong component is a term gone.

So this page starts from the specification rather than from the neighbourhood, because that is where the marks live. Sakamkam sits inland from the Fujairah coast, nearer the mountain edge, and the afternoon return from the city-centre schools runs longer than the distance suggests. The practical effect on tutoring is scheduling rather than supply: a session that depends on somebody else's drive tends to start late, and a weekly homework cycle only works if the sessions land where they were booked. An online slot at 17:30 stays at 17:30.

IB Gram teaches Sakamkam students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service and the statement appears on every country page this site publishes. The URL says home tutor because that is the phrase parents type, and the honest answer to it is this one rather than a quiet redirect halfway down a page. The in-home market exists and is priced at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour on published figures; what it buys inland from this coast is a shorter list of available subjects rather than a better one.

What follows is the specification detail that decides a grade. A board-by-board comparison so you can identify which one your child sits. The paper structure subject by subject with the percentage each component carries. The topics where Extended candidates predictably lose marks, which are narrower and more fixable than general revision advice implies. The difference between the 9-1 and A*-G grade scales and why a school's choice of syllabus version matters on a university application. And a method for using past papers properly, because almost every family already has a folder of them and almost nobody uses them in a way that produces marks.

One structural fact to hold onto throughout. Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series, and those are the two a UAE candidate sits; the February and March series exists but is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Entries close months ahead of the paper, and coursework components close earlier still, so the question of which board your child sits should be settled long before the revision question becomes urgent.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.programmesIntro: Three stages shape an IGCSE plan for a Sakamkam student, and the entry decisions made at each one constrain the next. Most of them are made by the school and explained to the parent afterwards, if at all.

programmes.name: The year before entry decisions
programmes.description: The last year in which a tier placement can be influenced cheaply. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, sat in March, May and October windows, are diagnostic rather than certificating, and schools use them for setting. A student who performs below their ability in Checkpoint maths can find themselves on a Core pathway for two years as a result.
programmes.countryNote: In a small school market the sets are coarser, so Sakamkam families have less room than a Dubai family would for a borderline student to be placed generously. Work on Extended-only content in Year 9, proved by a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme, is the evidence that reopens the conversation with a teacher.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years, assessed almost entirely by terminal written paper. Grades report as 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus version the school entered. Coursework exists in some subjects and not others, and the practical arrangements in the sciences differ by board rather than by subject.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education's sourced requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A ranking competitor page states six subjects. Five is what the published clarification reported, and the difference changes which subjects a Sakamkam family should protect.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken deeper. Entry is gated on IGCSE grades in the same subject, which is why a tier decision in Year 10 reaches further than the certificate. AS can be cashed in at the end of Year 12 as a standalone qualification at some schools and not at others.
programmes.countryNote: The equivalency rule continues at this stage: one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A Sakamkam student trimming to two AS subjects without checking that should verify it through the Ministry of Education's own channel, not through a tutoring site.

programmes.name: IB Diploma as the alternative route
programmes.description: Six subjects plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum. The step from Extended IGCSE to Higher Level is real but bridgeable with a term of targeted work, particularly in mathematics where the Analysis and Approaches course assumes fluency Extended does not require.
programmes.countryNote: Local Diploma provision in Fujairah is limited, so this route usually involves a school or emirate move for a Sakamkam family. No verified IB points threshold for Ministry of Education equivalency exists in any source this project could check, so none is published here even though competitor pages publish one.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Sakamkam families most often ask for, each with both boards' codes and the specific place marks go missing. The failure points are narrower than general revision advice suggests, which is what makes them worth tutoring.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge splits the entry between a non-calculator and a calculator paper at half the grade each; Edexcel runs two calculator papers at 50% apiece. Extended and Higher candidates lose most marks on bounds, algebraic fractions, vectors and the final parts of structured questions where the method has to be written out.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge: multiple choice at 30%, theory at 50%, practical component at 20%. Edexcel: two written papers with practical skills examined inside them. Circuit calculations and the distinction between series and parallel behaviour under load account for the largest predictable loss at Extended tier.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations that require two conversions, the exact wording of tests for ions and gases, and ionic equations balanced for charge as well as atoms. Organic reaction conditions are pure recall and are the fastest marks in the subject to recover in a short run of sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Water-potential and osmosis language, genetic-cross notation written out in full, and data-handling on an unfamiliar graph. The content load is large enough that a topic-by-topic risk list beats a general revision timetable by a wide margin.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Reading and writing papers rather than literature. Directed writing is assessed on register and audience, so a technically clean piece in the wrong voice sits below its potential. Summary questions reward the student's own words and penalise phrasing lifted from the passage.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries weight the prose around it cannot recover: an unlabelled axis or a shift drawn the wrong way loses marks outright. Extended papers reward a judgement supported by the diagram rather than a two-sided list with no conclusion attached.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: The case-study insert decides the answer, and the recurring error is a correct textbook point applied to a business the insert does not describe. Break-even, cash-flow and ratio questions are the most predictable marks and are usually lost to arithmetic.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode answers are marked on logic rather than syntax, which students find counterintuitive after a year of writing Python. Binary, hexadecimal and two's complement conversion appear every series and reward drilling until they are automatic.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, graphs and photographs are the dependable marks; case studies decide the grade, and a named example with figures scores where a generic one does not. Fujairah's coastline and water scarcity are usable local material students rarely think to deploy.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics
subjects.description: 0607 International Mathematics includes an investigation paper no other maths syllabus has, and is often chosen by schools feeding into the IB. 0606 Additional Mathematics bridges to A Level for strong Extended candidates. Both reward fully written methods and punish answers that jump to a result.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Inland and north-west of the city, closer to the mountain edge. The afternoon return from the coastal schools is the longest of the inner districts, so realistic session starts sit around 17:30 and a fixed slot beats a flexible one.

regions.note: Holds most of the emirate's private-school capacity and the widest local subject range, which is still narrow measured against Dubai or Sharjah. Short commutes make earlier session times workable for students schooling here.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal, near the corniche and the port, roughly fifteen minutes from the city schools. Earlier starts are achievable than in Sakamkam, and that timing difference is the only practical distinction between the two districts for tutoring.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Established residential area where demand concentrates on Extended-tier sciences and mathematics. That band is where Fujairah's specialist supply is thinnest, so changing format does more than changing district.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: South along the coast road and more dispersed, often with two separate school runs per family. Neither child tends to be home before 16:00, so sessions settle into the 17:00 to 20:00 window.

regions.note: Around ninety minutes north, with the fewest local secondary options in the emirate. Online delivery there is the only practical route to an Extended-tier subject specialist rather than one option among several.

regions.note: A Sharjah enclave on the Fujairah coastline, so its private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than the federal Ministry of Education that supervises Fujairah's schools.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Sakamkam works from, and where the lesson happens
paragraphs: Through IB Gram, this means a named specialist for one subject and one specification, teaching your child one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time on Gulf Standard Time. It does not mean somebody driving to Sakamkam. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and the same sentence appears on every country page this site publishes.

The specification is the thing that makes the match useful. A specialist should be able to tell you, without looking anything up, which papers your child sits, what each is worth, whether a practical component exists, and the three topics on which candidates at that tier most reliably lose marks. If they cannot, they know the subject rather than the examination, and in a two-year course assessed entirely at the end, those are different qualifications.

That matters inland from this coast more than it does in Dubai, because of supply rather than quality. Fujairah's private-school sector is small, so the number of adults within a reasonable drive of Sakamkam who have taught Extended Chemistry or Economics against a current specification may be one or none. Published rates for a travelling in-home tutor run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Here the premium buys a shorter subject list, not a better outcome.
Everything below is specification detail. If you read one section, read the board comparison, because identifying which board your child sits is the decision that makes every other decision possible.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: establish which one before you book anything
paragraphs: Schools choose their board subject by subject, and they do not always announce it. A Sakamkam school might enter Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson Edexcel for mathematics, or the reverse, and a student can sit two boards across one certificate set without it ever being mentioned at home. The code is on the entry confirmation, and the exams officer can tell you in a sentence. It is the single most useful question a parent can ask before paying for anything.

The structural differences matter in practice. In the sciences, Cambridge carries a separate practical component worth a fifth of the grade, sat either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper at the school's choice. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam; practical understanding is examined inside the written papers. A student prepared for an alternative-to-practical paper that they are not sitting has lost that preparation entirely.

In mathematics the tiering language differs. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. Edexcel 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher tier. The tiers are not interchangeable in content or in difficulty profile, and a tutor who has only taught one will guess at the other. Cambridge also offers 0607 International Mathematics, which includes an investigation paper that exists nowhere else and which schools feeding into the IB often prefer.

On session structure both boards run a November series alongside their main summer one, which makes a single-subject resit a realistic option rather than a year's wait. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Work from the timetable the exams officer provides.
