sections.heading: Paper structure subject by subject, and the percentage each component carries
paragraphs: Tutoring hours should follow the weightings, and most families never see them. A component worth half the grade deserves more attention than one worth a fifth, and an untimed coursework component is usually the fastest place to gain marks because the criteria are published and there is no clock. Yet revision conversations at home almost always start from the topic a student dislikes rather than from the component carrying the most marks.

On the Cambridge sciences the split is consistent across Physics, Chemistry and Biology: a multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent, a theory paper worth fifty, and the practical component worth twenty. That makes the theory paper the single largest target in every one of them, and it is also the paper where command-word errors do the most damage, because the answers are extended rather than selected. Multiple choice rewards elimination technique, which is a teachable skill in its own right and rarely taught.

Mathematics is split evenly between its two papers on both boards, which sounds simpler and in practice is not, because the non-calculator paper on Cambridge tests a different skill set from the calculator paper. A student who practises only with a calculator to hand arrives at the non-calculator paper with no arithmetic fluency and loses marks that have nothing to do with their understanding. Splitting practice between the two deliberately is a small change with a large return.

The rest of the subjects distribute across two or three papers with the inserts and case studies carrying the weight in Business Studies and Economics. The table gives the shape; your child's school can confirm the exact components for the entry year, and the board's own syllabus page is the authority. Specifications are revised, and a tutor working from a specification two revisions old is a real risk in subjects where the paper structure has changed recently.

sections.heading: Where Extended candidates lose marks, and why the list is shorter than you think
paragraphs: General revision advice assumes the problem is spread across the syllabus. In marked scripts it rarely is. A student sitting Extended papers in three sciences and mathematics typically has four to seven identifiable topics carrying the bulk of their lost marks, and the same topics recur across cohorts because they are the ones where a plausible wrong method produces a plausible wrong answer. That is why a diagnostic paper is worth more than a revision plan: it turns a vague anxiety into a list with seven items on it.

In Chemistry the recurring items are mole calculations requiring two conversions, the precise wording of tests for ions and gases, ionic equations balanced for charge rather than only for atoms, and the conditions attached to organic reactions. The last of those is pure recall and can be closed in two sessions, which makes it the cheapest mark recovery in the subject and the first thing a specialist should go after.

In Physics the list is circuit behaviour under load, the sign conventions in anything involving direction, moments where the pivot is not where the student assumes, and the difference between the quantities in a formula and the units they are measured in. In Biology it is water-potential language, genetic-cross notation written out in full rather than in shorthand, and the explain-versus-describe distinction, which alone accounts for a surprising share of lost marks across the whole paper.

In mathematics the recurring losses are bounds, algebraic fractions, vector geometry and the final parts of structured questions where a method has to be written out to earn method marks. A student who arrives at the right answer with no working loses marks they already earned; a student who shows a correct method and makes an arithmetic slip keeps most of them. Teaching that asymmetry explicitly changes behaviour faster than any amount of content revision.

sections.heading: Grade scales, tiering and the decisions a school makes for you
paragraphs: Two administrative decisions shape an IGCSE outcome before any teaching happens, and both are made by the school. The first is the tier: Core or Extended on Cambridge, Foundation or Higher on Edexcel maths. A Core candidate is assessed on a narrower syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade C, which removes the top four grades before the course begins. The second is the syllabus version, which determines whether grades report as 9-1 or as A*-G.

The tier decision is usually taken in Year 10 on Year 9 evidence and a teacher's judgement, and in a small school market it tends towards caution because the sets are coarser. From the school's point of view placing a borderline student on Core protects them from a poor Extended grade. From the family's point of view it closes the A Level routes that depend on a B or better. Neither view is dishonest; they are just different risks, and the parent is usually only told about one of them.

What reopens the conversation is evidence rather than argument. Extended-only content taught in Year 9 or early Year 10, followed by a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme, gives a teacher something concrete to re-set on. Ask in writing which tier has been entered and when the entry deadline falls, and ask well before that deadline rather than after the mock, because entries close months ahead of the paper.

The grade-scale question matters later and catches families out at application time. A 9-1 grade and an A*-G grade are not interchangeable, universities publish requirements in one or the other, and a certificate set that mixes the two across subjects needs explaining on a form. None of that is a problem; it is simply worth knowing which scale your child's subjects report on before the reference is written rather than after.

sections.heading: Using past papers properly: a method rather than a pile
paragraphs: Almost every Sakamkam family already has past papers. Very few use them in a way that produces marks, because the default method is to work through a paper, check the answers, feel either relieved or alarmed, and move to the next one. That produces familiarity rather than improvement, and familiarity is why a student can do forty papers and still sit the real one at the same grade.

The method that works has three steps and the first one is the hard part. Sit the paper under genuine exam timing, with no notes and no pausing. Mark it against the official scheme rather than against a model answer, because the scheme shows where the marks are allocated and that allocation is the actual information. Then attribute every lost mark to a cause: content not known, content known but not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method correct but not written, or time ran out.

Those six causes have different remedies and that is the whole point. Content not known needs teaching. Content not recalled needs retrieval practice, which is a different activity. A misread command term needs the command-term list and an hour sorting questions by it. A method not written needs a behavioural change rather than any teaching at all. Time ran out needs section timing targets. A student told simply to revise more will apply the wrong remedy to five of the six.

The second half of a preparation run should move to full papers under timing, one a week, because stamina and pacing are separate skills from content and are the last to develop. The final week should add nothing new. If a topic has not been learned by then, learning it costs more marks elsewhere in the paper than it can recover, and a student walking in tired from a late discovery is a worse bet than one walking in rested with a known gap.

sections.heading: Papers, mark schemes and coursework: the rules a tutor should already follow
paragraphs: Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. A tutoring provider that offers them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and where a paper has not yet been released it is a malpractice exposure as well. The correct practice is to reference the document, cite the official address, and link out so that a parent reads the real thing. Everything factual on this page about papers and series comes from the boards' own published guidance and should be confirmed there.

On coursework the line is about who produced the sentences. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria in the board's own wording, show how a comparable task is approached, read a draft the student has written and name where it falls short, and teach the student to fix it. A tutor may not write the coursework, draft the assignment, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become theirs. This search result contains pages selling finished assessed work outright, and the consequence of that falls on the candidate.

A useful test at the trial-lesson stage is to ask what they would do if your child asked them to write one paragraph of a coursework draft. The right answer is a refusal and a description of what they would do instead. An answer that treats it as negotiable tells you precisely what will happen in the week before the deadline, when the pressure is real and the parent is not in the room.

A statement on this site's own position, since the phrase circulates freely in this market. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by Cambridge International, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge or the Sharjah Private Education Authority. It holds none of those relationships, claims none, and operates no premises in the UAE. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is useful; implying an endorsement is not.

process.title: Get the syllabus code from the school first
process.description: It sits on the entry confirmation and the exams officer can give it to you in a sentence. The code decides the papers, the tiering language and whether a practical exam exists. Matching on subject name alone is how a term of alternative-to-practical preparation gets spent by a candidate who is not sitting that component.

process.title: Confirm the tier and the component in writing
process.description: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher, practical test or alternative paper. Ask before the entry deadline rather than after the mock, because entries close months ahead of the paper and a tier decision taken on Year 9 evidence is easier to revisit in Year 10 than in Year 11.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a specification test
process.description: Ask the tutor which papers your child sits, what each is worth, and the three topics where candidates at that tier lose the most marks. A specialist answers in under a minute. Your child's verdict on whether they could follow the explanation is the other half of the decision.

process.title: Diagnostic paper in the first fortnight
process.description: A full past paper under timing, marked against the official scheme, returned with every lost mark attributed to one of six causes. This is the document the plan should be built from, and it is the thing to ask for if you want to know what you are paying for rather than hoping.

process.title: Fixed weekly slot, with Ramadan planned in advance
process.description: Sessions run at the same time each week on Gulf Standard Time, after the Sakamkam school run. During Ramadan the slot usually moves later, often post-Iftar, agreed a week ahead so the work set between sessions still gets marked rather than being dropped in the shuffle.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 are both Chemistry and are assessed differently enough that the preparation diverges. Matching on the code is a small administrative step that prevents the most expensive mistake available in IGCSE tutoring, and almost nobody in this market asks for it up front.

whyPoints.title: Weightings drive where the hours go
whyPoints.description: A theory paper at fifty per cent and a practical component at twenty deserve different amounts of attention, and the published figures are the only honest basis for that decision. They are printed here in full because most families have never been shown them.

whyPoints.title: A short, specific loss list instead of general revision
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts usually show four to seven topics carrying most of the lost marks, and the same ones recur across cohorts. A diagnostic turns an anxiety into that list. Everything after it is targeted, which is why eight focused weeks can outperform a year of unfocused ones.

whyPoints.title: The tier decision treated as reversible while it still is
whyPoints.description: A Core entry removes the top four grades before teaching starts, and it is taken in Year 10 on Year 9 evidence. Evidence from a timed Extended paper is what reopens it. That is a cheaper intervention than a Year 11 scramble and almost nobody tells parents the window exists.

whyPoints.title: Dirham figures with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate here is a published market figure read in October 2026 and attributed as such, never presented as an IB Gram price. Three of the six pages ranking for searches like this publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, which no UAE family pays school fees in.

whyPoints.title: Board materials referenced, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: Specifications, papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and a provider handing them out as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material. We cite and link instead, which also means a parent reads the authoritative version rather than somebody's summary of it.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Sakamkam school uses Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code on the entry confirmation. Cambridge codes are four digits such as 0580 or 0625; Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 or 4PH1. Schools choose board by board, so your child can sit Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics in the same certificate set. The code decides which papers are sat, the tiering language and whether a separate practical exam exists, so it is the first question to settle before booking any tutoring.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam in Sakamkam for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the board. Cambridge science syllabuses carry a practical component worth twenty per cent of the grade, taken either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses which. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences have no separate practical exam at all; practical understanding is examined inside the two written papers. Those are genuinely different preparations, so confirm the component with the school before arranging any tutoring around it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge Core and Extended entry?
faqs.answer: Core candidates are assessed on a narrower syllabus and cannot be awarded above grade C. Extended candidates sit harder papers covering the full syllabus and can reach A*. The decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10 on Year 9 evidence, and in a small school market it tends to be cautious because the sets are coarser. What reopens it is evidence: Extended-only content taught, then a timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme and shown to the teacher.

faqs.question: Why does the non-calculator maths paper cause so many lost marks?
faqs.answer: Because students practise almost exclusively with a calculator in hand, then meet a paper worth half the grade where arithmetic fluency is itself examined. The content is not harder; the conditions are. Marks go on fraction work, surds, percentage calculations and estimation that the student can do with a calculator and cannot do without one. Splitting practice deliberately between the two papers is a small change in habit with a disproportionate return across the whole grade.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Sakamkam student actually do?
faqs.answer: Fewer than you would expect, used properly. Sitting a paper under genuine timing, marking it against the official scheme rather than a model answer, and attributing every lost mark to one of six causes is worth more than five papers worked through casually. The six causes are content not known, content not recalled under pressure, question misread, command term misread, method not written, and time. They need different remedies, which is why volume alone changes little.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to staff with a specialist in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Extended-tier Chemistry and Physics, Economics, Computer Science and Business Studies, with Additional and International Mathematics behind them. The cause is not difficulty but the number of local teachers who have taught that specification recently, and Fujairah's private-school sector is small. Core-tier mathematics, English as a first language and the sciences at Core are comfortable. If your request falls in the first group, ask for a realistic match timeframe rather than an assurance that everything is always available.

faqs.question: Can my child resit a single IGCSE subject without losing a year?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Both boards run a November series alongside the main summer one, so a single-subject resit is a matter of months rather than a year's wait. The entry is made through the school, and the deadline falls well before the paper. The practical decision is whether to resit the whole subject or only the component that failed, which depends on the board's rules for that specification, so ask the exams officer rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What are the Cambridge timetable zones and do they affect Fujairah candidates?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. It adds that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. The practical risk is a timetable downloaded from a revision forum rather than obtained from the school. Ask your exams officer which zone the centre sits in and use only their version.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tutoring effective for a student inland from the Fujairah coast?
faqs.answer: The variable that matters is match rather than format. A travelling generalist who has not taught the specification will not move the grade; a specialist on screen working from marked past papers usually will. Inland from this coast the choice is rarely between two equally qualified people, because at Extended tier in several subjects the local specialist does not exist. Online also holds the slot at the same time weekly, which is the condition the homework cycle between sessions depends on.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE tutors charge for Fujairah students?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500, and named specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Monthly estimates for one weekly hour run around AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. Those are published market rates with their sources named rather than IB Gram prices; a quote follows the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Should a Year 11 student in Sakamkam start tutoring in two subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Only if the diagnostic in both shows a short, specific loss list rather than gaps across the syllabus. Two subjects means two sessions a week plus the work between them, which is a real load on a student already carrying eight or nine certificates. The alternative that usually works better is sequencing: fix the subject with the shortest loss list first, bank it, then move the hours. Spreading thin is how a term produces two half-improvements.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic studies count towards the five IGCSE passes for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The sourced requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are specifically not included among those five. They still have to be taught, because private schools in the UAE must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum. Verify your own case through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: What should I ask for after a month of sessions in Sakamkam?
faqs.answer: The updated loss list from the diagnostic, with each item marked closed, improving or unchanged, and the marked work it rests on. An item that has not moved in three weeks is the conversation to have rather than something to wait out. Progress at IGCSE is visible as marks on marked scripts under timing. Anything reported only as improved confidence or better engagement is not yet evidence that a grade is moving.

faqs.question: Can lessons shift during Ramadan or while the family travels from Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning the change works better than improvising it. Most families move the slot later during Ramadan, often to a post-Iftar time, and because the lesson is online nothing depends on a tutor's journey. Travel is handled as a one-off time adjustment rather than a cancelled term. Agree the change a week in advance so the work set before it still gets marked before the next session instead of being quietly dropped.

fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.closingHeading: Get the code, then book one trial lesson
fujairah/igcse-home-tutor-in-sakamkam.closingBody: For a Sakamkam family the first step is a single question to the school: which syllabus code, which tier, and for the Cambridge sciences, practical test or alternative paper. With those three facts a match is possible and a plan can be built; without them the first two sessions go on discovery. Then take a free trial lesson and ask the tutor which papers your child sits and what each is worth. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, after the school day. Nobody is sent to a Sakamkam address, and every rate quoted here is a published market figure with its source named.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects live over video, to a named syllabus code and tier. Each works from a shared page the student can scroll back through afterwards, which is the part of online teaching that has no equivalent in a room with a whiteboard that gets wiped.

intro.heading: Four things sold as online tuition, and why only one of them reads your child's work
paragraphs: The phrase online tutoring covers at least four products that behave nothing alike. A recorded video course is a library: well made, inexpensive, available at two in the morning, and completely indifferent to whether your child understood lesson four. A large live group class is a lecture with a chat box. A small group class is a class. A marketplace hour bought one at a time is a conversation with a stranger who has not seen last week's work. Scheduled one-to-one with a matched specialist is the only format in which somebody reads your child's own written answers and tells them which mark-scheme point they missed.

That difference is the whole argument, and it is worth stating in terms of cost rather than quality. A recorded course at a low monthly price is excellent value for a self-starting student who is already on track. For a student who is stuck, it is the most expensive thing on the list, because nothing in it diagnoses anything and six months can pass with the same gap still in place. Parents in Fujairah who have already tried a subscription and seen no change usually arrive at this page having learnt that the hard way.

The east coast makes the comparison sharper than it would be in Dubai. Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman behind the Hajar mountains, and the private-school set is small, so a student taking a less common subject at Extended tier may have no local specialist within an hour and a half of driving. Online delivery is not a compromise in that situation. It is the only arrangement in which the tutor is chosen because they teach Cambridge 0625 rather than because they live in the right emirate, and it is why IB Gram delivers to UAE families this way.

Being clear about what that means: every UAE lesson here is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so it falls in a Fujairah evening. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; a tutor arriving at the door is a service we run only in India. That is a limitation, and it is stated at the top rather than discovered later. What this page does instead of apologising for it is explain exactly how the teaching works, because the mechanics are where parents' real doubts live and almost nobody writes them down.

So: the comparison table, then the anatomy of an hour, then how mathematics and chemical equations get written on a screen, then the practical science question, which is the one every science parent asks and which has a precise answer depending on which paper the school entered. After that, the setup a Fujairah household actually needs, what happens when a connection drops, how a timed paper is supervised on video, the attention arithmetic against a class of thirty, and what happens to recordings and a minor's data. None of it is difficult. It is just unwritten everywhere else.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Online delivery does not change which qualification a student is sitting, and the qualification is what a tutor plans against. Four families of specification cover almost every enquiry from the east coast, and the first job in any match is identifying which one is on the statement of entry.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International's international GCSE, taught as a two-year course and examined by written papers, with many syllabuses split into a Core and an Extended tier. The sciences are the ones where online delivery needs a specific answer, because Cambridge offers a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper and schools choose between them. Cambridge runs its examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Fujairah schools entering Cambridge are generally entering smaller cohorts than Dubai schools, which affects which tier is offered and sometimes whether a subject is offered at all. For an online tutor the practical consequence is that the syllabus code and the practical paper route both need confirming from the school rather than assumed from the subject name.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE, graded 9 to 1, with Foundation and Higher tiers in some subjects and a different approach to assessing practical science from Cambridge's. Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May/June and November each year, publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and released its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.
programmes.countryNote: It is common for one east-coast school to enter Pearson for mathematics and Cambridge for the sciences, which means a family can be managing two boards inside one child's timetable. An online tutor working across both needs to say so explicitly, because model answers from the wrong board actively mislead a student in English and in the sciences.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course, ending in Checkpoint tests that Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Nothing here counts towards a final grade, which makes it the cheapest stage at which to repair algebraic fluency, written science structure and reading speed. Online delivery suits this stage particularly well, because sessions can be short and frequent rather than long and weekly.
programmes.countryNote: On the east coast this stage is also when a family finds out whether the school can actually staff the subject combination a student wants at IGCSE. A Year 9 diagnostic that flags a problem leaves time for the school conversation, which is a different and often more useful outcome than a tuition booking.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The sixth-form route most east-coast British-curriculum students take next, in three or four subjects, with a sharp rise in mathematical demand across the sciences and in the length of reasoning the papers reward. Online one-to-one is heavily used at this stage, because the subject combinations get narrow enough that a local specialist frequently does not exist in a small emirate.
programmes.countryNote: Some Fujairah students sit sixth form in another emirate or as private candidates, which changes exam logistics as well as teaching. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so a student sitting at a centre outside their school's emirate needs the zone confirmed by that centre.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject below is about the screen: what a video lesson does better than a room, and what it has to work around. These are practical observations about teaching the specifications remotely rather than claims about outcomes.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject online delivery suits best, provided the tutor writes by hand on a graphics tablet rather than typing. Working appears line by line in the student's view and stays on the shared page afterwards, so a method can be reread three days later. The thing to watch is the student writing on paper off-camera; the paper needs to be visible or photographed into the page at the end.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Circuit diagrams and ray diagrams work well drawn live, and simulations handle what a Fujairah classroom often cannot set up quickly anyway. The genuine constraint is apparatus handling, which matters only if the school has entered the practical test rather than the alternative paper, so that question gets settled before the first lesson.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Equations, mole calculations and organic pathways are all writing, which the screen handles cleanly. Observation language is the part that needs deliberate work remotely: a student who has done the experiment in school still has to learn to describe a colour change in the words the mark scheme accepts, and video lessons can drill that against photographs and recorded demonstrations.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Mostly a retrieval and long-answer subject, which means most of the useful work happens between sessions and the lesson exists to set it up and audit it. That structure suits online delivery, because the question sets and the marking live in a shared document the student keeps rather than in a book that gets left at school.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Annotating a passage together on screen is better than doing it on paper, because both people see the same marks and the annotated text is saved. Directed writing is drafted live in the shared page and edited in front of the student, which is the fastest way to show how a response gains a mark rather than being told that it would.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: The speaking component is the strongest case for live video in the whole subject list: a scheduled conversation with targeted correction is almost impossible to arrange otherwise and impossible to replicate with a recording. Listening practice also works well, since audio is delivered cleanly and can be replayed at the exact point of confusion.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagrams are the marks, and drawing them live while the student narrates the mechanism is more effective than either reading them or copying them. Data-response work uses the shared page well, with the stimulus and the answer side by side so the tutor can point at the line of data a claim should have come from.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward planning, and planning is visible on a shared page in a way it never is in a notebook. The evaluative command terms get taught by rewriting the student's own six-line answers in front of them, which is the single most useful thing a screen does in this subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: The one subject where the medium is an outright advantage: code is written, run and broken in a shared editor, and the pseudocode conventions the written paper expects can be practised side by side with working Python so the student sees exactly where the two differ.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653)
subjects.description: The route many east-coast students take when three separate sciences will not fit the timetable. Remotely, the useful work is teaching the student to notice which discipline a question has moved into, because most lost marks here come from answering a chemistry question in physics register rather than from not knowing the content.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery makes distance irrelevant and makes two other things matter instead: a connection that holds for an hour and a room where nobody interrupts. The notes below are about those two, community by community, because they are the practical variables a Fujairah household controls.

regions.name: Fujairah city
regions.note: Fixed-line broadband is widely available and rarely the limiting factor here. The real constraint is household noise in the early evening, so the useful question is which room has a door and whether the session can be held there consistently rather than wherever is free that night.

regions.name: Sakamkam
regions.note: Residential and well served for connectivity, with the practical issue being shared bandwidth: a lesson competing with streaming in two other rooms degrades audio before it degrades video, and audio is the part that matters. Agreeing that the hour is a low-traffic hour costs nothing and fixes most complaints.

regions.name: Merashid
regions.note: Households here often run more than one school timetable, which means two children may need the same quiet room on the same evening. Consecutive slots work better than parallel ones on separate devices, since parallel sessions in one house compete for both bandwidth and quiet.

regions.name: Al Faseel
regions.note: Coastal and well connected, with a mobile fallback that is usually strong enough to finish a lesson if the fixed line drops. Worth testing the tether before it is needed rather than during a session, because the two minutes spent working it out mid-lesson always come out of the teaching.

regions.name: Al Gurfa
regions.note: Quieter households and fewer competing evening commitments, which tends to make the weekly slot easier to protect. Where the home has a single shared study area, a headset with a microphone is the cheapest improvement available: it fixes echo, cuts background noise and makes an hour markedly less tiring.

regions.name: Dibba Al-Fujairah
regions.note: The community where online delivery changes the subject list rather than just the convenience, because the nearest in-person specialist is a long drive in any direction. Connectivity is generally adequate for one-to-one video; the sensible precaution is a tested mobile fallback given the distance to any alternative.

regions.name: Qidfa and Mirbah
regions.note: Highway villages where the school journey is already long, so energy rather than bandwidth is the binding constraint. A fifty-minute session with a marked set to follow usually works better here than a full hour, and the plan should be written that way rather than defaulting to the longer slot.

regions.name: Masafi
regions.note: Inland at the mountain pass, with some students attending school in another emirate and therefore working to different term dates. For a video lesson the terrain matters less than it feels like it should; what matters is confirming that the household's upload speed holds, since upload is what carries the student's camera and handwriting.

schoolClusters.city: Fujairah city and the east coast
schoolClusters.note: The schools inside the emirate, where the practical paper route and the syllabus code both need confirming before a science tutor plans anything. Students we support attend schools in this group; none of them is a partner, client or sponsor of IB Gram, and none has endorsed this page.
schools: Our Own English High School, Fujairah

schoolClusters.note: Where east-coast families look when a subject is not offered locally, and where some Masafi and Dibba students attend. Different regulator and sometimes different term dates, which changes the lesson calendar without changing the board's own deadlines.
schools: Scholars Indian School, Ras Al Khaimah

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways the live format gets used, distinguished by what the hour is for rather than by price. The format should follow the diagnosis: a student who cannot do the topic and a student who cannot write the answer need different hours.

modes.title: Weekly teaching slot
modes.description: A scheduled hour with the same tutor, working through the specification in order on a shared page the student keeps. Handwritten working appears live, the question set for the week is issued in the same document, and last week's set is marked at the start of the next session so nothing is ever reviewed from memory.

modes.title: Supervised paper sittings
modes.description: A full past paper attempted to time with the camera on and the tutor present but silent, then marked against the published criteria. It is the closest thing to exam conditions a household can arrange, and it produces the only data that reliably shows whether a timing problem is real or imagined.

modes.title: Short targeted sessions
modes.description: Twenty-five to thirty minutes on a single skill, used where a weekly hour is too long for the student or the problem is narrow. It suits younger students, late-evening slots after a long school journey, and the final weeks before a series when the work is error-specific rather than topic-based.

sections.heading: The four products sold as online IGCSE tuition
paragraphs: Before comparing prices it is worth separating the products, because they are not variants of one thing. A recorded video course is a library of explanations with quizzes attached. A large live group class is a scheduled lecture, usually with a chat box and a presenter who cannot see thirty faces. A small group class is a class, with the pace set by the median student. A marketplace hour is one-to-one teaching bought singly, often from a different person each time. A matched one-to-one arrangement is the same specialist weekly, holding a written record of what your child specifically keeps getting wrong.

Each is the right answer for somebody. For a disciplined student revising subjects they already understand, a recorded course is unbeatable on cost and is available at hours when no tutor is. For a student who wants structure and company and is broadly on track, a small group class delivers both and spreads the hourly cost. For a one-off problem in a single topic, a marketplace hour is efficient and cheap. The format that costs the most and delivers the least is a recorded subscription bought for a student who is stuck, because nothing in it notices that they are.

The dividing line across all four is diagnosis. Only a format in which somebody reads your child's own written answers week after week can tell you that the marks are going to unshown working in question six, or that command terms are being misread, or that the content is fine and the timing is not. That information is the thing a parent is actually buying, and the table below is organised around which formats can produce it rather than around the headline rate.

One figure for context. Published market bands put a qualified online subject tutor in the UAE at roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with budget and university-student online rates from around AED 45 and specialists above AED 200. Recorded courses and large group classes sit well below all of that per hour of content, which is exactly why the comparison has to be about what each format does rather than what it costs.

sections.heading: What a live one-to-one hour actually contains
paragraphs: Parents who have never watched an online lesson imagine a video call with a person talking, which is a reasonable fear because plenty of online tutoring is exactly that. A lesson built properly has a shape, and the shape is visible in the shared document afterwards, which is the easiest way for a parent to check what they bought. The first ten minutes are the previous week's marked set: not a chat about how it went, but the specific questions that lost marks, with the mark-scheme point named against each.

The middle thirty minutes are teaching, and the teaching is written rather than spoken. A tutor working on a graphics tablet produces handwritten working that appears line by line in the student's view, so a method is built in front of them at the speed they can follow rather than revealed complete. The student writes too, in the same document or on paper held to the camera, because a tutor who never sees the student's own handwriting is guessing about where the method breaks.

The final fifteen minutes are the student working while the tutor watches and says as little as possible. This is the segment most online lessons skip and the one that carries the most information, because what a student does when stuck is diagnostic in a way that a correct answer never is. Do they reread the question, check units, write anything at all, or freeze? The set for the following week comes out of what happens in those fifteen minutes.

Then the record. Within a day the session produces written notes, the set that was issued, and the marks from the previous set with each loss attributed. Over five weeks that record becomes the only honest answer to whether the plan is working, because a specific error has either stopped appearing in the student's own written work or it has not. A parent can read that pattern without knowing any chemistry.

sections.heading: Writing mathematics and chemistry on a screen
paragraphs: The commonest objection to online tuition in these subjects is that you cannot write on a screen. You can, and the quality of the writing is the single biggest difference between a good online tutor and a poor one. A tutor using a graphics tablet writes as naturally as on paper, in colour, with the previous three lines still visible, and the page persists after the lesson instead of being wiped. For a method with eight steps, that persistence is a genuine advantage over a physical whiteboard.

What does not work is a tutor typing mathematics into a chat window, or talking through a method while the student takes it on trust. Nor does a tutor sharing a slide deck they prepared for somebody else. The test a parent can apply without understanding the subject is simple: open the shared document after the lesson and look for handwriting. If the page is empty, or it is a document the tutor brought in finished form, nothing was built with your child in it.

The student's side matters just as much. IGCSE mathematics and science papers are marked on written working, and method marks are thrown away by students who do arithmetic in their heads. A tutor who cannot see the student's page cannot catch that habit. The practical arrangements that work are the student writing directly into the shared document, or writing on paper with a second camera angle, or photographing the page into the document at the end of each segment so the tutor marks what was actually written.

For chemistry specifically there is a second benefit. Reaction pathways, mole calculations and balanced equations all reward being written out repeatedly in the same place with corrections visible, and a shared page accumulates that history across a term. A student revising in April can scroll to the week in November when the mole triangle finally made sense, which is not something a notebook does reliably and not something a recorded course offers at all.

sections.heading: Practical science when nobody is in the laboratory
paragraphs: This is the question every science parent asks, and it has a precise answer that depends on which paper the school entered. Cambridge offers two routes for assessing practical skills in its IGCSE sciences: a practical test, sat with apparatus, and an alternative-to-practical written paper that tests the same skills on paper. Schools choose which to enter, and the choice is not always visible to parents until the statement of entry arrives. A tutor who does not ask which one is being sat is planning in the dark.

Where the school has entered the alternative-to-practical route, the entire assessment is written, and online delivery is not a compromise at all. The skills examined are reading a scale, tabulating results, plotting and interpreting a graph, identifying a variable that should have been controlled, spotting the anomalous reading, and describing an improvement to a method. Every one of those is taught better on a shared page with a real data set in front of both people than it is in a room with a whiteboard.

Where the school has entered a practical test, the apparatus work happens in school and the tutor's job changes rather than disappears. Remote teaching covers method design, the language of observation, measurement precision and the write-up conventions the mark scheme rewards, while the school's laboratory covers the handling. That division is honest and it is what most tutoring, remote or not, has always done, since no tutor is running a titration in a family's kitchen either.

Pearson's international GCSE sciences take a different approach again, assessing practical skills through the written papers rather than through a separate practical test, so the specification should be checked rather than assumed from habit. In all cases confirm the route with the school and verify the current arrangements on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com, which publish the live documents and supersede any restatement elsewhere, including this one.

sections.heading: Sitting a timed past paper under video supervision
paragraphs: Most students have never sat a past paper under genuine exam conditions before the real thing, which is why timing problems appear for the first time in the room that matters. A supervised sitting over video solves it cheaply. The paper is opened at an agreed moment, the camera stays on, the tutor is present and says nothing, and the clock runs to the real duration. No questions are answered during the attempt, which is the part students dislike and the part that makes the data worth having.

Afterwards the student marks their own script against the published criteria first, and the tutor audits that marking rather than redoing it. This order matters more than it sounds. A student who has marked their own paper against the criteria has read the examiner's expectations in their own handwriting, which teaches more about how marks are awarded than any amount of being told. The tutor's audit then catches the places where the student was generous to themselves, which is itself diagnostic.

The output is marks per section rather than a total. A total tells a family a grade they already feared; marks per section tell them that the first four questions were fine, question seven lost six marks to unshown working, and the last two questions were never attempted because twelve minutes were spent on a diagram. Those are three different problems with three different fixes, and only one of them is about knowing the subject.

Scheduling matters too. Supervised sittings belong between mock weeks rather than on top of them, and two per subject across the final two months is usually enough to settle the timing question. A student who has sat the paper to time twice and read their own marking knows what the first ten minutes of the real paper will be spent on, which is the most useful thing anybody can carry into an examination hall.

sections.heading: The connection, the equipment and the room
paragraphs: The technical requirements for one-to-one video tuition are modest and the failures are nearly always the same four things: no headset, so the room echoes and both people tire; a phone instead of a laptop, so the shared page is unreadable; a shared space, so the hour is interrupted; and untested upload bandwidth, because upload carries the student's camera and handwriting while everyone only ever tests download. None of those needs money to fix, and all of them are better fixed before the first lesson than during it.

Across Fujairah, fixed-line broadband is generally adequate for a one-to-one video lesson, and a mobile tether is a reasonable fallback worth testing in advance rather than discovering mid-session. The practical variable in most households is not the line but what else is using it. A lesson competing with two streams elsewhere in the house loses audio quality before it loses video, and audio is the part that carries the teaching. Agreeing that the lesson hour is a low-traffic hour costs nothing.

The room is the underrated one. An hour in a kitchen with people moving through it produces a student who is present and not working, which looks identical to a student who is struggling with the subject. A door, a table at the right height, a light source that is not behind the screen, and a phone left in another room are worth more to the quality of the hour than any upgrade to the equipment. Families who set this up once rarely revisit it; families who improvise each week complain about online tuition in general.

When something does fail, the protocol should be agreed rather than improvised. If a connection drops for under five minutes the lesson resumes and overruns; beyond that the session is rescheduled rather than salvaged, because fifteen minutes of a broken link teaches nothing and costs the student their concentration. The shared page means nothing is lost either way: the work up to the drop is still on it, and the next session picks up from the visible line.

sections.heading: Attention arithmetic against a class and a group
paragraphs: A school class is a good place to learn and a poor place to be diagnosed. In a class of twenty-five, a teacher who gave every student equal individual attention would manage a little over two minutes each per hour, and no competent teacher distributes it that way: the time goes where the need is loudest, which is not always where it is greatest. A quiet student with a specific gap can go a term without anybody reading their working closely. That is not a criticism of schools; it is arithmetic.

A small online group of six changes the number without changing the kind. The pace is set by the median student, the questions asked are the ones somebody was confident enough to ask, and the written work marked is usually marked collectively. For a student who is on track it is good value and genuinely useful. For a student who is stuck, the same structural problem applies as in a class, just with fewer people in it.

One-to-one is bought for the fifteen minutes in every hour where somebody watches your child work and says nothing. That is where the diagnosis lives, and it cannot be delivered to two students at once because it requires undivided attention on one person's process. Everything else in a one-to-one lesson, including the teaching, is available more cheaply elsewhere. The honest pitch for the format is narrow and it is that.

Which means the sensible purchase for most families is not one format but a sequence. A recorded course or a group class for breadth and structure, one-to-one for the specific thing that is not moving, and a supervised paper sitting to check the timing. Any tutoring page that tells a parent one-to-one is the answer to every question is selling rather than advising, and a family that has already tried a cheaper format and seen it work does not need persuading otherwise.

sections.heading: Recordings, notes and a minor's personal data
paragraphs: Online lessons generate data about a child, and families are entitled to know what happens to it. The honest list is short: the shared document with the work in it, the written records and marked sets, the scheduling information, and whatever contact details a parent provided. Anything collected should have a stated purpose, and a form that asks for a child's school, grades and photograph without saying why is asking for too much. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the relevant framework, and a privacy link belongs on every page that collects anything.

Recording a lesson is useful and should be optional rather than default. A student who can rewatch the ten minutes where the method was built gets real value from it, particularly in mathematics. The conditions worth insisting on are that recording is agreed in advance by the parent, that the recording is available to the family, and that it is not used for anything else. If a provider cannot answer what happens to a recording and for how long, that is an answer in itself.

The shared page is the part families should actively keep. It is the record of what was taught, in order, with the student's own working on it, and it remains useful through a resit or a transition into sixth form long after the lessons stop. Ask whether it stays accessible after a block ends, because a document that is withdrawn when the invoices stop was never really the student's.

One related caution worth stating on a UAE page. Several providers competing for these searches route parents to non-UAE telephone numbers without saying where the teaching happens or where the data goes. Ask both questions directly. IB Gram's answer on delivery is on every page: one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE and no UAE office or centre.

process.title: Confirm the code, the tier and the practical route
process.description: Three facts before anything else: the syllabus code, the tier, and for sciences which practical route the school entered. All three sit on the option booklet or the statement of entry, and the practical route in particular changes what a remote tutor spends lesson time on. A tutor who does not ask for them is planning against a guess.

process.title: Set up the room and test upload once
process.description: A headset, a laptop rather than a phone, a room with a door, and one upload speed test at the hour the lesson will actually run. Test the mobile tether too, so the fallback exists before it is needed. Ten minutes of setup prevents the four failures that account for most complaints about online tuition.

process.title: Take the 45-minute diagnostic
process.description: One free trial session per family, no card details required. Your child attempts a timed question while the tutor watches what happens when they are stuck, and the session ends with a written statement naming the code, the tier, which topics are secure and whether the losses are content, technique or timing. If a cheaper format would do the job, it says so.

process.title: Agree the record you will receive
process.description: Settle what arrives after each session and when: notes, the issued set, and the previous set's marks with the mark-scheme point named against each loss. Agree whether lessons are recorded and who holds the recording. These are the documents a parent who was not in the lesson uses to tell teaching from supervision.

process.title: Book two supervised paper sittings
process.description: Across the final two months, two full papers per subject sat to time with the camera on and the tutor silent, marked by the student first and audited afterwards. It is the only way to find out whether a timing problem is real, and it is the single most useful hour in the whole plan for a student who already knows the content.

whyPoints.title: A page that persists after the lesson
whyPoints.description: Handwritten working built live on a shared document the student keeps and can scroll back through in April. A physical whiteboard is wiped and a recorded course was never about your child's working. The page is also how a parent checks, without knowing the subject, that something was built rather than presented.

whyPoints.title: The practical route settled first
whyPoints.description: For sciences, which practical paper the school entered changes what lesson time is for. Confirming it before the first session is the difference between teaching the assessment your child will sit and teaching a reasonable approximation of it. Most enquiries never ask, and the question takes one message to the subject teacher.

whyPoints.title: Fifteen silent minutes every lesson
whyPoints.description: The segment where the student works unaided and the tutor watches the process rather than the answer. It is the only part of the hour that cannot be delivered to two students at once, it is where the diagnosis comes from, and it is the honest reason one-to-one costs more than a group.

whyPoints.title: A written record within a day
whyPoints.description: Notes, the set issued, and the previous set's marks with each loss attributed to a mark-scheme point. Five of those in a row tell a parent whether a specific error has stopped appearing, which is a fact rather than an impression. Nothing about progress here depends on anybody's general sense of how things are going.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the cheaper formats
whyPoints.description: A recorded course or a small group class is better value than one-to-one for a student who is on track and wants structure, and this page says so with the reasons. The narrow case for one-to-one is diagnosis of work that is not moving, and overstating it would make the rest of the page less trustworthy.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and data stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Online one-to-one on Gulf Standard Time, no home visits anywhere in the UAE, no UAE office, recordings optional and agreed in advance, and a stated purpose for anything collected about a child. Several pages competing for this search answer none of those questions, which is itself worth noticing.

faqs.question: How does an online IGCSE lesson actually work for a student in Fujairah?
faqs.answer: A scheduled video call on Gulf Standard Time with a shared document open alongside it. The first ten minutes review last week's marked set, naming the mark-scheme point lost on each question. The next thirty are teaching, written by hand on a graphics tablet so the working appears line by line and stays on the page afterwards. The last fifteen are the student working unaided while the tutor watches the process. A written record, the week's set and the previous set's marks arrive within a day.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child need for live online IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet rather than a phone, a wired headset with a microphone, and a room with a door. That is the whole list. The screen has to be big enough to read working line by line and to write into the shared page; the headset removes the echo that makes an hour exhausting for both people; the door protects the hour you are paying for. A graphics tablet is useful for a maths student but not required, since paper held to the camera or photographed in works.

faqs.question: Is home internet on the east coast reliable enough for video lessons?
faqs.answer: Generally yes for one-to-one video, and the limiting factor in most Fujairah households is what else is using the line rather than the line itself. Run one speed test at the hour the lesson will actually fall and check upload as well as download, because upload is what carries your child's camera and handwriting while everybody only ever tests download. Configure a mobile tether as a fallback and try it once in advance, so the five minutes of troubleshooting happen outside a paid lesson.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals handled when the teaching is online?
faqs.answer: It depends which route the school entered, and that is the first question to settle. Cambridge offers both a practical test sat with apparatus and an alternative-to-practical written paper. Where the alternative paper is entered, the whole assessment is written and a remote tutor covers all of it: data tables, graphs, controlled variables, anomalous readings and method improvements. Where the practical test is entered, the apparatus work stays in the school laboratory and the tutor covers method design, observation language and write-up conventions. Confirm the route from the statement of entry.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 5 and Paper 6 in the Cambridge sciences?
faqs.answer: They are the two routes for assessing practical skills, and a school enters one of them. The practical test is sat with real apparatus at the centre; the alternative-to-practical paper examines the same skills in writing, using data and described experiments. The skills overlap heavily, which is why the alternative paper is a genuine assessment rather than a soft option. Ask your child's subject teacher which is on the entry, and check the current arrangements on cambridgeinternational.org rather than relying on any restatement.

faqs.question: How does a tutor teach algebra on a screen with no whiteboard in the room?
faqs.answer: On a graphics tablet, writing by hand into a shared page so the working appears line by line in your child's view and remains there afterwards. For a method with several steps this is better than a physical whiteboard, because nothing is wiped and the student can scroll back to it in April. What does not work is a tutor typing mathematics into a chat box or talking through a method with nothing written. Open the shared document after a lesson: if there is no handwriting on it, nothing was built.

faqs.question: Can my child sit a timed past paper while the tutor watches on video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful hours in a plan. The paper opens at an agreed moment, the camera stays on, the clock runs to the real duration and the tutor says nothing. Afterwards your child marks their own script against the published criteria and the tutor audits that marking rather than redoing it. The output is marks per section, not a total, because that distinguishes a content gap from unshown working from twelve minutes lost on one diagram.

faqs.question: Is a recorded video course cheaper than a live online tutor, and is it worth it?
faqs.answer: Much cheaper per hour of content, and genuinely good value for a disciplined student revising material they already follow. It becomes the most expensive option on the list for a student who is stuck, because nothing in a recording notices that they are, and a term can pass with the same gap in place. If a subscription has already been tried and the marks have not moved, that is useful evidence: the problem is probably diagnosis rather than access to explanations.

faqs.question: How many students sit in an online IGCSE group class, and does the number matter?
faqs.answer: It varies from a handful to several hundred depending on the provider, and the number matters less than the structure. Any group sets its pace by the median student, answers the questions somebody was confident enough to ask, and marks written work collectively if at all. For a student on track that is good value. For one who is stuck, a group of six has the same structural limitation as a class of twenty-five, because nobody is reading that particular child's working each week.

faqs.question: What happens to lesson recordings and my child's personal data?
faqs.answer: Recording should be optional, agreed by a parent in advance, available to the family and used for nothing else. The data a tutoring arrangement legitimately needs is short: the shared working document, the written records and marked sets, scheduling details and a contact. Anything else should have a stated purpose, and a form asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without explaining why is asking for too much. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the governing framework.

faqs.question: Will my son simply get distracted by his laptop during an online lesson?
faqs.answer: He can be, and the fix is structural rather than motivational. A phone left in another room, a single browser window, and a format where he is writing rather than watching remove most of it. The fifteen-minute segment where he works unaided while the tutor watches is the real safeguard: a distracted student is immediately visible in that segment in a way they are not while somebody is explaining. If attention is the binding constraint, two short sessions a week work better than one long one.

faqs.question: How quickly does written feedback come back after an online session?
faqs.answer: Within a day, and it should contain three things: notes on what was covered, the set issued for the week, and the marks from the previous set with the mark-scheme point named against each loss. That last item is the one that matters. A record saying your child worked hard and is improving tells you nothing you can check; a record saying three method marks went unshown in question six tells you exactly what the next session is for and whether it worked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor outside the UAE teach a Fujairah student at a sensible hour?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the scheduling is explicit rather than incidental. Lessons are set on Gulf Standard Time, which is UTC+4, so the slot lands in a Fujairah evening after the school bus and a meal rather than at an hour that suits the tutor's own timetable. This is worth asking any provider directly, because several competing for these searches route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without stating where the teaching happens or in which time zone it is scheduled.

faqs.question: Do online lessons work for a child who needs someone sitting beside them?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes not, which is a more honest answer than the format usually gets. For a younger student who needs an adult physically redirecting them every few minutes, a person in the room is better and visiting tuition is worth its higher rate. For a student aged fourteen and upwards who can hold attention for fifty minutes, the shared page and the silent working segment usually deliver more than proximity does. The trial lesson is a cheap way to find out which describes your child.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a lesson?
faqs.answer: The protocol should be agreed before it happens rather than improvised. Under about five minutes, the lesson resumes and runs over to make up the time. Beyond that, the session is rescheduled rather than salvaged, because a quarter of an hour of a broken link teaches nothing and costs the student their concentration for the rest of the hour. Nothing is lost either way: the shared page still holds the work up to the drop, so the next session restarts from the visible line.

faqs.question: Is online tuition any use for the IGCSE English speaking component?
faqs.answer: It is one of the strongest cases for the format. A scheduled conversation with a tutor who corrects specific things and keeps a written record is almost impossible to arrange otherwise, and completely impossible to get from a recording. Listening practice also works well on video, because audio is delivered cleanly and can be replayed at the exact second the student lost the thread. For Cambridge's English as a Second Language syllabuses in particular, these are the components most commonly underprepared.

fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Pick the format that reads your child's work
fujairah/igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: If your child is on track and wants structure, a recorded course or a small group class costs less and does the job, and this page has said so plainly. The narrow case for live one-to-one is a student whose marks are not moving and nobody can say why, because the only format that answers that question is the one where somebody reads their own written work every week and names the mark-scheme point they missed. One free 45-minute diagnostic over video, no card details, will tell you which of those two descriptions fits, in writing, before anybody asks you for money.

intro.heading: Four options, one fortnight, and no obvious answer
paragraphs: Most Fujairah parents arrive at this search in the same week of the school year. A mock result comes home, or a subject teacher writes two careful sentences in a report, and suddenly the question is not whether to get help but which kind of help exists on the east coast. Four answers come back, and they are genuinely different products sold at genuinely different prices: the school's own after-hours clinic, a tuition centre in Fujairah city or Kalba, a freelance tutor who drives across from Sharjah or Dubai, and one-to-one lessons taught over live video. Almost nothing written about tutoring in the UAE compares those four honestly, because almost everything written about it is selling one of them.

The comparison matters more here than it does in Dubai. Fujairah sits on the Gulf of Oman, the far side of the Hajar mountains, and the private-school set is small. A family in Jumeirah choosing a Chemistry tutor is choosing from a deep local pool and can afford to treat distance as a tiebreaker. A family in Sakamkam or Merashid is often choosing between one person who covers the subject within driving range and nobody. That changes the arithmetic of every option below, and it is the reason this page leads with the comparison rather than with a sales pitch.

The second thing that changes the arithmetic is the exam board. IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both publish international GCSEs in the same subjects, with different paper structures, different tiering rules and different entry calendars, and a school picks one per subject. A tutor who teaches Cambridge Physics 0625 to a student entered for Pearson 4PH1 will still teach physics well and will still cost the same per hour, while quietly preparing the wrong assessment. Half of the value in a good match is simply getting this right before the first lesson, and it is the single question most parents are never asked.

IB Gram is one of the four options, and this page is clear about which one. Lessons for UAE families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the school day. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors arriving at a family's door is a service we run only in India. That is a real limitation and it is stated here rather than buried, because the alternative on the east coast is not a local specialist waiting to be booked. It is usually a long drive, a narrow subject list, and a rate that includes the fuel.

What follows is the comparison, the syllabus codes, the tier decision, the market rates with their sources named, the entry deadlines counted backwards, the permit position under UAE law, and an honest account of what happens when no specialist covers the subject you need. Read the comparison table first. If one of the other three options suits your family better, the page has done its job, and the trial lesson is there to test the fourth without committing to it.
