sections.heading: How to read a marked paper in ten minutes
paragraphs: Most marked scripts come home, get looked at for the total, and go into a bag. Read properly they are the most useful document in a student's academic life, and the reading takes about ten minutes. The method is mechanical and a parent can do it without knowing the subject, because the question being asked is about pattern rather than physics.

Start at the back. Later questions carry longer, more structured marks, and a script that falls away in the last section is telling you about pacing rather than knowledge. Next, count the half-earned questions: parts where the student clearly knew the material and still lost one mark. If that count is high and spread across topics, the problem is presentation or command-term response, not content. If the losses cluster in one or two topics, it is a content gap and a short block will close it.

Then look for crossings-out and restarts. Frequent restarts in algebra or in essay openings indicate planning rather than understanding, which is a separate and very teachable fix. Finally, compare the script against the published mark scheme for two long questions only. Not to re-mark it, but to see what the scheme rewarded that the student did not supply. That comparison is the single most informative thing available.

Bring that reading to a trial lesson. A tutor who is handed a marked script and a sentence describing the pattern can diagnose in one session what otherwise takes three, and the diagnosis arrives in writing rather than as a reassurance.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that caps an answer
paragraphs: Both the IB and the Cambridge and Pearson specifications use a defined vocabulary of command terms, and each term tells the student the shape of answer the mark scheme will reward. Students who read every term as a general invitation to write about the topic lose marks in every section of every paper, consistently and invisibly, because each individual loss looks like bad luck.

The distinction that costs the most is between describing and explaining. Describe asks for what, explain asks for why with a causal link. A student who answers an explain question with an accurate description gets the description marks only, and in a six-mark question that can mean three marks forfeited on an answer that looked complete. Evaluate and justify go further again, requiring a judgement supported by the stronger of two cases.

The fix is not revision in any normal sense. It is a sorting exercise: take twenty past-paper questions, separate them by command term, write one-line answer plans rather than full answers, and check the plan shape against what the term demands. An hour of that moves more marks than an hour of content revision for most students sitting between the middle and upper grades.

sections.heading: Why the syllabus code decides which past papers are worth doing
paragraphs: A student who spends a term on the wrong board's past papers has not wasted the content knowledge, but they have practised the wrong format, the wrong question stems and the wrong practical assessment model. That shows up as marks lost on presentation rather than understanding, and it is entirely avoidable by asking the exams officer one question: which code, and which tier?

Cambridge identifies IGCSE syllabuses with four-digit codes, including 0580 Mathematics, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0610 Biology, 0478 Computer Science and 0606 Additional Mathematics, and separates Core and Extended tiers in several of them. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses its own series, including 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry and 4BI1 for Biology, with a different tiering approach and different arrangements for assessing practical skills.

The structural differences are not cosmetic. How practical skills are examined, whether a formula sheet is supplied, how a tier limits the grade and how questions are stemmed all vary. A Sakamkam student who moves school mid-course, which happens often enough in this emirate, may change board as well as school, and nobody always notices in time.

There is a second reason to hold the codes. Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the boards, and a legitimate provider references them and links to the official source rather than distributing copies. With the code in hand a family can find the right material through the school or the board's own site, which is both the correct route and the only one that guarantees the version is current rather than three cycles old.
Ask for the codes in writing and keep them. They belong at the top of any revision plan, and they are the first thing a tutor should ask for before agreeing that they teach the subject in question.

sections.heading: Higher Level versus Standard Level: what the supplement really costs
paragraphs: Families choosing Higher Level subjects usually weigh them by interest and university requirement, which is right, and then underestimate the time cost, which is predictable. The Higher Level version of a Diploma subject is not the Standard Level course with harder questions. It carries additional syllabus content, an additional paper in several subjects, and a different expectation of independence in the internal assessment.

The practical consequence shows up around the second term of Year 12. A student carrying three Higher Levels where one was chosen without much thought runs out of hours, and the subject that suffers is usually not the one they dropped attention from deliberately. Diagnosing that early is a scheduling conversation rather than an academic one, and it is better had in November than in April.

Where a Higher Level choice is right, the extra content needs teaching rather than revising. The supplement is new material, and a student who has only ever seen it in summary form will answer the Higher Level paper with Standard Level depth and lose the marks that distinguish the two. For a Sakamkam student in a small cohort, those topics are sometimes taught quickly because the class is behind, which makes them the obvious target for a session block.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: The internal assessment is where Diploma students most often lose marks they could have kept, because the criteria are published and specific and most students have never read them properly. A science investigation is marked against four criteria worth twenty-four marks in total. A mathematics exploration is marked against five criteria worth twenty marks. A history investigation is marked against three criteria worth twenty-five. Each criterion rewards a different thing and most students write as though there were only one.

Reading them changes what a draft looks like. A student who knows that evaluation is assessed separately from conclusion writes a distinct evaluation section that connects each limitation to the direction of the error, rather than a single closing paragraph that does both badly. A student who knows that personal engagement is assessed in the maths exploration chooses a context they can actually say something about rather than a topic copied from a list.

A tutor's role here is to teach the criteria and respond to the student's own draft. They can narrow a research question until it fits the word limit, challenge a method before data collection rather than after, and name the criterion that is currently capping the mark. What a tutor must not do is supply text or restructure the work into their own words. Schools require an authenticity declaration and supervisors are expected to have seen the work develop across drafts.
Mark totals and criterion names change between syllabus cycles, so treat the table as a reference frame and confirm the current figures in the subject guide your school is teaching from.

sections.heading: The Sakamkam week and when a diagnostic session can run
paragraphs: Diagnosis needs a slot where the student is capable of concentration, which is a narrower window than a slot where the student is physically available. For a Sakamkam family the morning run into the Fujairah City school cluster is short, but the return journey at pick-up time is not, because the whole city uses the same few roads at the same hour. Add an activity on the corniche and the usable block starts later than the school day suggests.

A diagnostic session is also harder work than a content session. The student has to look at their own mistakes, which is tiring in a different way from learning something new, and the first fifteen minutes of a session are the most valuable for it. That argues for an earlier slot than a weekly top-up session would need, and for sixty minutes rather than ninety.

In practice the pattern that works from Sakamkam is a 5.30pm or 6pm start on a day without a corniche commitment, with weekend mornings used for longer coursework work. During Ramadan the same session shifts to after Iftar and shortens. A diagnostic block of four to six sessions placed across three weeks gives enough time for marked work to come back between sessions, which is what makes the second mark meaningful.

None of that requires anyone to travel. Lessons are delivered online one to one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the slot is chosen on the student's capacity to concentrate rather than on a tutor's route across the city.

sections.heading: Changing school or board mid-course without losing marks
paragraphs: Mid-course moves are common in this emirate, and they are the most under-managed risk in a UAE student's record. A family relocates within the UAE or arrives from abroad, the new school teaches a different board, and a student who was two terms into Cambridge 0620 finds themselves entered for a Pearson paper with a different practical assessment model. Nobody involved is at fault and the marks go anyway.

The first thing to secure is the paperwork. Request the previous school's transcript and, for Diploma students, written confirmation of internal assessment progress and any marked drafts already produced. Coursework that cannot be evidenced may have to be restarted, and restarting an internal assessment in the second term of Year 13 is the worst position a Diploma student can be in.

The second is the board comparison. Ask the new school for the syllabus codes and tiers they will enter the student for, and compare them against the previous ones. Content overlap is usually high and structural differences are where the risk sits: tier limits, practical assessment, formula provision and question stems. A short block of work on the new board's past papers converts existing knowledge into marks under the new format.

The third is regulatory. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, while a move to Sharjah's east-coast towns puts a student under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and a move to Dubai or Abu Dhabi under a different authority again. Fee approval, inspection and record-keeping practices differ, so ask where the new school's records are held before rather than after the transfer.
bullets: Secure the transcript and written internal assessment progress before leaving
Compare syllabus codes and tiers, old against new, in writing
Budget a short block on the new board's past papers
Check which regulator holds the new school's records

sections.heading: What a session actually looks like from the first minute
paragraphs: Specificity about the session itself is the easiest promise to check, so it is worth setting out. A first session opens with the marked work the family sent, on screen and annotated by both people. The tutor names the pattern they can see, which usually takes under ten minutes, and then tests it: a question of the same type, worked live, to confirm the diagnosis rather than assume it.

The middle of the session is the student working, not the tutor talking. That distinction matters because a student who watches a problem being solved learns less than one who attempts it badly and is corrected mid-attempt. Screen sharing suits this well: both people see the same algebra, the same annotated graph, the same paragraph of a draft, and the correction lands at the point of error rather than at the end.

The last five minutes are a written summary. Which loss was identified, what was practised, what the student should do before the next session, and how many sessions the diagnosis suggests. That number is sometimes four. Families are better served by a tutor who says four and means it than by one who proposes a year and reviews it never.

Between sessions the student does a short, specific task rather than general revision, and brings the result. A diagnostic block closes with a second marked piece so the change is visible as a mark rather than an impression. If the second mark has not moved, the diagnosis was wrong and the sensible response is to change it or change the tutor.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a report
process.description: One recent assessment with the marker's annotations tells a tutor more in five minutes than a half-hour conversation. If you can, add a one-line note on the pattern you noticed yourself, because parents often spot the repeated error before anyone else does.

process.title: Confirm the code and tier
process.description: Ask the exams officer for the exact syllabus code and, where Cambridge applies tiers, which tier your child was entered for. Past-paper practice that does not match the entered specification costs marks on format rather than knowledge.

process.title: Take the diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: The first session is free and works on the marked paper you sent. It ends with a written diagnosis naming the specific loss, the criterion or command term behind it, and a recommended number of sessions, which is often four to six rather than a year.

process.title: Run a finite block and mark the end of it
process.description: A diagnostic block is three weeks of focused work with a second marked piece at the end. If the mark has moved, the diagnosis was right. If it has not, the diagnosis gets changed rather than the effort doubled.

process.title: Decide deliberately whether to continue
process.description: At the end of a block the options are stop, continue weekly, or move to a different weakness. Making that an explicit decision is what stops a short piece of work turning into a two-year standing order nobody reviews.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: A session built from a marked paper targets the mark the student is actually dropping. General subject support teaches content a student mostly has, which is why a term can pass with real effort and an unchanged grade.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and command terms taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Assessment criteria are explained letter by letter with their mark allocations, and command terms are taught as answer shapes rather than vocabulary. Both are published, both are learnable, and both are routinely left untaught.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers. A specialist is proposed against the exact code and tier your child's school entered, so the past papers practised are the ones they will sit.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery keeps the pool wide
whyPoints.description: Lessons are taught live online, one to one. In an emirate with small cohorts that is what makes a narrow Higher Level match possible at all, and it means the slot is chosen for the student's concentration rather than a driving route.

whyPoints.title: Finite blocks with a visible end
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic block ends with a second marked piece and a decision. Tutoring that continues by default is the most common waste in this market, and a planned stopping point removes it.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches criteria, questions method and responds to the student's own draft. No internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is produced for a student, and the boundary is stated before any coursework block begins.

faqs.question: My child's Sakamkam school report says 5 in Chemistry. What do we do with that?
faqs.answer: Ask for a marked paper rather than more detail on the report. A grade is a position; the script shows the cause. Read it from the back, count the questions where the student clearly knew the material and still lost a mark, and look at whether those losses are spread across topics or clustered in one or two. Spread losses point to a behaviour such as command-term response or missing working. Clustered losses point to a content gap that a short block will close. Bring the script to a trial lesson and the diagnosis takes one session.

faqs.question: How can a parent read a marked script without knowing the subject?
faqs.answer: By looking for pattern rather than content. Start at the back, where the longer structured marks sit, because a script that falls away in the final section is telling you about pacing. Count the half-earned questions. Look for crossings-out and restarts, which indicate planning problems rather than understanding. Then compare just two long answers against the published mark scheme to see what the scheme rewarded and the student did not supply. None of that needs subject knowledge, and it takes about ten minutes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in an exam answer?
faqs.answer: Describe asks what; explain asks why, with an explicit causal link. A student who answers an explain question with an accurate description earns the description marks only, which on a six-mark question can forfeit three marks on an answer that looked finished. Evaluate goes further again, requiring competing positions to be weighed and a judgement reached. Sorting twenty past-paper questions by command term and writing one-line answer plans rather than full answers moves more marks for most mid-to-upper students than an hour of content revision.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether my child sits Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1?
faqs.answer: Yes, for revision purposes it matters a great deal. The content overlap is high but the structures differ: how practical skills are examined, whether formulae are supplied, how tiers limit the grade, and how questions are stemmed. A student who practises the wrong board's papers loses marks on format rather than knowledge, which is the most avoidable loss available. Ask the exams officer for the codes and tiers in writing, keep them at the top of the revision plan, and give them to any tutor before the first session.

faqs.question: How many marks are available in an IB science internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A science individual investigation is assessed against four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, worth twenty-four marks in total. The point of knowing that is structural: evaluation is assessed separately from conclusion, so a single closing paragraph that attempts both tends to score poorly on each. Students who read the criteria write a distinct evaluation section connecting each limitation to the direction of the error. Mark totals and criterion names change between syllabus cycles, so confirm the current figures in the subject guide your school teaches from.

faqs.question: What are the criteria and mark totals for the IB maths exploration?
faqs.answer: The exploration is assessed against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, worth twenty marks in total. Personal engagement being separately assessed is the detail that changes topic choice: a student should pick a context they can genuinely say something about rather than one copied from a list of suggestions. The most common loss is calculation without justification, where a student performs correct mathematics and never explains why that model was the right one to choose. Confirm the current criteria in your school's subject guide.

faqs.question: How long is the Extended Essay allowed to be and what is it marked on?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay carries a four thousand word limit and is assessed against five criteria covering focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation and engagement, worth thirty-four marks in total. Critical thinking carries the largest share, which is why a research question that is too broad to answer within the limit is the most expensive early mistake. Narrowing the question before any writing begins is the highest-value hour in the whole process. Confirm the current criteria and limit against the subject guide your school uses.

faqs.question: Is three Higher Level subjects realistic for a student in a small Fujairah cohort?
faqs.answer: Three Higher Levels is the Diploma structure and it is manageable, but it is also the practical ceiling for most students, and the subject that suffers is rarely the one a family would predict. The Higher Level course is not the Standard Level course with harder questions: it adds syllabus content, often an extra paper, and a greater expectation of independence in the internal assessment. Review the subject mix in November of Year 12 rather than in April, when changing anything is harder and the internal assessment clock has already started.

faqs.question: What happens to coursework if we move school mid-course?
faqs.answer: It depends on what can be evidenced. Request the previous school's transcript and, for a Diploma student, written confirmation of internal assessment progress plus any marked drafts already produced. Work that cannot be evidenced may have to be restarted, and restarting an internal assessment in the second term of Year 13 is the hardest position a Diploma student can be in. Also compare the new school's syllabus codes and tiers against the old ones, because a change of board means a change of paper format even where the content overlaps.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's practice papers against the real mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful things a session can produce. Marking a script against the published scheme shows exactly which marks the scheme rewarded and the student did not supply, which is a different and more actionable finding than a percentage. Teaching a student to do that marking themselves is better still, because it transfers. What a tutor must not do is reproduce or supply board mark schemes and past papers as downloads; those are the boards' copyright and should be accessed through the school or the official site.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a specific weakness usually take to fix?
faqs.answer: A single diagnosable behaviour, such as missing interpretation sentences in maths or description where explanation was asked for, commonly takes four to six focused sessions spread over about three weeks, with a marked piece at the start and another at the end. A genuine content gap across several topics takes longer and is better run as a weekly slot through the term. The useful discipline is to set the block length in advance and measure it against a second marked piece, so the result is a mark rather than an impression.

faqs.question: What time can a diagnostic session run if we live in Sakamkam?
faqs.answer: Later than the school day suggests, because the afternoon pick-up run into Fujairah City is slower than the morning one and the whole city converges on the same roads at the same hour. A 5.30pm or 6pm start on a day without a corniche sports commitment works for most families, with weekend mornings kept for longer coursework sessions when the student is fresh. Diagnostic work is more tiring than content work, so sixty minutes usually beats ninety. In Ramadan the same session moves after Iftar and shortens.

faqs.question: Why does online teaching suit this kind of diagnostic work?
faqs.answer: Because both people look at the same thing at the same time. Screen sharing puts the marked script, the graph or the paragraph of a draft in front of both parties with the same annotations, so correction lands at the point of error instead of after the fact. It also keeps the specialist pool wide, which matters in an emirate with small cohorts where a narrow Higher Level match may not exist locally at all. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; lessons are taught live online, one to one.

faqs.question: What if the second marked piece shows no improvement?
faqs.answer: Then the diagnosis was wrong, and the right response is to change it rather than to add hours. A block that ends with a second marked piece exists precisely so that question can be answered with evidence. Sometimes the first diagnosis identified a real weakness that was not the binding one; sometimes the pairing is not working and a different specialist is the answer. Either way the decision should be explicit at the end of the block, not deferred until results day when nothing can be done about it.

faqs.question: Should we use tutoring for content or for exam technique?
faqs.answer: Whichever the marked paper says. If losses cluster in one or two topics, the problem is content and teaching those topics will fix it. If losses are spread thinly across the whole paper in the form of half-earned questions, the problem is technique and more content teaching will change nothing while everyone works hard. The reason to diagnose before booking is that these two problems look identical from the outside and respond to completely different sessions, and most families are sold the wrong one.

fujairah/sakamkam.closingHeading: Send one marked paper and we will tell you what it shows
fujairah/sakamkam.closingBody: The useful first step from Sakamkam is not a phone call about effort. Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, and one recent assessment with the marker's annotations on it. The free trial lesson is built around that script, taught online one to one over live video, and it ends with a written diagnosis naming the specific loss, the criterion or command term behind it, and how many sessions it should take. If that number is four, it will say four, and the block will end with a second marked piece so you can see whether it worked.

intro.heading: What a 7 in IB Maths costs, and what the money is actually buying
paragraphs: A 7 is the top band of the IB's 1-7 scale, and in Mathematics it is awarded on a scaled total rather than a percentage. Grade boundaries shift a little each session and the IB publishes them to schools after marking, so no honest page can print the exact number your child needs. What can be stated is the shape of the problem. At SL, two papers carry 40% each and the mathematical exploration carries the remaining fifth. At HL, three papers share 80% and the exploration carries 20%. Every mark is bought with one identifiable skill, and coaching hours are worth paying for only when they are spent on the skills your child is currently losing marks on.

That turns the price question into something you can actually audit. The UAE market charges roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist. Those bands come from published competitor rate cards and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, not from us. The useful figure is not the hourly rate. It is the rate multiplied by the number of hours the gap genuinely needs, divided by the marks those hours can reasonably recover.

Most families overpay in one of two ways. The first is buying a cheap general hour every week for two years, which keeps a student level at a 5 and never addresses the two topics costing them the grade. The second is buying a premium hour at AED 500 or more for work that a competent subject tutor could do in the same time: marking past papers, drilling algebraic fluency, or reading an exploration draft against the criteria. Scarcity pricing and a personal brand are real, but they are not the same thing as a higher mark.

The cheapest marks in IB Mathematics are almost always in the exploration and in Paper 1 technique. The exploration is 20 marks against five published criteria, marked internally and moderated by the IB, and a student who writes correct mathematics pitched below course level will cap Criterion E no matter how many hours of revision they do afterwards. Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without technology, so a student who has quietly learned the calculator route to every answer loses a third of the HL paper mark on skills that take weeks, not days, to rebuild. Both are diagnosable from one marked mock.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to the IB, to Cambridge, to Pearson or to any named school. We do not send a tutor to an address in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video, which is also why a family in Ras Al Khaimah can work with an Analysis and Approaches HL specialist instead of whoever lives within a reasonable drive. The sections below price the work, count the hours backwards from the session, and set out exactly where the academic-honesty line sits on exploration support.

ib-7-in-maths-coaching.programmesIntro: Maths does not start mattering in DP1. The route a student can realistically take at 16, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, is largely set by the fluency they arrive with. These are the four IB programmes UAE schools run, read through the single question of where the numbers go wrong.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led number work, measurement and early data handling, assessed by the school rather than by the IB. Nothing here appears on a transcript. What it decides is whether times tables, fractions and negative numbers are automatic by Year 7, because a student who still computes 7 x 8 deliberately will spend their Paper 1 time on arithmetic instead of on method. Coaching at this stage is fluency and confidence, in short sessions.
programmes.countryNote: UAE PYP schools run alongside the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies blocks, which KHDA counts in 40-minute lesson units. In practice a Dubai PYP week already carries a second language load, so additional maths work is best kept to two short weekday slots rather than one long weekend session.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics is assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-world contexts. Years 9 and 10 split into standard and extended routes, and that split is what determines whether Analysis and Approaches HL is open two years later. The MYP maths to DP maths transition is the most common reason a UAE student arrives in DP1 with a reported 6 and a real 4.
programmes.countryNote: MYP eAssessment is optional and not every UAE school enters students for it, so a Dubai or Sharjah family often has no external benchmark before DP1 begins. Ask the school for the extended-route decision in writing in Year 9. That single piece of paper tells you whether the AA HL door is still open.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two maths courses, each at SL and HL, plus the mathematical exploration in all four. This is where a 7 is won or lost. Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is technology-free; every Applications and Interpretation paper permits a graphic display calculator. HL adds Paper 3, two extended problem-solving questions worth 20% of the grade, which rewards stamina and structure rather than new content.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session functions mainly as a retake route for students who miss a university offer. Exploration deadlines are set internally by each school, so a Deira International School deadline and a Raha International School deadline can sit six weeks apart. Your child's own calendar, not a generic one, sets the coaching plan.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller UAE cohort takes the CP, combining DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where maths appears, it is a full DP course and is marked identically, so a CP student aiming at a 7 in Applications and Interpretation SL sits the same two papers and submits the same 20-mark exploration as a full Diploma candidate.
programmes.countryNote: CP students in the UAE frequently pair maths with business or design pathways, which makes Applications and Interpretation the common route. If the plan includes a UAE or overseas engineering degree later, check the programme's own entry page before assuming an AI grade satisfies it, because some faculties still list Analysis and Approaches.

ib-7-in-maths-coaching.subjectsIntro: Coaching for a 7 in maths rarely stays inside one syllabus line. The courses below are the ones UAE families book around a maths grade, including the two IGCSE codes that decide whether DP maths starts from solid ground and the subjects whose marks are really maths marks in disguise.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, algebraic manipulation, functions, trigonometry and calculus. Paper 1 is sat without technology at both levels, which is where fluency gaps become visible. Marks go missing on algebraic slips inside otherwise correct method, and on calculus questions where the student can differentiate but cannot say what the derivative means in context.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and interpretation, with a calculator permitted throughout. Maths AI SL is the most-taken route in UAE schools. Marks are lost less on arithmetic than on method conditions: choosing the wrong test, skipping the hypothesis statement, or reporting a regression result without commenting on what it means for the context given.

subjects.name: Mathematics AA HL Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions in 60 minutes, worth 20% of the HL grade. Paper 3 coaching is a separate skill from syllabus revision: students must hold a 20-mark build-up together, use earlier parts to reach later ones, and keep writing when the final part is not yet visible. Timed practice on full questions is the only route in.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A 20-mark internally marked piece against five criteria, carrying a fifth of the final grade. IB Maths exploration coaching is topic interrogation, criteria wording and feedback on the student's own draft. The most expensive error is a topic whose mathematics sits below course level, which caps Criterion E before a word is written.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Four assessment criteria and a standard or extended split in Years 9 and 10 that decides DP route access. Coaching here is about pattern-investigation tasks and written communication, which most students have never been taught explicitly, and about closing arithmetic and algebra gaps while there is still time for them to close.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended 0580 is the realistic minimum for Analysis and Approaches at HL. Core caps at grade C and leaves a student short of the algebra DP assumes. Marks are lost on multi-step algebra, on bearings and vectors, and on reading comprehension in longer structured questions rather than on the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: The best available bridge into Analysis and Approaches HL: calculus, matrices, series and more demanding trigonometry a year early. Not every UAE school offers Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606, and a student who has not sat it can cover the same ground in a summer block before DP1 begins.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A physics grade at HL is frequently a maths grade. Students who cannot rearrange formulae under time pressure, read a log-log graph or handle uncertainties lose marks that look like physics marks. Pairing physics with Analysis and Approaches in the same week lets one coach fix the algebra once rather than twice.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: HL economics adds quantitative questions on elasticity, cost curves and policy calculation. Students arriving from Applications and Interpretation usually have the statistics but not the algebraic confidence, and the internal assessment commentaries reward precise use of diagrams and data that maths coaching transfers to directly.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logic, binary and hexadecimal conversion, Big-O reasoning and the HL abstract data structures paper all sit on mathematical foundations. Students who find recursion opaque usually find it opaque for the same reason they find sequences opaque, and the fix is sequences, taught properly, not more code.

ib-7-in-maths-coaching.regionsTitle: Coaching for a 7 across the seven emirates
ib-7-in-maths-coaching.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in the UAE changes the local tutor pool, the commute, and the regulator whose inspection report describes the school's maths teaching. It does not change what a 7 requires. Online delivery is what makes an Analysis and Approaches HL specialist reachable from any of the seven.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools across 17 curricula, with IB programmes covering about 7 per cent of the emirate's private-school pupils. KHDA inspection reports break attainment down by subject and phase, so the maths line in your school's latest report is the cheapest diagnostic available. IB maths coaching in Dubai has the deepest tutor pool and the worst evening traffic.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation for private schools here, and its professional-ethics rules prevent school staff from taking paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school. IB maths coaching in Abu Dhabi therefore cannot mean your child's own teacher, which is one reason online matching outperforms the local word-of-mouth route.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, so a Sharjah school's maths option list can differ from a Dubai school's. The specialist IB maths pool living in the emirate is small, and a 19:00 session over video avoids the Dubai-Sharjah evening crawl entirely.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller international-school cluster and a thinner supply of DP maths specialists than the coast. Families here most often ask for Applications and Interpretation SL support and exploration coaching, both of which work identically over video. Session timing is easier than in Dubai because there is no commute to absorb.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees and curricula. There are few resident IB Mathematics HL specialists, so in-home tutoring at a sensible rate is largely unavailable regardless of budget. This is the clearest case in the country for one-to-one online coaching rather than a local compromise.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The practical constraint is supply: a family wanting Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 coaching will not find it locally. Over video, the same Paper 3 specialist who works with a Dubai Marina family is available at the same rate band.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with a short local list of IB schools and a correspondingly short list of DP maths tutors. Ajman families commonly ask whether a Dubai-based tutor will travel; the honest answer is that the travel time is charged for in the rate, and online removes it.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country, supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Returned zero IB maths tutor listings in our own searches of the local market. Families here are matched with the same coaches as Dubai families and sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, so nothing about the plan changes.

schoolClusters.note: These are established IB World Schools in Dubai whose DP students ask for maths support most often. Their internal exploration deadlines differ by several weeks, and their reported maths attainment differs more than their marketing does. Read your own school's KHDA report before committing to a coaching budget.

schoolClusters.note: ADEK-regulated schools offering the Diploma Programme. Because ADEK's ethics rules bar school staff from tutoring their own enrolled students, families in this cluster rely more on external coaching than Dubai families do, and more of that coaching is delivered online.

sections.heading: What a 7 in IB Maths actually is, and what no page can tell you
paragraphs: A 7 in IB Mathematics is the top band of the 1-7 scale, awarded on a scaled total across all components after the IB sets grade boundaries for that session. The boundaries are not fixed year to year and are published to schools after marking, which means any site printing a precise percentage for a 7 is telling you something it cannot know. What is stable is the structure: at SL two papers and the exploration, at HL three papers and the exploration, with the exploration always carrying a fifth of the grade.

That structure is the only honest basis for a coaching budget. A student sitting on a 6 is almost never uniformly a 6. They are usually a 7 on two topics, a 5 on one, and a 4 on the exploration criteria nobody has explained to them. Marks lost in those three places are not interchangeable, and they do not cost the same number of hours to recover. Rebuilding algebraic fluency for a technology-free Paper 1 takes weeks of short, frequent practice. Lifting a Criterion D reflection mark takes one conversation and a redraft.

This is also where the cost conversation becomes answerable. If a coach cannot name which component your child is losing marks in after reading one marked paper, the hours you buy are being allocated by guesswork, and guesswork at AED 250 an hour is the most expensive thing on this page. Ask for the diagnosis before you ask for the price. A plan that says 'Paper 1 trigonometry and Criterion B notation, eight weeks' is worth paying for; 'general IB maths support, ongoing' is not.

No coach can promise a 7, and any provider offering an outcome in exchange for a fee should be treated with real scepticism. What can be promised is a clear read of where the marks are going, a written plan with the hours and the arithmetic visible, and honest notice when the remaining weeks are too few for the gap in question.
bullets: Grade boundaries move each session and are published to schools, not to the public
A 6 is usually a composite of 7s, 5s and an unmarked exploration weakness
Diagnosis comes before pricing, from one marked paper and the school calendar
Ask any provider which component they will work on first, and why

sections.heading: The papers you are buying hours against
paragraphs: Both IB maths routes are assessed the same way at the level of components: two written papers and the mathematical exploration at SL, three papers and the exploration at HL. The differences that matter for coaching are in what each paper permits and what it rewards. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without technology at both levels, so it is a direct test of algebraic and calculus fluency. Every Applications and Interpretation paper permits a graphic display calculator, which moves the difficulty from computation to choosing the right method and interpreting the output.

HL Paper 3 is the component UAE students most often arrive at untrained. It is 60 minutes, two extended questions, and 20% of the grade. The questions are designed as build-ups: part (a) is accessible, part (f) depends on parts (c) and (d), and candidates who treat each part as independent lose the chain. Students who have practised only past Paper 1 and Paper 2 questions have never rehearsed the specific skill of staying inside one problem for 30 minutes, and that is a coachable skill with a measurable return.

The exploration is the component with the highest marks-per-hour ratio and the least classroom supervision. Twenty marks, five criteria, and a school deadline that is internal rather than set by the IB. A student who picks a topic whose mathematics sits below course level has capped Criterion E before writing anything, and no amount of polishing afterwards recovers those marks. The table below sets out the components, what each one actually tests, and where students in UAE schools most commonly lose the marks that separate a 6 from a 7.

Read it against your child's last marked mock rather than in the abstract. If the mock shows a strong Paper 2 and a weak Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches, that is a technology-dependence diagnosis and it has a known fix. If both papers are even but the predicted grade is a 6, the exploration is almost certainly where the grade is sitting.

sections.heading: AA or AI, and what the wrong route costs later
paragraphs: The single most expensive decision in IB Mathematics is made before the course starts, usually in Year 11, and often on incomplete information. Analysis and Approaches is the proof, algebra and calculus route. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and interpretation route. Neither is a soft option, and a 7 in Applications and Interpretation HL is a harder grade to earn than a 5 in Analysis and Approaches SL by any reasonable measure. What differs is which university doors stay open.

The honest position on university requirements is that they vary by faculty and change between admissions cycles, so the only reliable source is the programme's own entry page in the year your child applies. Engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics degrees commonly list Analysis and Approaches, frequently at HL. Business, design, psychology and most social sciences commonly accept Applications and Interpretation. Do not take a tutor's summary as the requirement, including this one: check the page and keep a screenshot.

Where coaching earns its fee here is in the honest assessment of fit. A student who is fighting for a 4 in Analysis and Approaches HL in DP1 and whose target degrees accept Applications and Interpretation is losing marks across their whole diploma to defend a route they do not need. A student who switches away from Analysis and Approaches to protect a total score, then applies to engineering two years later, has paid a much larger price. One diagnostic conversation in the first term is worth more than a year of weekly hours spent propping up the wrong choice.

If a switch does happen, budget for it. Moving down from HL to SL within the same route is routine in DP1 and usually needs little catch-up. Crossing from Analysis and Approaches to Applications and Interpretation, or back, needs the school's sign-off and six to ten hours of bridging, because the statistics content in Applications and Interpretation is heavier and the proof content in Analysis and Approaches has no equivalent.

sections.heading: Where a 6 becomes a 7, topic by topic
paragraphs: Marks in IB Mathematics are lost in predictable places, and the pattern is consistent enough across UAE schools that a marked mock usually identifies it in twenty minutes. The recurring causes are not conceptual mysteries. They are unpractised algebra, calculator dependence, unstated method conditions, and answers that stop one line before the question was actually answered. Each has a different hour cost, and that is what a coaching plan should be priced on.

The most common single leak at Analysis and Approaches HL is algebraic manipulation inside otherwise correct method. A student sets up a correct integral and then loses a sign, or differentiates correctly and cannot rearrange the result. In a mark scheme this reads as one lost accuracy mark per question, which across a paper is the difference between a 6 and a 7. The fix is high-frequency, low-duration practice: ten minutes of manipulation daily for six weeks beats two hours on a Saturday, and it is the cheapest intervention available because it does not need an hour of tutor time to deliver.

At Applications and Interpretation the leak is usually procedural. Students run a chi-squared test without stating the hypotheses, quote a correlation coefficient without commenting on what it means for the context, or choose a regression model because the calculator offered it rather than because the data shape justified it. These are method marks, and they are recoverable quickly because the content is already known. Coaching here is about writing the answer the mark scheme is looking for, which is a skill most students have simply never been shown.

Exploration marks sit in a category of their own. They are not lost through weak mathematics in most cases but through presentation, notation and reflection: a graph with no axis labels, calculator syntax left in the body, a reflection section bolted on at the end. These are the cheapest marks on the whole course and the ones families most often leave on the table while paying for extra Paper 2 revision they do not need.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria and the honesty line
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries 20% of the grade in all four IB maths courses and is marked by the school against five published criteria, then moderated by the IB. It is the component where coaching returns the most marks per hour and the component where the academic-honesty line matters most, because the work must be the student's own and an IB malpractice finding is an expulsion risk for the student rather than an inconvenience for the provider.

What a coach may legitimately do is well defined. A coach may teach the mathematics a topic requires, demonstrated on different numbers. A coach may ask why a topic interests the student until the answer is specific enough to be defensible under Criterion C. A coach may read a draft the student has produced and respond with the criterion wording: 'Criterion B asks for defined variables; find me the line where your variables are defined.' A coach may explain what moderation looks for and what a school's internal deadline means for the sequence of work.

What a coach must never do is produce any part of the assessed text. No coach at IB Gram writes, edits to completion, supplies or ghost-authors an exploration, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay or any coursework, and we decline the request when it is made. One provider ranking for these queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an integrity breach, and buying one puts the student's whole diploma at risk rather than their maths grade. The distinction is simple to state and we state it in writing before an exploration block starts.

sections.heading: What coaching for a 7 costs in the UAE, and who charges what
paragraphs: IB maths tutoring rates in AED span roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour in this market, and the spread is not explained by quality alone. It is explained by who is teaching, whether travel is included, and whether the hour is one-to-one. Most competitor pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all; two publish prices in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. The table below collects the published figures, with each attributed to the provider or rate card that published it.

Read the bands as a market, not as our price list. IB Gram is a matching platform, so what a family pays depends on the coach, the level and the session length agreed after the free trial lesson. The useful exercise with this table is not finding the lowest number. It is working out the cost per mark. Twenty-four hours at AED 200 is AED 4,800; if those hours are aimed at a diagnosed Paper 1 fluency gap and a capped Criterion E, they are buying identifiable marks. The same AED 4,800 spread over two years of general homework supervision is buying attendance.

Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Context helps here: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so a tutoring budget set last year has not been squeezed by fees this year.

Two cost traps are worth naming. The first is paying a premium rate for work that is not premium work: marking past papers and drilling algebra are the same tasks at AED 200 and at AED 650. The second is paying by the month for sessions that are not needed in that month, which is common in the quiet middle of DP1. Buy hours against a diagnosed gap and a deadline, and ask any provider to show the arithmetic that connects the two.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one versus an in-home maths tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Parents searching for a maths tutor in the UAE usually start by looking for someone who will come to the house, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring is real, widely available in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and priced at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded in. What you buy with the premium is a tutor sitting beside the student and a parent who can see the session happening. What you pay for it is a smaller pool, a commute that eats into the hour, and a specialist shortage the further you get from the two big cities.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own working held up to the camera. We are explicit about this because the alternative, implying a doorstep service and then delivering a video call, is a trust failure several providers in this market commit by routing UAE parents to an overseas phone number.

The case for online here is not that it is cheaper, although it usually is once travel is priced. It is that the selection pool stops being geographic. A family in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah has almost no chance of finding a resident Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 specialist at any price, and a family in Dubai Marina choosing from tutors willing to drive to Dubai Marina at 17:30 is choosing from a list shaped by traffic rather than by subject depth. Over video, the constraint is the coach's calendar.

Screen-sharing also changes what the hour contains. Past papers are marked live on screen, the error log is a shared document rather than a parent's memory, and recorded explanation of a worked question can be replayed before the next session. sections.heading: How many hours a 7 takes, counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session functions mainly as a retake route. Working backwards from the session is the only way to turn a grade target into a number of hours and therefore into a price. The variables are the starting grade, whether the exploration is already internally marked, and whether the student is at SL or HL, because HL carries Paper 3 and Paper 3 needs its own block of timed practice.

The honest ranges are wide and worth stating plainly. A student holding a 6 with a completed exploration and 20 or more weeks in hand typically needs one session a week. A student at a 5 with an unfinished exploration draft needs the exploration block first, then topic repair, and usually moves to two sessions a week in the final stretch. A student at a 4 in HL at the DP1 report is looking at a two-year rebuild, because the algebra and calculus underneath Paper 3 cannot be compressed into a term. Any provider quoting the same package to all three has not read the papers.

Deadlines that are not the exam also shape the plan. The exploration deadline is internal and set by your child's school, which is why two students in different Dubai schools can be on completely different timelines for the same session. A published parallel from another board shows how far ahead the paperwork sits. Pearson Edexcel runs an International GCSE series in November, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results from the November 2025 series reaching students on 22 January 2026. Entries for that series closed well before the autumn term was over, and the result landed two months after the last paper, so the administrative calendar stretches either side of the exam window rather than tracking it. The same is true of IB internal deadlines, which is why they are worth writing down in September rather than discovering in February of the exam year. Confirm every IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from a tutoring page, including ours.

Ramadan is the other fixed point in a UAE plan. School days shorten, family routines change, and the practical answer is to move sessions to post-Iftar timing, typically 21:00 to 22:30 Gulf Standard Time, rather than to pause for a month that sits immediately before the session. sections.heading: The regulator, the permit, and what a parent should verify
paragraphs: Private schooling in the UAE is regulated emirate by emirate, and knowing which authority governs your child's school is more useful than it sounds, because the inspection report is a free diagnostic. Dubai's KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi's ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and federally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified. MoHRE's own service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', with no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app and e-services.

Two things follow for a parent hiring maths help. Ask an individual tutor directly whether they hold the permit, because it costs them nothing to obtain and nothing to show. And do not ask for your child's own classroom teacher: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. A tutoring operation running premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal category again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and claims none. We are an independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE office, centre or branch, and nothing on this page should be read as an endorsement by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Where this page cites a regulator, it is to explain what that body does and to link you to its own page.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what maths has to show
paragraphs: A maths grade is not only a university currency. For families planning to stay in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency route for a secondary certificate also has subject and grade requirements, and the British-track rules are published clearly enough to repeat. Students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because at least one provider ranking for UAE tutoring queries publishes a six-subject requirement. On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. Those are the figures in the published guidance.

For the IB, no points threshold can responsibly be printed here. The guidance we can source does not state one, so any page quoting an IB score for equivalency is quoting something unverified. The correct step is to read the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, in the year you need it. IB Gram does not perform, submit or influence equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for any part of that process.

What this does mean for maths coaching is practical. If your child's plan includes a UAE university, the maths evidence the Ministry looks at may be an IGCSE grade and an SAT Math score rather than the DP grade you have been budgeting coaching hours against. A family in that position is often better served by a short block on SAT Math technique alongside the DP work than by more hours on the same DP syllabus.

sections.heading: The timetable your maths hours are competing with
paragraphs: A coaching plan that ignores the rest of a UAE school week fails on scheduling rather than on teaching. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, which is the rule every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement sits on.

The detail matters for timing. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in 40-minute lesson units, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

What a parent feels is a full week. An IB student carrying six DP subjects, the exploration, the Extended Essay, TOK and a mandatory-subject block has very little unallocated weekday time before 18:00. The practical answer is to place maths sessions after the mandatory block, usually from 18:00 onwards, and to move the heavier exploration work to a weekend morning when the student is not already five hours into a school day. Two 45-minute sessions often outperform one 90-minute session for exactly this reason.

Ramadan compresses this further. School hours shorten, the family rhythm shifts, and the month frequently sits close to the May session. Pausing for four weeks at that point is expensive in a way that is easy to underestimate. Moving to post-Iftar slots around 21:00 to 22:30 Gulf Standard Time keeps the error log alive, and an online session is far easier to reschedule that way than a visit that depends on somebody driving across the city.
