sections.heading: After the mark: moderation, equivalency and the route into medicine
paragraphs: The mark a Chemistry teacher awards is not automatically the mark that counts. Internally assessed work is marked by the school against the published criteria and then moderated by the IB, which can adjust a school's marks upwards or downwards across the cohort if the school's application of the criteria differs from the standard. Chemistry IA moderation is the reason a generous teacher is not a gift and a strict one is not a disaster: what matters is whether the work genuinely meets the descriptors, not how one department reads them.

That has a practical consequence for how a family uses tutoring. The useful question for a tutor reading a draft is not whether the student will be pleased with the mark but whether the evidence for each criterion is actually on the page. A draft that scores well in the school and thinly against the descriptors is the profile most exposed to moderation. A draft with explicit uncertainty treatment, a conclusion anchored to a cited value, and an evaluation naming a real systematic error is the profile that holds.

Looking further forward, UAE families should also know what their certificates have to show for the Ministry of Education equivalency process. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong. No IB points threshold is published here, because none has been read on an official Ministry source, and an unsourced figure on an equivalency page is worse than no figure.

For the Chemistry student aiming at medicine or engineering, the subject choice behind the investigation matters as much as the mark. Higher Level Chemistry is the standard expectation for medicine in the UK and for most Gulf medical programmes, generally alongside Biology. Mathematics route choice is the decision families get wrong: Analysis and Approaches is what many engineering and physical-science admissions expect, while Applications and Interpretation suits a statistics-led path. Check the published prerequisites for the actual universities on your list before DP2 begins, and verify equivalency requirements on the Ministry's own channels rather than through any tutoring provider, including this one.

process.title: Tell us the school deadline first
process.description: The consultation starts with one date: when your child's school wants the full draft. Everything else is planned backwards from it. We also ask which criterion the student feels least sure about and whether any data exists yet, because those two answers determine whether this is a teaching job or a triage job.

process.title: A trial session on the live work
process.description: The first session uses the student's actual investigation, not a diagnostic exercise. A Chemistry specialist asks about the question, the range and the uncertainties, and at the end you get a plain statement of what is strong, what is at risk and roughly how many sessions the remaining work needs. The session condition and the rate for your level are stated before you book.

process.title: Milestones, not a standing slot
process.description: We schedule against the checkpoints in the milestone table rather than booking a habitual weekly hour. For most families that is five or six sessions across a term. If the student needs weekly Chemistry teaching as well, that runs as a separate thread with the same tutor so nothing is repeated twice.

process.title: Each session ends with the student's task list
process.description: The tutor leaves the session with notes; the student leaves with decisions. What to measure next, which calculation to redo, which claim the graph does not yet support. Nothing is written into the student's file by anyone else, and the task list is deliberately short enough to be finished before the next session.

process.title: One pre-deadline read, then we stop
process.description: A full criterion-by-criterion read happens with roughly a fortnight to go, producing a fix list ranked by marks per hour of remaining effort. After that we deliberately stop suggesting improvements, because late rewriting damages sections that were already scoring. If no specialist is free at the time you need, we say so rather than substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The criteria are published here, not withheld
whyPoints.description: The marks, the four criterion names and the costliest error in each are on this page in a table. No competing page for this query publishes any of it. A family that knows an investigation is twenty-four marks across four criteria can read a draft themselves and ask better questions of their school.

whyPoints.title: Rates are attributed, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market band with the provider who published it named and the date stated. None of them is our price. Our rate is quoted for your subject and level before you commit to anything, which is the opposite of the pattern across this market, where one ranking agency asks the price question in its own FAQ and then refuses to answer it.

whyPoints.title: A stated honesty boundary you can hold us to
whyPoints.description: The table in the academic-honesty section lists, activity by activity, what a tutor does and what only the student does. In a market where a provider openly sells finished coursework, a published boundary is the practical difference between help your child can submit and help that puts the Diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not the nearest available person
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a student in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah gets a Higher Level Chemistry specialist rather than whoever teaches science within driving distance. For Higher Level work in the smaller emirates, where there is effectively no local specialist market, that is the whole of the value.

whyPoints.title: Planning built around the UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Shortened Ramadan days, Eid, and the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies periods all sit inside the investigation window. We count the school evenings that actually remain rather than the calendar weeks, which is usually the first time a family sees the real number.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what is still possible
whyPoints.description: If you arrive with nine days left and no data, the first answer is what can and cannot still be fixed, before any hours are sold. No new experiment is designed in deadline week and no grade is promised at any point, because no tutor can promise one. What a specialist can do is make sure the marks still available are the ones being chased.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB Chemistry Scientific Investigation worth, and how are they split?
faqs.answer: The investigation carries twenty-four marks and contributes twenty per cent of the final Chemistry grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Those marks are divided equally across four criteria, six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. The even split matters because students spend most of their effort on the write-up and almost none on the experimental design, even though both carry the same six marks. Treat the four criteria as four separate marking decisions rather than as four sections of a document, and confirm the current criteria wording with your child's Diploma Programme coordinator, since guide revisions do change the descriptors.

faqs.question: When should a UAE Chemistry student start the Scientific Investigation?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from your school's internal draft deadline rather than forwards from today. In practice a student wants candidate questions roughly twelve weeks out, a written method and a booked laboratory slot by ten, a trial run with real readings by eight, and the full dataset by six. The UAE calendar is what makes this tighter than it looks: shortened Ramadan days remove practical sessions, Eid removes more, and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies periods sit in the same weeks. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline in writing, then count actual school evenings, not calendar weeks.

faqs.question: My son's research question is whether temperature affects reaction rate. Is that good enough?
faqs.answer: Not yet, because it has no range, no measurement method and no constrained variables. The same interest becomes a usable question when it names the reaction, states the temperature range and the number of intervals, specifies how rate will be measured, and lists what is being held constant. Research design marks reward exactly those decisions. A question this broad also tends to produce three data points, and three points cannot establish a relationship. Five or six well-spaced values with repeats at each turns the same idea into work that can score across all four criteria.

faqs.question: Our school laboratory cannot run the experiment he designed. What are the options?
faqs.answer: This is common in UAE schools, where benches are shared across year groups and practical blocks are timetabled weeks ahead. There are three routes. Redesign the method around apparatus the school actually has, which usually costs a week and saves a month. Switch to a database investigation using published thermodynamic or kinetic data, which can score full marks and removes bench time from the critical path. Or move to a simulation-based investigation, provided the model's assumptions are interrogated in the evaluation. None of these is a soft option; the Evaluation criterion gets harder when the data is not your own.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with my daughter's raw Chemistry data?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach her how instrument uncertainty works, show propagation worked through on practice numbers, ask why she chose that range, and look at her graph and ask what it actually demonstrates. A tutor may not process her data for her, type into her file, supply the calculations, or write any part of the submitted report. Every number and every word in the file has to be hers. That boundary is not us being cautious; Data analysis assesses her own quantitative handling, and supplied or fabricated data is malpractice that falls on the student, not on the provider.

faqs.question: How long should an IB Chemistry investigation report be?
faqs.answer: There is a published length limit for the investigation, and your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the current figure for the guide your child is assessed under. Check it with them rather than relying on a number found on a tutoring site, because the limit changed with recent guide revisions and older exemplars circulating online were written to a different one. The practical advice is more useful than the number anyway: most over-length drafts are long because the method is narrated rather than specified, and tightening that usually improves Research design while solving the length problem at the same time.

faqs.question: Is a simulation or database investigation penalised compared with a wet-lab one?
faqs.answer: No. The criteria do not reward bench work for its own sake, and a database or simulation investigation can score across all four criteria if the processing and evaluation are genuine. What changes is where the difficulty sits. With your own data you evaluate your own method. With published data you have to interrogate someone else's collection method, sample and assumptions, which is harder to do convincingly. Students choose these routes for a real reason in the UAE, where laboratory access is tightly timetabled, and the choice is defensible provided the evaluation does the extra work.

faqs.question: What does uncertainty propagation actually have to look like to score in Data analysis?
faqs.answer: It has to be visible as numbers, not described in a sentence. Each instrument's uncertainty belongs in the raw table heading alongside the unit. Those uncertainties are then carried through every calculation, so a processed value arrives with its own uncertainty attached. The graph shows error bars derived from that work, and the gradient or trend is treated with its own range. Students who write that equipment has limitations but never carry a figure through lose marks in Data analysis, then lose more in Evaluation, because they have no quantitative basis for judging whether their result and the accepted value genuinely differ.

faqs.question: His Chemistry draft is due in nine days and he has no results. What happens now?
faqs.answer: The first job is an honest assessment, not a booking. With nine days and no data, no new multi-session experiment is realistic, so the real options are a rapid redesign around apparatus available this week, or a switch to a published-data investigation that can be completed without bench time. Both are legitimate. What does not work is writing the report first and hoping data appears. We will tell you which marks are still reachable before selling any hours, and we will not design an experiment in deadline week and pretend it can be run.

faqs.question: Will the mark my child's teacher gives for Chemistry be the mark that counts?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The school marks internally assessed work against the published criteria and the IB then moderates, which can move a school's marks up or down across the cohort where the school's application of the criteria differs from the standard. So a generous department is not a gift and a strict one is not a disaster. What survives moderation is evidence actually present on the page: uncertainties carried through, a conclusion anchored to a cited accepted value, and an evaluation naming a specific systematic error. A draft that pleases a teacher but reads thinly against the descriptors is the most exposed profile.

faqs.question: Do older IB Chemistry exemplars still match the criteria our school is marking against?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this trips up a lot of families. The Chemistry guide has been revised, and the criterion names, their number and the mark allocations in circulating older exemplars may not match what your child is assessed under now. An exemplar written to a five-criterion scheme will teach a student to foreground things the current four criteria do not reward in the same way. Ask the coordinator which guide applies and work from the criteria your school will mark against. We reference official documents and link to them rather than reproducing them, which is a copyright matter as well as an accuracy one.

faqs.question: Does the Chemistry investigation differ between Standard Level and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The investigation requirement and its weighting are the same: twenty-four marks, four criteria, twenty per cent of the grade at both levels. What differs is the syllabus a Higher Level student can draw on and the depth of chemistry a marker will expect in a Conclusion. An HL candidate explaining a kinetics result has more mechanism available and is judged against that. The practical implication is that HL students should not pick a question so simple that it gives them nowhere to show the extra syllabus, and SL students should not reach for one they cannot interpret.

faqs.question: Ramadan falls across our school's Chemistry draft deadline. How do we plan around it?
faqs.answer: Treat the shortened school days as a writing and processing period and finish all bench work before they start. Practical sessions need longer blocks than a reduced day gives, so they are the first thing a compressed timetable drops. Move tutoring to after Iftar, which most UAE families find easier than a late-afternoon slot anyway. Then assume the week following Eid produces nothing and plan as if it does not exist. Our sessions are delivered online, so an after-Iftar or late-evening slot is a scheduling choice rather than a traffic problem.

faqs.question: Can one block of sessions cover both the Chemistry investigation and Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the sensible arrangement, because the topics overlap. An investigation built on kinetics, equilibrium or energetics rehearses exactly the quantitative work those written papers test, so an hour spent on uncertainty treatment or on interpreting a gradient pays in both places. We usually run it as one thread with one tutor rather than two separate bookings, with the balance shifting towards papers once the draft is with the school. What we do not do is let paper revision quietly consume the weeks the investigation still needs.

faqs.question: What do Chemistry investigation sessions cost compared with weekly UAE tutoring rates?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE as at October 2026 run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to beyond 450 for IB and IGCSE specialists, with one premium provider publishing AED 650 and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. For an investigation the hourly rate matters less than the hour count, and five or six milestone sessions started early costs well below a twenty-week standing slot.

faqs.question: Does a strong Chemistry investigation mark help with Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed on the certificate a student ends up with, not on individual components, so the investigation matters only through its effect on the final Chemistry grade. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E. No IB points threshold is quoted here because none has been read on an official Ministry source. Verify your own case through the Ministry's channels.

ib-chemistry-ia-help.closingHeading: Start from the deadline, not from the draft
ib-chemistry-ia-help.closingBody: If your child is working on a DP Chemistry investigation anywhere in the UAE, the most useful thing you can do this week is get the school's internal draft deadline in writing and count the actual school evenings left before it. Then read the criteria table above and ask your child which of the four they could not currently evidence. Those two answers tell you whether you need a term of milestone sessions, a block of Higher Level teaching, or one honest conversation about what is still reachable. Book a trial session with a Chemistry specialist and bring the real work: the question, the readings, whatever exists. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and the student keeps the pen throughout.

ib-classes.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma and MYP subjects UAE families ask for most, and they plan in dates rather than in topics. Tell us your child's session, their school's internal coursework deadlines and the subjects at Higher Level, and the match is made against that calendar.

intro.heading: The IB year is a countdown, and most families start counting too late
paragraphs: Parents searching for IB classes in the UAE almost always type the words in the same week: the week a mock result lands, or the week a school emails about Internal Assessment deadlines. By then the calendar has already decided a good deal. Some things can still be changed cheaply in that week, some are expensive to change, and a few are fixed. The difference between those three categories is not a matter of effort or of how good the teaching is. It is a matter of how many weeks are left, and what those weeks are legally and practically allowed to contain.

So this page is built as a calendar rather than as a brochure. It starts twenty-four months before the first paper, at the point where subject choices and the Higher Level decision are made, and it walks forward in windows: the Internal Assessment term, the entry and registration term, mocks, the Ramadan question, the twelve-week revision block, the final fortnight, results day, and the enquiry and retake window after it. Each window has an owner. Some deadlines belong to the school, some to the exam board, some to the Ministry of Education, and only a few belong to you.

Knowing the owner matters more than it sounds. A school's internal Internal Assessment deadline can sometimes be negotiated by a week; a Cambridge final entry deadline cannot be negotiated at all, and Cambridge publishes its own worked example of how far ahead it sits. Cambridge runs two series a UAE candidate can sit, June and November, and for the June series the final entry closes in the spring, roughly a term before the first paper — well before most families have thought about exams. The exact day is set per series and published by Cambridge to centres, so the school is the only place to get it. Pearson works to its own published series pattern, with Edexcel International GCSE exams available in May/June and November each year.

The IB's own dates are the one thing this page will not print. The IB publishes its session windows on ibo.org, that page refuses automated checking, and an exam date that is wrong by a week is worse than no date at all. So the shape of the calendar is here, the Cambridge and Pearson dates are here with their sources, and the exact IB session dates are a question for your child's Diploma coordinator. Ask for them in writing, in September of the second Diploma year, and build everything else around them.

Lessons themselves are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is not a limitation hidden in a footnote — on a calendar-driven plan it is an advantage, because a specialist in the exact subject and level your child needs can start in the week you need them rather than whenever someone within a reasonable drive happens to be free. The sections below say what each window should contain, what the market charges for it, and where families most often lose the weeks they thought they had.
bullets: Twenty-four months out: subject and Higher Level choices, including the maths route
Eighteen months out: Internal Assessment topics approved and data collection started
Twelve months out: exam entries, timetable zone confirmed, private-candidate questions settled
Twelve weeks out: a counted revision block with hours per subject, not a vague push
After results: the enquiry window, the remark decision and the November session retake question

ib-classes.programmesIntro: Each IB programme has its own calendar shape, and the deadlines that matter are different in each. The notes below say where the pressure points sit for UAE families in particular, because the UAE school year, the mandatory Ministry subjects and the May session interact differently at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams, so the calendar is driven by units of inquiry, the exhibition in the final year, and the point at which a child transfers into MYP. Classes at this stage are about building the reading, writing and number fluency the MYP will assume, and about the exhibition process: research questions, note-taking, and presenting work that is genuinely the child's own.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the PYP runs alongside the mandatory Ministry subjects from the start, so a Year 5 week already contains Arabic, Islamic Education for Muslim pupils, and Moral, Social and Cultural Studies. KHDA calculates its mandatory-subject time in 40-minute lesson units, which is why adding a weekly class after school needs a realistic look at what the day already holds before anything is booked.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP is assessed against criteria rather than marks out of 100, which is where most parents lose the thread. A child can be working hard and still sit at a 4 because one criterion is never addressed. MYP classes are most useful when they decode the criteria the school is actually using, then rehearse the specific skill each one rewards, ending with the Personal Project in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma handover is the sharpest calendar point in the UAE, because many families also consider moving to an IGCSE school at the same age. A decision made in Year 9 about MYP mathematics shapes which Diploma maths route is realistic two years later, and that in turn shapes what the Ministry of Education will later count towards equivalency. This window closes quietly, without a letter home.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Twenty-four points are needed for the award and forty-five is the maximum, including up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together. Almost every deadline in these two years is internal until the final term, which is exactly why families miss them.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma students normally sit the May session, and the November session exists mainly for retakes and for schools on a different academic year. That single fact sets the whole countdown: a September start in the first Diploma year is twenty months from the first paper, and a September start in the second year is about eight. Both are workable; they are not the same plan, and they should not cost the same.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development strand and personal and professional skills. Its calendar is less uniform than the Diploma's because the career-related component is set by the provider rather than the IB, so the deadlines come from two directions at once and need writing down in one place.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools, and families on it often find that general IB advice online does not fit. Classes here tend to focus on the Diploma courses taken inside the CP, where the external assessment and session dates behave exactly as they do for a full Diploma candidate, and on the reflective project as a process rather than as a piece of writing someone else contributes to.

ib-classes.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed here with the deadline that actually bites in each one. In most Diploma subjects the internal component is not the hardest part academically — it is the part with the earliest hard date, and the part a family discovers late.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is twenty per cent of the grade at both levels and is marked against five criteria. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a short problem-solving paper that rewards unfamiliar extended questions. The calendar point: a topic chosen in the spring of the first year leaves time to collect and model data properly; one chosen in the autumn of the second year rarely does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same exploration weighting and criteria, different emphasis: statistics, modelling and technology use run through the papers. Higher Level again carries Paper 3. Families switching from Analysis and Approaches after the first term need to know what transfers and what does not, and that the switch window is usually set by the school rather than by the IB.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is a single internally assessed task of up to 3,000 words, weighted at twenty per cent, marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The common failure is a question that cannot generate enough usable data. That is a decision made months before the write-up, which is why it belongs in the first-year calendar, not the second.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and energetics absorb the most class time, but the earliest date is the investigation. Online IB Higher Level classes handle the practical side by working on the design, the uncertainty treatment and the data analysis, while the apparatus work stays in the school laboratory where the school supervises it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide marks here more than content recall does: outline, explain, evaluate and suggest each want a different shape of answer. The investigation needs a measurable variable and repeat readings. A class that starts in the second year usually spends its first fortnight repairing a question that was too broad to produce a conclusion.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is three commentaries, each capped at 800 words, each built on a different article and a different unit of the course, together worth twenty per cent. Because they are spread across both years, they are the component most often left as a block of three in one panicked month. Diary them at the start of the first year instead.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Paper answers live and die on applying a tool to the stimulus rather than describing the tool. The internal project needs a real organisation willing to supply information, and in the UAE that permission can take weeks to obtain. Securing the organisation is itself a calendar task, separate from any writing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is a fifteen-minute assessment combining a presentation and questions, and it is a fifth of the grade. Higher Level adds the HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. Both are internal, both are scheduled by the school, and both reward rehearsal over rewriting — which is also the only legitimate way a class can help with them.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Reading and listening papers move faster than most students expect, and the individual oral is based on a stimulus the school selects. For families who moved to the UAE mid-Diploma, this is often the subject where the previous school's approach differs most, so the first few classes are usually spent mapping the gap rather than teaching new content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution requires a real client, a documented design and working code, and the client relationship takes real calendar time to establish. Higher Level adds the case study published ahead of the session, which is a genuine revision advantage: it is one piece of the paper that can be prepared early with certainty.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: The fieldwork write-up depends on data the school's trip generates, so the date is fixed by the trip, not by the student. Higher Level adds the core extension paper. Classes are most useful immediately after fieldwork, while the data is fresh and the methodology can still be defended in writing.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The historical investigation is a short, tightly structured piece with a source-evaluation section that carries disproportionate marks for its length. Higher Level adds a regional options paper. Students who choose a question with no accessible sources lose weeks, and that loss is only visible once the first draft stalls.

ib-classes.regionsTitle: The seven emirates, and what changes about the calendar in each
ib-classes.regionsIntro: The IB Diploma exam calendar is federal in the sense that the session is the same everywhere, but the surrounding calendar is not. The regulator differs by emirate, the school year start can differ, and the practical question of when a class can begin on a weekday differs a great deal.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai is also where the IB is most concentrated, with the IB accounting for around seven per cent of a private sector of 227 schools in 2024-25. Weekday classes usually start from 16:30 once the school run is clear.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Island and mainland commutes differ by close to an hour in the afternoon, so Diploma families on the islands more often take the later evening slot and keep the earlier one for a sibling in MYP.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with fewer IB schools than the capital, which makes a Higher Level specialist harder to find locally and online delivery the practical answer. Summer heat pushes activity later into the evening, and the revision block before the May session usually settles around a 19:00 start.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — so more than inspection sits with SPEA. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai for work, which pushes the realistic class start later than a Dubai-resident family needs.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. The IB footprint is small, so families frequently sit outside the nearest IB school's catchment and plan around a school day that ends earlier than in Dubai, which opens up a genuinely useful late-afternoon slot.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by its own Department of Knowledge, which, like SPEA, approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. The emirate appears in almost no national tutoring content, and distance from Dubai makes any travelling-tutor arrangement expensive in time before it is expensive in money.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, with a short list of international schools and a long drive to the next one. For a Diploma subject at Higher Level, the local pool is the binding constraint rather than the budget, which is why online IB classes are the normal arrangement here rather than the fallback.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, and the one where a specific subject-and-level combination is least likely to be covered nearby. Families here tend to plan the whole two-year countdown online from the start rather than switching to it mid-course.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB schools sit mostly along the Sheikh Zayed Road corridor and in the southern communities, and their internal coursework calendars vary by several weeks. Students we support attend schools of this kind; the first question in a trial lesson is always which internal deadlines their own school has set, because that is the calendar the plan has to obey.

In ADEK territory the inspection framework and the reporting language differ from Dubai's, and so does the rhythm of internal assessment deadlines. Students we support attend schools in this cluster, and the capital's island-to-mainland commute is a real factor in choosing a weekday class time during the revision block.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi the IB is thinner on the ground and a single school may be the only one offering a given Higher Level subject for some distance. Students we support attend schools in these emirates, where the shortage of local specialists is the practical reason a family plans the countdown online.
schools: American School of Creative Science Sharjah

ib-classes.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the UAE IB landscape only; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and IB Gram is independent of all of them.
ib-classes.modesIntro: Three ways of working, chosen by where you are in the countdown rather than by preference. A family twenty months out needs something different from a family nine weeks out, and paying for the wrong one is the commonest waste in this market.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, pinned to the school's own calendar
modes.description: One hour or ninety minutes a week per subject, live online with one tutor and one student, booked at the same slot each week so it survives the school term. The plan starts from your child's school deadlines rather than a generic syllabus order, which means the week before an internal deadline looks different from an ordinary week.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time
Session order follows the school's internal deadlines, not a textbook
A short written note after each lesson saying what was covered and what is next
Pauses available for school exam weeks and family travel

modes.title: A counted revision block before the session
modes.description: A fixed number of hours across a fixed number of weeks, agreed in advance and mapped to papers rather than to topics. This is the format for a family that starts late: it names what will not be covered, which is more useful than pretending everything can be. The IB revision block is planned backwards from the first paper in that subject.
bullets: Hours per subject per week agreed before the block starts
Past-paper work under timed conditions from the official board materials
A written list of what the block deliberately leaves out
A mid-block review that can reallocate hours between subjects

modes.title: Coursework supervision windows
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions around the Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge deadlines, spaced so that the student does the work between them. The tutor reads, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. No part of an assessed task is ever produced for the student, and that boundary is stated to the family before the first session.

Feedback against the criteria letters the subject guide actually uses
Spacing that leaves the student time to revise their own draft
A record of what was discussed, which the student can show their supervisor

sections.heading: What a parent is actually asking when they search for IB classes in the UAE
paragraphs: IB classes in the UAE, in the sense parents mean, are scheduled one-to-one teaching in a named IB subject at a named level, timed against a specific exam session. The useful question is never whether classes help in general. It is which weeks are left, what those weeks are capable of changing, and whose deadline comes first. That is why this page is organised as a countdown rather than as a list of services.

The table below is the master version. It has four columns because four things need to be true of every window: you need to know how far out you are, what the window exists to do, what should be finished by the end of it, and who owns the deadline. The owner column is the one families find most useful, because it tells you who to email. A school deadline is a conversation with a coordinator. A board deadline is a form with a date on it. A Ministry deadline is a process you start yourself.

Read the table from the top if your child is in the first Diploma year and from the bottom if the papers are close. Neither direction is wrong. What does not work is treating all of it as one undifferentiated pile of work to be got through, because the earliest windows are the cheap ones. Hours spent at twenty months out are worth several hours spent at eight weeks out, not because effort compounds mysteriously but because at twenty months the choices are still reversible.

One caution before the dates. Cambridge and Pearson publish their series dates openly and this page quotes them with the source named. The IB publishes its own session windows on ibo.org, and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, so none is printed here. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the session dates in writing and treat that as the fixed point everything else hangs from.

sections.heading: Twenty-four months out: the choice that is cheap now and expensive later
paragraphs: The single most consequential decision in the whole Diploma is made before any teaching happens: which six subjects, which three at Higher Level, and for mathematics, which of the two routes. It is made in a week when nobody is thinking about exams, usually on the strength of a conversation about what a child enjoys. Enjoyment is a reasonable input. It is not the only one, and the other inputs are mostly about the destination rather than the starting point.

The maths decision deserves its own table because it is the one that most often has to be reversed, and reversing it is expensive. Analysis and Approaches is the more proof-and-algebra route; Applications and Interpretation leans on statistics, modelling and the deliberate use of technology. Both carry an exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade and both add a third paper at Higher Level. Neither is the easy one, which is the premise most families start from and the one that causes the trouble.

What should drive the choice is the course your child may want at university, and the only reliable source for that is the published entry requirement of the specific programme at the specific institution. Engineering, physics and many economics degrees commonly ask for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level; some do not. Read the prospectus of the actual programme rather than a summary of what universities generally want, and do it in the first Diploma year while a change is still administratively possible.

If the choice has already been made and looks wrong, there is usually a switch window in the first term of the first Diploma year, set by the school rather than by the IB. That window is the thing to ask about immediately, not at the end of the year. After it closes, the realistic response is not a change of course but a change of plan: more hours on the specific papers that route sets, and a frank look at whether Higher Level remains the right level in that one subject.

sections.heading: Eighteen months out: the Internal Assessment windows nobody writes down
paragraphs: Internal Assessment is where the Diploma quietly front-loads itself. In most subjects it is worth around a fifth of the final grade, it is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and its real deadline is not the submission date but the date by which the student must have something to write about. A physics investigation needs data that works. An economics commentary needs an article from the right unit. A geography write-up needs the fieldwork to have happened. None of those can be conjured in the final term.

The table below lists the internal components UAE families ask about most, with the criteria and the published limits attached. Treat the figures as the shape of the task and confirm the exact current detail against the subject guide your child's school holds, because guides are revised and the school's copy is the one the moderator will use. The column that matters most is the last one: what a class is allowed to do. The honest answer is narrow, and saying so is the point.

The commonest failure in this window is not laziness. It is a research question that cannot produce a conclusion — too broad, too dependent on data that does not exist, or too close to a textbook result for any personal engagement to show. That failure is invisible until a draft stalls, by which time weeks have gone. A single feasibility conversation at the topic stage costs one hour and saves a month, which makes it the best-value hour in the entire two years.

Diary the internal deadlines yourself, in one place, with the school's dates rather than the IB's. Ask the coordinator in September of the first Diploma year for every internal submission date across all six subjects, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge milestones. Schools set these independently and they cluster: three subjects can land in the same fortnight. Seeing that clash six months early is the difference between a hard fortnight and a lost one.

sections.heading: Twelve months out: entries, registration and the deadline that cannot move
paragraphs: This is the window where the calendar stops being advisory. Exam entries are submitted by the school to the board, to a published date, and after that date the options narrow sharply and get more expensive. Families almost never see this deadline because it is handled between the school and the board. You should still know when it falls, because a subject dropped or a level changed after entries have gone is a different and harder conversation.

Cambridge gives the clearest picture of how far ahead an entry deadline sits, once you know which series applies. In the UAE that is the June series and the November series; the February window that search results sometimes surface is offered to India only, and the Checkpoint tests in March, May and October belong to Primary and Lower Secondary rather than to IGCSE. For the June series the sequence runs entries in the spring, papers across May and June on a zone-specific timetable, forecast grades submitted by the centre shortly before the papers, and results released on Cambridge Direct in August with certificates following. Cambridge sets the exact dates per series and publishes them to centres on cambridgeinternational.org, which is why the number that matters to you comes from the school and not from this page. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026.

There is a Cambridge detail worth more than it looks. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone it sits in and get the zone-specific timetable, not the generic one circulating in a parents' group. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so link the live official timetable rather than relying on a date someone copied out.

For the IB itself, the registration mechanics mirror this pattern — entries are made by the school well before the session, and candidate registration, subject levels and any private-candidate arrangement are settled months ahead. The exact dates must come from your coordinator or from the IB's own assessment pages, because the IB's published windows were not verifiable for this page. Get them in writing, put them in the same document as the Cambridge and Pearson dates if your child sits more than one board, and work backwards from the earliest one.

sections.heading: Nine months out: mocks, and reading the result instead of reacting to it
paragraphs: Mocks exist to produce information, and most families extract about a tenth of what is available. The grade is the least useful part. What matters is the distribution of lost marks: which paper, which command term, which topic, and whether marks were lost because the content was not known or because the paper was not finished. Those four causes need four different responses, and only one of them is solved by more teaching of more content.

Ask the school for the mark breakdown per paper, not just the overall grade, and if possible for the script itself. A Higher Level science candidate who drops twelve marks across data-analysis questions and two marks across recall questions does not have a knowledge problem. A candidate who finishes two questions short on every paper has a timing problem, and timing is trainable in a few weeks. Conflating the two is how a family spends four months on the wrong thing.

Mock season is also the honest moment to revisit the Higher Level question. If one Higher Level subject is consistently several grades below the other two and the cause is content depth rather than technique, the conversation about moving that subject to Standard Level is a legitimate one, and it has a deadline attached that the school sets. It is an uncomfortable conversation, and it is cheaper in January than in March.

This is also where a plan should get written down. After mocks there are roughly nine months to the session, enough for genuine repair work, and little enough that the hours need allocating rather than assuming. A plan at this point names the two subjects getting the most hours, the component in each where the marks are being lost, and the date of the next honest measurement. Without that last item, the next real data point is the exam itself, which is too late to act on.
bullets: Ask for marks per paper and per question type, not the overall grade

sections.heading: Six months out: Ramadan, Eid and where the revision block actually lands
paragraphs: Any revision plan built for a UAE family has to survive Ramadan, and most generic plans do not. School hours shorten, the shape of the day inverts, and the useful hours for concentrated academic work move to the late evening after Iftar or to the hour before Suhoor for students who prefer that. Treating this as an interruption to be endured is the wrong frame. It is a known feature of the calendar, it recurs annually, and it can be planned for twelve months ahead.

The practical approach is to decide in advance which weeks are reduced and to protect the weeks either side rather than attempting to run a normal schedule through the middle. A Diploma student can hold a reduced load of shorter, later sessions through Ramadan, then return to full length immediately afterwards. Eid holidays then create a short block of completely free days, which is unusually good for past-paper work under timed conditions because there is no school day either side of it.

The school calendar has its own collisions in this window. Internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and for most Internal Assessments tend to cluster here, and in some years they land within days of each other and of a school exam week. Mapping the school calendar, the Ramadan window and the internal deadlines onto one page in September is a thirty-minute job that changes which weeks are realistically available for revision.

Scheduling itself is a smaller problem than it looks, because lessons are online. A post-Iftar slot that would be impossible for a travelling arrangement — the roads at that hour decide it — is straightforward over live video, and so is the reverse shift afterwards. The thing worth agreeing explicitly is who may change the slot and with how much notice, so the plan does not quietly dissolve over a month of ad hoc rescheduling.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks out: a revision block counted in hours, not in good intentions
paragraphs: Twelve weeks before the first paper, the work changes character. New content stops being the priority; retrieval, timing and paper technique take over. The useful unit of planning becomes hours per subject per week, agreed in advance and written down, because the instinct at this stage is to spread attention evenly across six subjects and that is almost always wrong. Marks are concentrated in a few components, and so should the hours be.

The table below is a template rather than a prescription, and the numbers assume a student carrying three Higher Level subjects alongside school. What makes it work is the fourth column. Every revision plan at this stage is a decision about what to abandon, and stating that explicitly — this topic will not be revised, this paper gets one timed attempt rather than three — is what keeps the plan from collapsing in week four under its own ambition.

Past papers are the engine of this block, and they come from the board, not from a tutor's private collection. Use the official materials your school holds or supplies; nobody should be sending you copies of syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and a provider offering a downloadable library of them is telling you something about how it operates. Classes work best when the student has already attempted the paper cold and timed, and the hour is spent on the marks that went missing.

Hold one review point in the middle. At six weeks out, re-measure with a full timed paper in the two weakest subjects and reallocate hours accordingly. The reallocation is the whole value of the review: a plan that cannot move hours between subjects after new evidence is a schedule, not a plan, and the evidence at six weeks is far better than the evidence at twelve.

sections.heading: The final fortnight, and the three things that still move a grade
paragraphs: In the last two weeks, almost nothing about what a student knows will change. What can still change is how much of that knowledge reaches the paper, and there are three levers. The first is timing: finishing the paper. A student who routinely leaves a question blank is losing marks that require no new learning to recover, and two weeks of deliberate timing practice recovers most of them. This is the highest-return work available at this point.

The second is question selection and command terms. Papers that offer a choice reward a fast, accurate decision about which question the student can actually answer well, and that decision is a trainable skill separate from the content. Command terms are the same story: a student who writes an explanation where the paper asked for an evaluation has demonstrated knowledge and still lost the marks. Both are fixable in a fortnight because neither requires new content.

The third is the administrative fortnight itself — the part nobody plans. Confirm the zone-specific timetable, confirm the start times, confirm what equipment is permitted, confirm the calculator model is allowed, and check the sequence of papers so that a two-paper day is not a surprise. Cambridge is explicit that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's problem, which is an unusually high price for a clerical error.

What should stop in this window is as important. New material stops. New resources stop. Comparisons with other students stop. Sleep becomes a performance variable rather than a luxury. A class in the final fortnight that introduces a new topic is doing harm, however well intentioned, and a plan that still has new content in it at this stage was mis-scheduled somewhere around week nine.
bullets: Rehearse finishing the paper, not just answering it

sections.heading: Results day, enquiries and the November session decision
paragraphs: Results day has its own short calendar, and it moves faster than families expect. Grades arrive, and within a tight published window there are decisions to make about whether to query anything. Boards run a formal process for this — Cambridge releases results on Direct to centres before certificates follow, and an enquiry about a result is raised through the school rather than by a parent directly. The window is short enough that the decision has to be prepared before the grades arrive, not after.

An enquiry is worth raising when there is a specific reason to think a mark is wrong: a grade far below every mock and every predicted grade, a component result that contradicts the pattern of the others, or a known problem during the exam itself that was reported at the time. It is not a general appeal against a disappointing outcome, and a remark can move a grade down as well as up. Ask the school what the process costs, what the deadline is, and what evidence they think supports it.

The retake question is the other decision, and it is genuinely a calendar question. A November session exists, and for a UAE student it usually means a focused few months on one or two subjects rather than a repeat of the whole Diploma. Weigh it against what the university offer actually requires: some offers can be deferred, some cannot, and the answer changes the value of a retake completely. Get the offer condition in writing before deciding anything.

If a retake is the plan, the countdown restarts immediately and it is short. The useful shape is a diagnostic in the first week to identify exactly which components lost the marks, a block of timed paper work through the middle, and a re-entry handled by the school to the board's published deadline. The one thing that does not work is waiting until the new academic year starts to begin, because by then a third of the available weeks have gone.

sections.heading: The deadline nobody counts backwards from: Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: There is one more date, and it sits outside the exam calendar entirely. A UAE secondary certificate equivalency from the Ministry of Education is what converts an international school leaving qualification into something UAE institutions and employers recognise. Families discover it late — often in the summer after results, when everyone wants the same document at the same time — and the process is administrative, so it rewards starting early and punishes nothing except delay.

For the British track the requirements are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published figure is five, and it is worth checking any claim like that against the authority rather than against a tutoring site.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold printed on this page, because none could be verified on the Ministry's own pages — and an invented number here would be worse than useless, since the whole point of the document is that it is checked.

Treat equivalency as a process you own, not a service someone performs for you. The Ministry sets the rules and the emirate attestation channels handle documents; a tutoring provider has no role in it beyond telling you it exists and when to start. Nothing about it requires tutoring, and any page suggesting that extra classes are needed to obtain equivalency is describing a regulatory process as a sales opportunity.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when a deadline is close
paragraphs: The pressure in this market concentrates at exactly the point where the rules matter most: a fortnight before an Internal Assessment deadline, with a student who has not started. That is when a family is offered a shortcut, and the UAE search results contain providers who sell finished Internal Assessments outright. One of them lists a price for a completed Internal Assessment. That is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers the IB's malpractice process, and the consequence lands on the student, not the seller.

The boundary a legitimate class works inside is narrow and easy to state. A tutor may teach the subject, explain the criteria, challenge a research question, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, ask what a paragraph is for, and hand the draft back for the student to revise. A tutor may not produce any part of an assessed task, supply text for it, or edit it to completion. Every sentence that is submitted has to be the student's own, and the student signs to that effect.

This is not only a rules question; it is also why the earlier windows in this page matter so much. A student who starts the exploration in the spring of the first Diploma year has months of legitimate help available. A student who starts it two weeks before submission has almost none, because the only thing that would rescue the deadline is the thing nobody may do. The calendar, in other words, is also the academic-honesty plan.

Two related points on materials. Nobody should supply you with reproductions of IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides; those belong to the boards and should be referenced and linked, not copied. And a provider describing its tutors as examiners should be asked to evidence current examiner status, because examiner status is often used to imply an access to marking and boundaries that it does not confer.

No part of an assessed task is produced, supplied or edited to completion for a student
Board materials are referenced and linked, never reproduced or handed over as downloads
A provider selling finished coursework is a risk to the student, not a shortcut

sections.heading: What IB classes cost across the UAE market, and how timing changes the bill
paragraphs: Published UAE tutoring rates are scarce, which is itself informative: of the competitor pages examined for this page, several publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The bands below are market rates collected from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and each row names where the figure comes from.

The pattern across the bands is consistent. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject specialist sits well below an in-home visit for the same hour, because the in-home figure contains travel: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, while online qualified-tutor rates start around AED 150 and specialist IB and IGCSE work runs AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Timing is the variable families control and rarely think about. The same subject help costs less per unit of benefit in September than in March, not because rates rise on a schedule but because specialist availability tightens as the session approaches and because late help has to be compressed into fewer, longer sessions. Starting at twenty months out also means fewer total hours are needed, since the expensive work is repair rather than instruction.

IB Gram's own arrangement is deliberately not a price list on this page. Lessons are one-to-one and online, the first trial lesson is free — one per student, arranged before anything is paid for and with no card details taken to book it — and the rate depends on the subject, the level and whether a coursework supervision window is involved. Ask for it against your actual plan, with the hours and the session date in front of you, because a rate per hour without a number of hours attached tells you very little.

sections.heading: Why online delivery is the right fit for a dated plan
paragraphs: Every class described on this page runs live online, one-to-one, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Saying so plainly matters, because several providers in these search results route UAE enquiries to an overseas number without ever stating where the teaching actually happens, which is the trust failure that the honest version avoids.

On a calendar-driven plan the online format is the thing that makes the plan possible. A countdown only works if the right specialist can start in the week the plan says, in the exact subject and at the exact level. A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain looking for a Higher Level chemistry specialist is not choosing between online and local; locally there may be nobody at that level, and the alternative to online is a compromise on specialism. In Dubai the pool is deeper, but the binding constraint becomes the drive at 17:00.

The format also removes the two things that most often break a schedule. Travel time disappears from both sides, so a ninety-minute session costs ninety minutes rather than three hours of someone's evening, and a post-Iftar or late-evening slot during Ramadan is as easy to run as a 16:30 one. Sessions can shift with a school exam week or a family trip without the whole arrangement unravelling, because there is no journey to re-plan.

What online delivery does not do is supervise practical work, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Laboratory apparatus work for the sciences stays at school under the school's supervision. What a class contributes there is the design of the investigation, the treatment of uncertainty, the data analysis and the evaluation — which is where the marks in that component sit anyway, as the criteria make clear.
