process.title: Tell us the session date first
process.description: The opening question is not which subject but which session, and what your child's school has set as its internal deadlines. With those dates, the subjects and the levels, the plan can be built backwards rather than forwards, which is the difference between a schedule and a countdown.

process.title: A free trial lesson, before anything is paid for
process.description: One free trial lesson per student, arranged before any payment and with no card details taken to book it. It is a working lesson, not a sales call: the tutor teaches something real, and you get a short written note of where the gap sits and what the first six weeks would cover.

process.title: A written countdown, with what is excluded
process.description: You receive the plan in writing: hours per subject per week, which components are being targeted, when the next measured check falls, and what the plan deliberately leaves out. The exclusions are the honest part. A plan that claims to cover everything in nine weeks is not a plan.

process.title: Weekly lessons, with a note after each one
process.description: Lessons run at the same slot each week with the same tutor, live online. After each one you get a short note of what was covered and what comes next, so the plan stays visible rather than living in the tutor's head. Slots pause for school exam weeks and travel.

process.title: Re-measure, then reallocate hours
process.description: At the halfway point of any block, and immediately after mocks, the student sits a full timed paper in the weakest subjects and the hours get reallocated on the evidence. A plan that cannot move hours between subjects after new information is not responding to your child; it is just a timetable.

process.title: Results, and whatever comes next
process.description: Before results arrive we agree what would justify an enquiry upon results and who raises it, since that window is short and runs through the school. If a November session retake becomes the plan, the countdown restarts in the first week rather than in the new academic year.

whyPoints.title: The plan is dated, not generic
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from your child's session and your child's school deadlines, including the internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay dates that schools set independently. A plan built on a generic syllabus order ignores the clustering of those dates, which is where most of the avoidable pressure in the Diploma comes from.

whyPoints.title: Rates on this page are attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider or rate table it came from and the month it was collected. Three of the competitor pages examined publish no price at all and two quote in dollars. A number without a source is not information, and a page that shows its working is easier to check.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is stated upfront
whyPoints.description: Help with an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is feedback on work the student has already produced. No part of an assessed task is produced or supplied, and the boundary is explained to the family before the first session rather than discovered during a difficult week.

whyPoints.title: Specialism by subject and level
whyPoints.description: Matching is done on the exact subject and level, which is the whole practical argument for online delivery. A Higher Level physics candidate in Ras Al Khaimah gets a Higher Level physics specialist, rather than the best generalist available within a reasonable drive of the house.

whyPoints.title: The regulator and the rules are explained, not borrowed
whyPoints.description: This page names KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the Ministry of Education because UAE families have to work inside them. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them and claims none; what you get is an explanation of what each one does and where to check it.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not assumed
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a subject and level in the week you need, you are told that in the first conversation, along with when one is expected and what the alternative would be. A page that implies instant availability for every Higher Level subject across seven emirates is not describing a real roster.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the May session should IB classes start?
faqs.answer: The honest answer depends on what you want them to do. To influence subject and level choices, including the maths route, classes need to start around twenty-four months out, in the first Diploma year. To do Internal Assessment work properly, eighteen months. To repair content gaps found in mocks, nine months is enough. To fix timing, question selection and command-term accuracy, twelve weeks works. All four are legitimate starting points; they are different plans with different costs. What does not work is expecting a six-week block to do the twenty-four-month job.

faqs.question: What should a Diploma student have finished by the end of the first year?
faqs.answer: By the end of the first Diploma year a student should have an approved Extended Essay research question and a supervisor allocated, Internal Assessment topics agreed in most subjects, any mathematics exploration data or model identified rather than merely imagined, at least one economics commentary written if they take economics, and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition complete. The exact list is set by your school, not by the IB, so ask the coordinator in September for every internal date across all six subjects. Seeing where three deadlines collide is the single most useful thing on that list.

faqs.question: When is the final entry deadline for Cambridge exams, and who submits it?
faqs.answer: Entries are submitted by the school to the board, not by parents, and they fall months before the papers. In the UAE the series to plan around are Cambridge June and Cambridge November, and for the June series the final entry closes in the spring, with forecast grades submitted by the centre shortly before the papers and results released on Cambridge Direct in August. Cambridge publishes those key dates to centres and revises them series by series, so we will not print a day and month that may already have moved. Pearson runs its own published pattern for International GCSE, with exams available in May/June and November and the November 2026 papers running to 19 November 2026. Ask the school for the exact entry deadline that applies to your child's board and series, and treat it as immovable.

faqs.question: Does the exam timetable depend on which zone our school is in?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, yes. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. So the generic timetable circulating in a parents' group is not reliable for your child. Ask the school which zone it is in, get the zone-specific timetable, and check it again in the final fortnight. Pearson also issues provisional timetables that are later revised, so always work from the live official version.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of IB classes are realistic twelve weeks before the first paper?
faqs.answer: For a student carrying three Higher Level subjects alongside school, around one and a half to two hours a week per priority subject is sustainable twelve weeks out, rising to around two and a half in the four-to-six-week window and dropping back to about an hour in the final fortnight. The number matters less than the allocation. Spreading hours evenly across six subjects is the common mistake, because marks are concentrated in a few components. Decide which two subjects get the most hours, write down what the plan is abandoning, and re-measure at six weeks.

faqs.question: Our child's mock results came back two grades down. What should happen next?
faqs.answer: Get the mark breakdown per paper and per question type before changing anything. Marks go missing for four different reasons: content that was not known, a command term that was misread, a paper that was not finished, and careless accuracy. Each needs a different response, and only the first is solved by more teaching. Timing is usually the fastest to fix and often the largest single loss. Mock season is also the honest point to revisit whether one Higher Level subject should move to Standard Level, and that decision has a school-set deadline attached.

faqs.question: How do we plan revision around Ramadan and Eid?
faqs.answer: Decide in advance which weeks run at a reduced load rather than trying to push a normal schedule through the middle. School hours shorten and useful study time moves to the late evening after Iftar, so shorter and later sessions through that period, with full-length sessions restored immediately afterwards, holds a plan together better than a month of ad hoc rescheduling. The Eid break then gives a short run of free days with no school either side, which is unusually good for timed past papers. Because lessons are online, a post-Iftar slot is as practical as an afternoon one.

faqs.question: What does the last fortnight before a paper actually change?
faqs.answer: Not what a student knows — there is no time for that — but how much of it reaches the page. Three levers still move: finishing the paper, choosing between optional questions quickly and accurately, and answering the command term the paper actually used rather than the one the student hoped for. All three are trainable in two weeks because none needs new content. What should stop is everything else: new material, new resources, late nights. A class that introduces a new topic in the final fortnight is doing harm.

faqs.question: What happens on results day if a grade looks wrong?
faqs.answer: Boards run a formal enquiry process and it is raised through the school, not by a parent directly, inside a short published window. Prepare the decision before results arrive: agree what would justify an enquiry, who raises it and what it costs. A grade far below every mock and predicted grade, or a component result that contradicts the pattern of the others, is a reason. General disappointment is not, and a remark can move a grade down as well as up. Cambridge releases results on Direct before certificates follow in late June, so the clock starts at the Direct release.

faqs.question: Should our child retake in the November session?
faqs.answer: Start with the university offer rather than the grade. Some offers can be deferred and some cannot, and that single fact changes the value of a retake completely, so get the condition in writing before deciding. For a UAE student a November session usually means a focused few months on one or two subjects rather than repeating the Diploma. If it is the plan, the countdown restarts in the first week: a diagnostic to find which components lost the marks, a block of timed paper work, and re-entry handled by the school to the board's published deadline.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the Ministry of Education count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no lower than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One tutoring site currently ranking states that six subjects are required, which is why this is worth checking on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation channel rather than on a tutoring page. No verified IB points threshold is published here, because none could be confirmed on the Ministry's own pages.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment two weeks before it is due?
faqs.answer: Only within a narrow boundary, and that boundary does not widen because the deadline is close. A tutor may explain the criteria, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, point out that a section is not doing what the criterion rewards, and hand the draft back for the student to revise. A tutor may not produce any part of an assessed task, supply text for it, or edit it to completion. Some providers in these search results sell finished Internal Assessments. That triggers the IB's malpractice process, and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: What do IB classes cost per hour in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published market bands, collected October 2026, run roughly like this: budget online tutors from AED 33 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; and premium named tutors above AED 500, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. Ask any provider for a rate against a stated number of hours.

faqs.question: Are these classes delivered online, or does someone come to the house?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In-home tuition does exist in the UAE market and the published rates are higher, because the fee contains travel: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. The practical trade is specialism against proximity. Online, a Higher Level chemistry candidate gets a Higher Level chemistry specialist rather than the nearest available generalist.

faqs.question: How do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies fit into an exam-term timetable?
faqs.answer: They are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires them to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, so they occupy real time in the week alongside the Diploma. KHDA calculates the instructional time in 40-minute lesson units and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. The practical consequence for a plan is simple: count those periods before booking anything after school, because the week is fuller than a Diploma subject list suggests.

faqs.question: Can lessons pause during the exam weeks themselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most students they should. Once papers begin, the useful work is a short daily retrieval routine and timing rehearsal for the next paper, not a full lesson schedule. Agree the pause in advance, including who may change a slot and with how much notice, so the plan does not dissolve through improvised rescheduling. The same applies to school exam weeks earlier in the year and to family travel. Because the format is online, a pause and a restart need no logistics beyond an agreed slot.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level specialist is free in the week we need to start?
faqs.answer: You are told in the first conversation, along with when one is expected to be free and what the alternative is. For niche Higher Level combinations this happens, particularly in the northern emirates where the local pool is thin, and the honest options are to wait a short time for the right specialist, start with a related-subject tutor on general technique, or begin with a shorter block aimed at the component losing the most marks. What we do not do is match a Standard Level generalist to a Higher Level plan and let the calendar reveal it later.

ib-classes.closingHeading: Start by putting a date on it
ib-classes.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the countdown. Find out your child's exam session and the school's own internal deadlines, write them on one sheet with the Ramadan window beside them, and see which weeks are actually free. Most families discover one collision they can still move and one deadline they had not counted at all. Then book a free trial lesson — one per student, arranged before anything is paid for — and bring that sheet to it. The tutor's job in the first hour is to tell you what those remaining weeks can realistically change, and to say plainly what they cannot.

ib-coaching.tutorsIntro: The coaches below are IB subject specialists rather than general tutors. Each teaches to one named subject guide at one named level, so a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level booking goes to someone who marks Paper 3 practice every week. Availability moves week to week, and the free trial lesson is where you test the match.

intro.heading: What a dirham of IB coaching actually buys
paragraphs: Of the six pages ranking for this search when the SERP was measured in October 2026, three published no price at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars, a currency no family in the UAE pays its school fees in. That is the gap this page fills. Below are the AED bands the market charges, the hour blocks a Diploma component tends to absorb, and the arithmetic that turns those two numbers into a figure you can actually approve.

Price here is less a mystery than a spread. A university student coaching a Standard Level subject online and a subject specialist coaching Higher Level Chemistry are both described as tutors, and the gap between their rates is roughly threefold. Published UAE rates run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 an hour for a premium named coach. Working out which band your child's actual problem sits in is worth more than any discount you will be offered.

The second number most families skip is hours. A rate without an hour count is not a price. Six hours of Internal Assessment supervision and sixty hours of weekly Higher Level coaching are the same service at the same rate and ten times the bill, and the difference between them is entirely a question of what is wrong. A child who has missed one topic needs a short, bounded block. A child who has been guessing at Paper 2 for a year needs a term.

What you are buying first, then, is a diagnosis: which topic, which paper, which criterion, and how many marks sit there. That is why IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson rather than a package. The trial is a real teaching hour on a real piece of your child's work, and it ends with an hour count. If the honest answer is four hours rather than forty, you should hear that before any money moves.

Delivery is worth stating plainly before the numbers. All IB coaching in the UAE that IB Gram arranges is delivered live online, one to one, over video, in Gulf Standard Time evening slots that fit after the school run and around prayer times. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India. In the UAE the online format is also the reason a family in Fujairah or Ajman can book the same Higher Level specialist as a family in Jumeirah, instead of choosing from whoever is willing to drive.

One more thing this page will not do is invent a price list. IB Gram's own rate depends on subject, level and how many hours the diagnosis calls for, and quoting a single number would be a fiction. Every AED figure below is a market figure published by somebody else, labelled as such, with the model of provider that charges it. Use them to judge any quote you receive, including ours.

ib-coaching.programmesIntro: IB coaching means something different in each of the four programmes, and so does the bill. A Primary Years parent is usually buying reading and number fluency. A Diploma parent in the exam year is buying paper technique at a specialist rate. These are the four programmes UAE schools run, with what coaching tends to cost and achieve in each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units rather than separate subjects, with no external examination and no published grade. Coaching at this stage is almost never about the IB framework itself. It is about reading fluency, number facts, written structure and the habit of finishing work. Hour blocks are short and the budget band is the lowest of the four programmes, because a general primary specialist can do this well.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE a PYP parent also meets the Ministry subjects early. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools from the start, taught in separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs under the KHDA mandatory subjects guidance. Families who budget for English and maths support and nothing else are often surprised by an Arabic report in Year 4.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria, with a Personal Project in the final year and optional eAssessment. The criteria are where marks are won and lost, and most students have never had them explained. Coaching here is cheap relative to the Diploma and unusually effective, because fixing how a student reads a criterion transfers across every subject at once.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools run MYP to Year 11 while the school down the road runs IGCSE, so families moving house inside Dubai or between emirates can change assessment systems mid-stream. A transfer from criterion-based MYP marking to graded IGCSE papers, or the reverse, usually needs a bounded block of coaching on assessment style rather than content, and it is worth buying in the term before the move rather than after the first report.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, scored out of 45. This is where almost all UAE coaching spend sits, and where the rate is highest because the pool of people who can teach Higher Level content and mark to a current subject guide is genuinely small. IB Diploma Programme coaching is best bought as named hour blocks against named components.
programmes.countryNote: The UAE Diploma year runs on a Gulf timetable: the May session is the one UAE schools sit, the school day ends early enough for a 4pm start, and the exam term overlaps Ramadan in some years. Families here also carry a second deadline the IB does not set, because a Ministry of Education equivalency file has to be assembled for a UAE university application, and the paperwork is easier to gather in DP1 than in July of DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller framework combining two or more DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Coaching demand is concentrated on the DP courses inside it and on the reflective project, which is marked against its own criteria. Hour counts are lower than a full Diploma and the budget behaves more like a two-subject plan.
programmes.countryNote: Few UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme, so a family considering it is usually choosing between two or three schools across an emirate rather than a dozen. The recognition question matters more here than for the Diploma: check the Ministry of Education equivalency position and the specific university's own entry page before committing, and ask the school to put its own recognition advice in writing.

ib-coaching.subjectsIntro: Rate follows scarcity, not difficulty. The subjects below are the ones UAE families book most, with what the assessment actually demands and why some of them cost more per hour than others. Where a subject has a Higher Level that adds whole topics rather than depth, the hour block is bigger and the coach pool is smaller.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with Paper 3 at Higher Level built from an extended unseen investigation. Higher Level sits at the top of the rate band because the people who can teach Paper 3 technique and mark it honestly are few. Most of the loss is method marks and unjustified steps rather than arithmetic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with a heavier graphical display calculator load. Cheaper to coach at Standard Level than Analysis and Approaches because content is broader and shallower, but Higher Level statistics catches students who chose the course expecting an easier ride. The exploration carries the same weight either way.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields and the Higher Level extension topics, plus the scientific investigation. Marks leak in uncertainty treatment, in explaining rather than describing, and in Paper 2 extended response. A physics coach who can also handle the maths behind it saves a family a second booking, which is the only real discount available here.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure, reactivity, organic mechanisms and energetics. A Higher Level Chemistry coach is the hardest booking in the UAE market and prices accordingly, partly because the organic and mechanism content is unforgiving and partly because so many Diploma medics take it. Six to ten coached hours on mechanisms is a common, bounded request.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than conceptual difficulty, and the data-based paper rewards reading skill over recall. Coaching is often better spent on command terms and on the scientific investigation than on re-teaching topics. That makes it one of the cheaper Higher Level sciences to support properly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation and the three internal assessment commentaries built from published news articles. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper. The commentaries are where the marks are cheapest to recover, because most students lose them on article choice and theory linkage rather than on writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, theories and the research project, with case-study analysis under time pressure. Coaching demand in the UAE is seasonal and clusters around the project, so a short block in DP1 term three is usually better value than a year-long weekly booking at the same rate.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and the Higher Level essay. Students arrive fluent and still lose marks for not answering the question asked. This is a subject where four or five coached hours on Paper 1 method moves more than a term of general essay practice.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, systems, and a solution developed and documented by the student. Coach scarcity, not content, drives the rate: few UAE schools have more than one specialist, and online booking is often the only way to reach one who knows the current subject guide.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking in Arabic as an acquired language, with themes set by the subject guide. UAE families frequently need this alongside the Ministry subject requirement rather than instead of it, and the two have different expectations, teachers and reports. Ask which one the low grade actually came from before booking.

ib-coaching.regionsIntro: Coaching rates do not change much between emirates, but availability, school density and the regulator do. Below is what each emirate means for a family buying IB coaching, including the three emirates no competitor page in this market mentions at all.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, with 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula. The deepest coach pool in the country and the one place where an in-home visit is genuinely purchasable, which is why rates here set the national reference band.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Fewer IB schools than Dubai and a wider geography, so the travel component of any visiting rate is larger. ADEK also applies professional-ethics rules to school staff who tutor privately.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai schools, so a 4pm session start is realistic only if the coaching is online.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller Diploma cohort than the Abu Dhabi coast. Higher Level specialists in sciences and economics are the scarce commodity rather than the price, which is the specific problem online delivery solves for Al Ain households.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here fall under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Coach supply inside the emirate is thin, so families routinely pay a Dubai rate plus a long drive, or book online and pay neither.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. A northern-emirates family searching for IB coaching locally will usually find general tutors rather than subject-guide specialists.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, two hours from the Dubai coach pool in traffic. Online one-to-one is not a compromise here; it is the only way to reach a current Diploma specialist at a weekday evening hour.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country and another Ministry of Education emirate. Families here are frequently told no local IB coach exists, which is true and also irrelevant once the format is live video rather than a car journey.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB cohort is concentrated in a handful of large schools, and 2026-27 adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Coaching demand in this cluster peaks in DP1 term three, when the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines land in the same six weeks.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: The ADEK cluster is smaller and more spread out, and subject coverage inside one school is thinner, so a student taking an unusual Higher Level combination may be the only candidate in their year group. That is the case where an online specialist is the difference between support and no support.

sections.heading: Five things sold as IB coaching in the UAE
paragraphs: The word coaching is attached to at least five different products in this market, at prices that differ by a factor of ten. Before comparing quotes, work out which of the five you are actually being sold, because a group revision class and a specialist one-to-one hour are not expensive and cheap versions of the same thing. They solve different problems and fail in different ways.

One-to-one subject coaching is the product most parents picture: a specialist takes one syllabus at one level and works through a diagnosed list of gaps. Published UAE agency rates for this start around AED 150 an hour for IGCSE and AED 200 an hour for IB, and a specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 and above is widely quoted. It is the most expensive per hour and usually the cheapest per mark recovered, because nothing in the hour is spent on another child's problem.

A group revision class is the opposite trade. At the budget end of the UAE market, online group rates have been published from about AED 45 to AED 65 an hour per student, and another platform advertises from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. A good class walks a cohort through a syllabus once. It cannot find out that your child is losing Paper 2 marks on command terms, because finding that out requires looking at your child's script.

Monthly packages and coursework supervision are the two products where families most often overpay. A published UAE example is AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and in-home packages of four two-hour visits have been advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month. Packages are good value when the need is steady and bad value when a coursework deadline moves, which in the Diploma it reliably does. The fifth product, assessed work sold ready-written, is not coaching at all and is dealt with further down this page.

sections.heading: The arithmetic to run before you book a single hour
paragraphs: A rate is not a price. The price is hours multiplied by rate, and the hour count is the number nobody publishes, because it is the number that varies by child. Any provider can tell you their hourly figure. A provider worth buying from will tell you, after looking at a script, roughly how many hours the problem in front of them needs, and will put the estimate in writing.

The table below does the multiplication at three points across the published UAE market: AED 180 an hour sits near the low end of qualified online support, AED 250 an hour near the middle of the specialist band, and AED 400 an hour towards the premium end. The plans are the ones families in the UAE actually ask for, from a single term of weekly support to a two-Higher-Level year. Nothing in it is an IB Gram price; it is the market arithmetic you should run against any quote, including ours.

Two patterns fall out of it immediately. First, a bounded component block is cheap. Eight hours of Internal Assessment supervision costs between AED 1,440 and AED 3,200 depending on the band you buy in, which is roughly one month of a weekly package and recovers marks in a component worth a fifth or more of the subject grade. Second, two Higher Levels taken weekly for a full year is a five-figure commitment at any sensible rate, and deserves to be treated like one rather than drifted into a session at a time.

The honest planning move is to buy the diagnosis first, then the smallest block that addresses what the diagnosis found, then decide. Families who start with the year-long booking tend to discover in February that the hours went on the wrong subject. Families who start with eight hours on the component that was actually failing usually need fewer hours in total.

sections.heading: Retainer, block or pay-as-you-go: how the commitment changes the price
paragraphs: How you buy changes what you pay more than which provider you choose. The three commitment models in this market are a monthly retainer, a pre-paid block of hours, and pay-as-you-go. Each is priced on a different risk. A retainer prices the provider's certainty of income, a block prices your certainty of delivery, and pay-as-you-go prices your freedom to stop.

Retainers are advertised in the UAE at round monthly numbers, with eight online sessions a month a common shape. They suit a steady, year-long need in one subject and they are the worst fit for the Diploma calendar, which is not steady at all. A Diploma student needs almost nothing in DP1 term one, a great deal in DP1 term three when coursework lands, and something different again in the eight weeks before papers. A flat monthly commitment pays for the quiet months at the same rate as the loud ones.

Pre-paid blocks behave better against that calendar if the block is tied to a component rather than a period. Ten hours bought against the mathematics exploration, or eight against the scientific investigation, expire when the component does and cannot quietly roll into a subscription. Ask two questions before paying for any block: what happens to unused hours, and whether the hours can move to a different subject if the diagnosis changes. A provider who refuses both is selling certainty of income, not coaching.

Pay-as-you-go costs slightly more per hour in most price lists and is almost always the right way to start. It lets the first four hours function as an extended diagnosis, after which you know whether you are buying a term or a block. IB Gram works this way by default: a free trial lesson, then hours as needed, with the pattern chosen once there is evidence to choose on.

sections.heading: IB coaching beside the school fee: the cost in context
paragraphs: A coaching budget looks different once it sits next to the school fee rather than on its own. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a Dubai family, that means the school line in next year's budget is known and flat, and any new education spend is a decision rather than an adjustment.

Against that, published UAE estimates for weekly one-hour sessions sit at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month for budget support, AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month in the middle of the market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above a month for specialist exam-year coaching. Those are monthly figures for one subject at one hour a week. Two subjects double them, and an exam-term intensive is a short spike on top rather than a replacement.

The line families most often miss is the one that is not tuition at all. A private-candidate exam entry, a remark request, a Ministry of Education equivalency file and attestation steps all carry their own costs and their own deadlines, and none of them is paid to a coach. Putting them in the same table as the coaching spend is the only way to see the real education budget for the year, and it tends to change which hours get bought.

The arithmetic that matters is not whether coaching is expensive in the abstract. It is what proportion of a flat, already-committed school fee you are prepared to add in order to defend the grade that fee is paying for. Many UAE families find the answer is a bounded number of specialist hours in the right term, rather than a general weekly booking across two years.

sections.heading: The travel line nobody puts on the invoice
paragraphs: Parents searching for a coach in the UAE usually picture someone sitting at the dining table. It is a reasonable thing to want, and the UAE market does sell it: published in-home one-to-one rates run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 450 for specialist support delivered online. The gap between those two bands is not profit. It is travel, and travel is the most expensive ingredient in the service.

Count what the drive actually costs. A coach crossing Dubai at 4.30pm, or coming down from Abu Dhabi city to a Khalifa City villa, spends twenty to sixty minutes each way. That time is inside the hourly rate whether or not it appears on the invoice, and it sets a floor on the booking length, which is why visiting coaches often ask for two hours rather than one. It also shrinks the pool to people willing to make that journey, which is the part that costs the student rather than the parent.

That last point is the one worth sitting with. A family in Dubai Marina who insists on a visit is choosing from Higher Level specialists willing to drive to Dubai Marina on a weekday evening. A family in Fujairah is choosing from almost nobody. Online, both are choosing from whoever is the right match for the subject guide and the level, at an hour that suits the Gulf school night. For a scarce booking like a Higher Level Chemistry coach, that is the whole difference between the right coach and an available one.

This is why IB coaching in the UAE through IB Gram is delivered live online, one to one, over video, and why we say so before the price rather than after it. Home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India, not here. The comparison below is the honest case for the format, laid out as a cost ledger rather than a sales argument.

sections.heading: How many coached hours a Diploma component absorbs
paragraphs: This is the table the market does not publish, because publishing it makes the bill predictable. The figures below are planning blocks that UAE families commonly ask for and that coaches commonly agree to, not measured averages and not a forecast of anybody's result. Treat them as the opening position in a conversation with whoever looks at your child's work, and expect the number to move once a real script is on the screen.

Component by component, the shape is consistent. Coursework blocks are small and front-loaded, because the marks are won at the design stage. A scientific investigation costs six to ten hours when the research question, the variables and the uncertainty treatment are addressed before data collection, and twenty when the student arrives in DP2 with results that cannot answer the question they asked. The mathematics exploration behaves the same way: the choice of topic determines most of the available marks.

Paper technique blocks are larger and sit late. Unseen data work, command-term discipline and timing improve through marked practice rather than explanation, so hours here are spent sitting papers, marking them against the published scheme and reworking the weak responses. Eight to sixteen hours across the final two terms is a common request, concentrated in the last eight weeks rather than spread thin.

Content catch-up is the most variable line and the one to diagnose hardest. One missed Higher Level topic is six to twelve hours. A year of guessing is not a block at all; it is a term of weekly coaching, and a provider who quotes it as a block is guessing too. The point of the free trial lesson is to tell these two cases apart before the money is committed.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years, read as a spending plan
paragraphs: Coaching money buys different things at different points in the two years, and the same hour is worth more in September than in April. The fixed points are not set by the coach: they are set by the school, the board and the Ministry. Reading them in order, backwards from the papers, is how a family decides when to spend rather than how much.

The entry deadlines are the clearest illustration of how early the real calendar starts, and in the UAE there are only two Cambridge series to build around: June and November. June is the main sitting and November is the resit route, which makes the autumn of the exam year a decision point rather than a quiet term. Cambridge closes final entries for the June series in the spring, a term or so before the first paper, publishes the exact dates to centres, and has the centre submit forecast grades shortly before the papers, with results reaching centres in August. We do not reprint those days here, because Cambridge revises them series by series and the school holds the current ones. Pearson's International GCSE sits in May or June and November series, with the November 2026 papers running to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the gap worth noting if a November retake has to serve a January application. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used.

For the IB itself, the May session is the one UAE schools sit, and this page deliberately publishes no IB session or results date. The IB's own calendar is the only authority worth relying on, so confirm every Diploma date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around it. What is safe to say is the shape: internal school deadlines for coursework sit months ahead of the IB's own upload dates, and those internal deadlines are the ones that should drive a coursework block.

The spending consequence is simple. Hours bought early go on choices and coursework design, which are cheap to influence and expensive to fix. Hours bought late go on technique and timing, which is the only thing that still moves in the last month. Hours bought in the wrong order get spent twice.

sections.heading: Who may legally coach in the UAE, and what the permit costs
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, and the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone presenting a licensing fee as a line on your invoice is charging you for something the state issues at no cost.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. The permit is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted as unverified.

Two conditions matter more than the permit itself. The first is the code of conduct attached to it, which bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school; in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK text before relying on it. The second is that a permit is a statement about legality, not about subject depth. A permitted university student and a permitted Higher Level Chemistry specialist hold the same document.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind and does not describe itself as having one; it is an independent matching platform delivering live online lessons, and the regulator facts above are published so that you can check any provider, including us, against the authority's own page.

sections.heading: What a coach may not touch, and why that protects your spend
paragraphs: There is a market in this SERP selling finished Internal Assessments and essays for four-figure sums. It should be understood as the most expensive product on sale, because the price carries a risk the invoice does not mention: assessed work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the candidate, not the supplier. No amount of coaching value is worth a withdrawn Diploma.

The boundary is workable and worth stating in plain terms. A coach may teach the skills a component needs, explain the criteria and what each one is asking for, discuss a proposed research question, ask hard questions about method, read a student's own draft and say which criterion is losing marks and why, and model technique on a different example. Every sentence of the submitted text comes from the student. Where a school supervisor is involved, the coach works behind them rather than in place of them, and the school's own deadlines take precedence over ours.

What that rules out is specific. A coach does not supply text for insertion, does not restructure a draft on the student's behalf, does not choose the research question, does not provide data, and does not polish a document into a submittable state. Feedback is given as questions and criterion references, so the revision is the student's work and so the school can see a trail of the student's own thinking. Where the IB requires an authenticity declaration, that trail is what makes it true.

This matters to the budget as well as to the ethics. Supervision bought as process coaching early is cheap, bounded and effective, because it changes the design decisions that carry the marks. Supervision bought as rescue three days before an internal deadline is expensive, limited and tempting in the wrong direction. Buy the hours in DP1 term three, and the question of who authored the document never comes up.
bullets: Taught: the criteria, the technique, the method, the command terms
Discussed: a research question the student has proposed, and its feasibility
Given: criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own draft, as questions
Never supplied: text, structure, data or a finished document of any kind
Respected: the school supervisor's role and the school's internal deadlines

sections.heading: The Ministry subjects and the equivalency file: two bills families forget
paragraphs: Two UAE-specific lines turn up in education budgets late, and both are avoidable with a term's notice. The first is the Ministry subjects that run alongside the IB. In Dubai private schools, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the KHDA mandatory subjects guidance required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The practical consequences are concrete. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic require the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited. That last rule is why nobody can offer your child an alternative Arabic syllabus: the content is fixed, and support means working inside it.

The second line is Ministry of Education equivalency, which converts a school-leaving certificate into something a UAE authority recognises. For the British track the published requirements are five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor page states six subjects; the published rule is five, and a family that plans on six has paid for an extra entry.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Maths test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so this page publishes none: check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process families complete themselves through the official channel, it is not something a coach performs, and no part of it requires tutoring.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what that does to the price
paragraphs: Every platform in this market implies infinite supply. None has it. The combinations that run short are predictable: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the exam term, Computer Science at any time of year, Economics in the fortnight before a commentary deadline, and the smaller language B options almost permanently. A family searching in late January for a Higher Level Chemistry coach is competing with every other Diploma family in the Gulf for the same handful of people.

What IB Gram does about it is disclose it. If no specialist is free for your subject and level at the hour you need, you will be told that at enquiry rather than matched to whoever is available and asked to hope. The usual alternatives are a different slot with the right coach, a bounded block with a coach whose depth is right but whose availability is thinner, or a wait with a date attached. Occasionally the honest answer is that we cannot help this term, and that is said plainly.

Scarcity moves the price as well as the wait, and it is worth knowing which direction. Rates do not generally rise in February because a provider decided to charge more; they rise because the only people left with Thursday evening availability are at the top of the band. The cheap way to avoid that is calendar discipline. Hours booked in October for a component due in March are bought from a full pool at a mid-band rate.

There is one structural advantage in the online format worth repeating here. Because lessons run live over video rather than by car, the pool a UAE family draws from is not limited to their community, their emirate or their time zone's daylight. That is what makes a specialist booking in Umm Al Quwain the same proposition as one in Jumeirah, and it is the reason availability conversations are about subject depth rather than about distance.
bullets: Scarce by subject: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Computer Science, language B options
Scarce by season: the eight weeks before papers, and coursework deadline fortnights
Disclosed at enquiry: a slot, a different coach, a dated wait, or an honest no
The cheapest fix for scarcity is booking a term earlier, not paying more

process.title: Send the mark, not the worry
process.description: Start with evidence rather than a description. A marked paper, an Internal Assessment draft with the school's comments, or the subject page of the last report tells us more in two minutes than a long conversation about confidence. Name the subject, the level and the deadline you are working to.

process.title: Ask for the hour count before the price
process.description: We read the evidence and come back with which topics or criteria are costing marks and roughly how many hours that implies. The estimate is written down, it is a planning figure rather than a forecast of a result, and it is the number you should ask every provider for before comparing hourly rates.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One real teaching hour with the proposed coach, on your child's own work, at no cost. Judge it on the diagnosis: did the coach find something the school had not named, and could your child explain afterwards what they were going to do differently this week?

process.title: Pick the buying model that matches your term
process.description: A fixed weekly hour for a persistent gap, a priced block for a component with a deadline, or a counted intensive for the final stretch. We will tell you when the smaller option is the right one, and the choice can change at the six-week review without a penalty.

process.title: Review the spend at six weeks
process.description: Six weeks in, we look at the school's marks rather than our own impressions and decide whether to continue, change subject or stop. Written notes after each session mean that review is a conversation about evidence. Plenty of families stop here, having bought exactly the hours they needed.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure on this page carries its source
whyPoints.description: Three of the six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all. Ours publishes the market bands, names the provider model that charges each one, and separates them from IB Gram's own quote, which depends on subject, level and hour count rather than on a tier.

whyPoints.title: The hour count comes before the money
whyPoints.description: A rate without an hour estimate is not a price. We look at a real script, say which topics and criteria are losing marks, and put a planning block in writing. If the honest number is four hours rather than a year, that is what you are told.

whyPoints.title: One coach, one subject guide, one level
whyPoints.description: Matching is done on the current subject guide and the level sat, not on who is nearby. That is the reason the lessons are online: a Higher Level specialist for a scarce subject is reachable from any emirate at a weekday evening hour, including the three nobody else writes about.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coursework support is teaching, criterion-referenced feedback and hard questions about method. Every sentence submitted is the student's own, the school supervisor's role comes first, and nothing is supplied for insertion. The boundary is published here so you can hold us to it.

whyPoints.title: Regulator facts linked to the authority that published them
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE each do a specific job, and this page says which. IB Gram holds no regulator permit and claims none; the facts are here so that you can check any provider against the authority's own page.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for your subject at the hour you need, you hear that at enquiry. What follows is a different slot, a dated wait, or an honest no, rather than a match with whoever happened to be available that week.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB coaching and ordinary subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: A general tutor teaches the subject. An IB coach teaches the assessment of that subject: the current subject guide, the command terms, the criteria and the marks attached to each one. The practical difference shows up in what the first hour looks like. A general tutor usually starts with the topic the student says is hard. A coach starts with a marked script and works out where the marks actually went, which is often somewhere the student had not noticed. For a Diploma subject, that distinction is worth more than any hourly saving, because the gap between a 5 and a 6 is frequently technique rather than content.

faqs.question: How many coached hours does one Higher Level subject usually absorb in a year?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong, which is why any single number you are quoted without a diagnosis is a guess. As planning blocks, families commonly ask for six to twelve hours to rebuild one or two missed topics, six to ten hours on the Internal Assessment, six to ten on Paper 3 and data technique, and eight to sixteen across a marking cycle of past papers. Weekly support across a full academic year is roughly thirty-four hours. Those are planning figures to open a conversation with, not averages and not a forecast of a result. A real script usually moves the number in one direction or the other.

faqs.question: Should we pay a monthly package or buy coaching hours as we go?
faqs.answer: Start pay-as-you-go, almost always. Monthly packages price a provider's certainty of income, and the Diploma calendar is not steady enough to reward that: a student needs little in DP1 term one, a great deal when coursework lands, and something different again before papers. A flat monthly commitment pays the quiet months at the same rate as the loud ones. If you do buy a block, tie it to a named component rather than to a calendar month, and get two things in writing first: what happens to unused hours, and whether they can transfer to a different subject if the diagnosis changes.

faqs.question: How do we build a coaching budget for the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Multiply hours by rate, and work out the hours first. Published UAE rates sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for qualified online support and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for specialists, so a term of weekly support in one subject is about AED 2,160 to AED 4,800, a full year in one Higher Level subject is AED 6,120 to AED 13,600, and two Higher Levels taken weekly for a year is a five-figure commitment. Build from component blocks rather than from a monthly figure: coursework supervision early, technique and marked papers late, content catch-up only where a diagnosis shows a real gap.

faqs.question: Is small-group IB coaching better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour and it buys something different. At the budget end of the UAE market, group online rates have been published from around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour per student, against AED 150 and up for one-to-one. A good group class walks a cohort through a syllabus once, which is useful if your child has missed a stretch of teaching. It cannot find out that this particular student is losing Paper 2 marks on command terms, because that requires reading this particular student's script. Groups are value for coverage; one-to-one is value per mark recovered.

faqs.question: Does my child need coaching in every subject or only the Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Rarely every subject, and often not the one the report looks worst in. Start by asking where the points are actually recoverable. A Higher Level subject carries more content and, in several subjects, an extra paper, so a fixable technique problem there is worth more points than the same problem at Standard Level. Coursework is the other high-yield target, because an Internal Assessment can be worth a fifth or more of a subject grade and is marked against published criteria the student can be taught to read. Two well-chosen subjects usually beat four thinly supported ones at the same total cost.

faqs.question: We wanted a coach at our villa in the UAE. Why is this delivered online instead?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is the most expensive ingredient and the one that hurts the teaching. Published in-home one-to-one rates in the UAE run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to AED 450 for specialist online support, and the difference is travel time priced into the rate. A visit also limits you to specialists willing to cross your emirate on a weekday evening. Lessons run live over video, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time evening slots, which is how a family in Fujairah books the same Higher Level coach as a family in Jumeirah. IB Gram offers home visits only in India.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking three providers for a coaching quote?
faqs.answer: Send the same four things to each, so the answers are comparable. One: the subject, the level and the exam session being sat. Two: a marked script or a draft with the school's comments, which is the only way anyone can estimate hours honestly. Three: the deadline you are working to, whether that is an internal coursework date or a paper. Four: the slot you can realistically hold each week in Gulf Standard Time. Then ask each provider for an hour estimate as well as a rate. A provider who gives you a rate but refuses an estimate has not read the script.

faqs.question: How do I check that a coach is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone charging you a licensing fee is charging for something the state issues at no cost. Two cautions: the permit is open to teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, so it says nothing about subject depth. And its code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher coach them privately for a fee?
faqs.answer: Not where the student is enrolled at that teacher's school. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring a permit holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at the same school. That report is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy text, so check the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording. The sensible reading for a parent is that a teacher who offers this arrangement is putting their own position at risk, and your child's with it.

faqs.question: What does Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge supervision involve, and what is it charged at?
faqs.answer: It is process coaching, charged at the specialist band rather than as a separate product, so published UAE rates of AED 200 to AED 450 and above an hour apply. Families commonly plan four to eight hours for Extended Essay supervision and three to six for the Theory of Knowledge essay. The hours go on the decisions that carry marks: a research question narrow enough to answer, sources that support an argument rather than decorate one, a structure that matches the criteria, and honest reflection. The school supervisor leads; a coach works behind them. Every sentence submitted is the student's own, and feedback is given as questions and criterion references.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level Chemistry coach harder to book than an English one?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. The pool of people who can teach Higher Level organic mechanisms and energetics to a current subject guide, and mark honestly against it, is small everywhere and smaller in one emirate. Demand is also concentrated, because a large share of Diploma medics take Chemistry at Higher Level and they all want the same eight weeks before papers. English A specialists are more numerous and their demand is spread across the year. The practical consequence is calendar discipline: a Chemistry booking made in October comes from a full pool at a mid-band rate, while the same booking in February comes from whoever is left.

faqs.question: Can coaching be paused during the exam block or the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and pausing is often the right call rather than a concession. Nothing useful is bought in the fortnight a student is actually sitting papers, and new content introduced inside the final two weeks tends to unsettle more than it adds. Summer works the same way: a short block in August aimed at one named topic is usually better value than weekly sessions across the holiday. Sessions can also move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan rather than being cancelled. With a fixed weekly hour, a pause takes a week's notice; with a component block, the hours stay attached to the component.

faqs.question: How does online coaching handle science practicals and the data-based paper?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself belongs to the school, which has the laboratory, the equipment and the supervision duty. Coaching targets what is actually assessed on paper: designing an investigation, controlling variables, treating uncertainties, processing data, drawing conclusions the data supports, and evaluating method. All of that is done on screen with the student's own data and real past-paper material, and the data-based paper is pure technique under time pressure. Where a student needs to re-collect data, the coach helps plan what to collect before the lab session rather than standing in it, which is usually where the marks were lost anyway.

faqs.question: Is there anything beyond lesson fees we should budget for before university applications?
faqs.answer: Yes, and none of it is paid to a coach. A Ministry of Education equivalency file converts a school-leaving certificate into something a UAE authority recognises, and it has its own steps, costs and attestation requirements through the official channel. Private-candidate exam entries, remark or enquiry-upon-result requests, and retake entries each carry board fees. Put those in the same table as the coaching spend, because they land at awkward moments: equivalency paperwork is far easier to gather in DP1 than in July of DP2. No part of the equivalency process requires tutoring, and no provider performs it on your behalf.

faqs.question: How should we plan a push from the low thirties to the high thirties in points?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise a points total, and any provider who offers one should be treated with real scepticism. What you can do is plan where points are mathematically available. Pull the subject-by-subject breakdown rather than the total, then ask three questions per subject: how many marks sit in a component the student is handling badly, how recoverable that component is at this point in the year, and what the hour cost of addressing it is. Coursework and paper technique are where points usually move. Buying hours across all six subjects at once is the pattern that reliably spends a budget without changing a breakdown.

faqs.question: Does a school rated Outstanding mean coaching is a waste of money?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, because an inspection band describes a whole school rather than your child's Higher Level set. KHDA, ADEK and the other emirate authorities inspect and publish ratings covering teaching, leadership and outcomes across the institution, and a strong overall band can sit alongside one subject with a staffing gap, a mid-year teacher change or an unusually large Diploma class. Read the subject-level detail in the report, then look at your child's own marked work. If the school is teaching well and the marks are still short, the question is usually technique or coursework design, which is a bounded block rather than a term of weekly support.

ib-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the arithmetic, then book one hour
ib-coaching.closingBody: You now have the two numbers this market usually withholds: the AED bands the UAE actually charges for IB coaching, and the hour blocks a Diploma component tends to absorb. Multiply them and you have a budget you can approve or refuse on evidence. The next step costs nothing. Send a marked script, the subject and the level, and the deadline you are working to, and we will come back with where the marks are going and how many hours that implies. Then take the free trial lesson with the proposed coach and judge the diagnosis. Lessons run live online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time evening slots, and you buy hours only once you know how many you need.

ib-crash-course.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors families book for a short, dated block rather than a long term. Each teaches one or two IB subjects at Higher and Standard Level, works from marked past-paper evidence rather than lesson plans, and quotes in hours. Availability tightens from February onwards, so a sprint booked in April starts with whoever is still free.

intro.heading: An IB crash course is a budget decision before it is a teaching decision
paragraphs: Most families reach this page carrying a date and a number. The date is an exam, a mock or an internal deadline. The number is what they are prepared to spend before it arrives. An IB crash course sits exactly between those two facts: a defined block of one-to-one hours, bought for a deadline, which ends unless you renew it. That shape is what makes it priceable in a way open-ended weekly tuition never is. You can count the hours, multiply by a rate, and then ask the only question that matters, which is what each individual hour is supposed to change.

The UAE market does not make that arithmetic easy. Three of the six pages ranking highest for this query publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here pays school fees in. The AED figures on this page come from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from provider pages read in October 2026. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list. What a block costs with us depends on subject, level, lead time and how many hours you buy, and the honest route to that figure is one free diagnostic lesson followed by a short conversation about scope.

Scale matters to the price because scarcity does. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment and the UK curriculum 37 per cent, according to figures published by Dubai Media Office. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places. More Diploma candidates each year chase a tutor pool that does not grow at the same rate, and the squeeze shows up first in the price of Higher Level Physics and Chemistry in April.

Five things move the number on a quote, and only one of them is the tutor's experience. Level is the first: a Higher Level block covers more syllabus and sits against longer papers, so it needs more hours than the same subject at Standard Level. Lead time is the second, because an eight-week block can be spaced while a ten-day block cannot. Subject scarcity is the third. Format is the fourth, since a tutor absorbing travel across Dubai prices that travel into the hour. The tutor's record with the actual mark scheme is the fifth, and it is the one worth paying for.

What follows is built in that order. First a definition of the formats on sale, then the hours each goal genuinely takes, then the AED bands and what a twenty-hour block costs at each. After that comes the arithmetic nobody publishes, the list of things a sprint cannot repair at any price, the calendar counted backwards from the session, the academic-honesty line a tutor may not cross inside a block, the mandatory UAE subjects that shape a revision timetable, and the permit position you should check before paying anyone. Lessons are delivered online over live video; that is stated here once plainly and explained properly further down.
