ib-crash-course.programmesIntro: Crash courses are bought most often by Diploma families, but the shape works further down the school too. The difference between programmes is not intensity, it is what the block is aimed at: a final grade, a criterion-marked task, or a transition into harder work next year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The programme almost every enquiry here concerns. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A Diploma sprint is usually aimed at one or two subjects where the mock grade and the predicted grade disagree, and it works backwards from the paper structure: what each component is worth, which topics appear in which paper, and what the command terms expect a candidate to actually do on the page.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session with their school as the registered centre, and most schools here run mocks in January or February. That puts the useful window for a DP crash course between the mock results and the start of study leave. Families moving between emirates mid-course are a recurring case: a transfer from an ADEK-regulated school in Abu Dhabi to a KHDA-regulated one in Dubai can change teaching order even when the syllabus is identical.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of interdisciplinary study assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. A crash course at this level rarely chases a grade. It usually targets one criterion the school reports as weak, most often criterion C or D in sciences and mathematics, where students lose marks for presenting a conclusion without linking it to the evidence they collected or the model they chose.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the MYP year that generates the most crash-course enquiries is the last one, because families realise late that MYP criterion marks do not convert into Diploma grades and that the step into Higher Level content is steeper than the school's reporting suggested. A short block in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 is cheaper than a long one in the following February.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework with no external examinations, so a crash course here is a misnomer and we say so. What parents actually want at this age is a short diagnostic block: six to eight sessions that establish where number fluency, reading comprehension or written expression actually sit against age expectations, and produce a plan the family can run themselves afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries in the UAE cluster around the transfer year into a selective secondary, when a school asks for an assessment and the parents have no independent read on where their child stands. A short block before that assessment is reasonable. A twenty-hour sprint for an eight-year-old is not, and no honest provider should sell one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The IB's fourth programme pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Crash-course demand is small because the cohort is small, and it concentrates on the Diploma courses taken alongside the career study, where a candidate is sitting a full DP paper without the full DP timetable to prepare for it.
programmes.countryNote: Very few UAE schools are authorised for the Career-related Programme, so families often discover it only when comparing post-16 options. If your child is a CP candidate, say so when you book: the subject hours are DP hours, but the reflective project runs to the school's own internal schedule rather than a published external one, and the block has to be timed against that.

ib-crash-course.subjectsIntro: A crash course is bought per subject, so the hours vary with how the subject is assessed. Below is what a block typically targets in each of the subjects UAE families book most, and where the marks usually go missing when a candidate already knows the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Blocks here are almost always about Paper 1, the non-calculator paper, where candidates who can solve a problem with technology cannot always do it by hand. Proof, binomial work and calculus manipulation are the recurring gaps. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a longer investigative paper that rewards candidates who write down what they are doing and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Marks drain away in modelling and statistics, not in arithmetic. Candidates fit a model and then fail to comment on its limitations, or quote a correlation without naming what it does and does not imply. A sprint here is mostly technology discipline: knowing which calculator function the question expects and showing the intermediate step anyway.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The content is rarely the problem by April. Lost marks sit in extended-response questions where a candidate describes an effect instead of explaining it, and in data analysis where uncertainties are quoted without propagating them. A block usually alternates one topic repair with one full timed paper, marked against the published criteria rather than a model answer.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the enquiries, with equilibrium close behind. The common failure is a correct answer with the working absent, which the mark scheme cannot credit. Higher Level candidates also lose marks on multi-step calculations where one rounding decision early in the chain costs the final mark.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where sprint hours go on precision of language. Candidates write plausible biology that does not answer the command term, or describe a process without naming the structures involved. Blocks work best when they drill one system at a time against past questions, so the candidate learns what a six-mark answer actually looks like on paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and most candidates draw them incompletely: axes unlabelled, the shift unexplained, the new equilibrium unmarked. Evaluation is the second gap. A sprint teaches a repeatable structure for the fifteen-mark questions and drills the diagram set until each one can be produced accurately under time pressure.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Candidates who know the tools still lose marks for applying them generically instead of to the stimulus in front of them. Blocks focus on reading the case material properly, selecting the right tool rather than every tool, and writing conclusions that commit to a judgement. Higher Level extension topics need separate hours and should be priced as such.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A sprint cannot read the texts for a candidate, so blocks target the transferable skill instead: unseen analysis for Paper 1, comparative structure for Paper 2, and preparation for the individual oral as a planned argument rather than a recited one. Most marks are recovered by writing about technique and effect together instead of listing devices.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written papers test tracing and reasoning more than coding, and that is where candidates who program confidently come unstuck. Blocks drill pseudocode tracing, data-structure questions and the HL abstract-data-type content, with the internal assessment handled separately as supervised feedback on the student's own solution.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies are remembered and then used badly. Candidates describe a study without connecting it to the question's demand, or evaluate methodology in general terms. A short block builds a defensible bank of studies the candidate can actually deploy, with one line of evaluation attached to each, and practises the essay structures the command terms require.

ib-crash-course.regionsIntro: A crash course has no travel cost, so where you live changes the timetable rather than the price. What it does change is which regulator oversees your child's school, when the school day ends, and therefore when a session can realistically start without colliding with the school run or prep.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, with the largest IB cohort in the country and the deepest competition for April tutor slots. Most schools finish between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, so sprint sessions cluster from 4pm, and families with two candidates often split a block across two evenings rather than doubling up.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Island and mainland commutes push realistic start times later than in Dubai, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff make the permitted route for paid tutoring a question worth asking early.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with far fewer IB Diploma places than the capital. The practical consequence for a crash course is that a Higher Level specialist in a scarce subject is unlikely to live locally, which is precisely the case online delivery is built to solve.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Commutes into Dubai for school are common, so evening sessions here often start after 5.30pm.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. The IB cohort is small, so most crash-course enquiries concern candidates travelling to Sharjah or Dubai for school and needing a block that fits around a long commute.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Returned zero mentions across the competitor pages we studied, which tells you how little published guidance a family here has had to work with.

regions.name: Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Both fall under the Ministry of Education's supervision of private schools. Diploma candidates are few and often the only one in a subject at their school, so a block is frequently the first time the student has worked with somebody who teaches that syllabus daily.

schoolClusters.note: The densest IB cluster in the country and the one where April availability disappears first. Students we support attend schools across these communities; a block booked for a candidate here is usually competing with mock results that arrived in February and a study-leave date already on the school calendar.

A smaller Diploma cohort spread over a wider area, which makes subject scarcity the binding constraint rather than price. Families here ask most often about Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, where a school may run a single class.

ib-crash-course.modesIntro: Four block shapes cover almost every enquiry. The difference between them is not teaching style but how the hours are distributed against a deadline, which is also what makes one cheaper per hour than another.

modes.title: Six-week exam sprint
modes.description: The standard shape, and the one the arithmetic favours. Twenty to twenty-four hours across six weeks, usually two sessions a week per subject, with a full timed paper every second week. Spacing matters more than volume here: the gap between sessions is where retrieval actually happens, and compressing the same hours into ten days removes it.

modes.title: Pre-mock diagnostic block
modes.description: Eight to ten hours in the four weeks before school mocks, bought to find out what is actually wrong rather than to fix everything. It is the cheapest useful block on this page and the one most families should buy first, because it converts a vague worry into a list of named topics and a decision about whether a longer sprint is warranted at all.

modes.description: Twelve to sixteen hours compressed into a school break, used when term-time evenings are already full. It suits content repair better than exam technique, because technique needs the feedback loop a spaced block provides. Priced per hour the same way, but the whole block lands in one week, so the family pays sooner and the tutor's calendar is harder to secure.

Sixteen to thirty hours across the autumn, pitched at the specific papers being retaken rather than the whole course. The scope is narrower than a first-sitting sprint and the timetable is easier, because the candidate is usually no longer carrying six subjects at once.

sections.heading: What an IB crash course actually buys you
paragraphs: An IB crash course is a fixed number of one-to-one hours, bought against a named date, after which the arrangement stops. That is the whole definition, and it is the reason the format can be priced while weekly tuition cannot. A retainer is an open commitment with a monthly cost and no endpoint. A block is a purchase: twenty hours, six weeks, one subject, one deadline, one figure.

The confusion in this market comes from providers using the word for three different products. Some sell a group revision course with a syllabus and a fixed start date. Some sell a recorded video library described as intensive. Some simply relabel a weekly package as a sprint and charge the same monthly rate. Only the first is wrong to call a crash course, and none of the three is the same thing as a one-to-one block scoped from a candidate's own marked papers.

The distinction has a direct effect on what you pay. A group course prices by seat and cannot change its route for one candidate, so it is cheap and generic. A one-to-one block prices by hour and exists precisely to be specific. A video library prices by subscription and asks the student to diagnose themselves, which is the one job a struggling candidate cannot do. Before comparing prices, make sure the three quotes in front of you describe the same product; in this market they usually do not.

IB Gram sells the third shape only: a scoped block of live, one-to-one online lessons, quoted in hours and dates. There is no group course, no recorded library and no monthly subscription, which also means there is nothing to cancel when the block ends.

sections.heading: How many hours a sprint needs, goal by goal
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake families make is buying hours before deciding what the hours are for. A block aimed at fixing one topic needs a fraction of the time a block aimed at lifting a whole subject does, and the two are often quoted at the same hourly rate, which hides the difference entirely. Decide the goal first and the hour count follows from it.

The figures below reflect what single-subject blocks typically run to, and they assume the candidate has already covered the content once in school. A block for a candidate who genuinely has not met half the syllabus is not a crash course; it is re-teaching a course, and anyone quoting twenty hours for that is selling you a shortfall. Say so plainly at the diagnostic stage and the scope can be set honestly instead of discovered in week four.

Spacing changes the yield of the same hours. Two sessions a week with marked work in between produces more than four sessions crammed into a weekend, because the recall interval is where the learning consolidates. That is also why a six-week block generally beats a two-week one at identical cost. If the deadline forces compression, expect the block to repair content rather than sharpen technique, and price your expectations accordingly.

One caution on the last row. A candidate aiming to move a grade from a 3 to a 6 inside six weeks is attempting something no quantity of hours reliably delivers, and no honest tutor will promise it. The useful conversation is about which single paper or component is most recoverable in the time left, and what that is worth.

sections.heading: What an IB crash course costs in the UAE
paragraphs: Parents searching IB crash course cost in the UAE meet a wall of silence: the best-ranking agency page in this cluster asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. The bands below are published market figures, drawn from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from provider pages read in October 2026. They are the market, not our price list, and they are quoted in AED because that is what a UAE family pays in.

Read the table by block, not by hour. An hourly rate is a comparison tool for tutors; a block total is the number that actually leaves your account. The same twenty-hour sprint costs AED 3,000 at the lower qualified-tutor band and over AED 10,000 at the premium end, and the gap between those two figures is larger than most families' entire planned spend. Knowing which band you are shopping in before you start saves a fortnight of quotes that were never viable.

Monthly packages circulate alongside hourly rates and confuse the comparison. Figures seen in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits, while Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run from AED 240 to 600 at the budget end up to AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Convert any monthly figure to an hourly one before comparing it with a block.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page, and the reason is not coyness. A block's price depends on the subject, the level, the lead time and the hours bought, and a single number printed here would be wrong for most of the families reading it. The free first lesson exists to produce an accurate figure instead of a plausible one.

sections.heading: The arithmetic nobody publishes: hourly rate is the wrong number
paragraphs: Two quotes at the same hourly rate can represent very different purchases, because the hour is not the unit of value. What a family is buying is marked practice with expert feedback attached, and providers include wildly different amounts of that inside the same hour. Ask how many full timed papers the block includes, who marks them, and whether marking time is inside the hourly rate or additional. A block of twenty hours containing four marked papers is a different product from twenty hours of conversation.

The format comparison below is where online delivery earns its place, and not on price alone. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we provide only in India. The case for online in a crash course is structural rather than financial. A sprint is bought under time pressure, and the constraint that bites hardest is not cost but choice: a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who happens to live twenty minutes from your community may not exist, and in Al Ain or Fujairah almost certainly does not.

Travel also consumes the thing a sprint is shortest of. A tutor crossing Dubai at 5pm loses an hour each way, which means they can teach three families an evening rather than five, and that scarcity is priced into their rate. The same hour bought online costs less, starts on time, and can be scheduled against the candidate's real timetable rather than the tutor's route. Screen-sharing a marked script, with annotations both people can see and the recording available afterwards, also beats passing a paper across a table.

The honest counterweight: a candidate who will not engage without somebody physically present is a real case, and online delivery will not fix it. That is a conversation to have in the free first lesson, not after a block has been paid for.

sections.heading: What a crash course cannot fix at any price
paragraphs: This is the section competitors leave out, and it is the one that saves families money. A sprint is a leverage tool. It multiplies something the candidate already has and it cannot create something from nothing, which means there are failure modes that twenty hours will not touch however good the tutor is.

The first is missing content at scale. If a candidate has genuinely not met a third of a Higher Level syllabus six weeks out, the realistic plan is to protect the components that are recoverable, not to attempt the whole course. A tutor who agrees to cover an entire HL syllabus in twenty hours is either not going to do it or is going to do it so fast that nothing survives the week. Ask for the scope in writing and check it against the hours.

The second is a mismatch between the candidate's effort and the family's urgency. A block only works if the student does the marked practice between sessions, because that practice is the evidence the next session is built on. Where a student is not willing to produce it, the hours convert into supervised reading and the money buys attendance. That is worth naming at the diagnostic stage, honestly and without blame, rather than discovering it in week four.

The third is an administrative problem dressed as an academic one. A missed registration deadline, a submitted internal assessment, an unresolved access arrangement or a school timetable clash is not solved by tuition at all, and buying hours to feel better about it is the single most common waste we see. Those belong with the school's Diploma coordinator the same week they are noticed.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the session: when to buy the block
paragraphs: Crash courses are bought late because deadlines feel distant until they are not. The fix is to count backwards from the session rather than forwards from today, and the table below does that without inventing dates. IB session and results dates are published by the IB each year and are not restated here; confirm every one of them with your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the registration and upload deadlines for your centre.

The lead times are long enough to surprise people, and the clearest published illustration comes from Pearson rather than the IB. Its International GCSE runs in a May or June series and again in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, while June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entry for a November series closes well before the autumn term has settled, months ahead of the first paper, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables that it then revises. Cambridge works on the same principle across its June and November series, the only two a UAE candidate can sit, because the February and March sitting is offered to India only. Neither board states a closing date you can carry from one year to the next, so the statement of entry your centre issues is the document that holds yours.

The practical consequence for a sprint is that the useful buying windows are narrow. The strongest moment is immediately after mock results, when you have marked evidence and enough weeks left to act on it. The second strongest is the autumn of the final year, before internal assessment deadlines eat every evening. The weakest is the fortnight before study leave, when availability has gone and the only hours left are compressed ones.

If your child is a retake candidate, the counting runs the other way: results arrive, the review and remark windows are short, and the decision to resit has to be made before the next session's registration closes through the school. Build the block around that date, not around when the hours happen to be available.

sections.heading: Where the honesty line sits inside an intensive block
paragraphs: Compressed hours and a near deadline are exactly the conditions under which academic-honesty boundaries get tested, so a page selling intensive support has an obligation to state them. Under IB rules the internal assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the candidate's own work. A tutor teaches, questions, marks against published criteria and gives feedback. A tutor does not produce any part of the submission.

In practice the line is clearer than it sounds. Explaining what a criterion is asking for is teaching. Reading a student's draft and telling them that their conclusion does not follow from their data is feedback. Asking a question that makes a student notice a gap in their own reasoning is coaching. Supplying sentences, restructuring an argument on the student's behalf, or rewriting a paragraph so it scores better is production, and it is the point at which the student's authentication of their own work stops being true.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because one provider in this market openly sells completed internal assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student, whose diploma is the thing actually at risk. A family paying for it is buying a liability. If a tutor offers to take an Extended Essay from draft to finished text, that is the moment to end the conversation.

One related point on materials. We reference IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes and link to the official sources, and we do not reproduce or distribute them. Your child's school holds legitimate access to the material their centre is entitled to, and the Diploma coordinator is the right route to it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the mandatory UAE subjects a sprint works around
paragraphs: A revision timetable in the UAE is not the same object as one in London, and treating it as one is how blocks get mis-scheduled. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the family rhythm shifts around Iftar, and the weeks containing Eid carry fewer usable teaching evenings than the calendar implies. A block planned across that period should be planned with it, which usually means post-Iftar sessions, shorter weekday slots and more weight on the weekend.

There is also a second curriculum running alongside the IB that families outside the region rarely account for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, which is the rule every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement rests on.

The detail affects timetabling more than most parents expect. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. For these subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

What that means for a crash course is simple. Those lessons occupy real hours in your child's week and they cannot be dropped to make room for Higher Level Physics. Build the block around the school timetable you actually have, and if Arabic itself is the weak subject, treat it as its own scoped block with a tutor who teaches that syllabus, not as something to bolt onto a science sprint.

sections.heading: Paying for it: the permit, the receipt and what a quote should say
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the position is clearer than the market's silence suggests. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system, with the service page listing a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and figures circulating online could not be verified, so no amount appears on this page. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: a training institute in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, obtained through initial approval and renewed annually at least 30 days before expiry. That permit belongs to centres with premises, which is why describing any online tutor as holding regulator approval would be wrong.

In Abu Dhabi there is an additional constraint worth knowing before accepting an offer from inside your child's own school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That reporting should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before anyone relies on it, but the direction is clear enough to ask the question.

The quote itself is the last checkpoint. Before money moves, a block quote should state the number of hours, the session length, the dates, the subject and level, how many full timed papers are included and who marks them, what happens to an unused hour, and the cancellation notice on both sides. If a quote is a monthly figure with no hour count attached, it is not a crash course quote.

sections.heading: What the money bought: judging a block after it ends
paragraphs: A block has a defined endpoint, which gives you something a retainer never does: a clean moment to judge whether the spend worked. Do it on evidence rather than impression. The marked papers from the start and the end of the block are the comparison, and if a provider cannot produce both, that itself is the finding.

Three signals are worth more than a grade. The first is whether the causes of lost marks changed character: a candidate who stops losing marks to method and starts losing them to harder content has moved, even if the raw total barely shifted. The second is whether the candidate can now explain why an answer scores what it scores, because that is the skill that keeps paying after the block ends. The third is whether the handover names what remains open, which is the difference between a tutor who was teaching and one who was filling hours.

Be realistic about timing. A block that finishes a fortnight before the first paper will not show its full effect in a mock, and the final session is not the moment for a verdict. The fair comparison point is the next timed paper under proper conditions, whoever sets it.

If the answer is that it did not work, stop. Buying a second block from the same route because the first was disappointing is how families spend AED 8,000 to learn what AED 3,000 already told them. A short diagnostic block with a different tutor, or a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about what the school can offer, is almost always the better next purchase.

Watch for the cause of lost marks changing, not just the total

process.title: Tell us the date and the subject
process.description: Start with the deadline, not the hours. A mock date, a study-leave date or a retake session is enough to begin. Say which subject and level, what the last reported grade was, and what the family's ceiling on spend is. That last figure is not awkward; it is what lets us scope a block that is actually buyable.

process.title: One free diagnostic lesson
process.description: Every student gets one free first lesson, one per student, booked through the site. It is a working session, not a sales call: the tutor looks at a marked paper, asks the candidate to attempt something live, and forms a view on what the lost marks are actually caused by. Families who decide against a block owe nothing.

process.title: A scoped quote in hours and dates
process.description: After the diagnostic you get a written scope: hours, session length, dates, subject and level, how many full timed papers are included, who marks them and what the cancellation notice is on both sides. If the honest answer is that a block is not worth buying, the scope says that instead, and some do.

process.title: Run the block on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are one to one over live video, scheduled around your child's school day and prep rather than a tutor's route across the city. Marked work goes back between sessions, and timetables shift for Ramadan, Eid and school breaks by arrangement rather than by cancellation.

process.title: Handover and a decision point
process.description: The block ends with a written handover: what moved, what did not, what the candidate should keep practising and what remains open. Then the arrangement stops. Renewing is a fresh decision made on that evidence, which is the point of buying a block rather than a subscription in the first place.

whyPoints.title: Priced as a block, not a subscription
whyPoints.description: You buy hours against a date and the arrangement ends there. No rolling monthly fee, nothing to cancel, no quiet renewal in July. The figure you agree is the figure the block costs, and the hours are written down so both sides can count them.

whyPoints.title: Subject match beats postcode
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the pool is every specialist whose hours overlap Gulf Standard Time rather than everyone within a 20-minute drive. For a Higher Level subject with one class in your child's school, or for a family in Al Ain or Fujairah, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever was nearest.

whyPoints.title: Marked evidence, not impressions
whyPoints.description: Blocks are scoped from the candidate's own marked scripts and run against full timed papers marked to published criteria. That gives a start point and an end point you can compare, which is also what makes it possible to judge honestly whether the spend worked.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with their source attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate band on this page names where it came from and when it was read. We publish market ranges rather than a tidy number, because a single invented figure would be wrong for most families reading it, and a range you can check beats a number you cannot.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor marks, questions and coaches. A tutor does not produce any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and we say which is which before a block starts rather than after a coordinator asks.

whyPoints.title: We say when not to buy
whyPoints.description: Some diagnostics end with a recommendation against a block: the problem is administrative, the content gap is too large for the time left, or the school's own support covers it. That recommendation costs you nothing and is the most valuable thing a free first lesson can produce.

faqs.question: What is an IB crash course, and how is it different from weekly tuition?
faqs.answer: A crash course is a fixed block of hours bought against a named date, after which it ends unless you renew. Weekly tuition is an open arrangement with a monthly cost and no defined endpoint. The practical difference is that a block can be priced and judged: twenty hours, six weeks, one subject, one figure, with marked papers at the start and the finish to compare. A retainer cannot be assessed the same way because there is no moment at which it concludes. For a deadline-driven problem, the block is usually the better purchase.

faqs.question: How many hours does an IB crash course need to be worth the money?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the goal, which is why the hours should be decided after a diagnosis rather than before. Repairing one named topic typically takes six to eight hours over three weeks. Fixing exam technique across a paper runs fourteen to eighteen. Lifting a subject broadly takes twenty to twenty-four across six to eight weeks. Those figures assume the candidate has already covered the content once in school. If a third of a Higher Level syllabus has genuinely not been met, that is re-teaching a course rather than a sprint, and twenty hours will not cover it.

faqs.question: What does an IB crash course cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB tuition in the UAE run roughly AED 150 to 450 an hour for a qualified or specialist tutor, with budget online options advertised from AED 45 and premium examiner-led provision published as high as AED 650. Those figures come from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from provider pages read in October 2026. They describe the market rather than our price. A twenty-hour block therefore spans AED 3,000 at the lower qualified band to over AED 10,000 at the premium end, which is why the band matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: Is a two-week crash course enough before Paper 1?
faqs.answer: It can repair content; it is poor at fixing technique. Exam technique improves through a feedback loop, which needs marked work attempted between sessions and time to absorb the feedback before the next one. Compress the same hours into ten days and that loop disappears, so the candidate gets more exposure and less consolidation. If the deadline leaves only two weeks, scope the block tightly around the single most recoverable component rather than attempting the whole paper, and expect it to tidy rather than transform. Six weeks at the same total cost generally produces more.

faqs.question: We have six weeks left. Which subject should get the crash course?
faqs.answer: Usually the one where the gap between the mock mark and the realistic ceiling is widest for method reasons rather than content reasons, because method is what moves fastest. A candidate losing marks to unlabelled diagrams, missing working or misread command terms can recover those in weeks. A candidate who has not met the content needs longer than six weeks whatever the subject. Bring the marked scripts from two or three subjects to the diagnostic lesson and the comparison is usually obvious within half an hour. Spreading one block thinly across three subjects is the common mistake.

faqs.question: Does a crash course cost less per hour than booking the same hours weekly?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and families should be sceptical of discounts framed that way. Hours cost roughly the same whether they are bought in a block or spread over months; what changes is the commitment and the lead time. Where a block does save money is in waste: a scoped block stops, so you do not pay for hours in May that were agreed in October and are no longer needed. Ask instead what is included inside the hour. Twenty hours containing four marked papers is better value than twenty hours at a lower rate containing none.

faqs.question: Can a crash course cover two Higher Level subjects at once?
faqs.answer: It can, but price it as two blocks rather than one, because that is what it is. Two Higher Level subjects at twenty hours each is forty hours of tutoring plus the marked practice between sessions, landing in the same six weeks the candidate is also revising four other subjects. In practice most families who try this end up doing both badly. The better plan is usually one properly scoped block in the subject with the most recoverable marks, and a shorter diagnostic block in the second to decide whether it needs hours at all.

faqs.question: My child needs a crash course during Ramadan. Can sessions run after Iftar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the normal arrangement here. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the family rhythm shifts around Iftar, so weekday sessions move later and often run shorter, with more weight placed on the weekend. Plan for fewer usable evenings in the weeks containing Eid than the calendar suggests, and build that into the block's dates at the quoting stage rather than cancelling sessions later. Because lessons are delivered online, a timetable change costs nothing but a reschedule; there is no travel arrangement to unpick each time.

faqs.question: Is a crash course useful for a November retake candidate?
faqs.answer: It is one of the better uses of the format, because the scope is genuinely narrow. A retake candidate is usually resitting specific components rather than a whole course, and is no longer carrying six subjects simultaneously, so sixteen to thirty hours across the autumn is realistic in a way the same hours in April are not. Register through a school acting as the registered centre, and check the review, remark and retake windows with that school's Diploma coordinator as soon as results arrive, because those windows are short and the block has to be built around them.

faqs.question: Can a crash course fix an Internal Assessment that is already submitted?
faqs.answer: No. Once a submission has gone to the school for upload, the door is closed, and buying hours to feel better about it is money spent on nothing. What a block can do is protect the components still ahead of the candidate, which in most subjects is the larger share of the grade anyway. Where an assessment is still in draft, a tutor marks against the published criteria and gives feedback on the student's own work, and never produces any part of the text. If the deadline itself was missed, that is a conversation for the Diploma coordinator this week.

faqs.question: How do we tell a real intensive programme from a repackaged weekly package?
faqs.answer: Ask for the scope in writing and read what is in it. A real block states hours, session length, dates, subject and level, the number of full timed papers included, who marks them, what happens to an unused hour and the cancellation notice on both sides. A repackaged weekly offer quotes a monthly figure with no hour count and no endpoint. The second test is diagnosis: a genuine block is scoped from your child's own marked scripts, so somebody has to look at them before quoting. If nobody asks to see a paper, the plan is generic.

faqs.question: Does a crash course need a permit if the tutor is a university student?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. University students and school students aged 15 to 18 are among the categories eligible to apply, alongside registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees and unemployed residents. Individuals tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Ask any tutor directly for their permit, whatever their age or rate.

faqs.question: What should a crash course quote include before we pay for the block?
faqs.answer: Eight things: the number of hours, the length of each session, the dates the block runs between, the subject and level, how many full timed papers are included, who marks those papers and against what criteria, what happens to an hour the family cannot use, and the notice period either side needs to give. A quote carrying all eight can be compared with another quote. One that says a monthly figure and a tutor's biography cannot. Insist on it in writing before money moves, not after the first session.

faqs.question: Are crash courses available for MYP students or only the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Both, though the purpose differs. Middle Years Programme subjects are assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, so a block there targets a named criterion the school reports as weak rather than an exam grade, most often the criteria covering analysis and conclusions in sciences and mathematics. The highest-value moment is the summer between the final MYP year and DP1, because criterion marks do not convert into Diploma grades and the step into Higher Level content is steeper than school reporting usually conveys. A short block then costs less than a long one in February.

faqs.question: Will a crash course help with Ministry of Education equivalency paperwork?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should imply otherwise. Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authorities, not something a tutoring provider performs or can guarantee. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Figures for the IB route should be verified on moe.gov.ae before anybody relies on them. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency.

faqs.question: What happens if the crash course is not working after the third session?
faqs.answer: Say so immediately rather than waiting for the block to finish. By the third session there should already be marked work that shows whether the diagnosis was right, and if it was not, the scope needs changing or the tutor does. A block carries a stated notice period on both sides precisely so that conversation is possible without an argument. The outcome we would rather reach is a changed route than a completed block that nobody believed in, and sometimes the honest recommendation is to stop buying hours altogether.

ib-crash-course.closingHeading: Start with the date, the subject and one free lesson
ib-crash-course.closingBody: An IB crash course in the UAE is worth buying when you can name the deadline, the subject and the number you are prepared to spend, and worth refusing when you cannot. Bring a marked paper to a free first diagnostic lesson, one per student, booked through the site. The tutor will look at where the marks actually went, and you will get a written scope in hours and dates, or a recommendation against a block if that is the honest answer. Every lesson runs one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and the northern emirates alike.

intro.heading: What a UAE family is really buying when they search for a Diploma home tutor
paragraphs: An IB diploma home tutor in the UAE is a phrase typed by a parent who has already worked out that the school timetable will not stretch any further. Your child is carrying six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, a 4,000-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a CAS file, all inside two years that end with external papers. The market answers that search with a visit. Published rates for a visiting tutor in Dubai run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel folded into the figure, and monthly visiting packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions are advertised openly. That is a real service, and some families want exactly that. It is worth knowing what the hour contains before you buy it.

IB Gram sells the same hour differently. Every family in the Emirates on this platform is taught one-to-one over live video: screen shared, the student's own document open, the paper annotated while the lesson runs. Visiting tuition is a service we run only in India, and we would rather say so on the page than let you find out on the phone. The reason is not cost. A Diploma problem is almost always a subject-and-level problem, and Higher Level Chemistry in the second week of DP2 needs a teacher who knows how the internally assessed investigation is moderated, not whoever teaches general science within a twenty-minute drive of your community.

The rest of this page is about the system your family works inside, because that is the part nobody writes down. Four separate bodies sit above a UAE Diploma student. The emirate authority licenses and oversees the school: the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah that authority also approves 'tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods', so its reach goes well past inspection. The Ministry sets the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement that runs beside the Diploma in every private school. And the IB, which licenses none of the above, is the body that actually awards the points.

None of those four bodies is your child's school, and the school is the one holding your deadlines. It owns the option blocks that decide whether Physics Higher Level is even available. It owns the exam entries, because it is the registered centre. It owns the predicted grades your university applications will quote. It sets the internal deadlines for the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, usually months before the IB's own upload dates. Separately, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation owns the question of whether a tutor may be paid at all: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. A tutor owns none of these levers. What a tutor moves is the quality of the student's own work before each of those decisions gets made.

So the page is laid out as a map of that system rather than a list of promises. It covers where the 45 points come from and who marks each part, the failing conditions that quietly stop a Diploma being awarded, who decides what across a UAE Diploma year, why your school may not teach the Higher Level your child needs, what the market charges and what the travel inside that fee buys, and the exact line a paid tutor does not cross on assessed work. Two things are deliberately missing. There is no IB exam or results date anywhere on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and your DP coordinator holds the calendar that counts. And there is no claim of approval, accreditation or partnership with any regulator or examination board, because IB Gram holds none of them and the phrase is the single most dangerous one in this market.

ib-diploma-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Most families arriving on this page have a DP1 or DP2 student, but the Diploma is not the only shape the IB takes in a UAE school. These are the four routes we support, and what each one means once the Ministry's own subject requirements are added to the timetable.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each group with limited substitution, three taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three more from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge taken together, for a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the floor, but the award also depends on separate Higher Level and Standard Level point thresholds, on no grade 1 appearing anywhere, and on CAS being completed and evidenced. Most of the grade sits in external papers; a fifth or so of several subjects is marked in school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the Diploma runs inside a school year shaped by the emirate authority and by the Ministry's mandatory subjects, so a DP student is carrying Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies on top of the six. That matters when you pick a weekly tuition slot: the evening is shorter than the subject list suggests, and Ramadan moves the whole school day for several weeks of the DP2 revision run.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.description: A student can be registered for individual DP subjects rather than the full Diploma, receiving certificates for the courses sat. The subject teaching, the papers and the internally assessed components are the same, and the grading is the same 1 to 7 scale. What changes is that there is no 45-point total, no core requirement and no failing-condition arithmetic, because there is no Diploma being awarded. Universities read the certificates subject by subject, which makes the choice of which subjects to take unusually consequential.
programmes.countryNote: UAE families end up here for practical reasons: a mid-Diploma arrival from another curriculum, a serious illness in DP1, or a student who needs two strong Higher Levels for a named course rather than a full Diploma. Because the Ministry of Education's equivalency route is written around complete certificates, check the position with the school registrar and the Ministry's own channel before committing to the course route.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the run-up to DP1
programmes.description: The two years before the Diploma are where the level choice is really made. MYP 4 and 5 use criterion-based assessment with achievement levels rather than examination papers, so a student can arrive in DP1 having never sat a timed paper under external conditions. The gap shows up first in Mathematics and the sciences, where Higher Level assumes fluency the criteria did not have to test, and second in extended writing against a word limit and a deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the MYP and the Diploma on one campus, which is an advantage: the subject-choice meeting happens with teachers who know the DP option blocks. Use it. Ask in MYP 5 which Higher Levels the school can actually timetable next year, because the honest answer is sometimes narrower than the brochure and it is better heard a year early.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element, personal and professional skills, and language development. It is graded differently from the Diploma: the DP courses keep the 1 to 7 scale while the career-related study is reported on its own terms. Students take it when they want recognised depth in two academic subjects alongside a vocational qualification rather than six academic subjects at once.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools, and university recognition varies by institution and by country, so the course-by-course conversation with an admissions office matters more here than on any other route. We support the DP course components; the career-related study belongs to the school and its partner provider.

ib-diploma-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects UAE families ask for most often, with what the assessment actually rewards. Online IB Diploma tuition in the UAE works subject by subject and level by level, so the first question we ask is never 'which year' but 'which paper, and which criterion'.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and economics applicants need. Higher Level adds proof, deeper calculus and an extra paper, and the marks go on method shown rather than answers reached. The exploration is marked in school and moderated, and the commonest loss is a piece of correct mathematics with no genuine personal engagement or reflection attached to it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work, with the graphical display calculator assumed rather than tolerated. It suits business, psychology and design routes, but some UAE and overseas university courses still specify Analysis and Approaches, so the route choice should be checked against the named programme before DP1 begins, not in DP2.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are lost in two predictable places: multi-step questions where no working is shown, and the internally assessed investigation where uncertainty is reported as a number with no account of where it came from. Higher Level adds topics and a longer paper, and the step up in algebraic fluency catches students arriving from criterion-assessed MYP science.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the panic, but the grade usually turns on data handling and on the scientific investigation, which carries about a fifth of the subject. A Higher Level Chemistry tutor in Abu Dhabi spends as much time on how the method was justified as on the chemistry itself, because that is where the criteria put the marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise the recall and under-practise the command terms, so answers describe where the question said explain or evaluate. The investigation rewards a narrow, well-controlled question over an ambitious one, and the students who choose narrow in DP1 are reliably calmer in DP2.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks, and so does the evaluation sentence that most students leave out. Higher Level adds quantitative demands and a further paper. The internally assessed commentaries need current articles and tight word discipline, and choosing the article badly costs more marks than writing the commentary badly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools applied to a real organisation, not recited. The common failure is a candidate who can define a framework and cannot use it on the case material in front of them. The internally assessed project needs an organisation that will actually supply information, which in the UAE is worth settling early rather than optimistically.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied text. The oral is where preparation shows most clearly, because it is built around a global issue and two chosen extracts. Practice has to happen on texts that are not the assessed ones, which is a boundary we keep to deliberately.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic can be a Diploma subject in its own right at either language level, which is separate from the Arabic lesson the Ministry requires every private school to run. Families frequently discover the two are different things in DP1. Arabic B rewards structured writing against the text types the guide lists, and oral fluency practised aloud rather than read.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work, essay structure and, at Higher Level, a third paper on a regional option. The internally assessed historical investigation is where students lose most: the source evaluation section is short, specific and heavily weighted, and a strong narrative with weak evaluation does not score.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for an argument, not listed. The experimental study written up for internal assessment is tightly specified, and candidates lose marks for an inexact replication or a results section that reports without interpreting. Higher Level adds extra topics and a further paper.

ib-diploma-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Which authority sits above your child's school depends on the emirate, and so does what that authority controls. Lessons reach all seven emirates the same way, over live video, so the differences below are about regulation, school supply and what time a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education here, across 227 schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25. Diploma supply is the deepest in the country, but a 4pm session still depends on Sheikh Zayed Road, which is exactly why an online slot starts when your child sits down.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by almost no tutoring site in this market. Island and Khalifa City families often have one or two realistic Diploma schools within reach, which narrows subject choice before tuition is even discussed.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with far fewer IB World Schools than the capital. Higher Level specialists are the pinch point rather than general subject help, and the drive that a visiting tutor would have to make is the reason an online specialist usually wins on both time and choice.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. An IB Diploma tutor in Sharjah therefore has to work with a school calendar the authority has signed off, not an invented one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. Families often commute to Sharjah or Dubai for a Diploma place, so the evening slot is set by the return journey rather than by the school bell, and a fixed online time removes that variable.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves curricula and assessment methods. Diploma cohorts are small, which makes an unavailable Higher Level option more likely and a specialist outside the emirate more useful.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, with the longest distances to a large IB cohort. This is where the visiting-tutor model breaks down first: there is no pool to draw from within a sensible drive, whatever rate a family is willing to pay.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The practical answer for a Diploma student here is online teaching with a specialist, planned around a commute that frequently crosses two emirates each school day.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the country's largest Diploma cohort, spread across schools that run the IB alone and schools that run it beside another curriculum. Programme offers change year to year, so confirm the current Diploma subject list with the school or against KHDA's own published listing before you plan a two-year route.

The capital's Diploma schools sit under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation in the emirate. Cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, so Higher Level option blocks are tighter and a subject combination that works on paper may not exist on the timetable. Ask before the choice form, not after.

Diploma places are fewer and further apart, which is the single clearest argument for teaching online rather than searching for a tutor nearby.

sections.heading: What the phrase 'Diploma home tutor' actually buys in the UAE right now
paragraphs: Three different services answer this one search. The first is an individual tutor who holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit and drives to your community; the permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The second is a tuition centre with premises, which in Dubai is a different legal animal again and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. The third is one-to-one tuition delivered over live video, which is what IB Gram provides to every family in the Emirates.

The visiting option is the one the search phrase implies, so price it properly. Published market figures for a visiting tutor in Dubai run from about AED 180 to AED 350 an hour at the mid tier and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors, with monthly visiting packages advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online bands sit below that: budget providers publish hourly figures from AED 33 to AED 65, qualified subject tutors from AED 150, IB specialists from around AED 200 to AED 450, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. The gap between the visiting band and the online band is not teaching quality. It is a car crossing the city at 5pm.

What that travel costs a Diploma family is not only money. It is the twenty minutes at the start of a session that belong to the road rather than to Paper 2, the cancelled lesson in a week with a sandstorm, and the hard geographic limit on who can teach your child at all. Families in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain feel this first: whatever rate you are willing to pay, the pool of people who can reach you and who have taught Higher Level Chemistry under IB moderation is very small.

IB Gram's position is plain. We teach UAE families one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing for the student's own work, and visiting tuition remains a service we run only in India. The first lesson is a free trial, with no card details taken, and if the fit is wrong we change the tutor rather than argue about it. What you give up is somebody in the room. What you get is the person who actually teaches your child's subject at your child's level, on a slot that starts on time in Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: Where the 45 points come from, and which of them tuition can move
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is not one number arrived at in one way. Six subjects are graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are read together to add up to three more, for 45. Inside each subject the marks split again: most of the grade comes from external papers marked by examiners who have never met your child, and a substantial slice, commonly around a fifth in the sciences and mathematics, comes from work marked by the school teacher and then moderated by the IB. Parents who understand that split ask much better questions at parents' evening.

The practical consequence is that different parts of the Diploma respond to different things. Paper technique responds quickly to coaching, because command terms, mark allocation and timing are learnable skills and a student who writes 'describe' answers to 'evaluate' questions can be retrained inside a term. Internally assessed work responds slowly, because it depends on a method chosen months earlier and on data the student actually collected. The core responds only to being started early. CAS responds to nothing at all except being done and evidenced.

This is also where an honest tutor has to be clear about limits. Nobody can promise a point total, and a provider promising a point total is describing something outside its own control: the papers are externally marked, the internal marks are moderated, and grade awards sit with the IB. What tuition can do is improve the work that goes into each component before it is marked, and give you a forecast based on work actually seen. A forecast that moves down after a bad mock is more useful than one that never moves.

Use the table below as the map of who marks what. It is also the quickest way to see why 'my child needs a tutor' is rarely the right sentence: what a Diploma student usually needs is a specific component fixed, and the component tells you what kind of help to buy.

sections.heading: The failing conditions nobody explains until February of DP2
paragraphs: Twenty-four points is the number families know. It is not the only test. A candidate can clear 24 and still not be awarded the Diploma, because the award also depends on how those points are distributed and on whether the core and CAS were completed. Every year, UAE DP2 families discover this in the spring, when a coordinator sits them down and explains that two low Standard Levels and an unfinished Theory of Knowledge essay have put the whole award at risk even though the total looks survivable.

The conditions are published, stable and genuinely useful to read in DP1 rather than DP2. Fewer than 24 points in total is a fail. A grade E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a fail on its own. A single grade 1 in any subject at either level is a fail. Three or more grade 2s is a fail, as is four or more grades of 3 or below. Higher Level and Standard Level carry separate floors: fewer than 12 points across the Higher Levels fails, and fewer than 9 across the Standard Levels fails. CAS requirements not met fails. Because the list can be refined between cohorts, confirm the version that applies to your child with the DP coordinator, who has the current handbook.

Read as a set, these conditions change what good tutoring looks like. The instinct is to put money behind the subject the student loves and is already strong in, because progress there is visible and pleasant. The arithmetic says otherwise: the award is usually threatened by the two or three subjects nobody is discussing, and by a core component that was left until the term it was due. One hour a week on the weakest Standard Level does more for the Diploma than a third hour on the strongest Higher Level.

It also changes what you should ask at a report cycle. Not 'how is she doing in Economics', but 'read me the six grades and the two core grades, and tell me which failing condition is closest'. Any tutor worth paying should be able to answer that for the subject they teach, and should tell you plainly when the answer is 'this is not the subject putting the Diploma at risk'.

sections.heading: Who decides what across a UAE Diploma year
paragraphs: This is the table we wish every Diploma family had in DP1. Almost every frustration that reaches us is really a misreading of who holds a particular lever. A parent spends three weeks trying to get a Higher Level added when the option block closed in June. Another asks a tutor to speak to the school about a predicted grade, which is not a conversation a paid tutor should be having. A third assumes the IB sets the Internal Assessment deadline, when the date that binds is the one the school set months earlier so it can mark and moderate before uploading.

The emirate authority sits further away from your daily decisions than its reputation suggests. It licenses and oversees the school, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah it also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. What it does not do is award your child's points or set your coursework dates. The IB awards the grades and sets the external framework. The Ministry of Education sets the mandatory subject requirement and, at the end, handles equivalency of the certificate. MoHRE governs whether the tutor may be paid at all.

Inside all of that, the school holds most of the levers that matter week to week: the option blocks, level changes, exam entries as the registered centre, predicted grades, and the internal calendar for the core and the Internal Assessments. That concentration is why the single most valuable thing a UAE parent can do in the first term of DP1 is ask the coordinator for the school's own written deadline calendar, and then plan everything, including tuition, backwards from it.

The right question to ask a prospective tutor is therefore not 'can you get her to a 7'. It is 'given that the school owns these decisions, what exactly will you change?' An honest answer is narrow and specific: the quality of the work before each of those decisions is made.

sections.heading: Option blocks: why your school may not teach the Higher Level your child needs
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. That last figure is the one Diploma families feel. A sector this large still produces small DP cohorts per school, and a small cohort cannot timetable every Higher Level against every other one. The result is the option block: a grid where Physics sits in the same column as Economics, and a student who wants both is told to choose.

Supply is improving rather than solved. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB schools eventually means more Diploma cohorts and more option combinations. It does nothing for a student already in DP1 whose timetable clash is live this term, and outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi the arithmetic is tighter still: in Al Ain, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain a family may have one realistic Diploma school within reach.

A clash cannot be solved by tuition, and no honest provider should pretend otherwise. A candidate is registered for the Diploma by an IB World School, so the subjects your child sits are the subjects the school enters them for. What tuition can do is make the forced choice survivable: carry the subject the student had to take at a level they can hold, protect the Higher Levels they did get, and keep the Higher Level point floor of 12 in view while doing it. Where a school cannot staff a Higher Level specialist for the subject it does run, a subject specialist outside the emirate is often the only realistic support available.

If you are still in MYP 5, this is the conversation to have a year early. Ask which Higher Levels the school expects to timetable, ask which combinations have failed to run in recent years, and ask what happens if too few students pick a subject. The answers are usually given honestly when asked in February and defensively when asked in September.

sections.heading: Your child's school is the examination centre, and that changes your deadlines
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate does not register with the IB. The school does, as the examination centre, and that single fact reorganises the family calendar. Exam entries are made by the school by the school's deadline. Subject and level changes have to be processed by the school through registration, which is why a request made in the same term as the problem is often possible and the same request made later is often not. Internally assessed work has to reach the school early enough for the teacher to mark it and for the IB to moderate, so the deadline that binds your child is the school's date, not the one on any published IB schedule.

This page publishes no IB session or results date. That is deliberate: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so nothing could be verified for this project, and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date at all. Your DP coordinator holds the authoritative calendar for your cohort. What is safe to say is that UAE schools sit the May session, that a November session also exists, and that the internal deadlines sit months ahead of the papers.

If you want to see how early entry deadlines really are, look at the examination boards that do publish. Cambridge International offers UAE candidates two series and no others: June and November. The February and March sitting belongs to India, and the March, May and October dates that circulate online are Checkpoint tests for younger year groups rather than IGCSE papers. That makes the choice in front of a Dubai family a straight one between a full teaching year ahead of June and a turnaround of about ten weeks between August results and the first November paper, and each series closes its entries months before anyone sits anything, on a date published for that series rather than carried over from last year. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it 'cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam' if the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with the November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026 and June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026. Those are sibling-subject facts for a family with an IGCSE child, and they illustrate the general rule: the administrative deadlines are months before the papers.

The practical move is dull and effective. In the first term of DP1, ask the coordinator for three things in writing: the internal deadline calendar for every Internal Assessment and core component, the date by which a level change must be requested, and the session the school intends to enter your child for. Pin tuition to those dates. A tutor who plans around a published external timetable instead of your school's internal one will be late twice.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, and the request a tutor should refuse
paragraphs: Predicted grades are issued by your child's subject teachers and signed off by the DP coordinator. Universities use them to make conditional offers, so for a UAE family applying to the UK, the US, Canada or into the region, these numbers arrive before any real results exist and do a great deal of work. They are not negotiable in the way parents sometimes hope, and they are not a reward for effort. They are a professional judgement based on evidence: mock papers sat under conditions, Internal Assessment drafts, classwork, and the teacher's read of trajectory.

What this means for tuition is a question of timing. Support that arrives before the evidence is gathered can genuinely change the prediction, because the mock paper that gets marked in November is the mock paper the prediction rests on. Support that arrives after predictions are issued changes the final grade, which still matters enormously, but it will not retrospectively improve an offer already made on a lower number. Families who come to us in DP1 about a subject that is drifting are usually surprised at how much of the prediction is still in play; families who arrive after offers have landed are often really asking about the final session, and should be told that plainly.

There is a line here that a paid tutor must not cross. A tutor should not contact your child's school to argue for a higher prediction, should not coach a student to present work that is not theirs as evidence, and should not offer to supply coursework that lifts a teacher's judgement. Any of those turns a legitimate service into interference in a school's professional process, and in the coursework case into academic malpractice with consequences that land on the student rather than on the provider. The acceptable version is narrow and effective: better work, produced by the student, in front of the teacher making the judgement.

What we will give you is our own forecast, based on the work the tutor has seen, with its reasoning attached and its uncertainty admitted. Where it differs from the school's prediction, the useful conversation is about which pieces of evidence the two of you are each looking at. That is a conversation a coordinator will have. A demand for a different number is not.
