process.title: Tell us the school and the authority above it
process.description: The first thing we ask is which school and which emirate, because that tells us the licensing authority, the mandatory subject load, the option-block style and the internal deadline culture. A Diploma student at a Sharjah-regulated school and one at a KHDA school in Al Barsha are planning around different weeks.

process.title: Send the subject combination, the levels and the session
process.description: Six subjects, which three or four are Higher Level, whether your child is a full Diploma or course candidate, and which examination session they are entered for. We also ask for the school's internal deadline list for internal assessments and the Extended Essay, because that calendar decides the order of work.

process.title: One diagnostic piece of work
process.description: A recent marked paper or a current draft, whichever matters more. We read it against the published criteria and come back with what is costing marks: content gaps, command-term misreading, criterion coverage or timing. This is also where we say honestly if tuition is not the right purchase yet.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge, then a plan
process.description: One free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, with no payment taken and no card details needed to book it. If the match is wrong you say so and we try again or step back. If it works, you get a written plan naming subjects, session count per week, and what the first half-term is meant to change.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written record
process.description: Lessons run over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with a short written note after each one: what was covered, what to practise, what is due at school next. The slot moves for the examination block, Ramadan timings and the school's mock window rather than being billed through them.

process.title: Reviewed against the school's own reports
process.description: Every half-term we compare what the school reports with what the sessions show. If the gap is closing, hours come down. If a subject has stabilised and the core has not, hours move. Tuition that never reduces is tuition nobody is measuring.

whyPoints.title: The school system is explained, not assumed
whyPoints.description: This page names which authority licenses your child's school, what that authority approves, how the mandatory UAE subjects sit in a Diploma week, and where a family can push. No competing page on this search names ADEK at all, and two mention the Dubai authority only inside a lead-capture widget.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and mark allocations in writing
whyPoints.description: Criterion letters, mark totals and word limits for the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge components, the mathematics exploration, the science investigation and the history investigation, with a clear instruction to verify them against the current subject guide. These are what internal assessment marks are actually decided by.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Market rates are published here in the currency UAE families transact in, attributed to whoever published them and dated October 2026. Where we do not have a sourced number, including any IB points figure for Ministry equivalency, the page says so instead of inventing one.

whyPoints.title: A stated position on academic honesty
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student produced. Nothing is supplied, rewritten or finished on the student's behalf, and we say so in detail because at least one provider ranking on these searches sells finished internal assessments.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from any emirate
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so a Fujairah or Ras Al Khaimah family can work with a Higher Level specialist in the subject they need rather than whoever lives nearby. Where no specialist is free for a combination, we say that rather than substituting a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Hours planned to come down
whyPoints.description: Plans are written with an end in view: a diagnostic first, a named target for the half-term, then a review against the school's own report. Diploma tuition that runs at the same intensity from DP1 to the final paper is usually a billing arrangement rather than a plan.

faqs.question: How many subjects does the Diploma require, and how many have to be at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Six subjects: one from each of the first five groups and a sixth from the arts or a second subject from groups one to four. Three of the six run at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and some schools allow a fourth Higher Level where the timetable permits it. Each subject is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three more from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together. Your child's coordinator confirms the exact combination registered, which matters because what is registered, not what is attended, is what gets graded.

faqs.question: Where do the three extra Diploma points come from, and can tuition help earn them?
faqs.answer: They come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which are considered together on a published matrix rather than scored separately. Strong performance in both can add up to three points; weak performance in both can fail the Diploma outright regardless of subject grades. Tuition helps by teaching what the criteria reward, narrowing a research question that is too broad, and giving criterion-by-criterion feedback on drafts the student has written. It cannot supply text or choose the question, and both components are supervised in school with recorded sessions, so the work has to be genuinely the student's.

faqs.question: What is creativity, activity, service, and does my child need tutoring for it?
faqs.answer: It is the third part of the Diploma core, running across both years in three strands, and it carries no points. It is signed off by the school's coordinator rather than marked, and an incomplete record can cost the Diploma even where the points total is comfortable. No, it does not need tutoring, and anyone offering to manage it for a fee is selling something your child is supposed to do themselves. The practical risk in UAE schools is the reflective record rather than the activities: students do plenty and document almost none of it until the deadline is close.

faqs.question: Two of my child's Diploma choices sit in the same option block. What can be done?
faqs.answer: Nothing a tutor can fix, so deal with it inside the school first. Option blocks are a timetabling structure: one subject per column, and two subjects in the same column cannot both be taken. Ask the coordinator whether the block can be rebuilt, whether the subject runs in another column in alternate years, and whether the school will support the subject outside the timetable. If the answer closes a university route, the realistic options are a different subject at the same level, the same subject at a lower level, or covering the content separately while understanding what that does and does not change on the transcript.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a full Diploma candidate and a course candidate?
faqs.answer: A full Diploma candidate takes six subjects across the groups plus the core and receives a points total out of 45. A course candidate takes individual Diploma subjects and receives a certificate for each, with no points total and no requirement to cover all six groups. UAE schools use the course route for mid-programme arrivals and for students whose combination will not fit the blocks. It changes tutoring priorities completely: there is no points total to protect, so hours go to the specific subject grades universities will read rather than to balancing a weak sixth subject.

faqs.question: Which failing conditions can cost the Diploma even when the points total looks safe?
faqs.answer: The points total is necessary but not sufficient. The published conditions cover matters such as an incomplete creativity, activity and service record, a grade 1 in any subject, repeated low grades at Higher Level, and an E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay. A student can therefore clear the points bar and still not be awarded the Diploma. Ask your child's coordinator for the current list in writing early in DP2, because every one of those conditions is visible months in advance and most are fixable while there is still time.

faqs.question: Who decides the predicted grades that go on a university application?
faqs.answer: Your child's subject teachers, through the school, not a tutor and not the IB. Predicted grades are the school's professional judgement based on the work it has seen, and they are submitted with the application while the real examinations are still months away. A tutor's useful contribution is indirect: better work in front of the teacher before predictions are set. Anyone who implies they can influence a prediction is describing something they do not control. If a prediction looks wrong, that conversation belongs with the subject teacher and the coordinator, in that order.

faqs.question: Which group does Arabic sit in for the Diploma, and what does that choice change?
faqs.answer: Arabic A can serve as a group one language for an Arab student, and Arabic B is a group two second-language course. The choice changes the assessment entirely, from literary analysis in one case to oral and written language work in the other. Separately from the Diploma, Dubai private schools must run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. So the two questions parents tend to merge, which Diploma language group and which school Arabic stream, are genuinely different questions with different answers.

faqs.question: Can my child take a Standard Level subject a year early as an anticipated subject?
faqs.answer: Some schools allow one Standard Level subject to be completed and examined at the end of DP1, which lightens the final year. Whether it is available depends on the school rather than the student, so ask the coordinator before assuming it. The trade-off is real: an anticipated subject moves an examination into a year that already carries the Extended Essay and the first internal assessments. For a student who is comfortable in that subject it can work well. For a student already stretched, it concentrates pressure in the wrong year.

faqs.question: May a tutor be present for the Individual Oral or the Theory of Knowledge exhibition?
faqs.answer: No. Those are assessed events run by the school, and an outside adult has no place in them. What a tutor can legitimately do beforehand is teach the criteria, run practice questions on different material, and give feedback on the student's own preparation notes. For the oral in particular, rehearsing with unseen extracts is useful and rehearsing a script is counter-productive, because the marks follow the quality of the live analysis. The school sets the conditions for both components and the coordinator is the person to ask about anything procedural.

faqs.question: What does my child declare when coursework is submitted, and where does a paid tutor stand?
faqs.answer: Assessed work is submitted with an authenticity declaration, and the school's supervisor signs to confirm it is the student's own. Extended Essay supervision sessions are recorded, and coordinators ask about outside assistance directly. A tutor is permitted in that picture as a teacher: content, criteria, questions, marked practice and written feedback on the student's draft. A tutor is not permitted to supply text, rewrite sections or make the judgements. The test a parent can apply at home is simple: can your child explain every sentence they submitted, and why it is there?

faqs.question: How does a Diploma lesson work over live video when the working is on paper?
faqs.answer: A shared whiteboard carries the working, and both people write on it. Your child photographs a handwritten attempt before the session so the tutor can read it in advance, or works live on the board while talking through the steps. Past papers are worked under timed conditions and marked against the mark scheme afterwards. The session leaves a written record of the board, which a kitchen-table lesson does not. What live video cannot do is run a laboratory experiment; the practical belongs at school, while the design and the data analysis are taught online.

faqs.question: Which published AED figures can we check a Diploma tuition quote against?
faqs.answer: The ones on this page, each attributed to whoever published it and read in October 2026. Budget online tuition is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya; Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table runs from AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists; BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are other companies' figures, not ours. Use them to judge whether a quote is inside the market, then ask what the hour actually contains before comparing two numbers.

faqs.question: Our school is being inspected during the first Diploma year. Does that affect my child?
faqs.answer: Usually less than the staffroom suggests, but two things are worth knowing. Inspection weeks compress teaching time and can push internal deadlines, so check whether any internal assessment dates have moved. And the published report that follows is the single most useful document you will read about the school, because it separates attainment from progress and comments on teaching by phase. Read it from the authority that licenses your school rather than from a tutoring site, and read the subject detail rather than only the headline band.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma student add a fourth Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: The Diploma allows four Higher Levels where the school's timetable supports it, and it is not automatically a good idea. Each Higher Level carries 240 published guided teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, so a fourth one adds the equivalent of a whole extra subject's teaching alongside the core and, in Dubai, the mandatory UAE subjects. The students who manage it are usually strong, well organised and not relying on tuition to hold three other subjects up. Ask the coordinator what the school's experience of it has been with recent cohorts.

faqs.question: The shortened Ramadan timetable lands on top of the DP2 mocks. How should the plan change?
faqs.answer: Sequence it rather than fight it. School days shorten, energy shifts later, and the mock window often sits close by. We move sessions to post-Iftar slots where that suits the household, reduce session length and raise frequency so concentration holds, and keep the heaviest timed-paper work for after Eid. What should not slip into that period is coursework with a school deadline immediately after the break, so the realistic plan brings internal assessment drafts forward by a fortnight and leaves Ramadan for consolidation and short, focused paper practice.

faqs.question: Which authority attests a Diploma transcript, and what should we not take on trust?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation channels handle equivalency and attestation for international secondary certificates. No school and no tutoring company performs it, and nobody should charge you to arrange it. What not to take on trust is any points figure for the IB Diploma published on a commercial site, including this one: we have not read an official Ministry threshold, so we do not print a number. The British-track requirements are published and specific, and one competing page on these searches states the subject count wrongly. Verify on moe.gov.ae.

ib-dp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the school's own paperwork, then one trial lesson
ib-dp-tutor.closingBody: Before paying anyone, read two documents: your school's latest inspection report from the authority that licenses it, and the internal deadline list for your child's internal assessments and Extended Essay. Those two tell you more about whether tuition will help than any tutoring website can. Then send us the school, the emirate, the six subjects with their levels and the examination session, plus one recent marked paper or current draft. We read it against the published criteria, propose a tutor, and run one trial lesson at no charge with no card details taken. If the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What Economics portfolio help costs here, and what the money actually buys
paragraphs: IB Economics IA help in the UAE is paid one-to-one teaching time spent on the three commentaries that form the Economics portfolio. It is teaching, questioning and feedback on drafts the student has written. The market band is public if you go looking: Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Online tuition from a qualified subject teacher starts lower, from roughly AED 150. None of those figures is ours; they are what this market charges.

Where those hours sit in the year decides whether they were worth paying for. A commentary is won or lost at three points: the article chosen, the diagram picked to explain it, and the evaluation paragraph that weighs one effect against another. Most families buy hours at a fourth point, the fortnight before upload, when the article is fixed, the diagram is drawn and the word count is already blown. Those hours cost exactly the same and change far less. Booking earlier is the cheapest single decision available to a UAE family, and it costs nothing to make.

Economics is also a thin subject in staffing terms. A Dubai or Abu Dhabi school running the Diploma may have one Economics teacher covering both Standard and Higher Level, two year groups and portfolio supervision for all of them. That teacher marks the portfolio and a sample of those marks goes to the IB for moderation, so the teacher's judgement is the starting number. A parent paying for outside help is buying a second reader who knows the criteria by letter and mark, not a replacement writer. The distinction is the whole of what follows on this page.

There is a version of this service sold in the UAE that we will not sell. Sites advertise finished commentaries at four-figure AED prices, and one researched provider lists completed Internal Assessments outright. Submitting text the student did not produce is malpractice under IB academic-honesty rules, the sanction lands on the candidate rather than the seller, and both your child and the teacher sign to say the work is genuine. The money is better spent on five to eight hours of teaching, which costs about the same and leaves a student who can explain every line of the file.

Lessons for UAE families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. No tutor is sent to a UAE address; home visiting is a service IB Gram offers only in India. For portfolio work that is an advantage rather than a compromise: a screen-shared draft with version history is the format the task wants, a 25-minute check on a diagram is a sensible booking, and a family in Al Ain gets the same Economics specialist as a family in Jumeirah. The sections below put AED figures, criterion marks and a backwards calendar against each of those claims.

ib-economics-ia-help.programmesIntro: Economics sits inside a wider IB structure, and the portfolio competes for time with everything else in it. These are the parts of the programme that touch a UAE Economics student's year, with what each one does to the calendar and the budget.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics runs at Standard and Higher Level inside the Individuals and Societies group. Standard Level sits Paper 1 and Paper 2; Higher Level adds Paper 3, the policy paper, which rewards calculation and a recommended policy. The portfolio of three commentaries is internally marked and externally moderated, and it is the only component of the subject the student controls the timing of. That makes it the one place where paid support can change a number months ahead of the examination.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is a minority curriculum in the UAE and a growing one. Dubai's private sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate at 7% of enrolment, according to the Dubai Media Office. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate. A thin cohort means few Economics teachers per school and a small local pool of specialists, which is exactly why delivery format matters.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and the Diploma core
programmes.description: An Economics Extended Essay is a 4,000-word research project with its own criteria, and it is frequently written by the same students who find the 800-word commentary hard. The skills overlap: a researchable question, data that exists, and an argument that weighs effects rather than listing them. TOK adds an essay and an exhibition. A student carrying an Economics Extended Essay plus the portfolio has two writing projects running against the same term.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma cohorts tend to hit core deadlines in the same fortnight, because schools across Dubai and Abu Dhabi set internal dates to similar term structures. The practical consequence for a family budgeting support is that Economics portfolio hours and Extended Essay hours compete for the same weeks in DP1 summer and DP2 autumn. Deciding which one gets paid attention first is a planning question worth one session, not a reason to double the spend.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in the Middle Years Programme is assessed against criteria A to D, and its investigation tasks are the closest thing a pre-Diploma student does to a commentary. Students who arrive in DP1 from Middle Years Programme Individuals and Societies often know how to research and not how to diagram. Those arriving from IGCSE Economics usually know the diagrams and not the evaluation. Both gaps are specific and both are cheap to close before DP1 begins.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma on one campus, and others feed the Diploma from an IGCSE Year 11. A family moving between the two inside the UAE should expect a different starting point for Economics: the Middle Years route brings stronger investigation habits, the IGCSE route brings stronger diagram technique. Naming which one your child comes from in the first message saves a session of diagnosis.

ib-economics-ia-help.subjectsIntro: IB Economics SL and HL is what this page is about, but the portfolio term rarely arrives alone. These are the subjects whose own internal assessments land in the same weeks for a UAE Diploma student, with what each one takes out of the calendar.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries of 800 words, 45 marks, one per syllabus unit and one key concept each. Standard Level sits two papers, Higher Level three. The portfolio is the component a tutor can legitimately help with months in advance, and the component most often left until the term it is due.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project with a defined word limit, built on real organisational data. Students who take Business Management alongside Economics often reuse the same analytical habits and the same bad habit: describing a situation instead of weighing options. The two subjects' assessment calendars overlap in DP2 autumn at most UAE schools.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Fieldwork-based written report with primary data collection. The data-gathering stage cannot be compressed, so a Geography student also writing Economics commentaries has a fixed immovable block in the calendar. Knowing where that block sits is the difference between a workable plan and three late drafts.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: An engagement activity and written report requiring sustained contact with a political issue. Economics students taking it tend to find the evaluation criterion easier, because the subject trains it. The reverse is also true: a Global Politics student who struggles to weigh perspectives will struggle with criterion E in Economics.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A historical investigation with a source evaluation section and a strict word limit. The source-criticism habit transfers directly to screening a news article for an Economics commentary. Students doing both often produce the sharpest article choices in a cohort, because they already ask who wrote this and what is missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The exploration is a mathematics project of its own, and it is the usual pairing for Economics students. Applications and Interpretation carries statistics and modelling that help with Higher Level Paper 3 calculation work. Check the published entry requirements of any economics degree your child is aiming at, because some prefer the other route.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus-heavy and the route some university economics programmes name in their own published requirements. A Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student handles Paper 3 calculation comfortably but has the heaviest exploration deadline in the cohort. Verify the requirement on the university's own page rather than on any tutoring site, including this one.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: An experimental study report with its own criteria and ethical constraints. Psychology's report writing is tightly structured, which suits students who find the open brief of an Economics commentary intimidating. The two internal assessments usually fall in different terms, so the pairing is a scheduling relief rather than a clash.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An individual investigation with data collection and analysis. The subject shares vocabulary with Economics around sustainability and externalities, and students sometimes try to reuse a commentary topic here. Each piece of assessed work must be separate, and schools check, so overlap of subject matter is a conversation to have with both teachers first.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the higher level essay sit in the same DP2 window as the final commentary for many UAE cohorts. For a student whose written expression is the limiting factor in Economics, hours bought here sometimes move the Economics mark more than hours bought on economics content.

ib-economics-ia-help.regionsTitle: Where Economics portfolio deadlines land across the emirates
ib-economics-ia-help.regionsIntro: The portfolio is identical wherever your child sits it, but the practical detail is not: when a session can start, which schools set which internal deadlines, and which UAE stories the local cohort reaches for when choosing an article. These notes are what families in each area actually tell us.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: A dense Diploma belt with several schools setting internal portfolio deadlines inside the same fortnight. Students here reach for Dubai-specific stories first, from utility tariff changes to school fee policy, and two commentaries from the same story run the risk of a thin second source.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Sheikh Zayed Road and the tram mean a 4pm start is unreliable for a student travelling home, so most Marina families book at 6pm or later. A Dubai IB Economics tutor working to that slot can hold a weekly 45-minute checkpoint without touching homework time.

regions.name: Academic City, Silicon Oasis and Mirdif
regions.note: Longer school runs and more mixed-curriculum households. Economics students here often have siblings on IGCSE timetables, so the family calendar is already full of exam weeks. Short, fixed, same-time-every-week sessions survive that better than long weekend blocks.

regions.name: Al Reem Island, Saadiyat and Al Raha
regions.note: Abu Dhabi Diploma families whose schools answer to ADEK rather than KHDA. Local article choices skew towards Abu Dhabi infrastructure and energy policy, which is useful for the global economy unit and risky for microeconomics, where a narrower market story works better.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Villa communities with a long drive to the island schools. Parents here are the most likely to have priced an in-home tutor and found the travel premium inside the quoted hour. The comparison table further down this page is the one they ask for.

regions.name: Sharjah: Al Khan, Al Majaz and Muwailih
regions.note: Schools in Sharjah answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves fees, curricula and assessment methods as well as inspecting. The Diploma offer is thinner than in Dubai, so some Sharjah students commute across the border and lose an hour each way to the morning queue.

regions.name: Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
regions.note: The thinnest Diploma provision in the country, and the clearest case for online delivery. A student in Fujairah taking Economics Higher Level may be the only one in their year group doing so. Ras Al Khaimah schools answer to the emirate's Department of Knowledge; Fujairah's answer to the federal Ministry of Education.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of Diploma Economics cohorts in the country, and the one where internal deadlines cluster tightest. Students we support in this group most often need help with the global economy unit, because it is taught last and the third commentary is the one that runs out of time.

Schools here answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. For a family planning Economics support that matters mainly because ADEK's staff ethics rules restrict who may be paid to teach your child privately, as the section on permits sets out.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Diploma provision thins out north of Dubai, and Economics Higher Level thins out faster still. Families in this cluster are the ones most likely to be told no local specialist is available for a niche unit, which is why the availability and fallback rules on this page are published rather than discovered later.

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying when they search for Economics IA help
paragraphs: IB Economics IA help in the UAE is paid teaching time on the three commentaries that make up the Economics portfolio. It is not an editing service and it is not a writing service. The market band for IB subject specialists in this country runs roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour: Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Online tuition from a qualified subject teacher starts closer to AED 150.

What the hours are spent on decides whether they were worth buying. A commentary turns on the article chosen, the diagram selected to explain it, and the evaluation paragraph that weighs one effect against another. Families overwhelmingly buy hours after all three of those decisions have been made badly, in the fortnight before upload, when the only remaining move is cutting words. Those hours cost the same as the early ones and achieve a fraction as much. Nobody in this market tells parents that, because the late booking is the profitable one.

Economics is also thinly staffed. A UAE school running the Diploma may have one Economics teacher covering Standard and Higher Level, two year groups, and portfolio supervision for every one of those students. That teacher marks the portfolio and a sample goes to the IB for moderation, so the teacher's mark is the number everything else moves around. What a parent is buying from outside is a second reader who knows the Economics IA criteria by letter and by mark allocation, and who will ask the student the questions the teacher has no time to ask twice.

sections.heading: The Economics portfolio, criterion by criterion, with the marks attached
paragraphs: The portfolio is three commentaries. Each takes a different published news article, covers a different unit of the syllabus, and uses a different key concept. Each is capped at 800 words. Each is marked out of 15 against five criteria, which gives 45 marks across the portfolio, and the portfolio carries roughly 30% of the Standard Level grade and 20% at Higher Level. Those numbers are the entire basis for deciding where to spend money, and almost no competing page in this market prints them.

The five criteria are diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, key concept, and evaluation. They are not equally weighted and they are not equally difficult. Evaluation carries four marks a commentary, twelve across the portfolio, and is the criterion most drafts never reach properly. The key concept carries three a commentary, nine in total, and is the one students name in a title and then forget. Diagrams also carry three, and are usually the best-prepared part of the work by the time anyone pays for help.

Read the table below as a spending plan rather than a syllabus summary. Twenty-one of the 45 marks sit in evaluation and key concept, so that is where paid hours earn most. Six marks sit in terminology, which is close to free to fix once a student stops defining words they never use again. Confirm the current criteria wording and mark allocations against the subject guide your child's school issues, because the IB revises subject guides and the school's copy is the one that applies.

sections.heading: Where the 45 marks actually leak
paragraphs: The article is the first leak and the most expensive. An article with no numbers in it leaves nothing to analyse, so criterion C collapses. An opinion column reporting no event gives the student nothing to diagram, so criterion A follows. An article covering three policies at once cannot be handled inside the Economics commentary word limit of 800 words, so the evaluation gets cut to fit and criterion E goes with it. One bad choice therefore damages three criteria at once, which is why twenty minutes of screening is worth more than an hour of editing.

The second leak is the Economics key concept. Students pick one at the planning stage, write it into the title, and then write a commentary that would read identically without it. The criterion wants the concept doing work: if the concept is intervention, the analysis has to be about what the intervention changes and what it costs; if it is interdependence, the argument has to cross a border or a market boundary. A tutor's job here is to ask, at every paragraph, which sentence is carrying the concept.

The third leak is the word count, and it is structural rather than editorial. Commentaries that run over usually spend 150 words restating the article, 80 more on definitions, and arrive at evaluation with no room left. Teachers and examiners stop reading at the limit, so the four-mark criterion is the one that vanishes. The fix is to cut the summary paragraph and move evaluation earlier, not to shave adjectives. Check with the school what counts towards the limit, because practice on footnotes, captions and diagram labels varies between schools.

sections.heading: What Economics portfolio support costs in the UAE
paragraphs: Here are IB Economics tuition rates in AED as this market publishes them, with the source named on every row. Nothing in the table is an IB Gram price list; our own arrangement starts with a free first lesson of one hour, with no card details taken, and a conversation about how many hours the remaining work actually needs. Quoting someone else's rates honestly is more useful to a parent than quoting ours without context, and three of the six competing pages researched in this market publish no price at all.

Read the fourth row carefully, because it is the one families ask for most and the one that returns least. A pre-upload read-through buys a reader for work that can no longer change much: the article is fixed, the diagrams are drawn, the structure is set. It is the same hourly rate as a session in week one and it moves a fraction of the marks. If your budget stretches to only two hours this term, spend them at article choice rather than at the end, even if the end feels more urgent.

Two practical cautions on any quote in this market. Ask whether the figure includes VAT, and get the answer in writing rather than assuming either way. Ask what is inside the hour: some providers bill materials, mock marking or a report separately, and a cheaper headline rate with charged extras can land higher than a dearer all-in one. Ask also how a replacement works if the first match is wrong, because that is the term most likely to be missing from a cheap quote.

sections.heading: What moves the number up or down, and the question to ask first
paragraphs: A quote for Economics portfolio support can differ fourfold between two providers in the same emirate, and almost none of the difference is explained on their pages. Six things move it: who is teaching, which level, when you book, what format, how the hour is delivered, and what is billed outside the hour. A parent who asks the six questions in the final column of the table below will understand a quote better than most of the market intends them to.

Tutor background is the largest single driver. The budget end of this market, roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour at EdFlik and Tutopiya's published starting rates, is largely university students and recent graduates. That can work for syllabus content. It works much less often for portfolio supervision, where the value is in having read dozens of commentaries against the criteria and knowing what a teacher will flag. Ask directly which units and which key concepts a tutor has supervised, and at which level.

Timing is the driver families control and ignore. A booking made in DP1, before any article is chosen, spreads three to five hours per commentary across quiet weeks. The same spend inside the final fortnight buys triage. Delivery format is the one worth naming plainly: an in-home rate in this market, AED 180 to AED 500 an hour on Bestimate's and local home-tutor figures, has travel inside it. You pay for the drive whether or not anybody teaches during it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with a commentary
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that costs us work and keeps your child's Diploma intact. A tutor may teach the economics, explain a criterion, ask why a paragraph exists, point at a sentence and say this does not analyse, and refuse to accept a vague answer. A tutor may not compose any part of the commentary, supply a sentence to be pasted in, rewrite a paragraph into finished form, or choose the article. Everything in the file must be the student's own production, and the student signs to say so.

The practical test we use with UAE families is whether the student could be asked about any line in the file by their teacher and answer it unprompted. If a sentence exists that the student cannot explain or did not build, it should not be there, regardless of who wrote it or how good it is. Schools in this country ask that question more often than parents expect, because teachers authenticate the work before it is marked and a sample goes to the IB for moderation.

The commercial reason this matters is that a competing market exists for exactly the opposite service. Researchers found a provider in this cluster advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That purchase puts the student, not the seller, in front of a malpractice process whose sanctions can reach the whole Diploma rather than one subject. Paid proofreading sits in a greyer place: ask your child's coordinator what your school permits, because the school's own policy on third-party help is the rule that applies to your child.

sections.heading: The portfolio counted backwards from your school's upload deadline
paragraphs: No IB examination or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checks, so nothing in this project confirms an IB session date from the source, and publishing an unverified one across a large set of pages would be worse than publishing none. Instead the table below counts backwards from the date your child's school sets, which is the date that governs the work anyway. Confirm every row with your Diploma coordinator, who holds the real calendar.

The logic of counting backwards is not ours either, and the clearest published illustration comes from a different board. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE November 2026 series runs its final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026, the entry window closes months before that first paper, and the results from the equivalent November 2025 series only reached students on 22 January 2026. Almost all of the administrative work sits ahead of the assessment and the feedback sits a long way behind it. Internal assessment behaves the same way: an Economics portfolio deadline is a point by which three separate pieces of production must already be finished, not a day to work towards.

Use the table to find the week you are in now and read down from there. If you are inside four weeks and commentary three is not drafted, the honest position is that paid help is doing damage control rather than adding marks, and it should be priced accordingly. If you are 16 weeks out, one session mapping all three commentaries is likely the highest-value hour available to you this year, and it costs one hour at the market rate rather than fifteen.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home Economics tutor in this market
paragraphs: Hiring somebody to teach Economics at a UAE address is a real market with real rates, and a parent asking about it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and independent home tutors in this market advertise AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate widely. Travel time sits inside all of those numbers whether or not it is itemised.

IB Gram does not operate that way in the Emirates. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address; visiting tuition is a service we provide only in India. For portfolio work specifically, the online format is the better fit rather than the cheaper compromise. A commentary is a document. Screen-sharing a document, with a version history showing what changed and who changed it, is exactly the evidence an authentication question needs, and a paper draft across a table leaves none.

The pool argument matters more in Economics than in most subjects. An online IB Economics tutor can be matched by syllabus unit and level rather than by driving distance, which is decisive for a Higher Level student in Fujairah or Al Ain who may be the only one in their year taking the subject. Scheduling follows: a 25-minute check on one diagram is a sensible booking over video and an absurd one for someone who has just driven 40 minutes to reach a villa.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and who may legally be paid to tutor
paragraphs: UAE private schools answer to five different bodies, and no competing page researched in this market names all of them. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate'. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge 'supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools'. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulate private education in their emirates and approve fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

Paid private tutoring is separately regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service, listed as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Working without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so none is quoted here.

Two points follow for a family buying Economics support. First, you may ask any prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, and a straight answer is reasonable to expect. Second, your child's own Economics teacher is the wrong person to pay. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement. Verify the current wording with the school and the regulator before agreeing to anything, and treat the mark-and-help conflict as a reason on its own.

sections.heading: Equivalency, universities and the route after Economics
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency looks at the certificate rather than at individual components, so no single commentary decides it. The published British-track rule is specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page ranking in this market states six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold is published on this page, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel directly. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

The decision that does follow from Economics is the mathematics route. University economics programmes publish their own entry requirements and some name Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. Read the requirement on the university's own admissions page rather than on any tutoring site, including this one, and read it before the subject choice is locked at the end of DP1. A student heading for a quantitative economics degree with Applications and Interpretation Standard Level has a harder conversation than one who checked in Year 11.

process.title: Send the brief, not the panic
process.description: Four lines is enough: the level, which unit and key concept each commentary is meant to cover, the school's internal deadline, and what state each draft is in. That tells us whether you need three hours or ten, and whether any of it is still worth buying. A message that says help with Economics IA costs a session to unpick.

process.title: Free first lesson, one hour, no card
process.description: One tutor, one hour, no card details taken and nothing to cancel afterwards. Bring a real draft or a real article shortlist rather than a general chat, because the point is to see whether this tutor asks your child useful questions about their own work. If the answer is no, say so and we match differently.

process.title: Agree the hours in writing before money moves
process.description: You get the number of hours, the stage each one covers, what is inside the hour and what is not, and whether VAT is included. If a provider in this market will not put that in writing, that is information too. We would rather sell three useful hours than a fifteen-hour block that nobody can justify at the end of term.

process.title: Checkpoints against the school's calendar
process.description: Sessions are set against the deadlines your child's school published, not against a generic schedule. If the school moves a date, the plan moves with it. The checkpoints that matter are article approval, first full draft and the final word-count cut, and each of those is short rather than a full hour of talking.

process.title: Stop, pause, or change the match
process.description: Pause for school examinations without losing the slot. Stop after any session. Change the tutor if the match is wrong, and the replacement starts from the notes rather than from the beginning. If no specialist is free for a niche unit at the level you need, we say so on the first call instead of booking somebody who will improvise.

whyPoints.title: The AED numbers are published and sourced
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page carries the provider that published it and the month the figure was read. Three of the six competing pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. A parent should be able to check a number before deciding whether it is reasonable.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may do with a commentary, and what no payment buys, is set out on this page rather than left to a conversation. A provider in this cluster advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. The sanction for submitting that work falls on the student, so the boundary belongs in public where a parent can read it before paying.

whyPoints.title: Specialists by syllabus unit, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Matching is done on level and unit: microeconomics, macroeconomics or the global economy, Standard or Higher Level, with or without Paper 3. A Higher Level student in Ras Al Khaimah gets the same specialist as one in Jumeirah, because nothing in the match depends on driving distance to the student's community.

whyPoints.title: Gulf Standard Time, Ramadan included
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time, and a slot that normally sits at 5pm can move to after Iftar during Ramadan without anybody travelling. Families often keep one short weekly checkpoint through the month and shift heavier drafting work to the fortnight after Eid, which is a planning decision rather than a scheduling favour.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not discovered
whyPoints.description: Economics Higher Level with Paper 3 is a narrow specialism, and there are weeks when no UAE-based tutor is free for it. When that happens we say so, name the alternative, including a specialist based outside the UAE teaching over the same video link, and let you decide. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How much does IB Economics IA help cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours: online tuition from a qualified subject teacher runs about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and IB specialists AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. One commentary usually absorbs three to five hours, so a single piece lands between roughly AED 450 and AED 2,250 depending on who teaches it. Ask whether a quoted figure includes VAT, and ask what is inside the hour before paying for it.

faqs.question: What is in the IB Economics portfolio, and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Three commentaries. Each takes a different published news article, covers a different unit of the syllabus and uses a different key concept, and each is capped at 800 words. Each is marked out of 15 against five criteria, which gives 45 marks across the portfolio. The portfolio carries roughly 30% of the Standard Level grade and 20% at Higher Level. Your child's school sets the submission dates, marks the work and authenticates it, and the IB moderates a sample of those marks. Confirm the current criteria wording against the subject guide your school issues, because guides are revised.

faqs.question: Which Economics commentary criterion loses the most marks?
faqs.answer: Evaluation, criterion E, carries four marks a commentary and twelve across the portfolio, the largest single block, and it is where most drafts stop short. A student who lists the stakeholders affected by a policy has described rather than evaluated. The marks come from weighing short run against long run, naming the assumptions behind a diagram, and saying which effect is larger and why. The key concept, criterion D, is the second leak at nine marks: named in the title and then abandoned. Diagrams carry nine and are usually the best-prepared part of the work.

faqs.question: Is it better value to pay for one commentary or all three?
faqs.answer: Pay for the first one properly, then decide. The first commentary is where the habits form: how an article is screened, how a diagram is labelled and tied into the text, how an evaluation paragraph is built. A student who learns that on commentary one often needs half the hours on commentaries two and three. Buying a fifteen-hour block in advance fixes a price before anybody knows which units will be hard. The usual advice we give UAE families is three to five hours on commentary one, then a review of what still needs buying.

faqs.question: Why does the news article choice decide so much of the mark?
faqs.answer: Because almost every criterion depends on it. An article with no numbers leaves nothing to analyse. One older than the window your school permits is not admissible whatever its quality. An opinion column reporting no event gives nothing to diagram. An article covering three policies at once cannot be handled inside 800 words, so the evaluation gets cut to fit. Screening is fast work: twenty minutes with a tutor who knows the units can replace a fortnight of rewriting. Sources must differ across the portfolio, so the screening has to consider all three pieces together.

faqs.question: Can a tutor pick the article my daughter writes about?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is doing her no favours. The selection is part of the assessed work and her school will expect her to show the choice was hers. What a tutor may do is teach her how to screen: does the article report an event, does it contain data, is it inside the permitted date window, does it sit in a unit she has studied, can one diagram carry it. She brings five candidates to the session and leaves having rejected four for reasons she can explain to her teacher unprompted.

faqs.question: What happens if a commentary goes over 800 words?
faqs.answer: Readers are instructed to stop at the limit, so anything beyond it earns nothing. In practice the part that disappears is the evaluation paragraph, the four-mark criterion, because it sits at the end. The fix is structural rather than editorial: cut the paragraph that restates the article, cut definitions the student never uses again, and move evaluation earlier in the piece. Check what your school counts towards the limit, because practice on footnotes, captions and diagram labels varies between schools and the school's instruction is the one that applies to your child.

faqs.question: Must all three commentaries use different key concepts?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they must also come from different units of the syllabus and different news sources. That constraint turns the portfolio into a planning problem rather than three separate essays. A student who writes two strong microeconomics commentaries and then finds the third must cover the global economy, with a concept not yet used, has lost options rather than time. Mapping all three before the first is written costs one session and prevents the expensive version of the problem. Your child's teacher will confirm which units are eligible and how your school records the concept for each piece.

faqs.question: Is diagram coaching worth paying for when the criterion carries three marks?
faqs.answer: Three marks a commentary is nine across the portfolio, so it is not trivial, but Economics IA diagrams are usually the part students already handle. Pay for it only if the diagrams are wrong or decorative. The common fault is a correctly drawn diagram the text never refers to: axes labelled, curves shifted, no sentence explaining which shift the article describes. That is a ten-minute fix rather than a paid block. Spend the hours on evaluation and the key concept instead, where twenty-one of the 45 marks sit and where drafts genuinely stall.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Paper 3 change what portfolio support is worth?
faqs.answer: It changes the order of spending. At Higher Level the portfolio carries about 20% of the grade and the HL Paper 3 policy paper carries roughly 30%, so a student with polished commentaries and untrained Paper 3 technique is buying in the wrong place. Paper 3 rewards calculation, a recommended policy and the same evaluative habit the portfolio trains, which is why families often buy a combined block: portfolio checkpoints through the year, then six to ten hours on Paper 3. Standard Level students sit no Paper 3 and should weight the portfolio more heavily.

faqs.question: Someone offered a finished commentary for AED 1,500. What is wrong with that?
faqs.answer: Submitting text a student did not produce is malpractice under IB academic-honesty rules, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller. A sanction can reach the whole Diploma rather than one subject. Your child also signs an authenticity declaration and the teacher authenticates the work, so somebody has to put a false statement in writing. Pages advertising finished commentaries at four-figure AED prices are selling a risk rather than a service. The legitimate version of that spend is five to eight hours of teaching, which costs about the same and leaves a student who can defend every line.

faqs.question: Our school Economics teacher offers paid evening help. Is that permitted?
faqs.answer: Not for students at their own school, in Abu Dhabi at least. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in the emirate prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at that school, and the private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring the same arrangement. A teacher tutoring outside school hours needs that permit. Beyond the rule there is a plain conflict: the person who will mark and authenticate the portfolio should not be paid to help build it. Verify the current wording with the school and the regulator before agreeing to anything.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should we start paying for portfolio support?
faqs.answer: Early in DP1, once the first microeconomics unit has been taught and before any article is chosen. One or two sessions then, mapping which unit and key concept each commentary will take and learning how to screen an article, cut the hours needed later. The expensive pattern is the reverse: nothing until the Economics portfolio deadline is three weeks away, then a scramble no amount of money compresses. If your child is already late, the honest answer is that help still works but it buys damage control rather than marks, and it should be priced that way.

faqs.question: Do Economics commentaries count towards Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency looks at the certificate rather than at individual components. For the British track the published rule is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No International Baccalaureate points figure appears on this page because none has been read on the Ministry's own site, so check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, and no provider performs the process for you.

faqs.question: Can portfolio sessions move to post-Iftar times during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so a slot that normally sits at 5pm can move to 9pm or 10pm with nobody travelling. UAE school days shorten during Ramadan and afternoon concentration drops, which matters because drafting a commentary is composition work rather than revision. Families often keep one short checkpoint a week through the month and move heavier drafting to the fortnight after Eid. Tell us the timing you want at booking, and the schedule is built around your child's school calendar rather than ours.

faqs.question: How many hours of support does one commentary usually take?
faqs.answer: Three to five for a student working to a deadline they have not yet missed: one session screening articles and fixing the key concept, one on the diagram and the analysis, one on evaluation and the word count, plus a short read-back before the school's internal date. Five to eight if the article was already chosen badly, because the work restarts. Fewer than three usually means somebody is editing rather than teaching. Ask any provider to break a quote into those stages, so you can see what you are buying and what you can drop.

ib-economics-ia-help.closingHeading: Start with the cheapest hour, not the most urgent one
ib-economics-ia-help.closingBody: If your child's Economics portfolio is 16 weeks away, the most valuable hour you can buy this year is a single planning session that fixes the unit, the key concept and the article type for all three commentaries. If it is three weeks away, buy triage and know that is what you are buying. Either way, start with the free first lesson: one hour, one tutor, no card details taken. Send the level, the school's internal deadline and the state of each draft, and you will get an honest number of hours rather than a block price. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Pricing the final stretch of the Diploma, honestly
paragraphs: Most UAE parents come to IB exam preparation with one question and get an answer to a different one. The question is what the last two terms will cost and whether the money will change a grade. The answer offered is usually a rate card with no work attached to it. Published rates across the Emirates in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 for a premium named specialist, and nothing in that spread tells a parent which hour will shift a Paper 2 mark upward.

The honest way to price Diploma preparation is to start from where the marks sit. A Diploma candidate carries six subject grades on a one-to-seven scale, giving a maximum of 42, plus up to three further points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination, for a ceiling of 45. In most subjects the internal assessment is already worth a fifth of the final grade and is submitted months before the papers. That means a family paying for preparation in February is buying a change to roughly 80 per cent of the grade, not all of it, and a provider who does not say so is selling you a number rather than a plan.

The UAE adds its own arithmetic. Dubai's regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so a household budget that absorbed a fee increase every year suddenly has room in it, and a lot of that room is going into tuition. At the same time every Dubai private school, whatever curriculum it is licensed for, must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which takes real hours out of the week a DP2 student would otherwise spend on three Higher Levels. Ramadan then moves the useful part of the evening. None of that appears on a rate card, and all of it changes how many hours a family actually needs.

IB Gram delivers this work as one-to-one online tuition, over live video, to families anywhere in the Emirates. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. A Sharjah family paying for a visiting tutor pays for travel and is limited to whoever teaches within a reasonable drive; the same family online is choosing from specialists who teach Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 or the Chemistry scientific investigation all day, and can take a 7pm Gulf Standard Time slot without anyone sitting in traffic on the Emirates Road first. The saving is real, but the subject match matters more than the saving.

What follows is the cost case in full: the market rate bands with their sources, the six things that legitimately move a quote, a twenty-week ladder counted back from the first paper with hours and indicative spend attached, the paper weightings for eleven subjects, the internal-assessment criteria by letter with their marks, the academic-honesty line that no budget can move, and what happens on results day if a grade lands one mark under a boundary. Figures are market figures, dated and attributed. Nothing here is a quoted IB Gram price list, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks are left.
