process.title: Tell us the emirate, the school and the year group
process.description: The first message needs three things: where you are, which school, and which year. That tells us which authority licenses the school, whether the mandatory UAE subjects stream applies, and which board is likely to be in play. It takes a parent two minutes and saves a session of diagnosis later.

process.title: Confirm the board, the syllabus code and the tier
process.description: We ask you to get the statement of entry from the exams officer, or the subject list from the Diploma coordinator. Board, code and tier decide the papers, the content and the grade ceiling. For an MYP student we ask for the criterion marks out of eight rather than the overall 1-7 grade.

process.title: A free trial hour with the proposed coach
process.description: One hour, over live video, with the coach we think fits, before any payment and with no card details taken. You see the teaching rather than a sales call. If the fit is wrong, say so and we propose someone else or tell you plainly that we do not have the right specialist free.

process.title: A plan counted back from the entry deadline
process.description: After the trial you get a written plan that starts from the board's published key dates and works backwards: entry deadline, forecast-grade date, mock window, then the papers. It states how many sessions a week, on which day at Gulf Standard Time, and what the first four will cover.

process.title: A written review after four sessions
process.description: At four sessions we write to you with what has changed, what has not, and whether the hours should go up, down or move to a different subject. If a subject is better served by someone else, we say that. A plan nobody reviews becomes a standing order rather than a teaching decision.

whyPoints.title: The regulator map is on the page, not saved for a sales call
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education each govern different emirates, and ADEK was named by none of the competitor pages we examined. Knowing which one applies to your school tells you where to read its inspection judgement for free before you spend anything on coaching.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes before subject names
whyPoints.description: Coaching starts from the statement of entry rather than the report card, because Cambridge and Pearson set different papers for subjects that share a name, and a Core entry caps the grade before any teaching happens. A coach working from a code is planning; a coach working from a subject name is guessing.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory UAE subjects have a stream of their own
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever the international curriculum, organised in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and taught in a specified language. We coach them as their own stream, within the school's own material, because the rules do not allow substituting different content.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do in the Emirates
whyPoints.description: We do not visit addresses in the UAE, hold no UAE premises or permit for a training institute, and claim no approval from any UAE authority or examination board. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Saying so costs enquiries and is still better than a parent discovering it after paying.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and its date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are each attributed to the provider that published them, read in October 2026, and presented as the market rather than as our price list. Where a source does not exist, such as an IB points figure for Ministry equivalency, we publish nothing and tell you where to check instead.

faqs.question: Our two children sit different boards, one on IGCSE and one in the Diploma. Can a single coaching plan cover both?
faqs.answer: Yes, but not with a single coach. The content, the papers and the assessment calendars are different enough that each child needs a subject specialist for their own board and level. What can be shared is the planning: one review conversation, one calendar covering both sets of deadlines, and sessions arranged so the household has one predictable evening pattern rather than two competing ones. Families with children on both boards usually start with the one closer to an exam series, add the second after a term, and keep both plans on the same written review cycle so hours can move between the two children when one needs them more.

faqs.question: Which authority actually licenses our school, and why should that change how we buy coaching?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. Dubai schools are overseen by KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, Sharjah by SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. It changes three things. It tells you where to read a published inspection judgement on your own school, which is free and more specific than most advice you will pay for. It tells you whose professional-ethics rules bind your child's teachers. And in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves assessment methods as well as fees, so the board and tier can be confirmed locally.

faqs.question: Dubai licenses seventeen curricula across its private schools. How do we work out which one our child is really examined on?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the statement of entry. A report card is not reliable evidence here, because one school building can run a British primary, a Cambridge IGCSE middle school and an IB Diploma sixth form at once, and a line that says Science can hide three separate entries or one combined award. The statement of entry names the board, the syllabus code and the tier. Those three facts decide which past papers are relevant, which content is on the course and what the grade ceiling is. Get them in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because the tier decision closes with the board's entry deadline.

faqs.question: The school says Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are compulsory. Does that really apply inside an IB building?
faqs.answer: It does. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point. The federal rule behind it is that private schools need not follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while still adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In practice this means those lessons occupy timetable minutes alongside six Diploma subjects or nine IGCSEs, not instead of them, which is why revision planning has to account for them.

faqs.question: KHDA separates Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Does a coaching session have to follow the same split?
faqs.answer: It follows the stream the school placed your child in, which is effectively the same thing. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. A coach works to the course your child is actually taking, so a non-Arab student on Arabic as an additional language is supported on that syllabus rather than on the first-language one. Moving a child between streams is a school decision, not something tutoring can arrange.

faqs.question: Our son's school teaches in English but his Islamic Education is in Arabic. Which language should a coach use?
faqs.answer: The same one the school uses, which is set by rule rather than preference. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Non-Arab students take Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum, so in an English-medium school that is English. If your son is in the Arab stream, his coaching runs in Arabic. If he is in the non-Arab stream at an English-medium school, it runs in English. Ask the school which stream he is in before booking, since the two are taught separately.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education want to see in an equivalency file for an IGCSE and A Level leaver?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs rather than something a tutoring company performs or guarantees, so verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or through your emirate's attestation channel, and be wary of anyone charging a fee to arrange it.

faqs.question: The Ministry asks for five accredited subjects. Does our daughter's IGCSE Arabic grade count towards that five?
faqs.answer: No. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count on the British track. That matters more than it sounds. A student carrying nine IGCSEs of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education has seven subjects available for the count, not nine, and dropping two more in Year 11 brings the margin uncomfortably close. One page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published five-subject rule. Count the subjects that will actually be counted before any are dropped.

faqs.question: A tutoring website quotes an IB points figure for UAE equivalency. Should we trust it?
faqs.answer: Not without checking it on an official page. The source we read sets out the British-track requirements in plain numbers and the American-track test thresholds, and states no IB points threshold at all. We therefore publish none, and we would treat any figure appearing on a tutoring site without a moe.gov.ae citation as unverified. The cost of inheriting someone else's wrong number is paid by your child's application, not by the website that published it. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator and check the Ministry's own page, in that order, before building subject choices around a points target.

faqs.question: Is the person coaching our child legally allowed to charge us in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the application through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so ignore any amount quoted on a tutoring page. Ask to see the permit before the first paid hour.

faqs.question: A teacher at our daughter's own school has offered paid evening lessons. Is there a problem with that?
faqs.answer: There usually is. The code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Those rules exist because the same person would be teaching, assessing and privately charging for the same child. Treat the offer as one to decline politely, and verify the current wording against your emirate's own policy document rather than relying on a summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Our school's inspection report came back Good rather than Outstanding. Where should coaching money go after reading it?
faqs.answer: Into whatever subject area the report judged weakest at your child's phase, not into the overall band. An inspection judgement is reported by phase and by subject, so a school rated Good overall can carry a noticeably weaker judgement in secondary mathematics or in a science, and that paragraph is the most useful free diagnostic a parent gets. What the report cannot tell you is anything about your individual child. Use it to decide which subject to ask about at parents' evening, then use the subject teacher's answer to decide where an hour a week actually goes.

faqs.question: Cambridge gave our centre a zone letter. Does that really change which timetable we read?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth taking seriously. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your exams officer which zone your school sits in and work from that version of the PDF on Cambridge's own site. Revision planning backwards from a paper date is only as good as the date, and a zone mismatch can move a paper by a day or more.

faqs.question: Final entries close in November for a February exam series. What should be finished by then?
faqs.answer: The decisions, not the revision. For Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 series the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that placed a candidate in that window went through the centre in the term before it. By that entry date the tier should be settled, the subject list fixed and the syllabus codes confirmed with the exams officer, which means the evidence for those choices has to exist a month or two earlier again. Predicted grades are then requested by the school ahead of the series, so enough marked past-paper work has to exist by then for the school to forecast honestly. A plan that begins in the exam month has skipped both of those checkpoints. A Cambridge candidate runs the same sequence against June, with November waiting as the resit.

faqs.question: Does a coaching company need a KHDA permit, and does IB Gram hold one?
faqs.answer: A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, occupies no premises in the UAE and claims no endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. No UAE authority approves individual private coaches either, so a provider describing its tutors as regulator-endorsed is describing something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can a coach look over an Internal Assessment draft, and where exactly does the line sit?
faqs.answer: A coach can explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help narrow a research question until it is investigable, check that a method will produce data the criteria can reward, teach the statistical handling needed, read a draft the student wrote and give feedback on it, and explain referencing conventions. What a coach must not do is author any part of the submission, supply wording to be pasted in, or edit a draft into a final version. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, the TOK essay, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. Providers selling finished assessments exist in this market and the risk falls on the student.

faqs.question: Nobody comes to the villa, so how does an hour of coaching actually run?
faqs.answer: On live video, one-to-one, at a fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time. The coach shares a screen for working, the student writes on paper and photographs it in or works directly on the shared document, and annotated scripts and written feedback stay available after the session. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, so there is no UAE in-home option to compare on price. The practical gain is that your child gets the specialist who teaches that specific paper rather than whoever is within driving distance, which matters most in Al Ain, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Umm Al Quwain.

faqs.question: Our daughter is on the Cambridge Core tier and wants a UAE university place. Is a Core entry enough?
faqs.answer: It depends on the grade the Core tier allows and on what the university asks for, so check both before assuming. The tier caps the grade available, which is why the Core or Extended decision is the first thing a coach examines, and it closes with the board's entry deadline rather than at the end of the course. Separately, the Ministry's British track counts five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education. Ask the school whether a tier change is still possible for the next series, and verify the university's own published entry requirements directly.

ib-igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the paperwork, then book the hour
ib-igcse-coaching.closingBody: Before you compare coaches, collect four things: which authority licenses your child's school, which stream the mandatory UAE subjects put them in, which board and syllabus code appear on the statement of entry, and when that board closes entries for the next series. Those four facts turn a vague search for IB IGCSE coaching in the UAE into a specific request a specialist can answer properly. Send them to us and we will propose a coach for a free trial hour, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card details taken. If we do not have the right specialist free, we will tell you that instead of offering a near match.
